## 0. How to use this document

### 0.1 Structure

| § | Content |
|---|---|
| 1 | Repository layout, package responsibilities, layer rules, generated files |
| 2 | Toolchain, dependencies, environment variables, database roles and URLs |
| 3 | Running the system: ports, processes, PID files, proxy rules, temporary files |
| 4 | Make targets with exact semantics: loop targets (§4.1 to §4.4) and supervisor targets never run by the loop (§4.5) |
| 5 | Kernel APIs with binding signatures, including keys and secrets (§5.19) and tenant provisioning (§5.20) |
| 6 | Backend conventions: command pattern, state machines, lists, API routes, migrations, logging, AI, architecture tests |
| 7 | Engine package conventions |
| 8 | Frontend conventions |
| 9 | Testing: markers, database fixtures, isolation suite, answer-key schema and loader, golden parity runner, Hypothesis, Playwright, performance |
| 10 | Gates, git hygiene, forbidden commands, done checklist per BUILD_SPEC item |
| 11 | Gaps closed |
| 12 | Open questions for supervisor |

### 0.2 Identifier families

Every normative item has a stable id of the form `DG-<AREA>-<NN>` (make targets use `DG-MK-<target>`). Ids are never renumbered or reused. A withdrawn item keeps its row, marked "Withdrawn" in a supervisor amendment.

| Area | Scope | Area | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| LAY | Repository layout | ARC | Architecture tests |
| ENV | Toolchain and environment | ENG | Engine package |
| RUN | Processes and ports | FE | Frontend |
| MK | Make targets | TST | Test infrastructure and markers |
| KRN | Kernel APIs | AK | Answer-key schema and loader |
| CMD | Command pattern | PAR | Golden parity runner |
| SM | State machines | PROP | Hypothesis profiles and invariants |
| LST | Lists | E2E | Playwright harness |
| API | API routes and schemas | PERF | Performance harness |
| MIG | Migrations | GATE | Gates |
| LOG | Logging and personal data | GIT | Git hygiene |
| AI | AI conventions | FORBID | Forbidden commands |
| READ | Reading lists and document authority (rev 1.1) | DONE | Done checklist |

These ids do not collide with the other families in use: `REQ-`, `CTL-`, `POL-`, `ALG-`, `JET-`, `CHK-`, `DEV-`, `PJR-`, `DS-`, `NC-`, `TY-`, `SC-`, `RLS-`, `IM-`, `PT-`, `AUD-`, `E-nn`, `T-…`, `DB-`, `API-C-`, `API-R-`, `API-S-`, `LM-`, `J-nn`, `SF-nn`, `WLD-`, `BR-`, and invariants `P1`..`P14`, which are cited as `PROP:Pn` (`docs/03-REQUIREMENTS.md` §1.4). Where two other documents share a prefix (`PT-` in 04 and POLICIES; unprefixed `OQ-nn` in POLICIES, 04 and DESIGN_SYSTEM), this guide names the document in the citation, for example `POLICIES PT-03` or `04:OQ-05` (B1-027). Ids of `docs/05-ARCHITECTURE.md` are cited with "05" (for example `05 SBX-07`).

### 0.3 Facts, assumptions and judgements

- **[F] Fact:** a statement about a source document, a decision or the observed machine, with a citation.
- **[A] Assumption:** a premise owned elsewhere. Material assumptions are repeated in §12.
- **[J] Judgement:** a call made in this document, with a one-line rationale.

### 0.4 Normative words

"Must", "is" and imperative sentences are requirements for the build loop. "May" marks an allowed option. A code block titled "Binding signature" fixes names, parameters, return types and raised problems. Private helpers may be added freely; the public names, their meaning and their observable behaviour may not change without a supervisor amendment.

### 0.5 Paths and choices other documents delegated to this guide

| Delegating document and id | Default proposed there | Binding value here | Rationale [J] |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design brief "backend/app" | `backend/app` | `backend/erev_api` (the application package) | `docs/04-DATA_MODEL.md` already cites eleven module paths under `erev_api.*` (NC-14, IM-X, T-PLT-11, T-PLT-19, T-PLT-31, E-03, §3, DB-03, DB-10, DB-14). The import name must equal the directory name. |

### 0.6 Split contracts, identifier authority and reading lists (rev 1.1)

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-READ-01 | The engine specification is two files with one precedence rank (D-74): `docs/accounting/ENGINE_SPEC.md` (index and stages 01 to 08) and `docs/accounting/ENGINE_SPEC_B.md` (stages 09 to 15). "ENGINE_SPEC" in this guide means both files. Reading starts from the index in `ENGINE_SPEC.md`, which lists every section of both. |
| DG-READ-02 | The screen specification is two files with one precedence rank (D-74): `docs/design/SCREENS.md` (index, information architecture, core workbench) and `docs/design/SCREENS_B.md` (close, reports, admin, AI, onboarding). "SCREENS" in this guide means both files. SCREENS owns the route path of each SF id; PRD SF ids are stable (D-73). |
| DG-READ-03 | Identifier authority (D-73). `docs/04-DATA_MODEL.md` owns enumeration literals (§3), permission codes (T-PLT-11), problem slugs (§15.2), and finding and exception codes (§15.4). `docs/accounting/POLICIES.md` §1 owns registry keys and option literals (D-13a, D-21a). Code, tests, answer keys and this guide cite them verbatim; UI labels are copy. When another document spells a literal differently, the loop uses the owner's spelling and records a SPEC-Q (DG-DONE-12). |
| DG-READ-04 | Before starting a BUILD_SPEC item, the loop reads the rows of the table below for the item's type, in the order given. When the item depends on a listed document that does not exist yet, the loop writes `BLOCKED:` (DG-GATE-02). |

| Item type | Read first | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Any item | `PROMPT.md`; this guide §0, §4 and §10; the item's REQ rows in `docs/03-REQUIREMENTS.md`; the `docs/01-DECISIONS.md` §7 amendments the item cites | the sections of this guide the item names |
| Engine helper or stage | `docs/accounting/POLICIES.md` ALG, JET and CHK rows; the `docs/accounting/ENGINE_SPEC.md` index, then the stage sections in `ENGINE_SPEC.md` or `ENGINE_SPEC_B.md`; this guide §5.9, §5.16 and §7 | the answer keys the item cites (§9.5) |
| Schema, command or API route | `docs/04-DATA_MODEL.md` table, enumeration, invariant and API rows; this guide §5 and §6 | the `docs/05-ARCHITECTURE.md` sections the item names; `docs/02-PRD.md` SM-nn and journeys |
| Screen | the `docs/design/SCREENS.md` index, then the screen sections in `SCREENS.md` or `SCREENS_B.md`; `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`; this guide §8 | `docs/02-PRD.md` SF-nn and J-nn rows; this guide §9.8 |
| Legacy parity | `docs/legacy/DEVIATIONS.md`; `docs/legacy/golden/deviations.json`; this guide §9.6 | `docs/legacy/07-golden-master.md` |
| Performance | `docs/05-ARCHITECTURE.md` §4; this guide DG-MK-perf-seed, DG-MK-perf and §9.9 | `docs/03-REQUIREMENTS.md` REQ-OPS-008, REQ-OPS-009, REQ-CLS-014 |

### 1.2 Layout rules

| Id | Rule | Rationale [J] |
|---|---|---|
| DG-LAY-01 | Top-level directories are exactly those in §1.1. The loop may not create other top-level directories. Gitignored tool cache directories at the top level — exactly `.ruff_cache`, `.pytest_cache` and `.mypy_cache` — are build artefacts, not layout: `test_repository_layout.py` ignores those three names and every other unexpected entry keeps failing (supervisor ruling 2026-09-19, after four lanes hit a stray root cache from direct ruff runs; rev 1.8). Tool caches still belong under `backend/` (the Makefile exports `RUFF_CACHE_DIR` and `MYPY_CACHE_DIR`; the GATE-BIND-1 execution context exports the same for its stages, and its own marker lives at `<ctx>/.run/gate-pid`, never at the context root). `docs/` is supervisor-owned except `docs/api/` (OpenAPI), `docs/guides/` (runbook, user guide, migration guide, customer-operated ITGC guide: REQ-OPS-003, REQ-OPS-004, REQ-CTL-004) and `docs/security/` (threat model and ASVS checklist: REQ-SEC-005). `docs/qa/` belongs to the supervisor (`docs/00-GOAL.md` §3). | One predictable tree for fresh-context agents |
| DG-LAY-02 | `backend/` is one uv project (`erev-backend`) that builds two import packages, `erev_api` and `erev_engine`. There is one virtual environment, `backend/.venv`. | One lock file and one interpreter. Engine purity is enforced by tests (DG-ARC-02) rather than by a second distribution. |
| DG-LAY-03 | Layer order inside `erev_api`: `api` → `domain` → kernel modules (`uow`, `db`, `auth`, `audit`, `approvals`, `idempotency`, `problems`, `money`, `clock`, `periods`, `numbering`, `events`, `jobs`, `files`, `registry`, `explain`, `projections`, `schemas`, `logging`, `controls`) → `erev_engine`. A module may import only from its own layer or lower layers. `adapters` implement protocols defined in kernel or domain modules and are wired only in `main.py`, `worker.py`, `cli.py` and test fixtures. `erev_engine` imports nothing outside the Python standard library. | Clean dependency direction; the engine stays DB-free (D-10) |
| DG-LAY-04 | `erev_api/domain/<area>/` uses these areas, one directory each: `platform` (tenants, users, roles, SoD, API clients, support grants, webhooks, access reviews), `reference` (entities, books, calendars, periods, currencies, FX, accounts, mapping, dimensions, customers, products), `ssp`, `policies` (POB templates, rule sets, registry versions, overrides, judgements), `contracts` (contracts, events, modifications, estimates, holds, combination, computation orchestration and bundle building), `costs`, `close` (period states, close runs, locks, reconciliations, sign-offs), `journals` (subledger postings, journal runs, export, acknowledgements, manual adjustments), `reports` (report runs, disclosures, evidence packs), `imports` (templates, uploads, validation, diff, commit, exception queue, mapping profiles), `integrations`, `forecast`, `ai`, `migration`, `demo` (demo and volume generators). Each area holds `commands.py` (state-changing handlers), `queries.py` (read handlers) and private helper modules. | Areas mirror `docs/03-REQUIREMENTS.md` §1.1 so items map to folders |
| DG-LAY-05 | SQLAlchemy is used in Core style only: `Table` objects in `erev_api/db/tables/`, statements built with `insert`, `select`, `update`. There are no ORM mapped classes and no `relationship()`. | Append-only tables, forced RLS and set-based writes are easier to audit without an identity map, autoflush or lazy loading |
| DG-LAY-06 | Naming: Python modules `snake_case.py`; tests `test_<subject>.py`; React components `PascalCase.tsx`; hooks `useThing.ts`; route modules `kebab-case.tsx`; Playwright journeys `j-nn-<slug>.journey.ts`. | Predictable discovery |
| DG-LAY-07 | Generated and copied files are committed and each has a staleness check in `make ci` (table §1.3). A generated file is never edited by hand. | Reviewable diffs; no hidden generation step |
| DG-LAY-08 | Additions to `.gitignore`: `.data/`, `backend/.hypothesis/`, `backend/.pytest_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `frontend/dist/`, `frontend/e2e/.screens/`, `frontend/e2e/.results/`, `deploy/terraform/gcp/.terraform/`, `*.tfstate`, `*.tfstate.*`, `dist/`, `coverage/`, `release-manifest.json` (rev 1.1; DG-MK-release-manifest). The existing entries (`.scratch/`, `.run/`, `.ralph/`, `node_modules/`, `__pycache__/`, `.venv/`, `.env` and others) stay. `deploy/terraform/gcp/.terraform.lock.hcl` is committed. | Keeps artefacts and secrets out of git |
| DG-LAY-09 | `legacy-harness/`, `research-harness/` and `~/dev/erev-legacy` are read-only inputs. No code imports from them. Only `scripts/build_fixtures.py` reads files from them, and it copies bytes with SHA-256 verification (DG-PAR-02). | M-ARCH-09 guard |
| DG-LAY-10 | `backend/pyproject.toml` uses the hatchling build backend with `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = ["erev_api", "erev_engine"]` and `[project.scripts] erev = "erev_api.cli:app"`, so `uv sync` installs `backend/.venv/bin/erev`. `requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"`. | The binaries named in §3 and §4 exist after `make setup` |
| DG-LAY-11 | SQLite (D-40a; rev 1.1). SQLite is never an application datastore or test database: the API, worker, CLI, seed and every test run on PostgreSQL 17 (D-40). The Python `sqlite3` module may be imported only by (a) modules under `backend/erev_api/domain/migration/` that read an uploaded legacy `ASC606.db` (D-31, REQ-MIG-001), opened read-only through the URI `file:<path>?mode=ro&immutable=1` on the file-store copy, and (b) `scripts/build_fixtures.py` and `backend/tests/support/parity/`, which build or read SQLite fixtures derived from the golden inputs (DG-PAR-02). DG-ARC-05 enforces this. | The legacy import and the parity fixtures need SQLite as a file format, never as a store |

### 1.3 Generated and copied files

| File | Generator | Source of truth | Staleness check in `make ci` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/api/openapi.json` | `make openapi` (`erev openapi --out docs/api/openapi.json`) | FastAPI routes and schemas | `scripts/openapi_check.sh` regenerates into `.run/openapi-check/` and compares bytes |
| `frontend/src/lib/api/schema.d.ts` | `make openapi` (openapi-typescript over `docs/api/openapi.json`) | `docs/api/openapi.json` | same script |
| `backend/erev_api/registry/policies.py` | `make registry-seed` (`erev registry-seed`) | `docs/accounting/POLICIES.md` §1 tables | `erev registry-seed --check` |
| `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` | `make tokens` (byte copy) | `docs/design/tokens.css` | DS-LINT-14 inside `make design-check` |
| Trigger functions for IM-S tables inside each revision | `erev_api.db.migration_ops.transition_trigger_sql(table)` | `erev_api.db.transitions.TRANSITIONS` | DG-ARC-07 drift test |
| `backend/erev_api/controls/controls.yaml` | hand-maintained, validated | `docs/03-REQUIREMENTS.md` §4.1 | DG-ARC-10 test compares the control ids and titles |
| `backend/tests/fixtures/legacy_*` | `make fixtures` (`scripts/build_fixtures.py`) | legacy UAT workbooks, probe inputs, shipped database | `scripts/build_fixtures.py --check` verifies every SHA-256 in `backend/tests/fixtures/manifest.json` |

## 2. Toolchain and environment

### 2.1 Toolchain

| Id | Tool | Required | Observed 2026-09-12 [F] | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DG-ENV-01 | uv | ≥ 0.11 | 0.11.7 | Python environment and lock (`backend/uv.lock`) |
| DG-ENV-02 | Python | 3.12.x (`backend/.python-version` = `3.12`; `requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"`) | 3.12.13 (system `python3` is 3.14; never use it for the project) | Backend, engine, scripts |
| DG-ENV-03 | Node.js and npm | Node ≥ 22 (`"engines": {"node": ">=22"}`), npm with `package-lock.json`; `npm ci` only | Node 25.9.0, npm 11.12.1; pnpm absent | Frontend and Playwright |
| DG-ENV-04 | PostgreSQL | 17, Homebrew server on 127.0.0.1:5432; `psql` 17 client | 17.11 | Every backend test, the API, the worker (D-40) |
| DG-ENV-05 | GNU Make | 3.81 compatible: no `.ONESHELL`, no `--output-sync`, no `$(file …)`, no grouped targets. A recipe of more than three commands calls a script in `scripts/`. | 3.81 | Entry points (§4) |
| DG-ENV-06 | Docker | optional; `make compose-verify` records `skipped-no-daemon` when `docker info` fails | 29.4.0 | Image and compose verification (G11) |
| DG-ENV-07 | Terraform | optional; `make tf-validate` records `skipped-not-installed` when absent | 1.15.6 | `terraform validate` (G11) |

### 2.2 Dependencies

Majors fixed by D-40 and D-41 are mandatory. Every other package is pinned by the lock files. DG-ENV-08: adding a runtime dependency requires (1) a licence on the REQ-SEC-010 allow-list, (2) the lock-file update in the same commit, and (3) a passing `make licence-check`. Rev 1.2 (D-76, DG-OQ-13): the loop adds a dependency by editing `backend/pyproject.toml` or `frontend/package.json` and running `make setup LOCK=1` (DG-MK-setup), the only command that may update a lock file or download packages; `uv add`, `uv lock`, `uv pip`, `npm install` and `npm update` are never run outside `make setup` (DG-FORBID-08). DG-ENV-09: tests, scripts and the engine add no dependency that performs network calls at import or run time.

| Scope | Packages |
|---|---|
| Backend runtime | fastapi, uvicorn (no `--reload` in background processes), pydantic 2, pydantic-settings, sqlalchemy 2, alembic, psycopg 3 (`psycopg[binary]`; NOTICE entry), procrastinate (exact pin; its SQL schema is installed by migration, DG-MIG-09), openpyxl, xlsxwriter, argon2-cffi, pyotp, cryptography, uuid-utils, structlog, httpx (adapters only), anthropic (adapter only), typer, pyyaml, python-multipart |
| Backend dev | pytest, hypothesis, ruff, mypy, types-PyYAML |
| Frontend runtime | react 19, react-dom 19, react-router 7, @tanstack/react-query 5, @tanstack/react-table, @tanstack/react-virtual, recharts, @phosphor-icons/react, openapi-fetch, react-hook-form, zod, @hookform/resolvers, clsx |
| Frontend dev | vite 6, @vitejs/plugin-react, tailwindcss 4, @tailwindcss/vite, typescript 5, vitest, @testing-library/react, @testing-library/user-event, @testing-library/jest-dom, jsdom, msw, eslint, typescript-eslint, eslint-plugin-react-hooks, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, prettier, openapi-typescript, @playwright/test, @axe-core/playwright, otpauth |

### 2.3 `.env.example`

`.env.example` is committed with exactly these names. Values are placeholders. `.env` is never committed, never printed and never overwritten by any target (DG-FORBID-01).

```dotenv
# eRev Cloud local configuration. Copy to .env and replace placeholders. Never commit .env.
EREV_ENV=dev

# PostgreSQL 17 on 127.0.0.1:5432 (roles and databases provisioned by the supervisor; D-42)
# erev_owner: migrations and test schema reset only. erev_app: API, worker, CLI, seed, tests.
EREV_DB_OWNER_URL=postgresql://erev_owner:CHANGE_ME@127.0.0.1:5432/erev
EREV_DB_APP_URL=postgresql://erev_app:CHANGE_ME@127.0.0.1:5432/erev
EREV_TEST_DB_OWNER_URL=postgresql://erev_owner:CHANGE_ME@127.0.0.1:5432/erev_test
EREV_TEST_DB_APP_URL=postgresql://erev_app:CHANGE_ME@127.0.0.1:5432/erev_test
EREV_E2E_DB_OWNER_URL=postgresql://erev_owner:CHANGE_ME@127.0.0.1:5432/erev_e2e
EREV_E2E_DB_APP_URL=postgresql://erev_app:CHANGE_ME@127.0.0.1:5432/erev_e2e

# Ports (defaults are the docs/00-GOAL.md §5 values; override only in supervisor review worktrees, D-70)
EREV_API_PORT=8190
EREV_WEB_PORT=5270
EREV_E2E_API_PORT=8199
EREV_E2E_WEB_PORT=5279

# Master keys (64 hex characters each), read through EnvSecretStore; per-tenant keys are derived by HKDF (DG-KRN-KEY-02). Production reads Secret Manager.
EREV_ENCRYPTION_KEY=CHANGE_ME_64_HEX
EREV_AUDIT_HMAC_MASTER_KEY=CHANGE_ME_64_HEX
EREV_SECURITY_EVENT_HMAC_KEY=CHANGE_ME_64_HEX

# Demo and e2e credentials (docs/02-PRD.md WLD-U-R1, WLD-U-R2)
EREV_DEMO_PASSWORD=Demo1234!Demo
EREV_DEMO_TOTP_SECRET=CHANGE_ME_BASE32
```

[F] Rev 1.1 (B1-008): `EREV_RUN_DIR`, `EREV_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, `EREV_CORS_ORIGINS`, `EREV_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS`, `EREV_WORKER_CONCURRENCY`, `EREV_WORKER_QUEUES`, `EREV_KEY_PROVIDER`, `EREV_EMAIL_BACKEND`, `EREV_METRICS_ENABLED` and `EREV_METRICS_TOKEN` are added for 05 §2.8. Three 05 variables are not used: `EREV_AI_DISABLED` (the name is `EREV_AI_KILL_SWITCH`), `EREV_LOCAL_KEYRING_PATH` (no keyring file, D-75 Q8, DG-KRN-KEY-05) and `EREV_MOCKS_BASE_URL` (in-process mocks, D-72, DG-API-09). Hosted-only variables of 05 CFG-05, CFG-07, CFG-13, CFG-18 and CFG-21 are read by the production adapters from the secret store and never appear in `.env.example`.

### 2.4 Environments, database roles and URLs

| Id | Rule | Rationale [J] |
|---|---|---|
| DG-ENV-10 | `EREV_ENV` selects the database pair: `dev` → `EREV_DB_OWNER_URL`, `EREV_DB_APP_URL`; `test` → `EREV_TEST_DB_*`; `e2e` → `EREV_E2E_DB_*`; `production` → `EREV_DB_APP_URL` read from the process environment for every `EREV_KEY_PROVIDER` (rev 1.33, D-98 105, lane P2: the deployment injects it from a pinned Secret Manager version — `secret_key_ref` in `deploy/terraform/gcp/cloud_run.tf` hosted, `deploy/compose.env.example` under compose; the secret store is where the deployment reads secrets, never a runtime resolver of the database URL, so `Settings` requires the variable under `production` and fails construction without it, DG-KRN-CFG-02) and `EREV_DB_OWNER_URL` only for the processes that migrate (the hosted api and worker never hold it, DPL-33); under `EREV_KEY_PROVIDER=local` (compose; 05 DPL-13, OQ-ARC-11; rev 1.2) `EnvSecretStore` serves the CFG-26 master keys from `deploy/compose.env.example`. These four are the only values; 05 CFG-01 `perf`, `compose` and `staging` are not `EREV_ENV` values (B1-008). Pytest forces `EREV_ENV=test` in `backend/tests/conftest.py` before any `erev_api` import, with one exception (rev 1.1): when `EREV_PERF_RUN=1`, which only `make perf` sets, conftest sets `EREV_ENV=dev` and collects only `backend/tests/perf/` (DG-PERF-06). `make e2e` sets `EREV_ENV=e2e`; `make db-reset`, `make perf-seed` and `make perf` set `EREV_ENV=dev` and take the development database the environment names — `erev` in the main checkout (D-75 Q7; rev 1.200: `make db-reset` takes the development database the environment names, which in a lane's worktree is its `erev_rv_*` database, DG-ENV-13; rev 1.206: so do `make perf-seed` and `make perf`, whose recipes name no database and check none — this row gave them database `erev`, which is where they are run: the main checkout, never a lane, 05 PERF-11). | One switch; ordinary tests can never touch the dev database, and the perf tenant survives test sessions |
| DG-ENV-11 | URLs may use `postgresql://`. `Settings` normalises them to `postgresql+psycopg://` and passes them to SQLAlchemy. The application logs the host, port and database name, never the user or password. | Accept the supervisor's URL form; keep secrets out of logs |
| DG-ENV-12 | Role guard. On first connection of the app engine, the process runs `SELECT current_user, r.rolsuper, r.rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles r WHERE r.rolname = current_user` and refuses to start unless the user is `erev_app` with both flags false. The owner engine requires `erev_owner` with `rolsuper = false`. | REQ-PLT-001; D-42: a superuser connection is never used by application code or isolation tests |
| DG-ENV-13 | Database allow-list. Every URL's database must be `erev`, `erev_test`, `erev_e2e` or match `^erev_rv_[a-z0-9_]+$` (supervisor review databases, D-70). Destructive resets (`DROP SCHEMA`) are allowed only when `current_database()` is `erev_test`, `erev_e2e` or `erev_rv_*`, or when the target is `make db-reset` (also run by `make seed RESET=1`) on `erev` with `EREV_ENV=dev` (DG-MK-db-reset). Rev 1.200 (supervisor ruling R-120 (i)): `erev db reset` resets the development database the environment names, and three things together make a database one — the environment's name (`EREV_ENV=dev`); the database's name (`erev` or `erev_rv_*`, which the server must answer for `current_database()`; never `erev_test` or `erev_e2e`, which their gates rebuild); and its tenants (none without the demo marker: a tenant with `is_demo` false, or a sandbox whose source tenant has it false or is gone, makes the command refuse; a database without the `tenant` table holds none; tenants that cannot be counted are not reset). The command names the one that does not hold and drops nothing (`controls/reset.py`). | `docs/00-GOAL.md` §5 shared-machine constraints |
| DG-ENV-14 | No code, target or test creates, drops or alters a database, role, extension, tablespace or server setting. `ALTER SYSTEM`, `CREATE DATABASE`, `CREATE ROLE`, `ALTER ROLE` and `CREATE EXTENSION` are forbidden strings in `backend/` and `scripts/`; DG-ARC-05 fails the build if they appear. | `docs/00-GOAL.md` §5; D-42; NC-18 |
| DG-ENV-15 | Assumption [A]: `erev_owner` owns the three databases, so it can create schema `erev` and install the Procrastinate objects in `public` (`docs/04-DATA_MODEL.md` OQ-02). `make setup` verifies `has_database_privilege('erev_owner', current_database(), 'CREATE')` on each database and stops with `BLOCKED: erev_owner lacks CREATE on <db>` otherwise. | Fail early with an actionable message for the supervisor |
| DG-ENV-16 | Keys. `scripts/check_env.py --ensure-keys` appends missing `EREV_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `EREV_AUDIT_HMAC_MASTER_KEY`, `EREV_SECURITY_EVENT_HMAC_KEY` and `EREV_DEMO_TOTP_SECRET` lines to `.env` with fresh random values (`secrets.token_hex(32)`; base32 from `secrets.token_bytes(20)`). It never changes an existing line, never prints a value and reports only the names it added. It never adds `EREV_DEMO_PASSWORD` (docs/02-PRD.md WLD-U-R1 requires `make e2e` to fail when it is missing). | Makes a fresh checkout runnable without anyone reading secrets |
| DG-ENV-17 | Keys and secrets (rev 1.1; D-75 Q8 confirms this model). Local master keys live in `.env` (`EREV_AUDIT_HMAC_MASTER_KEY`, `EREV_SECURITY_EVENT_HMAC_KEY`, `EREV_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) and are read through the `SecretStore` adapter `EnvSecretStore` (`erev_api.adapters.secrets`). Per-tenant key material is derived with HKDF-SHA256 (DG-KRN-KEY-02). `LocalKeyProvider` implements the 05 SAR-21 `KeyProvider` protocol over `EnvSecretStore`; there is no keyring file (DG-KRN-KEY-05). Hosted deployments use `GcpSecretManagerStore` and `GcpKeyProvider` (Secret Manager, Cloud KMS), artifacts only and never exercised in tests. Key identifiers follow 05 KEY-03 to KEY-05: `audit-hmac:<tenant id>:<n>` (stored in `tenant.audit_hmac_key_id`), `security-hmac:<n>`, `kek:<n>`. | D-43, REQ-SEC-003; tenant keys rotate by id without schema change |
| DG-ENV-18 | Operator alerts (05 OPR-24, CFG-31; rev 1.71). `EREV_OPERATOR_ALERT_EMAIL` names the recipient of platform-operator alerts through the CFG-17 email backend; `EREV_OPERATOR_ALERT_DELIVERY=log-only` is the operator's explicit acknowledgement that a `production` deployment delivers them by log and the non-durable local file trail (`<EREV_RUN_DIR>/operator-alerts/`) only. Both are hosted variables, absent from `.env.example`; under `dev`, `test` and `e2e` the email backend is `fake`, so nothing is ever sent live. `erev doctor` `operator-alerts` fails under `production` when neither is set. | Alerts never go silent unnoticed; no live provider call from a developer machine |

## 3. Running the system

### 3.1 Ports and processes

All servers bind `127.0.0.1` only. Ports are the `docs/00-GOAL.md` §5 values (overridable only through the `EREV_*_PORT` variables, DG-ENV-10 note).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| DG-RUN-02 | `worker` | none | `backend/.venv/bin/erev worker` (no `--queues`: all eight queues of DG-KRN-JOB-10, B1-009) | `.run/worker.pid` | `.run/worker.log` | `.run/worker.heartbeat` modified within 60 s |
| DG-RUN-03 | `web` | 5270 | `node frontend/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js --config frontend/vite.config.ts` with `EREV_API_PROXY_TARGET=http://127.0.0.1:8190`, `EREV_VITE_MODE=dev`, `VITE_EREV_DESIGN_GALLERY=1` | `.run/web.pid` | `.run/web.log` | `GET http://127.0.0.1:5270/` returns 200 |

### 3.2 Process control

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-RUN-10 | `scripts/proc.sh start <name> <port or -> -- <command…>`: (1) if `.run/<name>.pid` exists and `kill -0 <pid>` succeeds, print "`<name>` already running (pid N)" and exit 0; (2) if the port is in use (`lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN -t`) by a PID that is not in any `.run/*.pid` file, print "port `<port>` in use by another process; not stopping it" and exit 1; (3) otherwise run `nohup <command…> >> .run/<name>.log 2>&1 &` and write `$!` to `.run/<name>.pid`; (4) poll the readiness check of §3.1 every 0.5 s for up to 60 s (`scripts/wait_for_http.py`), then exit 0, or exit 1 and print the last 40 lines of the log. |
| DG-RUN-11 | `scripts/proc.sh stop <name>`: read `.run/<name>.pid`; if the process is alive send `kill -TERM <pid>`, poll `kill -0` every 0.5 s for up to 15 s, then send `kill -KILL <pid>`; remove the PID file. A missing PID file prints "`<name>` not running" and exits 0. No other stop mechanism exists: no `pkill`, `killall`, `kill $(lsof …)` or pattern matching (DG-FORBID-02). |
| DG-RUN-12 | `scripts/proc.sh status`: for every `.run/*.pid` print name, PID, alive or stale, port and readiness result. Stale PID files are reported, not deleted. |
| DG-RUN-13 | The PID in a PID file is the server process itself. That is why DG-RUN-01 to DG-RUN-06 call the binaries directly: `uv run` and `npm run` interpose a parent process, and stopping the parent can orphan the server. |
| DG-RUN-14 | Background servers never use auto-reload. `make backend RELOAD=1` may use `--reload` in the foreground only. [F] Mass edits by concurrent agents can make `uvicorn --reload` exit. |
| DG-RUN-15 | At the end of an iteration the loop stops every process it started (`make dev-down`, and the e2e and perf targets stop their own processes). A running dev stack left by the supervisor is detected by DG-RUN-10 step (1) and reused, never restarted. |
| DG-RUN-16 | Production startup (05 REL-03; rev 1.8). Under `EREV_ENV=production` the api (`erev api`; the first step of the `create_app` lifespan) and the worker (`erev worker`; before its connection pool and heartbeat) read `release-manifest.json` at the repository root (`/app/release-manifest.json` in the images; `erev_api.controls.release.MANIFEST_PATH`) before any database access, and stop when it is absent, not a JSON object, or names another engine version or schema head (`ReleaseManifestError`; uvicorn logs "Application startup failed. Exiting." and exits 3, the worker exits 1). The file is written by `make release-manifest` and enters the images through `make docker-build` (DG-MK-docker-build, DG-MK-release-manifest); `docker compose build` copies it too, so run `make release-manifest` before a compose build. `dev`, `test` and `e2e` derive the release when the file is absent. Both processes log `release.stamped` with `engine_release_id`, `engine_version`, `build_sha`, `schema_revision` and `source` (`manifest` or `derived`), so a deployment's api and worker identity is checked from their logs (one `engine_release` row, equal ids). |

### 3.3 Frontend proxy and cache rules

| Id | Rule | Rationale [J] |
|---|---|---|
| DG-RUN-20 | `frontend/vite.config.ts` reads `process.env.EREV_API_PROXY_TARGET` through `frontend/config/proxy.ts` `resolveProxyTarget`. When a dev or preview server starts and the value is unset or does not match `^http://127\.0\.0\.1:\d{2,5}$`, it throws `Error("EREV_API_PROXY_TARGET must be set, for example http://127.0.0.1:8190")`. `vite build` needs no proxy target, because DG-MK-build sets none (rev 1.3; BUILD_SPEC BS1-D-12). There is no default target. | A silent default would point the browser at the wrong API (design brief: "proxy target required or fail") |
| DG-RUN-21 | `server.host = "127.0.0.1"`, `server.port = Number(process.env.EREV_WEB_PORT ?? 5270)`, `server.strictPort = true`; `preview.host = "127.0.0.1"`, `preview.port = Number(process.env.EREV_E2E_WEB_PORT ?? 5279)`, `preview.strictPort = true`. Both `server.proxy` and `preview.proxy` map `/api` to the target with `changeOrigin: false` and `ws: false`. | Fixed ports; no port drift into another session's range |
| DG-RUN-22 | `cacheDir = "node_modules/.vite-" + (process.env.EREV_VITE_MODE ?? "dev")`, so dev and e2e servers never share pre-bundled dependencies. | [F] Two Vite roots sharing one `.vite/deps` cache clobber each other and blank the UI |
| DG-RUN-23 | `preview.headers` sets the same security headers as `deploy/docker/nginx/security-headers.conf` (CSP without inline scripts, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`). | e2e exercises REQ-SEC-004 |
| DG-RUN-24 | Fonts are vendored under `frontend/src/assets/fonts/` (DS-TYP-05). No `server.fs.allow` override is needed or allowed. | Avoids the symlinked-`node_modules` font 403 in worktrees |

### 3.4 Temporary files, logs and credentials

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-RUN-30 | Nothing writes to `/tmp` (`docs/00-GOAL.md` §5). The Makefile exports `TMPDIR := $(CURDIR)/.run/tmp` for every recipe and creates the directory. Pytest uses `--basetemp=$(CURDIR)/.run/pytest`. Playwright uses `outputDir: "e2e/.results"`. `mktemp` is always called with `-p "$TMPDIR"`. |
| DG-RUN-31 | Process logs are JSON lines appended to `.run/<name>.log` (§6.6). Logs are never committed and never deleted by targets. |
| DG-RUN-32 | Generated demo credentials (docs/02-PRD.md WLD-U-R2 recovery codes and WLD-U-R3 `svc-*` client secrets) are written to `.run/demo-credentials.txt` with mode 0600. No target prints them. Demo passwords come only from `EREV_DEMO_PASSWORD` (D-75, rev 1.1): the seed never generates or writes a password, and it fails with "EREV_DEMO_PASSWORD is not set. Copy it from .env.example." when the variable is missing. This supersedes the generation fallback of WLD-U-R1. |
| DG-RUN-33 | Gate reports are written under `.run/reports/<target>/` (for example `.run/reports/parity/report.json`). PROGRESS.md cites counts from these files; the files themselves are not committed. |
| DG-RUN-34 | The worker's probe listener (05 OPR-23 rev 1.28, CFG-32; `erev_api.jobs.probes`) opens only when `EREV_WORKER_PROBE_PORT` or `PORT` is set: `make worker` and the pid-file runbook (DG-RUN-01 to DG-RUN-03) set neither, so no port is opened locally and `erev worker --check` stays the local health check. Hosted, Cloud Run sets `PORT`; `/startupz` and `/livez` answer with status only. Tests bind 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port (rev 1.72). |

## 4. Make targets

### 4.1 General rules

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-MK-00a | Every target is `.PHONY`, runs from the repository root and exits non-zero on failure (REQ-OPS-007). The final line of output is `OK <target>` or `FAIL <target>: <reason>`. Rev 1.97 (ruling R-53 (9); observed on every failing target): that line is the last line on **standard output**. When a target fails, GNU make then writes its own line on standard error — `make: *** [<target>] Error <n>`, and one `make[1]: *** […] Error <n>` more for a target whose recipe runs an inner make (the DG-MK-00i wrappers) — because a recipe cannot exit non-zero without it. A reader of a combined log therefore finds the `FAIL` line directly above make's lines; a program reads standard output, or the target's `report.json` (DG-MK-00g). |
| DG-MK-00b | Makefile variables: `PY := backend/.venv/bin/python`, `EREV := backend/.venv/bin/erev`, `PYTEST := backend/.venv/bin/pytest`, `ALEMBIC := backend/.venv/bin/alembic`, `NODE_BIN := frontend/node_modules/.bin`. Every target except `setup` first checks that `backend/.venv` and `frontend/node_modules` exist and otherwise fails with "run make setup first". |
| DG-MK-00c | The Makefile exports `TMPDIR := $(CURDIR)/.run/tmp` and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE := 1` (DG-RUN-30). |
| DG-MK-00d | Backend test targets run as `erev_app` on `erev_test`, after the session fixture resets schema `erev` and applies migrations as `erev_owner` (D-40, D-42; DG-TST-10). Two runs never overlap: the session fixture takes the PostgreSQL advisory lock `TEST_DB_LOCK_KEY = 0x6572657654455354` on `erev_test` and waits for it (DG-TST-11). |
| DG-MK-00e | Targets that bind the e2e ports (`e2e`, `perf`) take the directory lock `.run/locks/e2e-ports` with `mkdir`. If the lock exists and its recorded PID is alive, they fail with "e2e ports busy (pid N)". The lock is removed on exit through `trap`. |
| DG-MK-00f | Loop targets (§4.2 to §4.4) run offline (D-48a; rev 1.1). The loop's only network use is dependency installation inside `make setup`: package and browser downloads, and lock-file updates with `LOCK=1` (DG-ENV-08; D-76, DG-OQ-13; rev 1.2). Supervisor targets (§4.5) may use the network or Docker and are never run by the loop (DG-FORBID-12). |
| DG-MK-00g | Every target that produces a report writes `.run/reports/<target>/report.json` with `{target, command, build_sha, worktree_dirty, started_at, finished_at, exit_code, counts, failures[]}`, on success and on failure. JUnit-derived `counts` entries carry `{passed, failed, skipped, xfailed}`: an expected failure (pytest `<skipped type="pytest.xfail">`) is never folded into `skipped` (rev 1.8), and `--fail-on-skipped` refuses both for the suites DG-TST-09 names. `command` is the make invocation with its variables; `build_sha` is the output of `git rev-parse HEAD` (`"nogit"` outside a repository); `worktree_dirty` is true when `git status --porcelain` prints anything. `make release-manifest` reads these files; `.run/reports/` replaces the `.run/gates/` of 05 REL-02 (B1-010). |
| DG-MK-00i | Source binding of gate evidence (GATE-BIND-1; rev 1.8; 05 REL-02). Every gate target (`ci`, `test-pg`, `properties`, `parity`, `answer-keys`, `controls-report`, `e2e`, and the supervisor target `tf-validate`, whose banner comes first; `perf` and `perf-seed` when they exist) is `scripts/gate_context.sh <gate> -- make <gate>-gate` (`e2e` exports `EREV_RUN_DIR=<worktree>/.run` so PID files, logs and the ports lock stay in the worktree and DG-RUN-10 dev-stack detection keeps working, while `e2e.sh` writes its report where `EREV_REPORTS_DIR` points, the context, and the wrapper copies it back; rev 1.81: the supervisor targets `backup` and `restore-verify` export `EREV_RUN_DIR=<worktree>/.run` the same way and `backup` also `EREV_BACKUP_DATA_ROOT=<worktree>`, because a backup captures, and a restore leaves behind, live data of the deployment that the context — code and a copy of `.env` only — never holds; their scripts write the report alone under `<context>/.run/reports/<target>/`, DG-MK-backup, DG-MK-restore-verify), a thin entry into `scripts/gate_report.py <gate> --exec -- <command>` (the inner make is `$(GATE_MAKE)`, a plain variable defaulting to `make`, never `$(MAKE)`, so `make -n <gate>` only prints and clones nothing); `gate_report.py` itself (standard library only, so a copy runs anywhere) holds the mechanism and applies it to its own stage lists too, and recognises an inner invocation through `EREV_GATE_CONTEXT`: with a clean worktree the inner recipe runs in an immutable execution context, a scratch `git clone --shared --no-checkout` of the repository checked out `--detach` at the captured HEAD under `.run/gates/ctx-<gate>-<sha12>-<pid>/` (never the lane worktree, never a write to the shared `.git`; `git worktree add` is not used), with `.env` copied (mode 0600, never printed), `backend/.venv` symlinked from the worktree and `frontend/node_modules` cloned copy-on-write into the context (APFS `cp -Rc`; a hardlink tree where clonefile is unavailable; a symlink only as the last resort, recorded as such) because npm resolves real paths and reports every package of a symlinked `node_modules` as extraneous (the `licence-check` inventory failed that way on 458e01d) — the reused artifacts, whose identities and binding kind (`venv.binding`, `node_modules.binding`) are recorded and `PYTHONPATH=<ctx>/backend` so the context's packages shadow the editable install. Before the stages the wrapper proves the binding (`erev_api.__file__`, `erev_engine.__file__`, `REPO_ROOT`, `ALEMBIC_INI` and the Alembic versions directory resolve under the context; the console script's interpreter imports the context's `erev_api.cli`). After the run the context's tree sha and the content hash of its tracked files must equal their start values, else the report is `FAIL` with `failures[].stage` `source`. The report the gate wrote in the context is copied to the worktree's `.run/reports/<gate>/` together with every other file under that directory — so a gate's JUnit files must live there to survive the context's removal: `ci-gate` runs its `test` stage with `TEST_REPORTS=$(CI_REPORTS)` (`CI_REPORTS ?= $(CURDIR)/.run/reports/ci`) and names the same files in its `--junit` options, while `make test` alone keeps writing `.run/reports/test/` (rev 1.21 follow-up, after the 209120c wrapped run retained the counts but not the per-test JUnit) and gains `source_binding: {mode, captured_sha, run_id, run_started_at, tree_sha, tree_sha_end, context_sha256_start, context_sha256_end, context_path, context_kept, context_inner, worktree_head_after, worktree_dirty_after, python, uv_lock_sha256, package_lock_sha256, venv {path, source, binding, python, python_version, installed_sha256, installed_sha256_end, distributions}, node_modules {path, source, binding, installed_sha256, installed_sha256_end, packages}, dependencies {venv, node_modules, mismatches[]}, executed_erev_api, executed_erev_engine, executed_repo_root, executed_alembic_ini, executed_versions_dir, executed_python, executed_python_version, console_script, console_script_cli}`. Lock identity and the dependency policy (Codex draft review, 2026-09-19): `uv_lock_sha256` and `package_lock_sha256` are the executed source's lock files in the context, never the worktree's (`worktree_head_after` and `worktree_dirty_after` are the diagnostic observations of the original checkout); the reused `backend/.venv` and `frontend/node_modules` are identified by content (`installed_sha256`: the SHA-256 of the sorted `name==version` list of the venv's `*.dist-info` directories; npm's hidden `node_modules/.package-lock.json`), and before any stage runs every installed distribution must appear in the context's `backend/uv.lock` at its version and every entry of the hidden npm lock in the context's `frontend/package-lock.json` at its version, else the run is `FAIL` with `failures[] {stage: source, check: dependencies}` and the mismatches listed in `source_binding.dependencies.mismatches` (an absent or unreadable lock file next to an existing artifact is a mismatch; an absent artifact is `not applicable`); the identities are re-taken after the run and a change is the same failure. Evidence contract of wrapped writers (`--exec`): the command must leave `.run/reports/<gate>/report.json` in the DG-MK-00g shape — `target` a string naming the gate, `command` a non-empty string, `build_sha` a 40-hex sha equal to the captured commit, `worktree_dirty` a boolean (the wrapper's own measurement is written over it), `started_at` and `finished_at` RFC 3339 date-times with an offset (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.fraction](Z|±hh:mm)` only; ISO week dates, ordinal dates and a space separator are refused) and `finished_at` not before `started_at`, `exit_code` an integer, `counts` an object, `failures` a list — and a populated `counts` (a figure at the top level or one level down, or a non-empty `stages` map all `pass`); a missing, unreadable, malformed, schema-invalid or foreign-build report, or a report that claims success (`exit_code` 0) without population, is `FAIL` with `failures[] {stage: report, detail}` even when the command exited 0 (a report that itself records a failure needs no population), and the wrapper never writes a successful empty record in its place (`scripts/tf_validate.sh`, DEP-5, must write such a report). The entry `gate_report.py <gate> --exec -- <command…>` is exactly what `gate_context.sh` emits; the command is split off before argument parsing, its own options and `--` intact. Run binding (rev 1.43, REL-COV-1 / Codex 1510): the wrapper mints a `run_id` per run, hands it to the inner command as `EREV_GATE_RUN_ID`, records `run_id` and `run_started_at` in `source_binding`, and refuses an inner report that carries another `run_id` or a `started_at` before the run began (`FAIL {stage: report, detail: stale …}`) — an archived or previous report is never taken for the evidence of this run. A dirty worktree (or no repository) runs in place with `mode` `worktree-dirty (development; not release evidence)` and a printed warning (before GATE-BIND-1 the dirty state was merely recorded and disqualified only at manifest acceptance; the wrapper now labels the run itself, and the manifest rule is unchanged). Contexts are removed on exit unless `EREV_GATE_KEEP_CONTEXT=1`; contexts whose recorded pid is dead are swept at start. `make release-manifest` never classifies a report `PASS` unless `source_binding.mode` is `immutable-context`, `captured_sha` equals `build_sha` and both hash pairs are equal (DG-MK-release-manifest step 2). Chains on heads without the wrapper remain progress or merge evidence; release evidence is produced under the wrapper. Rev 1.97: the supervisor target `restore-drill` is wrapped the same way and exports nothing — its directory `<run directory>/restore-drill/` lies inside the context and is removed by the script itself (DG-MK-restore-drill). |
| DG-MK-00h | Target classes (rev 1.1). Loop targets are those of §4.2 (developer), §4.3 (quality) and §4.4 (gates). Supervisor targets are those of §4.5; each supervisor recipe first prints `SUPERVISOR TARGET <target> (D-48a)`. The loop never invokes a §4.5 target. When an item needs one, the loop records `SUPERVISOR VERIFICATION NEEDED: make <target>` in PROGRESS.md and continues. |

Rev 1.243 (05 PERF-15 rev 1.182; BUILD_SPEC PRF-2; item PERF-SEED-LOCK-1): in step (3) a month is closed for every entity and book by `perf_seed._close_and_lock` through `demo.closing.close_period`, the helper of `make seed CLOSE=1` (DG-MK-seed): `perf-accountant` starts the soft close and the close run, submits, exports and acknowledges the journal run and requests the lock, `perf-reviewer` approves the journal run, `perf-controller` decides the lock. A journal run without a line — the run of a month in which the entity posts nothing — is left as the close run calculated it, `draft`: it holds nothing to approve or export, the lock asks a run of the period that is not cancelled, and item JRN-EMPTY-RUN-1 refuses the submission of such a run. At a test scale an entity has such months before its first contract begins; on the dataset's manifest no entity has one. The jobs of a close run in the command's process, which therefore registers the CSV ledger adapter as a composition root (DG-LAY-03) — for steps 1 to 3, not for `--snapshot-only`; a persona whose second-factor verification is older than five minutes verifies again by the product's command before a decision that asks a fresh one (BR-PLT-06). Before the reference data the seed publishes `close.require_reconciliations_for_lock = false` by a `CLOSE` registry version of scope TENANT, authored by `perf-accountant` and approved by `perf-reviewer` and resumed by its persisted state: the lock of the volume tenant asks no reconciliation, at every scale, and the reconciliations' witness is the module of the close stage, `backend/tests/domain/demo/test_close_history_seed.py`. After a period's close run and journal run and before its lock is asked, the open `LATE_EVENT` items of source `ENGINE` that hold it — the late events the generator plans — are waived: `perf-accountant` requests, `perf-reviewer` decides (PRD BR-DAT-04: committed input is waived, not dismissed), and a request left pending by an interruption is decided, not asked again. Any other open item that holds the lock stops the command before the lock is asked: stderr names the period and each item — number, code, source, severity, message, the first five — with exit 1, and no report is written. Such an item is `OPEN` or `IN_PROGRESS`; the operator clears it in the workspace by the action the exception queue offers for it — reprocess, mark resolved, a waiver that another person decides, the dismissal of an input that was never committed — and runs `make perf-seed` again, which resumes at that lock, or rebuilds the tenant (`make db-reset`, then `make perf-seed`); in `perf-volume`, which only this seed writes, the item is a defect of the generator or of the product, to be reported. A lock the gates refuse ends the command with the gates as before (PRD ERR-14); the period stays in soft close and the next run resumes at it. A close run that fails ends the command with the helper's error — the period, the job and the state it ended in — and no report; the cause stands on the close run and on its `CLOSE_RUN_FAILED` item, which holds the lock. The operator opens the close run, clears the cause and runs `make perf-seed` again: the next run starts a close run for the period, and a run that succeeds settles the item. A run that finds a month of the dataset in soft close or locked does not repeat the bulk recompute of the groups, which 05 PERF-15 places before the first close (`volume.recompute_due`). That condition is PERF-15's own and right on its own terms; it is not the answer to the engine's defect of item ENG-COST-READBACK-1 and does not stand in for it — the defect has its own item and its own witness in the engine's lane, so nothing is hidden by the seed, and no seed-side avoidance is claimed. Step (5) stores a stored backup: `perf-controller` asks a snapshot of purpose `STORED_BACKUP` with a fresh second factor, and the job her request defers runs in the command's process, as the jobs of a close do, so that none is left queued for a worker. Until this revision the step asked purpose `SANDBOX_SEED`, of which the product asks the name of the sandbox it creates and which loads that sandbox in the same job (04 API-R-04 rev 1.67): the request was refused, 422 "a sandbox copy or seed names the sandbox it creates (SNP-2).", before any export. A stored backup loads nothing; `make perf` restores it (DG-PERF-02). The export asks a confirmed retention policy (PRD ERR-77), which no seed stated: before the reference data, beside the `CLOSE` version, the seed publishes `platform.snapshot_retention_families` — the five families with the literals of `snapshot_dataset.RETENTION_FAMILIES` — by a `PLATFORM` registry version of scope TENANT, authored by `perf-accountant` and approved by `perf-reviewer`, the named human approval the parameter asks, and resumed by its persisted state; `--snapshot-only` states it too for a tenant seeded before it was. That catalogue is the product's proposal — counsel owns the periods — and the seed confirms it for its own synthetic dataset: nobody's legal judgement, and no default for a workspace of real data. A snapshot that is not `SUCCEEDED` when its job returns stops the command, with exit 1 and no report, and stderr says which of two things happened. The job ended and the snapshot is `FAILED`: the state and the job's own sentence, the retention refusal among them; nothing of that snapshot is used, and the next `--snapshot-only` asks a new one. Or the job did not run in the command and is still `QUEUED` or `RUNNING` — a worker beside the seed holds it or fills the job slots of the workspace: nothing has ended, and the next `--snapshot-only` uses that snapshot when it has succeeded by then and asks a new one otherwise; a request left unfinished is not taken up. Binds no port; idempotent. | none |

### 4.5 Supervisor targets (never run by the loop)

These targets need the network, Docker, or access to secrets and live data. The supervisor runs them; the loop never does (D-48a, DG-MK-00h, DG-FORBID-12). Each writes `.run/reports/<target>/report.json` (DG-MK-00g).

| Id | Target | Needs | Exact semantics | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DG-MK-audit-deps | `make audit-deps` | Network | `scripts/audit_deps.sh`: (1) `uv export --project backend --no-dev --frozen --no-emit-project --all-extras --output-file .run/tmp/audit-requirements.txt`; (1a) every requirement of that file must be `name==version` (an editable, path, URL or unpinned line is `export-invalid`, exit 1, before any scanner runs) and its environment markers are removed into `.run/reports/audit-deps/audited-requirements.txt`; (2) `uv tool run pip-audit --strict --require-hashes --disable-pip -r .run/reports/audit-deps/audited-requirements.txt --format json`; (3) `npm --prefix frontend audit --omit=dev --json`; (4) write counts by severity and `output_sha256`, the SHA-256 of the two captured outputs concatenated in that order. Exit 1 when pip-audit reports any vulnerability or npm reports a `high` or `critical` advisory. Rev 1.68 (GATE-BIND-1): `make audit-deps` runs the script through `scripts/gate_context.sh` (DG-MK-00i) so its report and the two captured outputs (`pip-audit.json`, `npm-audit.json`) gain `source_binding`; the advisory databases are the accepted network step of the audit; `uv` or `npm` absent is `skipped-not-installed` (exit 0, with the SUPERVISOR VERIFICATION NEEDED line); a tool exiting without JSON is a tool failure (exit 1), not a verdict. A result is accepted only in its expected shape and with explicit execution semantics: pip-audit `{dependencies: [{name, version, vulns: [{id, …}]}], fixes: []}` with no `skip_reason` (an unaudited dependency is incomplete) and exit 0 if and only if no vulnerability, exit 1 otherwise; npm `auditReportVersion` 2 with `metadata.vulnerabilities` carrying the five severity counts and a `total` equal to their sum and consistent with the `vulnerabilities` map, exit 0 if and only if `total` 0, exit 1 otherwise (any advisory makes npm exit 1: low and moderate advisories are a valid result and pass this target's policy). An error object, a missing field, another exit code or an exit code that disagrees with the result is `pip-audit-invalid` / `pip-audit-inconsistent` / `npm-audit-invalid` / `npm-audit-inconsistent` (exit 1), never a verdict; the report's `scanners` object records each exit code, the dependencies audited, the npm total and whether the result was accepted. Under a versioned file store the shredded rows' `erasure.all_generations_gone` is answered only from an explicit complete inventory (`sidecar_versions(key)` → `live`, `noncurrent`, `soft_deleted`, `retained_copies` counts and a `completion` state; anything less is `versioned-store-inventory-invalid` with `null`, never "gone"). Rev 1.81 (lane OPS; the first run on a clean tree with a real database, 2026-09-29): under GATE-BIND-1 the restore directory `.run/restore/<backup id>/` — the extracted file store a cutover points `EREV_FILE_ROOT` at (RB-04) and the `migrate`, `verify`, `doctor` and `pg_restore` logs — was created inside the execution context and removed with it, and the final line and `restore.verify_document` named paths of the removed context. The recipe now exports `EREV_RUN_DIR=$(RUN_DIR)`, so the restore directory and the logs are the worktree's and outlive the run; the report and `verify.json` alone are written under `<context>/.run/reports/restore-verify/` and copied back; the final line names the record as `.run/reports/restore-verify/report.json` and `restore.verify_document` is the file name `verify.json`. | 05 OPR-11, OPR-12, RB-04, RB-06 |
| DG-MK-restore-drill | `make restore-drill` | Docker; the PostgreSQL 17 client tools (`pg_dump`, `pg_restore`); `.env` with the master keys | Rev 1.97 (lane OPS; the supervisor's addition of 2026-09-30; 05 OPR-12 rev 1.53). `scripts/restore_drill.sh` rehearses the NATIVE backup-and-restore procedure end to end on a throwaway server; it reads and writes nothing of a deployment. (1) If `docker info` fails, write `{"result": "skipped-no-daemon"}`, print "SUPERVISOR VERIFICATION NEEDED: Docker daemon unavailable" and exit 0. (2) Fail when `127.0.0.1:5446` is in use (`port-in-use`; `DRILL_PORT=<1024 to 65535>` chooses another port), and when compose project `erev-verify-drill` holds a container or a volume (`project-exists`): what an interrupted drill left is removed only with `RESET=1`, so a drill that runs elsewhere on the daemon is refused by its listener and never destroyed. (3) `docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml -f deploy/compose/drill/override.yaml --env-file deploy/compose.env.example -p erev-verify-drill up -d postgres`, then wait up to 120 s for the container's health. The override publishes the drill's port and mounts, beside the compose init file, `deploy/compose/drill/02-recovery-roles.sql`: the container's first start creates the RB-11 roles `erev_backup` and `erev_restore_admin` and the empty database `erev_rv_drill` owned by `erev_owner`, inside the container, as it creates the compose roles; the script creates no role and no database (DG-ENV-14). The three passwords of the service and the two of the recovery roles are generated for the run (`secrets.token_urlsafe(24)`), exported to the compose calls and so to the container, handed to the programs below in their environment, and written to no file and no report. (4) As the container's superuser, confirm that the two recovery roles (`BYPASSRLS`, not superusers) and the two databases exist (`roles-failed` otherwise). (5) `erev migrate`, then `erev seed demo` (`TENANTS=<codes>` narrows the seed), under `EREV_ENV=dev` with the drill's URLs, a file root and a run directory under `<run directory>/restore-drill/`, and the master keys of `.env`. (6) `scripts/backup.sh` (DG-MK-backup) with `EREV_BACKUP_DIR` inside the drill's directory, never `.data/backups`. (7) The row count of every table of schema `erev` and of the Procrastinate tables. (8) `docker compose -p erev-verify-drill down -v`; no volume of the project may outlive it. (9) Steps (3) and (4) again: a fresh server, initialised as the first. (10) `scripts/restore_verify.sh` (DG-MK-restore-verify) for the backup of (6) into `erev_rv_drill`. (11) The row counts of the clone against (7): a table that is missing in the clone or holds fewer rows fails the drill (`rows-lost`); a table may hold more, because the verification appends its own events. (12) Always, through the exit trap: `down -v`, and removal of the drill's directory, which holds the backup set with its `.env` copy. (13) `.run/reports/restore-drill/report.json` (DG-MK-00g): `result` (`verified`, or the failure's name), `counts` (`stages`, `stages_passed`, `tables`, `rows_source`, `rows_clone`, the three difference counts and the restore script's counts), `seconds` (`server`, `source`, `backup`, `destroy_to_fresh_server`, `restore_verify`, `destroy_to_verified_clone`, `total`), `backup_id`, `row_counts`, and the restore script's `restore` measurements and `restore_test_record`; beside it `backup.report.json`, `restore-verify.report.json`, `row-counts.json` and the logs of the steps. A failed (12) is a failure of the run: `cleanup-failed`, or `<primary result>+cleanup-failed`. Only project `erev-verify-drill` is touched. The final line is `OK restore-drill` or `FAIL restore-drill: <reason>`; diagnostics name stages, the port and file names only. GATE-BIND-1: `make restore-drill` runs the script through `scripts/gate_context.sh` (DG-MK-00i), and the drill's directory then lies inside the execution context. The drill proves the recovery procedure and tooling of the release being validated, on demo data; a deployment's own restore test remains `make restore-verify` of its latest backup (RB-06). | 05 OPR-11, OPR-12; RB-06; D-48a |

## 5. Kernel APIs

Each subsection gives a binding signature followed by rules. Types named in signatures come from `erev_api.enums` or `erev_engine.enums`; their values are the 04 §3 enumerations. `UnitOfWork` is defined in §5.18.

### 5.1 Configuration (KRN-CFG)

```python

REPO_ROOT: Final[Path]                                   # Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
```
