| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-CFG-01 | Only composition roots call `get_settings()`: `main.py`, `worker.py`, `cli.py`, `db/session.py`, `logging.py`, adapter factories and test `conftest.py` files. Domain code receives values through `UnitOfWork` or parameters (DG-ARC-03). |
| DG-KRN-CFG-02 | Construction validates: each key is 64 lowercase hex characters; `ai_provider = "anthropic"` requires `anthropic_api_key`, `env` not in {`test`, `e2e`} and `perf_run = false` (DG-AI-01; rev 1.2); the selected database URL pair exists; ports lie in 1024 to 65535; `file_root` and `run_dir` are resolved against `REPO_ROOT`. Rev 1.1: `cors_origins` and `worker_queues` are comma-separated lists parsed by a `field_validator` (`NoDecode`, so pydantic-settings never JSON-decodes them; an empty value is the empty tuple); each `worker_queues` value is one of the eight queue names of DG-KRN-JOB-10; `public_origin` matches `^https?://[^/?#]+$` and, when `env` is `dev`, `test` or `e2e`, starts with `http://127.0.0.1:`; `env` in {`dev`, `test`, `e2e`} requires `key_provider = "local"` and `email_backend = "fake"`; `env = "production"` accepts `key_provider` `local` (compose) or `gcp` (hosted) (DG-ENV-10; rev 1.2); `engine_processes`, when set, lies in 1 to 64; `metrics_enabled = true` requires `metrics_token`; `trusted_proxy_hops` lies in 0 to 5 and `worker_concurrency` in 1 to 64. Rev 1.33 (lane P2; SPEC-Q-116 ruling): `security_hmac_secret_version` (`EREV_SECURITY_HMAC_SECRET_VERSION`) is a positive integer, required when `env = "production"` (`latest` or a non-numeric value fails construction naming the variable); it selects `security-hmac:<n>` for every new security event, for the readiness `keys` check and for the worker's startup check (`KeyRing.verify_current_security_key`), both of which fail when the provider serves a different version than requested. The three CFG-26 keys are required only when `key_provider = "local"`; `key_provider = "gcp"` requires `gcp_project` and a `gcp_kms_kek` of the form `projects/<project>/locations/<location>/keyRings/<ring>/cryptoKeys/<key>`. A failure stops the process with the variable name and the rule, never the value. Rev 1.97 (R-34 SD-5, SD-6; 05 SAR-40 rev 1.53): construction still admits `email_backend = "fake"` and any well-formed master keys under `production`, so that `erev doctor` can report them; the api lifespan and the worker entry point refuse them before the release is stamped (`controls/startup.py` `refuse_unsafe_production`: the doctor predicates `email-backend` and `master-keys` over the process settings; `StartupRefused`, a `SettingsError`; log event `startup.refused`). `Settings.master_key_findings()` is the CFG-26 rule: under the local provider a key with fewer than 16 distinct byte values is a placeholder and two keys with one value are repeated. `smtp_host`, `smtp_username`, `smtp_password`, `smtp_from` and `operator_alert_email` treat a blank value as unset (compose interpolates an unset variable to the empty string). Rev 1.97 (R-39 (4); 05 CFG-18, SAR-15 rev 1.53): `smtp_private_relay` (`EREV_SMTP_PRIVATE_RELAY`, default false; blank is false) and `smtp_ca_file` (`EREV_SMTP_CA_FILE`; a path, relative ones against `REPO_ROOT`; blank is unset) are read by `adapters/email/smtp.py` alone: the first reaches `adapters/http/guard.py` as `check_host(..., private=True)`, which then also admits loopback and the private-use networks `PRIVATE_USE`, and `check_destination` has no such parameter; the second is the `cafile` of the STARTTLS context in place of the system store. `Settings.smtp_ca_findings()` loads the bundle and names the variable when it cannot be read as PEM certificates. Rev 1.97 (ruling R-53 (6); 05 SAR-40 rev 1.53): `cli.cli_services()` applies the same refusal to the operator commands — it calls `refuse_unsafe_production` after the pipeline is installed and before the key ring is built, prints the findings (`StartupRefused.findings`, one `FAIL` line each) and a closing line on stderr and exits 3. `erev doctor` and `erev verify` build their services with `cli_services(gated=False)`; nothing else may. |
| DG-KRN-CFG-03 | Secrets are `SecretStr`. `repr(settings)` and log output never contain secret values. |

### 5.2 Database sessions and tenant context (KRN-DB)

October 7, 2026 continuation — policy approval and period locks: after locking the combination
group and contract, approval of an override on a non-draft contract calls
`period_ends.refuse_policy_change_a_lock_met`. Under tenant entity scope it shares the close-window
rows of the contracting and performing entities, before publishing an approval or superseding
another one. The period-lock decision then waits and reads the committed dirty-group mark.
If a lock has already overtaken the approval transaction's record cutoff, the approval rolls back
with `PERIOD_STATE_MOVED` in its decision form; the reviewer can retry after the lock. An approval
that began after the lock's cutoff may complete after waiting for that lock. Draft contracts skip
the check because their policy has no calculated or frozen output yet. The scope widening is
limited to these control reads and is listed in the architecture test's closed allowlist.

This applies even when the pending-approvals gate has an approved waiver. That waiver permits
pending decisions; it does not authorize publishing an in-flight policy change behind a lock's
read. The API concurrency tests use the real waiver, lock and policy-approval workflows.

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/db/session.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DbContext:
    tenant_id: UUID
    user_id: UUID | None                                  # principal id; None for SYSTEM
    entity_scope: Literal["*"] | tuple[UUID, ...]

class TenantContextMissing(RuntimeError): ...

def app_engine() -> sqlalchemy.Engine: ...                # erev_app; pool_size=10, max_overflow=10, pool_pre_ping=True
def owner_engine() -> sqlalchemy.Engine: ...              # erev_owner; the operator's provider commands and the test schema reset (05 TXN-02 rev 1.162)
def migration_engine() -> sqlalchemy.Engine: ...          # erev_owner, one Alembic run; statement_timeout from Settings.migration_statement_timeout_seconds (rev 1.264)

@contextmanager
def tenant_session(ctx: DbContext, *, read_only: bool = False,
                   statement_timeout_ms: int = 60_000, lock_timeout_ms: int = 10_000) -> Iterator[Session]: ...

@contextmanager
def identity_session(*, request_id: str, user_id: UUID | None = None) -> Iterator[Session]: ...

@contextmanager
def platform_session(scope: Literal["tenant_directory", "provisioning"], *,
                     actor_user_id: UUID | None, request_id: str) -> Iterator[Session]: ...

def set_tenant_context(session: Session, ctx: DbContext) -> None: ...
def allow_idle_in_transaction(session: Session) -> None: ...   # rev 1.165 (DG-KRN-DB-01; 05 TXN-03)
def connect_options(component: str) -> str: ...                 # rev 1.255 (DG-KRN-DB-11; 05 TXN-03 rev 1.193)
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-DB-01 | `tenant_session` begins a transaction on `app_engine()`. Its first statement is `SELECT set_config('app.tenant_id', :tenant_id, true), set_config('app.user_id', :user_id, true), set_config('app.entity_scope', :scope, true), set_config('statement_timeout', :statement_timeout, true), set_config('lock_timeout', :lock_timeout, true)`. `:user_id` is `''` for None; `:scope` is `'*'` or the entity UUIDs sorted ascending and comma-separated. `read_only=True` adds `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`. Normal exit commits (unless the UoW already committed); an exception rolls back and re-raises. The settings are transaction-local, equivalent to `SET LOCAL` (REQ-PLT-001; 04 §1.4). `allow_idle_in_transaction(session)` (rev 1.165; 05 TXN-03 rev 1.121; supervisor ruling R-116 (h)) sets `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` for the session's CURRENT transaction to `Settings.dataset_freeze_idle_seconds`, with a transaction-local `set_config`; its one caller is `close.freeze.allow_idle`, the function every caller of a dataset freeze calls (DG-AK-60; supervisor ruling R-119 (d)) — a transaction that is idle while another connection of the same command works is not ended by the connection default of 60 s. |
| DG-KRN-DB-02 | `identity_session` sets only `app.user_id` (when given). It is used only by `erev_api.auth` repositories for the RLS-NONE-U tables and for `tenant_membership` through the RLS-TM user policy. |
| DG-KRN-DB-03 | `platform_session` sets `app.platform_scope` and inserts `security_event` kind `PLATFORM_SCOPE_USED` in the same transaction (04 §1.4). `tenant_directory` sessions are read-only. `provisioning` is used only by `tenant.provision` and sandbox copy (DB-15). Rev 1.200: every caller of `platform_session` is listed in 05 TXN-07 and held by DG-ARC-18; nothing else sets `app.platform_scope`. |
| DG-KRN-DB-04 | Refusal of context-free SQL: `app_engine()` installs a `before_cursor_execute` listener that raises `TenantContextMissing` unless `connection.info["erev.context"]` is set. The three factories set it at transaction start and remove it at transaction end. Code that builds a `Session` in any other way therefore fails on its first statement (REQ-PLT-001). |
| DG-KRN-DB-05 | `set_tenant_context` re-issues DG-KRN-DB-01's `set_config` statement inside the current transaction. It is used only by provisioning, after the tenant row exists, and by test fixtures. A second in-transaction re-issue exists for the close gates (rev 1.89; supervisor ruling R-42 (d), item CLO-GATE-SCOPE-1): `db.session.every_entity_scope(session, ctx)` sets `app.entity_scope` to `*` for the statements of a block and re-issues the caller's own scope on exit (tenant, user and timeouts unchanged; the setting is transaction-local, so a rollback discards it). It is used only by `close.gates.evaluate_gates`, after the command has authorised the principal for the period's entity — a control's own reads and the rows it stores, never data returned to the caller. A figure of an entity the caller reads is computed from every row it needs, whoever owns the row; the rows themselves are not returned (rev 1.195; the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-01 13:14 and 13:54): `reports.dashboard.home` reads the datasets of its three figure panels — revenue, contract liability, RPO — for the context's entities inside the block and returns sums (DG-CMD-13). Rev 1.227 (item RPT-EXPLAIN-READER-SCOPE-1; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01; 04 §16.11 rev 1.239): `reports.framework.explain_cell` enters the block for the explainer of a report cell, after the caller is authorised for the run and its report, so that the cell is explained as the run's job read it. Of the contributors it then names those the caller's scope reaches — reach judged as the record's own address judges it, the line's entity for a schedule line and a subledger line, the contracting entity of its contract for an obligation version — and returns the rest as one sum per entity with that entity's reference (id, code, name; ruling R-85 (d)): a sum, no row. Rev 1.90 (ruling R-29; 05 IPL-05, IPL-07, IPL-10): the import pipeline also re-issues it, only to NARROW the entity scope of its job transaction to the uploader's scope while the cross-file rules, the dry run and the commit plans run, and re-issues the job's own context afterwards (`domain/imports/scope.py`); the scope it sets is never wider than the job's. `system_entity_scope(session)` (rev 1.87 part 6; supervisor rulings R-42 (d) and R-64 (1)) is a context manager that sets `app.entity_scope` to `*` — the tenant's SYSTEM entity scope: tenant isolation only — inside the caller's transaction and gives the caller's scope back on the way out; `app.tenant_id`, `app.user_id` and the timeouts stay, so every write is still attributed to the caller. Nested uses keep the wide scope; when the block raises, the scope is given back if the transaction can still run a statement (a rolled-back savepoint or transaction restores it anyway). It is for what a control reads, hashes or recomputes and must not depend on who decides: the approvals kernel uses it (DG-KRN-APR-01, -02), and a domain module never uses it to show a caller rows outside its scope — but for the reference to a legal entity of rev 1.126 and the text of a batch's lines of rev 1.272, both below. The two blocks are one implementation (rev 1.87 part 11): `every_entity_scope(session, ctx)` is `system_entity_scope(session)` for a caller that holds its context, and each gives back the scope that was in force when it began — the caller's own, or the SYSTEM scope of an enclosing block — so the gates the `PERIOD_LOCK` approval hook evaluates leave the rest of the hook reading every entity. Rev 1.126 (rulings R-95, R-98 (3); 05 TXN-10; one implementation with the blocks above, by the supervisor's order of 2026-10-01): the computation of a combination group widens through `system_entity_scope` as well. `bundles.build` and `bundles.index` read a bundle inside it, and `UnitOfWork.as_system` (DG-KRN-UOW-05) enters it together with `db.session.system_user(session)`, which re-issues `app.user_id` as SYSTEM for the block, gives the caller's user back as the scope is given back, and has no other caller. Inside a narrowed import context the block gives back that narrowed scope, not the job's. Beside the computation the block is entered for two references to a legal entity that a row names, one statement each — the performing entity of an obligation the caller may read (`queries._entity_refs`, DG-CMD-13; ruling R-85 (d)) and the performing entity a booked line names by code (`commands`, 05 RCP-18): the id, the code and the name of that entity, and nothing else of it. Rev 1.272 (register index 182; the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-02; 04 §16.7 rev 1.245): a third such reference — the counterparty entity of an intercompany journal line (`journals.queries.counterparties`): the id, the code and the name, read for the lines whose counterparty the statement could not join and for no other, so that a caller of every entity sends no statement more — and one read that is not a reference: `journals.export.chunk_of` reads the lines of a batch, with the external ids of their contracts, inside the block, for the export job and for a download alike. A line's reference is text of the entry, and what a caller who may download the batch receives is the batch as it leaves, so the file and the digest of its audit event do not depend on who asks; the batch itself is read before, under the caller's own scope, and permission and entity scope go on deciding whether it is downloaded. Rev 1.191 (rulings R-98 (9) as refined and R-109 (d); 04 §16.10 rev 1.198): an import commit enters the block for one more read, `imports/commit._answering_approvers` — who answered for each approval the commit performs. The commit runs narrowed to its uploader's scope, and whom an act names must not depend on that scope, so the request, its decisions and the routing of the upload's approvals are read under the tenant's SYSTEM scope; the read returns the ids of approvers for the acts the commit writes and shows the caller nothing. Rev 1.210 (item APR-SETUP-RULE-2; ruling R-42 (d); 04 T-PLT-01 rev 1.224): the setup completion enters the block for one read, `setup.open_period_exists` — whether some legal entity of the tenant has an open period (PRD BR-PLT-02). The command that evaluates setup is whoever's makes its last condition true — a member accepting an invitation for one entity, an approver of one entity deciding a grant — and the conditions are the tenant's; the read answers a truth value and shows the caller no row. Rev 1.260 (item SSP-ENTITY-SCOPE-1; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02; 04 §16.4 rev 1.277): the SSP resolve read (`ssp.resolution.resolve`) enters the block for one read, `resolution.approved_versions` — the approved versions with the code of the entity each book names, as `bundles.build` reads them. A book's entity is a reference to a legal entity that a row names: in the caller's own session an entity she does not read came back as none, and the engine took that book for a book of all entities. The read shows her nothing of that entity — she names only an entity her `ssp.read` covers, and no book of another entity matches her case (ENGINE_SPEC S05-R-02 (2); the parity fallback of (3) applies whatever its scope, to her case as to her entity's contracts). Rev 1.214 (item PINP-PERIOD-VALUE-1; ruling R-42 (d); PRD ERR-75 rev 1.178): the effective-date rule of a configuration version enters the block for one read, `lifecycle.has_legal_entity` — whether the tenant has a legal entity yet. `legal_entity` is RLS-TE, so a reader whose scope names no entity sees none; the fact is the tenant's, whoever submits or decides a policy version, and the read answers a truth value and shows the caller no row. Every call site of the three blocks is listed once in the architecture test DG-ARC-16. Rev 1.201 (items CLO-QUARANTINE-READ-1 and EXC-IMPORT-SCOPE-1; supervisor rulings R-42 (d) and R-121 (i)): the counts of a period (`close.queries.with_close`: API-S-Period `blockers`) are read inside `system_entity_scope` as well — a count is a fact about the period's lock and the same for every reader of the period, a number over rows and never a row. The LIST behind a count is not: it is read in the caller's own scope under the reading rule of the exception queue (`imports.exceptions.readable`; 04 T-IMP-05 "An item that names no entity: who reads it, and who acts on it"), so a reader of one entity is told a count that includes an item he is not shown. That rule needs no widened scope and enters none of the three blocks: T-CON-04 and T-IMP-02 are tenant-level in the policy and T-CON-01 is bound to its entity, so "every member of the group has a contract I read whose entity my permission names" is asked in the caller's session. `require_tenant_scope(session)` refuses by name (`ScopeNotTenantWide`) unless the transaction is under the tenant's scope: the writers of a computation, `computation._persist` and `compute_job._refused`, call it before their first statement. Rev 1.276 (item CLO-RATE-AFTER-RUN-1; supervisor ruling R-42 (d); 04 T-CLS-01 "What a run read" rev 1.291): `close.run_inputs.read` enters `system_entity_scope` for three statements (third row of rev 1.276, with item PINP-PERIOD-VALUE-1: the period-pinned values are read for the run's period, per legal entity) — the digest of the exchange rates in force, the registry versions known at the cutoff, and the legal entities with their time zones. The first period-end step of a close run records what they answer and the gate `CLOSE_RUN_COMPLETED` compares it with the same read later: a registry version at the level of an entity is a row of that entity (T-PLT-32 is RLS-TE), and what a run read must be the same for the job that records it and for every reader of the gate. The read answers two digests and shows the caller no row. Rev 1.259 (SCOPE-WORKSPACE-LISTS-1 part (d); the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02): the generation of a fiscal year enters `every_entity_scope` for one read and the rows it stores, `reference.commands._sync_calendar_states` — the enabled books kept on the calendar and the period states each still lacks. The periods are the calendar's and every entity on it computes into them, so the states are written for every entity whoever generates the year (until then: for the entities the caller's session read, and the engine quarantined the first contract of another entity dated into the year, ENGINE_SPEC CV-13); the caller is answered a count, `inserted_state_count`, and no row. Rev 1.286 (item SBX-COPY-OPEN-INVITATION-1; 04 T-PLT-07 rev 1.293; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02): `users._void_stale_role_requests` enters `system_entity_scope` for one read and what follows from it — the `PENDING` `ROLE_ASSIGNMENT` requests of a removed membership, which the invitation of that person voids while they are stale (DG-KRN-APR-05). A request for one legal entity is hidden from an inviter of another (RLS-TE on `approval_request.entity_id`), and what an invitation ends must not depend on who invites; nothing the block reads is returned to the inviter, whose answer is read outside it. The call site is listed in the door of DG-ARC-16 with this reason. Rev 1.273 (item ACT-FLAGS-1; ruling R-64 (1); 04 §16.10 rev 1.287): `activation.submit_activation` enters `system_entity_scope` for one read, `activation.routing_facts` — the flags and the amount its request states. What a request states must not depend on who submits it, and one flag asks whether any other contract of the workspace holds a line of a product, which a submitter of one entity does not see; the read returns flags and an amount and shows the caller no row. Rev 1.295 (04 §16.10 rev 1.319; the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-03): since a guarded transaction runs under the scope of its route's permission (DG-KRN-AUTH-03), the kernel's statements on a request's own row enter `system_entity_scope` once the kernel's question has admitted the caller — `engine.submit` (the second look for a pending request, the insert, the read-back), `engine.withdraw` through a subject, `engine.void_if_stale`, `engine.void_subject` — and so do the basis and the content a submission re-derives (`modifications._stored_preview`, `modifications.submit`, `estimates.submit_version`) and the Home's count of the requests waiting for the caller, which `dashboard.home` reads inside its `every_entity_scope` block: a count, as the inbox counts them, and no row. Item PREVIEW-INLINE-SCOPE-1 (04 API-S-ImpactSummary rev 1.319; ruling R-64 (1)): three reads of what a request states of its own contract enter the block — `events.impact_summary` for the revenue the stored schedule holds (`_before_revenue`), `void.request_void` for the posted-state basis (`subjects.posted_basis`), `adjustments._measure` for the stored revenue an adjustment's amount is measured against (`_stored_revenue`). A schedule line and a posted line are rows of the entity that performs; the job of a preview reads them as SYSTEM, and a command that summarised in its caller's transaction read fewer for a preparer of the contracting entity alone. Each read returns figures of the subject's own contract, which its preparer reads through her request and her preview jobs. The call sites are listed in the door of DG-ARC-16 with these reasons, and `tests/architecture/test_scope_questions.py` holds each of the three reads inside the block. |
| DG-KRN-DB-06 | All SQL uses bound parameters. `text()` built with f-strings, `%` or `.format()` is forbidden (REQ-SEC-006; ruff rule S608; DG-ARC-05). |
| DG-KRN-DB-07 | A statement that must affect exactly one row checks `result.rowcount == 1` and raises the stated problem otherwise (for example the event append of T-CON-05 raises 412 `precondition-failed`). |
| DG-KRN-DB-08 | Lock order inside one transaction: (1) domain rows — one order for every path that touches `combination_group` rows (D-98 candidates 101a, 101b, 101c; rev 1.36): every group row the unit of work will lock or update — a join's or leave's target, each member's current group, the leave singletons, the group of a judged contract — `FOR UPDATE` in **one globally ascending id order, the target included** (a caller never takes the target first; it passes the target's id into the sorted set); **then** the proposal / judgement record (`judgement_record` `FOR UPDATE`); **then** the `contract` row(s) `FOR UPDATE` in ascending id order. The group ids come from unlocked reads (the contract row's `combination_group_id`, the proposal's `contract_ids`) and the revalidation under the locks proves **equality**: each contract's current group id equals the id observed at the unlocked read — any difference is 412 `precondition-failed` (`REGROUPED`), never a continuation on a group that was not locked; no pre-lock check is the last check. Before rev 1.36 this row named the inverse contract-then-group order that `activation.submit_activation` / `activate` followed (two paths taking the same two locks in opposite orders can deadlock). The order covers **implicit `UPDATE` locks and transitive callers**: `events/stream.py` `_raise_head` locks the `contract` row and `_mark_dirty` the `combination_group` row by `UPDATE`, so every unit of work that appends contract events or computes while holding a contract row — `record_events`, holds, memos, imports, the approval hooks, `judgements.submit_judgement` / `review_judgement` (the judged contract's group, then the record through the helper's `between`, then the contract) — takes the group lock at its entry through `erev_api.db.locking.lock_group_then_contract`; a combination create, submit, join or leave locks all of its groups through `combination._lock_groups_then_contracts` (groups ascending, `between` = the proposal record, contracts ascending, equality). A residual `40P01` (deadlock detected; no path is known to produce one under this order) is 409 `lock-conflict` (DG-KRN-ERR-02): the command's transaction rolled back and nothing was saved; `run_command` does not keep that 409 under the command's `Idempotency-Key` (rev 1.200; DG-KRN-IDEM-03 rev 1.127: `lock-conflict` is one of `deps.UNSTORED_SLUGS`, and the attempt's record is deleted in a transaction of its own — until rev 1.127 the 409 was kept as the command's first response and replayed to a resubmission with the same key), so the client resubmits with the same key or a new one and the command runs afresh; **no automatic retry exists** (the synchronous approval chain `api/v1/approvals.py` → `api/deps.py run_command` → `approvals/engine.py decide` → the subject hook rolls back and rethrows; the frontend sends once). An approval hook re-validates the approved basis under these locks immediately before it applies (DG-KRN-APR-05; D-98 candidate 101d, rev 1.40). A manual adjustment command and the hooks of subject `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` take the group, the contract and then the T-SL-05 row `FOR UPDATE` (`adjustments._locked`; rev 1.98), the order of a T-CON-06 modification; **The tenant's `book` rows (rev 1.109; supervisor rulings R-77 (5) and R-80).** A decision that reads the enabled books of an entity to decide a not-a-contract gate — `events.step1_outcome` on a recording path, `combination._gated_member_errors` — takes every T-REF-02 `book` row of the tenant `FOR SHARE` in code order (`events.step1.lock_books`), AFTER the combination-group, judgement-record and contract rows and before it reads `entity_book`, and holds it to its commit. The commands that change what `step1.enabled_books` answers — `reference.put_entity_book`, `reference.update_book` — take the `book` row of their code `FOR UPDATE` at their entry and take NO `combination_group` or `contract` row lock afterwards in that transaction: a recomputation that adopting a book may need is deferred to a job, never inline (an inline one would take group rows after `book` and close a cycle with the gate decision). Shared locks do not block each other or the foreign keys that reference a book; (1a) the `period_state` row (rev 1.96, second row; 04 DB-07 rev 1.113; supervisor rulings R-31 and R-40 (b)): the DB-07 guards take it `FOR SHARE` for every line a posting inserts — after the domain rows of (1) and before (2) — and hold it until the transaction ends; for a line of the LEGACY book the subledger guard takes the state row of the tenant's primary book for the same entity and period first, then the LEGACY row, both `FOR SHARE` (rev 1.138; 04 DB-07 rev 1.155, revision 0105; supervisor rulings R-112 (e) and R-114 (d)): the LEGACY book has no close of its own, so the lock decision of the primary book waits for a LEGACY posting in flight on the one row it holds and takes no LEGACY row of the period it locks, and a change of a LEGACY row's own state takes that row alone; a change of a period's state takes it `FOR UPDATE` as its first read of the period (`close.commands._move`, the lock, permanent-lock and reopen decisions through `close.gates.period_scope`, `reference.commands.open_future_period`) and, when the period is postable, takes no lock of (1) and none of (2) while it holds it — the lock decision reads `ledger_chain_head` without a lock and takes the NEXT period's row only when that period is `future` — read without a lock first, then `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` directly after the closing period's row and before the gates and the freeze (`_hold_future_next_period`; rev 1.165; 04 DB-07 rev 1.182; supervisor ruling R-116 (h)): a held row is 409 `lock-conflict` with rule `NEXT_PERIOD_HELD` before anything is produced, and `_open_next_period` later writes on the row already held; rev 1.218 (finding F11 of the independent review of 2026-10-01; 04 §14.1 "The next period's row" rev 1.229): the `NOWAIT` read runs inside a savepoint, and a row that is no longer `future` once it is locked — the period was opened between the two reads — is given back by the savepoint's rollback, so the decision holds no row of a period it does not open (a state condition in the locking statement does not do it: such a statement locks the row's newest version, returns no row and keeps the lock; measured) — it does not wait for another period's state row while it holds the closing period's row: `reference.commands.open_future_period` holds a `future` row across its SCH-06 re-dirtying, which takes `combination_group` rows of (1), and a wait for that row would close a cycle through a posting; a held row answers the decision 409 `lock-conflict` at once (55P03); a lock decision of a period of the tenant's primary book takes one more row by the same rule, directly after the next period's: the `LEGACY` book's state row of that next period, when it is `future`, the entity keeps the LEGACY book and the LEGACY row of the period being locked is not `future` (`_hold_future_legacy_period`; rev 1.197; 04 DB-07 rev 1.214; PRD BR-CLS-03 rev 1.143) — read without a lock first, then `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`, refused under the same rule and copy, and opened by the same writes with a `PERIOD_OPEN_REDIRTY` job of its own; the decision still waits for no state row but the closing period's, and a `future` row is no row of a window (1c), whose rows are postable; the decision takes no row of (1) for the period it opens — the SCH-06 re-marking is deferred to a `PERIOD_OPEN_REDIRTY` job (`reference/period_redirty_job.py::defer_single`, behind `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on the period state: one live job per period state), whose handler reads the state row without a lock and takes the group rows in id order (rev 1.147; supervisor rulings R-101 (a) and R-106 (a)); the lock decision also updates, while it holds the state row, the `close_run` row of the period's latest `SUCCEEDED` run (`close_runs.lock_marked`, the `LOCK` step; rev 1.146) — no job holds the row of a `SUCCEEDED` run, and a period-end step of a close run takes the row of its own `RUNNING` run last, after its group rows of (1), the state rows its lines pin and the ledger head of (2), so neither waits for the other in a cycle; a close command that leaves the state as it is (`request_lock`, `request_permanent_lock`, `request_reopen`, `sign_checklist_item`, `waive_checklist_item`) pins the row `FOR SHARE`, which is compatible with the guards', and the three requests take `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on the period state before it, so two requests for one period are still serialised. Rev 1.216 (items CLO-RUN-START-PIN-1 and CLO-GATE-RUN-2; 04 §14.1 rev 1.228) — three more holders of that pin, none of which takes a row of (1) before or after it: `close_runs.start` and `close_runs.resume`, each after its advisory key `close:<entity>:<book>:<period>` and before it asks whether the period is open (`close_runs._pinned`; the resume locks its own `close_run` row only after the pin, where it took it first); `gates.evaluate_gates`, for every caller — the close run's `EXCEPTION_CHECK` step held nothing, and pins before it runs the monitors; and `gates.materialise_for_view`, once it has found something to store, which then reads the state again and stores nothing for a period that is no longer evaluated. Rev 1.276 (item CLO-RATE-AFTER-RUN-1, second part; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02 08:56, point 4, and the ruling of 11:08 on the lane's line; 04 §14.1 and T-REF-11 "A rate changed after a lock", rev 1.291) — one more holder of state rows: the approval of an FX rate set version. `close.rate_changes.approved`, the hook the reference commands register on the approval, reads `FOR SHARE` every state row that is not `future` and whose period ends on or after the first date whose rate the version changes — ONE statement, `ORDER BY` period start, then state id, the order of (1c) — and holds the rows to the end of the decision's transaction; a version that changes no rate takes none. Its place is that of (1a): after the approval's own rows of (1), the `approval_request` row and the `fx_rate_set_version` row, each `FOR UPDATE`, and before (3) — the `EXCEPTION` series of the items it raises — and (4); it takes no group or contract row and no `ledger_chain_head`. An FX rate set version is no subject of an automatic approval (`routing.AUTO_APPROVABLE`), so the hook runs in a decision alone and never under `submit`, which takes the `APPROVAL` series before a hook. A change of a period's state takes none of the rows the approval holds exclusively and waits for no second state row but `NOWAIT`, so the share adds a wait and no cycle; `future` rows are left alone because the lock decision takes the next period's `future` row `NOWAIT` and would be refused at once by an approval in flight. Its purpose: the lock decision evaluates its gates under its row, so a decision in flight ends before the approval judges the period — which then reads `closed` and raises its item — and a decision that arrives later evaluates after the approval's commit and reads the version; without it the period closed on the old rate with neither the gate nor a finding. The reopen decision, holding its state row `FOR UPDATE`, then settles the items of that period state (`rate_changes.settle_reopened`): `exception_item` rows are locked after the state row, as `gates.evaluate_gates` and the monitors take them. Witnesses: `backend/tests/domain/close/test_rate_changed_after_lock.py` (both orders against the real lock decision, the decision that began before the approval's instant, and the wait beyond `lock_timeout`), `backend/tests/unit/close/test_rate_changes.py` (the statement and its order). Rev 1.281 (item FX-REPUBLISH-DIRTY-1; supervisor ruling R-116 (b) and the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-02 on the lane's pre-build line; 04 T-REF-11 "The groups a changed rate reaches" rev 1.297) — the approval of an FX rate set version takes group rows as well, and takes them FIRST. `close.rate_reach.marked`, registered in front of `rate_changes.approved` (`reference.commands`; the kernel runs the hooks in the order of their registration), locks the contract groups the version's changed rates reach `FOR UPDATE` in ascending id order — ONE statement (`rate_reach.rows_statement`), rows of (1) — and stamps them; a version that changes no rate, or reaches no group, takes none. Its place is after the approval's own rows and before the state rows of (1a), the order in which a computation takes its group row and then the state rows of its window (1c); "it takes no group or contract row" above holds for the finding alone. A change of a period's state takes no row of (1) while it holds a row that is not `future`, so the approval, holding group rows, waits for a lock decision's state row and closes no cycle; a computation that holds a group row is waited for and its group is marked once it has ended, and one that arrives waits for the approval and then reads the version. The other order — the state rows shared first, the group rows after — closes a cycle of three: the approval waits for a group row, the computation that holds it waits for a state row behind a lock decision that is queued for it, and that decision waits for the approval's share. Either wait beyond `lock_timeout` is 409 `lock-conflict`. Witnesses: `backend/tests/domain/close/test_rate_reach_db.py` (the approval against a computation inside a window, both ways — the awaited row read from `pg_locks`), `backend/tests/domain/close/test_rate_changed_after_lock.py` (lane F-CLO-B's two-session witnesses of a lock decision in flight, run with the mark in front), `backend/tests/unit/close/test_rate_reach_statements.py` (the statement, its order, the registration). Two orders follow and hold on every path. The state row precedes a `close_run` row: the lock decision (`lock_marked`), a period-end step (its own run's row last) and the resume. The state row precedes the `close_checklist_item` rows: the decision, sign, waive, the requests, the `EXCEPTION_CHECK` step and the reader's write. A start or a resume that arrives while the lock is decided therefore waits and is refused once the period is `closed`; a cockpit read that has something to store waits likewise and then stores nothing; a read with nothing to store takes no lock. `request_lock` and the lock decision of kind `LOCK` also read the state rows of the EARLIER periods of the entity and book `FOR SHARE NOWAIT` (`close.commands._earlier_postable`; rev 1.139; PRD BR-CLS-08; 04 DB-07 rev 1.156): the read shares those rows with the guards and never waits — a row held `FOR UPDATE` by a state change of an earlier period is 409 `lock-conflict` at once (55P03), under rule `EARLIER_PERIOD_HELD` naming the earliest held period (PRD ERR-85; rev 1.165; supervisor ruling R-119 (d)): the read runs in a savepoint, and after a refusal the rows are read again `FOR SHARE SKIP LOCKED` to learn which one it was — so it adds no wait to this order. A posting and a close command therefore wait for each other only around a change of the state — the lock decision for the postings in flight, a later posting for the decision — and never in a cycle; either wait beyond `lock_timeout` is 409 `lock-conflict` (DG-KRN-ERR-02); (2) `ledger_chain_head` (taken by the seal trigger, DB-06); (3) `numbering_series`; (3a) the `tenant` row, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (rev 1.165; supervisor ruling R-119 (d), item SETUP-COMPLETION-LOCK-1): `platform.setup.evaluate_setup_completion` takes it as the last step of a command that can complete a tenant's setup (PRD BR-PLT-02: an entity's creation, a period's opening, a role-assignment request, an approval, and — rev 1.210 — the acceptance of an invitation and a member's reactivation) — once per tenant, after every lock of (1) to (3) the command took. Rev 1.210 (item APR-SETUP-RULE-2): a role request must not be approved by rule `AUTO-BOOTSTRAP` in a workspace whose completion is due, and stamping before it is routed would take this lock before (3); so the request READS the conditions first (`setup.completion_due`, no lock) and is submitted with auto-approval withheld, and the stamp stays this last step. Rev 1.231 (the supervisor's word of 2026-10-01 on the report of item APR-SETUP-RULE-2): `memberships.accept_invitation` evaluates setup BEFORE it opens the session and not as its very last statement. Opening the session appends a security event under the global advisory lock of that chain, and a wait for one tenant's row with that lock held would stop every tenant's sign-in behind it; the tenant row is still taken after the command's own row locks. The strength is part of the order: every table references `tenant`, so a transaction of the tenant that has inserted a row holds this row `FOR KEY SHARE` to its end; `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` does not conflict with that lock and still serialises two completions, where `FOR UPDATE` (until rev 1.165) waited for every such transaction and closed a cycle with one that waited for a row the command held — the approval of a period lock against a reopen decision waiting for an earlier period's state row (40P01); (4) `audit_chain_head` (taken at audit flush, last). No code takes these locks in any other order. **A job's transactions (rev 1.266; item JOB-STALL-COMMIT-RACE-1; 05 JOB-06 rev 1.200).** A unit of work of a job's attempt takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(hashtextextended('erev-job-unit:' \|\| job_id, 0))` as its first statement, before every lock of (1), and writes its heartbeat on the `job` row as its last statement before (4): job row, then chain head, the order in which the settlement of a job (`registry._fail_job`) and a cancellation (`jobs.cancel_job`) take them. The key is a class of its own beside the session-level slots `erev-job:<tenant>:<k>` of DG-KRN-JOB-03, and it is transaction-level on both sides: shared and waiting for a transaction of the job; exclusive and without waiting (`pg_try_advisory_xact_lock`) for the sweeper's settlement of a stalled job, which asks for it before the job's row and holds it to its commit. The unit of work therefore waits for a settlement only where it holds nothing yet, and the settlement waits for no lock of the job's: no cycle passes through the key. The heartbeat is a plain `UPDATE` of `updated_at` and takes no key of the row. Eleven tables refer to `job` by foreign key — `audit_chain_verification`, `close_run`, `contract_computation`, `evidence_pack`, `import_upload`, `journal_run`, `migration_batch`, `report_run`, `ssp_calculator_run`, `tenant_snapshot`, and `job` itself through `parent_job_id` — and each insert takes `FOR KEY SHARE` on the job's row; the update's `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` passes beside that lock, where a keyed lock would wait for it and, with the chain head behind, close the ring that DG-KRN-AUTH-08 took from the identity's row. A transaction of the attempt that cannot write the job's row (another workspace, a platform scope, a copy step) takes the shared lock on its own connection and writes the heartbeat on a second one, in a transaction of its own that holds nothing else. Witnesses: `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_job_stall_rule.py` (the order read from the statements; the two sides of the key against each other, read from `pg_stat_activity`; an insert that refers to the job beside the open heartbeat, with the catalogue's list of the referring tables). Rev 1.110 (BUILD_SPEC CLO-14; ruling R-52 (b)): among the domain rows of (1), the journal commands lock the `journal_run` row, then its `journal_batch` rows in batch and chunk order (`commands._locked_run`, `_locked_batches`; `export._locked_batch`), and a cancel then takes the transaction advisory lock of the run's entity, book and period (`summarise.lock_coverage`); the calculation of a run takes that coverage lock first — before the period state row of (1a) that its journal lines take — and locks no existing run, so the two never wait for one another in a cycle. **File rows (rev 1.130; supervisor ruling R-98 (1)).** An import's submission and its commit lock the `import_upload` row, then the `file_object` row of the upload's source (`domain/imports/commit._shredded_source`), and only then — the commit — the group and contract rows in the order above. `file.shred` (`privacy.shred_file`) locks the `file_object` row and no upload row: it reads the records that hold the file in a session of its own, without a lock. No path takes the two locks in the other order. Rev 1.125 (rulings R-49 (a), R-86): the request and the approval of an `EVIDENCE_SHRED` shred (`domain/platform/evidence_shred`) lock the `file_object` row the same way — the approval after its own `approval_request` row, as every decision does — read the holding records in a session of their own, and take no upload, group or contract row. **The period-end mark and the window (rev 1.155; item CLO-GATE-RUN-1; supervisor rulings R-114 (b) and R-116 (e), and of 2026-10-01 02:35 for (1c)).** `computation.persist` calls `period_ends.window_held` before its first insert. It reads the group row `FOR UPDATE` — on every path that follows (1) the transaction holds that lock already — and then, **(1c)**, the `period_state` rows of the window's periods `FOR SHARE`: one statement, `ORDER BY` period start, then state id, over the postable periods of the bundle's entities that have a close run whose first period-end step is `SUCCEEDED`. Their place is that of (1a): after the group row of (1), before the `ledger_chain_head` of (2). Rev 1.218 (finding F4 of the independent review of 2026-10-01; 04 §14.1 "The period rows before the ledger's head" rev 1.229; PRD ERR-98) — that place is kept by two rules, since `persist` reads the window before ITS first write and a transaction may have posted before. (i) A command that posts before it computes, or computes a second group after the first one posted, calls `period_ends.hold_windows(uow, group_ids)` before its first posting: `journals.adjustments._approved` before the adjustment's posting, `contracts.combination` before the first recomputation of a leave, and `imports.diff.hold_plan_windows` before the first plan of a template that computes (`CsvTemplate.computes`: the legacy imports of progress and of modifications), after the group and contract rows of every contract the plans name. It reads the entities a bundle of the groups would name (`bundles.entity_codes`: contracting, and performing by the lines of the booking and amendment events) and shares their window rows under the tenant's scope. The regroup and the pair of modifications applied together are not among the callers (04, same note). (ii) `journals.subledger.post` marks the transaction where it takes the head (`db.locking.mark_chain_head`; the mark ends with its transaction), and under the mark `period_ends._window_rows_held` asks the window rows `NOWAIT` inside a savepoint: a row a lock decision holds is 409 `lock-conflict` with rule `PERIOD_LOCK_IN_FLIGHT` (`problems.period_lock_in_flight`), never a wait under the head. Several windows' rows are taken by that one statement in that one order, never one by one in arrival order. Outside a window the statement returns no row: it locks nothing and waits for nothing, and a computation makes the same number of statements as before (the read existed; it had no lock and came after the postings). Inside a window one read follows it (rev 1.216; item CLO-GATE-RUN-2): the last day of the latest window period of each scope, over the same rows and without a lock — the computation holds them — from which a group without a mark is given its mark (04 T-CON-03 rev 1.228). These rows are taken `FOR UPDATE` by a change of a period's state alone, each as one row and as the first read of the period — the lock decision alone holds further state rows, the NEXT period's while that period is `future` and, for a lock of the primary book, the LEGACY book's row of that next period (rev 1.218: both named here), each taken `NOWAIT` directly after the closing period's row and given back when it is no longer `future` (above; rev 1.189, rev 1.218), and a `future` period is no row of a window —: the lock, permanent-lock and reopen decisions (`close.gates.period_scope`), the start and the end of a soft close (`close.commands._move`), the opening of a `future` period (`reference.commands.open_future_period`, also from the SCH-05 tick) and the replay of each of these into a sandbox (`platform.sandbox_periods`). None of them waits for a second state row — the decision's further reads are `NOWAIT` (above) — and none takes a row of (1) while it holds a postable period's row, so the share lock adds a wait and no cycle. Its purpose: the gate `CLOSE_RUN_COMPLETED` reads `period_ends_open` without a lock and the lock decision takes no group row, so a computation that lowered a mark and inserted no line into the period — an invoice dated in the period under `billing.posting = ERP` — held nothing the decision waited for and could commit between the decision's gate read and its commit. Now the decision waits for every computation in flight inside the window, as it waits for a posting, and reads the mark that computation wrote; a computation that arrives while the lock is decided waits before it writes anything and, once the period is closed, finds no window — its lines of the closed period are then refused by the DB-07 guard as before, and a computation that posts none completes without a pass. The decision also waits for a computation of the entity's contracts that posts only into a later period, and such a computation for the decision: whether a mark is lowered is known only after the three dry passes, and the lock has to precede the first posting. A close run's first period-end step updates `period_ends_open` on the group rows it locked under (1); rev 1.216: it reads the mark it is refused over, or leaves as it is, on the same rows (`period_end._group_lines`, `period_ends.passed`), and the gate reads the marks without a lock as before — the rules of 04 rev 1.228 add no lock to this order. For a mark that lies before its period the step also reads which postable period that mark waits for (`period_end._postable_from`; second part of 04 rev 1.228): the period states of the run's entity and book, without a lock and once per distinct mark in the step. Witnesses: `tests/domain/close/test_close_run_gate.py` (both orders against the real approval, and the statements of a computation outside a window), `tests/domain/close/test_lock_freeze_db.py::test_sc1_a_posting_that_arrives_while_the_lock_is_decided_waits_and_is_refused`, `tests/unit/close/test_period_ends.py` (the statement). **A journal run and its period (rev 1.188; item JR-CLOSED-PERIOD-GUARD-1; supervisor ruling R-97 (7); 04 DB-07 rev 1.205, revision 0104).** The writers of a journal run take the `period_state` row of the run's entity, book and period `FOR SHARE` themselves (`journals.summarise.hold_period`): the calculation directly after the coverage lock of rev 1.110 and before it reads the key's runs, and the cancel — of a run with or without a failed batch, at the command and in the job of a failed run's cancel — after the `journal_run` row, its `journal_batch` rows and the coverage lock. `tg_journal_run__period_guard` takes the row again at the run's insert and at its move to `cancelled`. Their place is that of (1a): after the journal rows and the coverage lock of (1), before the `ledger_chain_head` of (2) and the `numbering_series` of (3) — the run number and the entry numbers are taken after any wait for the state row. The three writers take the coverage lock before the state row, and a change of a period's state takes no journal row and no coverage lock, so the share lock adds a wait and no cycle: the lock decision waits for a calculation or a cancel in flight and then counts that run, and one that arrives while the lock is decided waits and is refused 409 `period-closed` (PRD ERR-86). `tg_journal_line__batch_draft` (04 DB-16) takes the `journal_batch` row of a line `FOR SHARE` at the line's insert, before the state row its period guard takes — in a calculation a row of its own transaction, so no wait; an approval, which locks the batch rows `FOR UPDATE`, waits for a line in flight. Witnesses: `backend/tests/domain/journals/test_closed_period_guard.py` (both orders against the real lock decision), `backend/tests/pg/test_journal_guards.py`. |

| DG-KRN-DB-10 | Index conditions under the policy (rev 1.164; 04 NC-20 and §1.4 rev 1.181; supervisor ruling R-116). An index a read of `erev_app` depends on binds only columns compared with leakproof operators — `uuid`, `text`, the integers, `date`, `timestamptz`, `boolean` — up to the last column the read names. (1) An enumeration or a `numeric` column goes LAST in a key, behind every column a read binds, and never directly behind `tenant_id`; when a read asks for a few of its values it is the predicate of a partial index instead. (2) A read that relies on a partial index implies the predicate in EVERY arm of its condition, in a form PostgreSQL proves: a list of values is proved from an arm that names one of them, not from an arm that is itself a list — where the reads have such arms the predicate is written as the complement (`status NOT IN (<the values no read asks for>)`). (3) A value inside `jsonb` or an array that a read filters on is written a second time as columns (04 T-PLT-48). (4) A prefix search is `starts_with` on a text key in "C" collation, case-folded when written; `LIKE`, `ILIKE`, `lower()` and regular expressions bound no scan. (5) A read that depends on an index has a plan test read as `erev_app` in a tenant session, with the planner's alternatives switched off: it runs the product's own read, takes the statement and the values the engine sent (`tests/support/plans.py`: `sent`, `plan`) and asserts with `bound_by` that the columns the read binds LEAD the key of the index it enters and are its index conditions. Neither the index name nor a column among the index conditions proves that a scan is bounded: a condition on a column behind an unbound one is listed as an index condition and compared entry by entry. Where two indexes could serve a read the test writes enough rows for the costs to decide. `backend/tests/pg/test_rls_index_plans.py` and `test_audit_log_plans.py` are the patterns. Enforcer of the keys: `erev_api.db.index_conditions.findings` over the catalogue — an index of a table with a policy that is not a b-tree, has an expression in its key, has a usable column behind one the policy cannot use, or has nothing but the tenant in front of such a column — with the closed list `ALLOWED` (index → reason; an entry without a finding fails), held by `backend/tests/pg/test_index_conditions.py`. The api and the worker check nothing at run time. Rev 1.200 (lane OPS; 05 SAR-40 rev 1.156): under `EREV_ENV=production` `erev doctor` evaluates `findings` on the deployed schema as its check `index-conditions` (DG-MK-doctor) and prints each finding as a warning — the migrated schema has none, so a finding there says that the deployed schema is not the tested one: an index built or dropped by hand, another revision's (`backend/tests/pg/test_doctor_index_conditions.py`). |
| DG-KRN-DB-11 | Connect-time settings (rev 1.255; 05 TXN-03 rev 1.193; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02). `db.session.connect_options(component)` is the one statement of the session settings a connection of the application starts with, sent through libpq `options` and equal to 05 TXN-03's string to the letter. The application opens a PostgreSQL connection in three places: `db.session.build_engine`, for every engine — the app engine, the owner engine, an engine built for one run (`migration_engine`, the command line's) — and `jobs.pool.worker_pool`, for the pool Procrastinate works on, both with that string — the builder is a module of its own, which the worker calls and which registers no job handler, so that a test opens the worker's pool without importing the worker —; and `controls.recovery_preflight`, which asks each server it is given who it is and does none of the application's work, with none. A setting the application needs is a `-c` of that string, never a server's, a database's or a role's default: the application depends on no setting outside its repository. `jit=off` is one of them — the application's statements are meant to end in milliseconds, and a plan compiled before it runs cost a member's exception queue 684 ms where 36 ms were the work (05 TXN-03). Held by `tests/unit/test_connect_options.py` — the string against 05, the three places, the pool's arguments — and `tests/pg/test_session_guards.py`, which reads the setting and its source (`client`) on a connection of each road. |
| DG-KRN-DB-12 | A read of `tenant_membership` names the tenant (rev 1.256; 04 §1.4 RLS-TM rev 1.272; item USERS-MEMBER-TENANT-1). The table's user policy shows a user their own memberships of every tenant in any transaction that carries the user, a tenant's included, and a loaded sandbox holds the memberships of its source under their ids: a SELECT that names no tenant returns the caller's memberships of other workspaces beside the members of this one, and a read by id returns two rows for a member of a workspace and its copy. A statement that reads the table as the members of the workspace therefore states the tenant in the statement itself: (1) `erev_api.db.session.of_session_tenant(tenant_membership)` — `tenant_id = (SELECT erev.current_tenant_id())`, the condition of the tenant policy; (2) `tenant_membership.c.tenant_id == <a tenant id the caller holds>`; (3) `tenant_membership.c.tenant_id == <the tenant_id of a row it joins>`, the composite key of NC-06 — a join on the membership id alone is not enough; or (4) by continuing `users.member_select()`, which names it. The condition is one every row must meet — not an arm of `or_`, not negated, not a value of the SELECT list — and it stands in the statement, or in the row source the statement is built from: a function that hands out a join of the table names the tenant in it (`notifications._assignments_in_force`), while a helper that builds the condition alone is not read (`audit_labels._member` writes its two conditions out). No condition is needed for the row a statement writes or locks — the target of an INSERT or UPDATE, the sources a `with_for_update` covers: such a row passes the policies of UPDATE too, and the tenant policy is the only one. A source the same statement only reads (`FOR UPDATE OF` another table; an UPDATE of another table that reads this one) is named as in any SELECT. A table taken from the model by name may be this one: the copy's reader (`snapshot_job.DbSnapshotReader`) names the tenant in each of its reads, whoever's transaction runs it. The reads that are meant to cross tenants are a closed list — the identity repositories of DG-KRN-DB-02 (`auth.sessions`, `auth.credentials`, `auth.mfa`) and the memberships of `platform.me.me` — and a read of the members of a workspace is never added to it. In a transaction without a tenant `of_session_tenant` holds for no row, so a module that opens an identity session does not call it — `auth.invitations` apart, which sets a tenant context without a user before each read. Enforcer: DG-ARC-20; the database's part is held by `backend/tests/pg/test_rls_isolation.py::test_rls_tm_in_a_tenant_transaction_of_a_user`. |
| DG-KRN-DB-13 | The person of a membership is read through one rule (rev 1.293; 04 T-PLT-02 rev 1.315; D-80 on SPEC-Q-182 (c); item IDENTITY-BEFORE-ACCEPTANCE-READERS-1). `app_user` has no row-level security (RLS-NONE-U): a statement that joins a membership to its person reads what the person is in every workspace. The MFA state goes with the last sign-in, and API-S-User states `sign_in_withheld`. In a report the two cells of such a row hold `reports.outputs.NOT_SHOWN`: null in the API, empty in CSV, "Not shown" in XLSX and PDF — a column has one `empty_text`, and "Never" is untrue of a sign-in that is withheld. One builder emits the value, RPT-24, and by the row's own `membership_status`, so that the dataset decides the printed cell (REQ-RPT-002); it never sits in a money column (`tests/unit/reports/test_not_shown.py`). Measured before this rule: ten functions of five modules read the two columns past it, and through the routes a workspace read the name, and in an access review the last sign-in, of a person it had only invited. Held by `tests/architecture/test_shown_identity.py` (DG-ARC-21) and, through the routes, by `tests/api/test_users_api.py::test_a_person_only_invited_is_named_by_no_reader_before_acceptance`. |

October 7, 2026 — `db.locking.hold_fx_publication` adds a transaction-scoped advisory gate
keyed by tenant. Estimate submission and final approval take it shared before their subject's
group/contract locks. The FX approval hook takes it exclusive before status mutation and before
its hooks acquire group/period locks. A new rate set is covered too; no existing parent row is
needed. Estimate readers coexist, tenants have different keys, and transaction end releases the
gate. Current routing-rate reads use no publication-time cutoff, so an earlier-started decision
cannot overlook a newly committed rate. A changed functional amount or threshold flag uses the
existing stale-request rollback/void path, followed by fresh submission and routing.


October 7, 2026 — `contracts.repo.product_reference_date` is also a named scope entry.
After the calling contract command or checklist reader authorizes the subject, it reads only
the minimum inception date of current members of the same tenant's group under
`system_entity_scope`. This matches bundle component selection across contracting entities.
It returns a scalar date, exposes no member rows and restores the caller's scope on exit.

### 5.3 Authentication dependencies (KRN-AUTH)

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/auth/principal.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Principal:
    kind: PrincipalKind                                   # E-15
    id: UUID | None                                       # app_user.id or api_client.id; None for SYSTEM
    tenant_id: UUID
    membership_id: UUID | None
    display_name: str
    roles: tuple[str, ...]                                # role codes, sorted
    permissions: frozenset[str]
    permission_scopes: Mapping[str, Literal["*"] | frozenset[UUID]]      # permission → entities where held
    entity_scope: Literal["*"] | tuple[UUID, ...]                         # union; feeds app.entity_scope
    auth_method: Literal["password", "oidc", "client_credentials", "system"]
    mfa_verified_at: datetime | None
    session_id: UUID | None
    support_grant_id: UUID | None
    on_behalf_of_id: UUID | None

    @property
    def db_context(self) -> DbContext: ...

def system_principal(tenant_id: UUID, *, on_behalf_of_id: UUID | None = None) -> Principal: ...

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RequestContext:
    principal: Principal
    tenant_kind: TenantKind                               # E-16
    request_id: str
    source_ip: str | None
    user_agent: str | None
    idempotency_key: str | None
    if_match: str | None
    now: datetime                                         # Clock.now() captured once at request start
    format_locale: str
    tenant_status: TenantStatus = TenantStatus.ACTIVE     # E-101 of the request's tenant (rev 1.108; 05 SBX-07)

def require_authenticated() -> Callable[..., RequestContext]: ...
def require_operator() -> Callable[..., OperatorContext]: ...   # rev 1.1; §5.20 DG-KRN-TEN-05
def require_for_entity(ctx: RequestContext, permission: str, entity_id: UUID | None) -> None: ...
```
