| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-AUTH-01 | Authentication order: (1) `Authorization: Bearer erevt_<tenant hex>_…`: parse the tenant, open `tenant_session` for it and look up `api_token.token_sha256` (T-PLT-16); (2) cookie `erev_session`: look up `user_session.token_sha256`, enforce idle and absolute expiry, use `active_tenant_id`; (3) otherwise 401 `unauthenticated`. Operator principals require an active `support_grant` (REQ-PLT-036). |
| DG-KRN-AUTH-02 | CSRF: cookie-authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE require `X-CSRF-Token` whose SHA-256 equals `user_session.csrf_token_sha256`; otherwise 403 `forbidden` with `errors[0].rule_id = "API-C-02"`. Bearer requests skip the check. |
| DG-KRN-AUTH-03 | `require(permission)` records the code as `openapi_extra["x-erev-permission"]`, raises 403 `forbidden` when the principal lacks it, and raises 403 `mfa-required` when `spec(permission).requires_mfa` and `mfa_verified_at is None` (REQ-PLT-005). **Second factor of the session (rev 1.91; 04 API-C-03; 05 SAR-26).** `authenticate_session`, which every cookie guard calls (`require`, `require_authenticated`, `require_operator`, `require_step_up`) and `GET /session` calls itself, refuses a session that owes a second-factor step with 403 `mfa-required` — `mfa.ENROLMENT_REQUIRED` while `mfa.next_step(auth).mfa_enrolment_required`, `mfa.VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` while `.mfa_required` — and, in an open workspace, writes the DG-KRN-AUTH-05 `DENIED` event first (`action` = the route's permission, else `session.second_factor`); with no workspace membership open it writes the security event `MFA_PENDING_DENIED` first, through `mfa.record_pending_denied` (rev 1.172; 05 SAR-26; ruling R-111 (6)) — one record per refusal, in exactly one of the two logs. A route answers such a session only when its guard is declared `require_authenticated(tenant=False, open_to=…)`: `POST /session/logout` (both steps), `POST /me/mfa/enroll` and `POST /me/mfa/confirm` (enrolment), `POST /session/mfa` (challenge); `backend/tests/architecture/test_routes.py` pins that set and `backend/tests/api/test_mfa.py` walks every route with both kinds of pending session. `mfa.next_step` is the one statement of the step: the guard, `GET /session` and the sign-in answers read it through `auth.dependencies.second_factor_step`. MFA is mandatory when `mfa.holds_mfa_permission` finds a `requires_mfa` permission in an `ACTIVE` membership's grants or among the permissions of the approval delegations to it that stand (`mfa.delegated_permissions`; rev 1.172; ruling R-111 (2)). The `requires_mfa` check of `require` stays for API clients, which never pass `authenticate_session`. Every route has exactly one of `require(...)`, `require_authenticated()`, `require_operator()` (§5.20) or membership in the API-C-01 unauthenticated allow-list; in `dev`, `test` and `e2e` the allow-list also covers the mock routes under `/api/v1/__mocks__/` (DG-API-09) (DG-ARC-04). **A tenant-wide list or act (rev 1.202; 04 API-C-03 rev 1.219; rulings R-28, R-115 (c)).** `require_all_entities(permission)` is `require(permission)` and then, for a principal whose `permission_scopes[permission]` names entities, 403 `forbidden` after one `DENIED` event (DG-KRN-AUTH-05) whose detail adds `scope` `"*"` to the method and the path; the code travels on the dependency as on `require`, so `x-erev-permission` is unchanged. `command(permission, all_entities=True)` guards a command with it. A route takes the guard when its rows carry no entity and may hold the data of any, or when its act reaches the whole workspace — 04 API-C-03 lists them, and a route is not added to the list without its row there. The guard reads the caller's scopes and widens none: it calls neither `system_entity_scope` nor its kin (DG-ARC-16). **A row that names its own entities (rev 1.232; 04 API-C-03 rev 1.243).** Where a row lists the entities it serves and no row policy reads the list, the query module of its resource decides the reach, once: `domain.integrations.queries` has `reaches(principal, permission, connection)` for one row, `in_reach(principal, permission)` as the same test in SQL for a list, and `get_connection_in_reach(session, principal, permission, id)` — the row for a read or a command, 404 `not-found` out of reach; the unscoped `get_connection_row` serves the worker's paths, which act as SYSTEM. A list of dependent rows filters through the owner (`sync_run_statement`, `external_id_statement`). A command that sets such a list compares it with `entity_scope.held_scope` and answers a list beyond it as a finding of the field, after `audit_writer.record_denied` under the command's action. A command on a member under a permission other than `user.manage` calls `users.require_member_scope(uow, membership_id, action=…, permission=…)`. **A row read through its owner (rev 1.258; 04 API-C-03 rev 1.275; ruling R-28).** Where a table carries no entity and its rows say what a contract is, the module that owns the table states the reach once, as a condition of SQL, and every read — and every command's first read of its subject — takes it. `contracts.repo.reads_group(tenant_id, group_id)`: a contract the session reads is or was a member of the group, or a `COMBINATION` record of the group names one; a group that names no contract is the workspace's. `repo.read_group(session, id)` is the row for a read or a command, 404 out of reach; the unscoped `repo.get_group` serves the steps that follow an authorisation. `repo.reads_proposal(record)`: the session reads every contract a `COMBINATION` record names. `policies.judgements.read_by_the_session()` joins the three rules of 04 for a judgement record and is taken by `_row` and `judgements_statement`. The conditions name T-CON-01 through aliases of their own, so that the contract's row policy decides and a statement that already joins the contract is not captured by the correlation. An answer lists what its reader reads and counts all of it: `combination._members_read` and `queries._members` answer the members read and the number of members, for `member_contract_ids` and `member_count`. `journals.subledger.get_posting` reads the entities of the posting's visible lines first, answers 404 without one unless the session is of all entities, and filters the seal's control totals by them. None of these widens the session's scope (DG-ARC-16). **The workspace's reference data (rev 1.259; 04 API-C-03 rev 1.276).** A route whose permission is an any-of set cannot take `require_all_entities`, which asks one code: its command asks. `reference.commands._lacks_workspace(uow, action=, object_type=, object_id=)` is `authorize` — one of the codes at any scope, else 403 with its `DENIED` event as before — and then answers whether `entity_scope.holds_all` fails for both codes; `_lacks_entity(uow, entity_id)` is `entity_scope.holds_for` negated, asked after the row was found, so that an entity outside the session stays 404. A command whose caller lacks the scope records the refusal itself — `audit_writer.record_denied` under its action and its own object type, a constant where the call stands (DG-KRN-AUD-09), with `_scope_denied` (the two permissions and `users.scope_denial`, `scope` `"*"` for an act on the workspace) — and raises `users.beyond_scope(sentence)`: 403 by name, rule `T-PLT-10`, the sentence saying who makes the change. `put_entity_book` asks `_holds_workspace` once more where it would enable the workspace's book. **A guarded transaction is a transaction of its permission (rev 1.295; 04 API-C-03 rev 1.319; item READ-SCOPE-BY-PERMISSION-1).** `require(permission)` hands on the request context of a transaction of ITS permission: `auth.dependencies.admitted_by(ctx, permission)` replaces the principal's `entity_scope` — which feeds `app.entity_scope` through `Principal.db_context` — by `permission_scopes[permission]`, and nothing else of the principal. What she holds (`permissions`, `permission_scopes`, `roles`, `role_scopes`) is unchanged, so every check that reads a permission's scope answers as before. `require_all_entities` and `api.deps.command` take their context from that guard. A route guarded by `require_authenticated` or by `command(per_subject=True)` keeps the union and asks in its handler (`require_for_entity`, `entity_scope.holds_for`). A check that must answer for the member rather than for the route — the kernel's question, `entity_scope.held_scope`, the reach of a grant — reads `permission_scopes`, never `Principal.entity_scope`. `backend/tests/architecture/test_route_scope.py` holds the three ways the rule could come apart: the guard's one `return`; the session question asked under a permission guard only, in the dependency tree of every route that declares a permission; and `admitted_by` called by `require` alone. Witnesses: `backend/tests/api/test_read_scope_by_permission.py` (the 42 reads of `config.read`, a command, a contract read, the preparer, the content of a request) and `backend/tests/unit/approvals/test_subject_readers.py` (`admitted_by`, and `require` over the catalogue). |
| DG-KRN-AUTH-04 | `require_for_entity` passes when `permission_scopes[permission]` is `"*"` or contains `entity_id` (a `None` entity means a tenant-wide object and passes when the permission is held anywhere). Failure → 404 `not-found` (REQ-PLT-012). Rev 1.260 (item SSP-ENTITY-SCOPE-1; 04 T-REF-28 and T-REF-32 rev 1.277): a table that is RLS-T and still belongs to an entity is scoped by its own area, in ONE module that every read and command of the area asks — `domain/ssp/scope.py` for an SSP book (`in_reach` for the list, `require_book` and `require_version_book` for everything that names a book, a version or an entry: 404 out of reach) and `domain/ssp/calculator.py` for a run (`requested_scope` at the request, `run_in_reach` and `reaches_run` for every read and command). They take the principal's scope from `entity_scope.held_scope`, not from `permission_scopes`, so a command that a job also runs — the commit of an import, a seed, the calculator's job — is reached by SYSTEM as by a holder of all entities. A read that must answer what a computation would — `GET /ssp/resolve` — loads its inputs under `db.session.system_entity_scope`, as `contracts.bundles.build` does, and asks the caller's scope only for what the caller names. Rev 1.289 (item POLICY-TENANT-SCOPE-ALL-ENTITIES-1; 04 §16.5 rev 1.309): where the scope a permission is asked for is on the row or in the body — a registry version's `scope` and `entity_id` — the route's guard cannot ask it — rev 1.295: the guard's transaction now hides an `ENTITY` version of another entity (DG-KRN-AUTH-03), and what no guard can ask is "all entities" of a row that names none — so the COMMAND does, in one function its lifecycle shares: `registry_versions.require_authority` asks `config.author` for all entities for a `TENANT` or `BOOK` version (`entity_scope.holds_all`) and for the version's entity for an `ENTITY` version (`entity_scope.holds_for`), records the refusal (DG-KRN-AUTH-05; the detail of `platform.users.scope_denial`) and answers 403 by name (the answer of `platform.users.beyond_scope`, rule `T-PLT-10`). The registry module is imported on the way to `platform.users` (DG-ARC-17), so it builds the two shapes itself and `tests/unit/policies/test_registry_authority.py` holds them equal. `tests/architecture/test_policy_authority.py` holds the rule in place: every route guarded by `command(AUTHOR)` runs one lifecycle command of the registry, and every such command asks the authority right after its scope key or its lock — before the row's version, state or content is told. Rev 1.131 (SECFIX-SCOPE item 1): `erev_api/auth/entity_scope.py` is the one place that decides the entity scope of access itself — `resolve` for the scope a grant request names (04 T-PLT-10: no route or domain module reads the `entity_codes` of a grant otherwise), `covers` for a command on an assignment or a membership (the actor's permission for every entity the grants name), `holds_all` for a tenant-wide act on access such as a role's definition (the permission for all entities; R-115 (c), R-28) and, since rev 1.202, for the guard `require_all_entities` of DG-KRN-AUTH-03 and the jobs and source records a holder of named entities does not read, and `holds_for` for a command on an entity's row authorised by one of several permissions (`POST /periods/{id}/open`: the permission for THAT entity, security finding S18). The domain raises the problem: 422 for a request, 403 `forbidden` by name with rule `T-PLT-10` for a command on a grant — after the command's `DENIED` event (DG-KRN-AUTH-05), which each command writes under its own action and object — and 404 for a row of another entity. Rev 1.170: `reaches_beyond` tells a refused grant request that reached beyond the grantor's own access — all entities, or a code the grantor does not cover, whether or not it names an entity — from a mistake; the grant command records it as a `DENIED` event of its own and still answers 422 (04 T-PLT-10). Rev 1.295 (04 T-REF-13 and T-REF-15 rev 1.319; ruling R-28): a row of a workspace table that NAMES entities is changed by a holder for those entities, asked in its command — `reference.commands._authors_for(uow, entity_ids)` over `entity_scope.held_scope(principal, "config.author")`, for the `entity_ids` of a GL account as they stand and for the entity of a posting rule that is deleted; `_entity_ids_errors` looks each ADDED id up in the command's transaction, which reads under the scope of `config.author`. The answer is the one of every command on a row outside the scope of its permission (04 API-C-03): 404 `not-found` and no `DENIED` event; an added entity outside it answers as one that does not exist, 422. |
| DG-KRN-AUTH-05 | Denied commands write an `audit_event` with `outcome = 'DENIED'` through `audit.record_denied`, in a separate transaction (REQ-PLT-019). Rev 1.251 (item APR-DENIED-AUDIT-1): the 403s of the approvals kernel — a decision, a withdrawal — are stated in DG-KRN-APR-02; an event of a refusal carries what identifies the attempt and never content its reader may be refused elsewhere. |
| DG-KRN-AUTH-06 | Credentials: argon2id through argon2-cffi defaults (time cost 3, memory 65,536 KiB, parallelism 4); lockout and session limits per REQ-PLT-004; TOTP per RFC 6238 with a 30-second step, 6 digits, ±1 step window and replay rejection through `user_mfa_factor.last_used_step`; session and CSRF tokens are 32 bytes from `secrets.token_bytes`, stored as SHA-256. |
| DG-KRN-AUTH-07 | Cookie `erev_session` is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, and Secure unless `EREV_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` is an `http` origin on a loopback host (`config.LOOPBACK_ORIGIN_HOSTS`: `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`) (REQ-SEC-004; rev 1.97, 05 SAR-09 rev 1.53, R-34 SD-2 and R-53 (1): `api/deps.py` `cookie_secure` reads the configured origin and never the request's host, which the client chooses, and an `http` origin on any other host still gets `Secure` — fail closed; this replaces "unless the request host is `127.0.0.1`". The local environments run on `http://127.0.0.1` origins and set none). The CSRF token is returned in the body of `POST /session/login` and `GET /session` and held in memory by the SPA (DG-FE-05). |
| DG-KRN-AUTH-08 | A provider's sign-in and its sessions (rev 1.238; item OPS-IDP-SESSIONS-1; 05 SAR-27 rev 1.178). `auth/sessions.sign_in_external` opens a session only after it holds the identity's `app_user` row (`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`) and has then read the provider's `is_enabled` in that transaction: a provider that is not enabled refuses with `LOGIN_FAILED`, reason `provider_disabled`, whatever the callback read before it went to the provider. `auth/sessions.end_provider_sessions`, behind `auth/oidc.end_sessions` and `erev idp end-sessions`, locks the rows of the provider's identities in id order (`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, so that inserts which reference an identity go on) before it ends a session, in an identity session as `erev_app`. The provider's own row is read and never locked by either — `erev_app` holds no write grant on `identity_provider` (04 §14.2) — so the two meet at the identity's row alone: a sign-in that holds it commits its session before the command's statement, which then ends it; a sign-in that takes it afterwards reads a provider the operator had disabled before the command began. The command therefore refuses an enabled provider. A session row names no provider: a provider's sessions are the open `oidc` rows of the identities bound to it (04 T-PLT-08). The provider commands that write `identity_provider` or an identity's binding stay the owner's (05 TXN-02); this one reads no owner URL. Rev 1.238, item SESSION-ROTATION-END-1 (05 SAR-09 and SAR-10 rev 1.178). A rotation and every act that ends an identity's sessions meet at the same row. `auth/sessions.reissue` takes it first (`_hold_identity`: `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` on the one `app_user` row) and opens the successor only when `_end` — which answers whether its statement ended the session — ended the session the request presented; one that has ended since the request was authenticated raises 401 `unauthenticated`. `end_user_sessions` takes the row before its UPDATE; the password's writers and the erasure hold it by their update of the identity. The order is identity before session everywhere, factor before identity where a factor's row is held (MFA verification, enrolment, the MFA reset), and membership before identity in a tenant's transaction (the MFA reset, the erasure). A new act that ends an identity's sessions takes the identity's row first; a new path that gives a session a successor goes through `reissue`. The security event chain's lock comes last (item AUTH-LOCK-ORDER-1; the supervisor's order of 2026-10-01 on a sign-in refused 409 beside the same member's code step, measured in lane F-CLO-WEB's e2e gate): `record_security_event` takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock and then inserts a row whose `user_id` refers to the identity, so (1) no statement locks an `app_user` row with its key — every lock of one is `with_for_update(key_share=True)`, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, and `tests/unit/test_identity_row_locks.py` scans `erev_api` for the statements and holds their count by module — and (2) a step that locks the identity takes it before its first security event (`mfa.verify` reads `locked_until` under that lock, right after the factor's row). With a keyed lock, an event written by a step that holds no row of the member waits at its foreign key while it holds the chain's lock, and the holder of the row waits for the chain: the deadlock of two sign-ins of one member. Rev 1.267, item INVITE-ACCEPT-SESSION-1 (05 SAR-09 rev 1.201). The acceptance of an invitation is the fourth place a session is opened, and the one whose password is verified in an earlier transaction: `invitations.check_acceptance_password` counts a wrong password and sets the lockout in a transaction that commits whatever follows. `memberships.accept_invitation` takes the membership's row first (its activating update) and then the identity's, through `invitations.claim_identity` — the first password of a person who has none, or `sessions.hold_password`, which takes the row `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` and verifies the password again under it — before `open_workspace_session`; a password that no longer verifies is 404 `not-found`. A path that opens a session on a credential it verified in another transaction looks at the credential again under the identity's row; it verifies, and does not compare hashes, because a sign-in rewrites the hash of an unchanged password. `erev idp list` (`oidc.list_providers`) reads the providers as `erev_app` and writes nothing. |
| DG-KRN-AUTH-09 | The session question of a route is asked before its body is read, and the identity store answers once a request (rev 1.270; item AUTH-BEFORE-BODY-1; 05 §2.5 rev 1.203; 04 API-C-17 rev 1.284). FastAPI reads and decodes a route's body before it solves the route's dependencies, so a guard that is only a dependency answers a caller without a session for the body first. Every guard ends in one marked function of `(request, clock)` — `get_request_context` (under `require`, `require_all_entities`, `require_authenticated()` and `command`), `get_optional_request_context`, the question of `require_authenticated(tenant=False)` (with `require_step_up` on it) and that of `require_operator` — which `auth.dependencies.session_questions(dependant)` finds in a route's dependency tree and `api.deps.GuardedRoute.get_route_handler` calls in a worker thread before the handler that reads the body: the session or token, the synchronizer token, the request rate and the second factor. The permission, `refuse_operator_command`, `refuse_inactive_tenant` and the key stay in the dependencies, after the body is decoded. What the store answered is kept on `request.state` — the `AuthenticatedSession` of `sessions.authenticate` with whether the synchronizer token was checked (an answer kept without the check does not serve a call that needs it), the `RequestContext` of a bearer token, an operator's context with its one `support_grant.access` event — beside `membership_grants`, `second_factor_step` and the two rate admissions, so the later call of the same guard asks the store nothing. A kept answer serves for `KEPT_FOR`, one second of the application clock (the clock the tests move, no wall-clock promise): a question asked later, or before the answer's own instant, asks the store again, so a body that takes its time is followed by a fresh check and a session ended meanwhile is refused when the command starts. A refusal is not kept. A handler that ends the session it was called with — a rotation or the sign-out — calls `forget_session(request)` once the session is ended. A new guard factory marks its question and a new handler that ends a session forgets: `backend/tests/architecture/test_routes.py` holds both, `backend/tests/unit/test_session_questions.py` the kept answer's rules and `backend/tests/api/test_auth_before_body.py` every operation that changes something. |

```python

class PermissionSpec:

    is_approval: bool; is_access_admin: bool; requires_mfa: bool

CATALOGUE: Final[tuple[PermissionSpec, ...]]              # exactly the T-PLT-11 seeded rows
DEFAULT_ROLES: Final[Mapping[str, frozenset[str]]]        # the ten T-PLT-09 role codes
def spec(code: str) -> PermissionSpec: ...                # KeyError for an unknown code

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Grants:
    roles: tuple[str, ...]
    permissions: frozenset[str]
    permission_scopes: Mapping[str, Literal["*"] | frozenset[UUID]]
    entity_scope: Literal["*"] | tuple[UUID, ...]

def effective_grants(session: Session, membership_id: UUID, *, at: datetime) -> Grants: ...
def api_client_grants(session: Session, api_client_id: UUID, *, token_scopes: Sequence[str], at: datetime) -> Grants: ...

# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/auth/sod.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SodConflict:
    rule_code: str
    function_a_permissions: frozenset[str]
    function_b_permissions: frozenset[str]
    sod_exception_id: UUID | None                         # APPROVED, unexpired exception covering it

def conflicts_for(session: Session, membership_id: UUID, *, adding_role_ids: Sequence[UUID] = (),
                  at: datetime) -> list[SodConflict]: ...
def assert_assignment_allowed(session: Session, membership_id: UUID, role_id: UUID, *, at: datetime) -> UUID | None: ...
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-PERM-01 | The migration that creates `permission` inserts `CATALOGUE`. Tenant provisioning inserts `role` and `role_permission` from `DEFAULT_ROLES` (04 §14.3). DG-ARC-09 compares both with 04 T-PLT-11 and its constraints on `tenant_admin`, `auditor` and `service_account`. |
| DG-KRN-PERM-02 | `assert_assignment_allowed` returns the covering `sod_exception_id` or raises 409 `sod-conflict` with one `ProblemError` per conflicting rule code (REQ-PLT-010, CTL-034). What a member holds (rev 1.172; ruling R-111 (4); 04 T-PLT-21): `effective_grants`, plus the permissions of the delegations to the member that have not ended — `permissions.standing_delegations(..., scheduled=True)`: started or not, because a delegation given for a later start comes into force without a further command —, plus what the command adds — roles (`assert_assignments_allowed`) or the permissions of a delegation (`assert_delegation_allowed`, each error on `permissions[i]`). `assert_role_change_allowed` and `conflicts_for` count delegations the same way. `conflict_report` answers for an instant: it counts the delegations that stood then and were given by then (`created_at <= as_of`). `SodConflict.delegation_ids` names the delegations a conflict is held through. No caller adds a term of its own: a new way of holding a permission is added to `auth/sod.py`. |
| DG-KRN-PERM-03 | SoD content comes only from PUBLISHED `sod_rule` rows; no rule content is hard-coded. |
| DG-KRN-PERM-04 | `api_client_grants` excludes approval permissions (DB-12, REQ-PLT-033). Rev 1.151 (supervisor ruling R-38 (iii)): a client's scopes are an access grant. `auth.api_clients.create_api_client` writes the row `PENDING_APPROVAL` and calls `approvals.submit` with subject `ROLE_ASSIGNMENT`, `subject_id` = the client's id, the proposal `subjects.api_client_grant_proposal(…)` and the `auto_approval` its caller read (DG-KRN-APR-08); the specification's hooks branch on the proposal (`subjects.is_api_client_grant`): `_apply_role_assignment` → `_activate_api_client`, and `_close_role_assignment` (`on_rejected`, `on_voided`) sets `REJECTED` for a client and does nothing for a role assignment. Nothing else is special-cased: the routing, the entity statement, the seeded rule `AUTO-BOOTSTRAP` and the self-approval checks are those of the subject. The creating command returns the secret only when the request came back `APPROVED`; `rotate_secret` issues the first secret otherwise. The client's entities are resolved by the kernel resolver of a grant — `entity_scope.resolve(…, held=entity_scope.held_scope(principal, "api_client.manage"), …)`, one call, as roles and users make it (item API-CLIENT-ENTITY-SCOPE-1): one shape, codes that name legal entities, nothing beyond the creator's own scope. Rev 1.261 (item API-CLIENT-COMMANDS-SCOPE-1; 04 T-PLT-10 and T-PLT-15 rev 1.278): the same scope bounds every later act on the client. `api_clients.reaches(principal, row)` — `entity_scope.covers` with the actor's `api_client.manage` and the client's entities — and `api_clients.in_reach(principal)`, the same in SQL, are the one rule of the reads and the commands, as `integrations.queries.reaches` and `in_reach` are for a connection: `list_api_clients` filters by it, `get_api_client` answers 404 without it, and `rotate_secret` and `revoke_api_client` ask `_require_reach` once the row is read and before its state is looked at: for a client out of reach it writes the `DENIED` event of the command under the client and raises 404 `not-found` — the answer of an unknown id, and the one 404 that records (04 T-PLT-15). A request that reaches beyond its creator's scope (`entity_scope.reaches_beyond`) writes the `DENIED` event of the creation before its 422. A new read or command of a client asks the rule too; `api_client` is RLS-T, so nothing else does. |

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-AUD-01 | `record` buffers the event on the UoW with `occurred_at = uow.now`, `request_id` and the actor fields of `uow.ctx.principal`. Nothing is inserted before `flush`. |
| DG-KRN-AUD-02 | `flush` is the last database work of `UnitOfWork.commit()`: `SELECT last_chain_seq, last_hmac FROM audit_chain_head WHERE tenant_id = :t FOR UPDATE`; then for each buffered event in buffer order assign `chain_seq = last + 1`, set `prev_hmac`, compute `hmac`, insert, and finally update the head. DB-09 re-verifies. Zero buffered events write nothing. |
| DG-KRN-AUD-03 | `canonical_event` applies `erev_engine.canonical.canonical_bytes` (§5.17) to a mapping of every T-PLT-19 column except `hmac`. `hmac = HMAC-SHA256(key, (prev_hmac or "").encode("ascii") + canonical)`, lowercase hex. The key is `KeyRing.tenant_audit_key(tenant.audit_hmac_key_id)` (DG-ENV-17). |
| DG-KRN-AUD-04 | `action` matches `^[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+$` and is `<object_type>.<verb>`, for example `contract.book`, `ssp_book_version.approve`, `period.lock`. |
| DG-KRN-AUD-05 | For IM-M and IM-S updates, `before` and `after` hold the changed columns and `record` computes `diff = [{path, before, after}]` over changed leaves (AUD-CMD, REQ-PLT-018). Money and decimals are strings. AUD-FACT commands call `record_facts`, which stores the ids, or above 100 ids the count, first id, last id and the SHA-256 of the sorted id list (04 §1.7). |
| DG-KRN-AUD-06 | Personal fields of master records are recorded as SHA-256 values, never in clear, in `before` and `after` (REQ-SEC-007). |
| DG-KRN-AUD-07 | `verify_tenant_chain` recomputes every HMAC in `chain_seq` order and checks continuity. A failure writes `audit_chain_verification` with `result = 'FAIL'`, notifies every Tenant Admin and Controller who holds the role for all entities (`CHAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED`, PRD NTF-09, which nobody can turn off; rev 1.250: the audit chain is the workspace's own, so `notifications.role_holders` is asked without an entity and a holder of either role for named entities is not told — PRD rev 1.175, which this row had not followed) and raises the `SEV-1` operator alert `AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED` (05 OPR-24; REQ-PLT-020, CTL-039). It creates no exception item (rev 1.212, item JOB-FAILED-ITEM-1: until this revision the row said that it does, and BUILD_SPEC BS1-D-13 had deferred it; an item would be workspace-wide and add no reader to the two that exist). Job kind `AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY` runs daily per tenant and on demand. On demand (rev 1.89; security finding SC-8, supervisor ruling R-32): `POST /audit-events/verify` defers a job unless the tenant has an `AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY` job pending — RUNNING, or QUEUED and either not yet dispatched or with a Procrastinate task that can still run it (`todo` or `doing`) — in which case it answers 202 with that job and defers none (`jobs.registry.defer_single`: the check and the insert are serialised by a transaction-level advisory lock on tenant and kind). The route is counted by the SAR-13 session and API-client buckets like every authenticated request. |
| DG-KRN-AUD-08 | Security event key attribution (rev 1.33; SPEC-Q-116 ruling; 04 T-PLT-06 rev 1.42). `record_security_event` writes `hmac_key_id = KeyRing.current_security_key_id()` and `canonical_version = 2`. The preimage of a version-2 row is `prev_hmac ‖ canonical(row without hmac)`, including both columns; the preimage of a version-1 row (written before migration 0061, `hmac_key_id` NULL, attributed to `security-hmac:1`) is `prev_hmac ‖ canonical(row without hmac, hmac_key_id, canonical_version)`, so no stored hash changes. `verify_security_event_chain` selects the preimage form by `canonical_version` and the key by `hmac_key_id`, requires `prev_hmac` continuity across forms and keys, refuses a row whose `canonical_version` or key version is lower than the previous row's (a rotation only moves forward), and returns FAIL naming the key id when the provider cannot serve a historical version. Admission (Codex review of 76cbee4): under the chain lock and before the sequence advances or the INSERT runs, `record_security_event` reads the head's `hmac_key_id` and `canonical_version` and refuses a writer whose pin or form is behind it with `StaleSecurityKeyWriter`, naming the head's key id and the writer's; `check_writer_admission_at_startup` applies the same rule when the worker starts and in the readiness `keys` check, so a stale process never starts or becomes ready. Cutover protocol, two steps (Codex acceptance of 5c6e5be): (1) drain EVERY pre-admission writer first — binaries at 76cbee4, c37b002 and older lack the admission check, and migration 0061's default form 1 gives no inter-row prevention, so such a writer would append a downgrade row that only a later verifier detects; no form-2 or new-pin write may happen while one runs; (2) then add the Secret Manager version, set the pin, release. Only admission-capable revisions (this rule or later) that still carry the older pin may instead be left running to fail closed on their next append and on readiness; "accept their refusals" is never an alternative for pre-admission code. | KEY-03; CTL-039; SCH-02 |
| DG-KRN-AUD-09 | Contract key (rev 1.137; 04 T-PLT-19 rev 1.154; supervisor ruling R-108). An event of an object that belongs to a contract names the contract. The writer passes `contract_id=` (one contract) or `contract_ids=` (several) to `uow.audit` / `record`, `record_facts`, `record_now` or `record_denied`; `audit.contract_key.keyed` — the one way in — writes `detail.contract_id`, or `detail.contract_ids` (ascending, two or more) and no `contract_id`, and refuses a `detail` that carries either member itself. `contract_key.ALWAYS`, `WHERE_NAMED` and `OTHER` are closed, disjoint and together every object type an event is written for: an `ALWAYS` event without a contract raises `ValueError` when it is built, so the command fails in its tests rather than write an event the contract's trail would miss (a `DENIED` event is never refused: a permission is refused before the object is read); a `WHERE_NAMED` writer passes the keyword too, and its value may be None or empty. Nothing is looked up in the writer: the command holds the contract, and where the rule of an object is more than its `contract_id` one function of its module says it (`imports.exceptions.item_contracts`, `policies.judgements.record_contracts`). Enforcers: `backend/tests/architecture/test_audit_contract_key.py` reads every writer call of `erev_api` — the object type is in one of the lists, a scoped type passes the keyword, no `detail` literal carries the key, an object type computed where the call stands is in a listed module; `backend/tests/unit/test_contract_key.py` holds the helper; the audit-coverage walk (`tests/domain/platform/test_audit_coverage.py`, CTL-038) holds the stored events of every command route — type classified, key present for a scoped type unless `NO_CONTRACT` names the operation and why, every named id a contract of the tenant. A new audited table is classified in `contract_key` before its first event is written. **The index of the key (04 T-PLT-48).** `audit.chain.append_events` writes one `audit_event_contract` row for each contract the stored key names (`contract_key.named`), in the event's transaction — the one writer of that table. A read by contract goes through those rows (`domain.platform.audit_log.trail_source`: the link's rows of the contract, and LATERAL the one event each names) and never through `detail`: under a row-level-security policy an index takes only leakproof comparisons of columns, and the `jsonb` operators are not leakproof. `backend/tests/pg/test_audit_log_plans.py` holds the rows against the events' keys and reads the plan as `erev_app`. |

### 5.6 Approvals engine (KRN-APR)

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/approvals/subjects.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SubjectSpec:
    subject_type: ApprovalSubjectType                       # E-08
    table: str                                              # 04 table name
    required_permission: str                                # default step permission
    revenue_affecting: bool                                 # impact preview required (REQ-PLT-015)
    min_approvers: int                                      # 1; PERIOD_REOPEN 2, one a controller (REQ-CLS-011)
    content: Callable[[Session, UUID], Mapping[str, Any]]
    entity_id: Callable[[Session, UUID], UUID | None]
    amount_functional: Callable[[Session, UUID], tuple[Decimal, str] | None]
    flags: Callable[[Session, UUID], frozenset[str]]
    on_approved: Callable[[UnitOfWork, UUID, UUID], None]   # (uow, subject_id, approval_request_id)
    on_rejected: Callable[[UnitOfWork, UUID, UUID], None]
    on_voided: Callable[[UnitOfWork, UUID, UUID], None]

SUBJECTS: Final[Mapping[ApprovalSubjectType, SubjectSpec]]  # one entry per E-08 value

# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/approvals/engine.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ImpactPreview:
    before: Mapping[str, Any]                               # revenue by period, contract balances, journal lines
    after: Mapping[str, Any]
    retained_file_id: UUID | None = None                    # rev 1.75: the snapshot the subject's command retained,
    retained_sha256: str | None = None                      # both or neither; the request keeps this file and hash
    def sha256(self) -> str: ...

def submit(uow: UnitOfWork, *, subject_type: ApprovalSubjectType, subject_id: UUID, summary: str,
           impact_preview: ImpactPreview | None = None, comment: str | None = None,
           reason_code: str | None = None) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
def decide(uow: UnitOfWork, *, approval_request_id: UUID, decision: Literal["APPROVE", "REJECT"],
           subject_content_sha256: str, impact_preview_sha256: str | None,
           comment: str | None, reason_code: str | None) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
def withdraw(uow: UnitOfWork, *, approval_request_id: UUID, comment: str | None) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
def void_if_stale(uow: UnitOfWork, *, subject_type: ApprovalSubjectType, subject_id: UUID) -> Mapping[str, Any] | None: ...
def bulk_approve(ctx: RequestContext, items: Sequence[BulkApproveItem], *,
                 comment: str | None) -> list[BulkApproveResult]: ...
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-APR-01 | `submit` computes `subject_content_sha256 = sha256_hex(spec.content(...))` — the content, the entities and the routing facts of the subject are read under the tenant's SYSTEM scope (`db.session.system_entity_scope`; DG-KRN-APR-02), and the preparer's own entity scope must cover every entity (DG-KRN-APR-06). It resolves steps through the PUBLISHED `APPROVAL_ROUTING` rule set (entity, functional-currency thresholds, flags), falling back to one step with `spec.required_permission`. It evaluates PUBLISHED `AUTO_APPROVAL` rules — both readings taken ONCE, by `engine.route_submission` into an internal `RoutingDecision` (never a request parameter) that `submit` reads and does not repeat; a subject command whose own side effects depend on the outcome (`judgements.submit_judgement`: the REQ-POL-010 hold) evaluates it first, under its locks, and hands it to `submit`, so a concurrent publication of a superseding version cannot split the hold from the request's outcome (rev 1.40; D-98 candidate 101d, Codex ROUTING-R1); a match inserts `approval_decision` with `decision = 'AUTO_APPROVE'` naming the rule set version and rule (REQ-PLT-016). When `revenue_affecting` it stores the preview as a file of purpose `IMPACT_PREVIEW` — or, when the subject's own command retained its preview before the submission (`ImpactPreview.retained_file_id` / `retained_sha256`, both or neither; `modifications.submit`, 04 §16.14 rev 1.92; from rev 1.98 also `adjustments.submit` and `adjustments.request_defer_past_lock`, whose T-SL-05 row holds `impact_preview_file_id` — the posting request and the deferral request that may replace it keep the one file), keeps THAT file and hash as the request's snapshot once `preview.retained_snapshot` has verified the row's purpose and hash, the file's document carrying `before` and `after` beside the subject's own members (rev 1.75: one hashed snapshot is what the preparer ran and what the approver decides on); a missing preview → 422 `validation-failed`, rule `REQ-PLT-015`. It notifies holders of the active step permission (`APPROVAL_ASSIGNED`) and audits `approval_request.submit`. **Rules cannot lower the subject's own approval (rev 1.87; supervisor rulings R-26, R-38 and R-41 (7); DG-KRN-APR-08).** The subject's own steps (`routing.fallback_steps`: the subject's permission and approver count — held by its step role where `SubjectSpec.step_role` names one — and its second step with its role for a second-step flag) together with the steps its content demands (`SubjectSpec.floor`, resolved by `engine._content_floor`) are the steps of a request without a matching rule and the floor under a matching one: `routing.resolve_steps` returns the rule's steps raised to them (`routing.apply_floor`), and the `approval_request.submit` audit (`engine.submit_audit_after`) lists the steps as raised, each with the role code it is narrowed to, and the entities the request froze. A subject whose routing facts live in its own preview hands them to `engine.route_submission(amount=…, flags=…)` (`modifications.submit`; `estimates.submit_version`: the absolute P&L impact and the flag `PL_IMPACT_GE_50K`, from `estimates.routing_facts`). `engine.routed_steps` is the one routing reading (the `entity.code` fact is the codes of the request's entities, `engine._entity_codes`; ruling R-66 (8)). `engine.auto_approval_rule` reads no `AUTO_APPROVAL` rule unless `routing.evaluation_admitted` — the function that answers the evaluation of a case, so the two paths cannot differ — admits the subject type and the source channel (`routing.AUTO_APPROVABLE`; `engine.source_channel`: the preparer's principal kind, and `USER` for a SYSTEM principal that acts on behalf of a user) or, for a seeded-only subject (`routing.SEEDED_RULE_SETS`: `ROLE_ASSIGNMENT`, `MIGRATION_SSP_REPLAY`), its own seeded rule set — for which `engine._seeded_admitted` then establishes the facts of 04 §14.3 from the tenant's rows and `routing.auto_approval(rule_set_code=…)` reads that one rule set; so `auto_approval=True` at a call site is a permission to look, never an approval. **Routing facts a command states itself (rev 1.273; item ACT-FLAGS-1; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02; 04 §16.10 rev 1.287).** `submit` also takes `amount=` and `flags=`: the routing facts of a subject command that holds what a Session cannot read and has no outcome of its own to bind to the reading. `activation.submit_activation` holds its dry run — a financing adjustment, and the transaction price that ruling R-66 (4) sets beside the booked consideration — and states the request's flags and amount from it and from the record (`activation.routing_facts`). `submit` hands both to its own `route_submission`, which then calls neither `spec.flags` nor `spec.amount_functional`; the command reads no routing, so a withheld auto-approval stays `auto_approval=False` with no routing decision (ruling R-66 (9)), and `amount` or `flags` beside a `routing_decision` raises `ValueError` — the decision states them already. The command reads the facts inside `system_entity_scope` (DG-KRN-DB-05), as the kernel reads a subject's registered functions. A subject's `amount_functional` that needs a conversion is stated by its domain module and registered with the lifecycle (`SubjectLifecycle.amount`: `CONTRACT_ACTIVATION`, `CONTRACT_VOID`), since the kernel imports no domain module (DG-LAY-03). `THRESHOLD_CURRENCY` — the currency the routing thresholds of PRD §2.5 are amounts of — is defined in `approvals/subjects.py` and nowhere else; `activation`, `estimates`, `modifications` and `journals.adjustments` import it (`tests/unit/approvals/test_activation_routing_facts.py` holds both). |
| DG-KRN-APR-02 | `decide` locks the request. It recomputes the content hash; when it differs from the stored hash or from the client's value, it voids the request (`void_reason = 'STALE_SUBJECT'`, notification `APPROVAL_VOIDED`) and raises 409 `stale-approval` (REQ-PLT-014, CTL-007). It requires the step permission for the subject entity and an MFA-verified session, then inserts `approval_decision` (DB-10 errors map to 403 `self-approval`). It advances the step when `min_approvers` is reached and, on final approval, calls `spec.on_approved` in the same transaction. It audits `approval_request.approve` or `approval_request.reject`. **Entity scope (rev 1.87; supervisor rulings R-25 and R-41; 04 §16.10 rev 1.104).** `decide` and `withdraw` first answer 404 `not-found` for a request the principal cannot read — `engine.visible_to`, the rule of `approval_queries.visible` for one request: within its entity scope (`engine.in_entity_scope`; RLS-TE does this for a request of one entity) the principal prepared the request, decided it, or holds the permission of one of its steps for at least one of its entities, through its own grants or through a delegation when its OWN entity scope covers every entity — so no command confirms an id the read denies, and the 404 precedes the status check. Rev 1.210 (item APR-SETUP-RULE-2; 04 §16.10 rev 1.224): after the status check both refuse, 409 `invalid-transition` by name, a pending request whose subject type has no specification (`engine._require_specified`; `subjects.PENDING_SUBJECTS`): `can_decide` is false for it, it waits for nobody, and `spec_for` would raise an error that no route answers. A command of the subject's own domain that withdraws the pending request of its subject passes `engine.withdraw(through_subject=True)` (rev 1.87 part 11): its route names the subject and has authorised the principal for it, so the request-read check is not asked and anyone but the preparer receives 403 `forbidden` (`engine.WITHDRAW_DETAIL`; PRD SM-01) — `tests/architecture/test_withdraw_through_subject.py` holds that every domain call passes it and that the approvals API never does. `decide` then requires ONE authority for the step permission over EVERY entity of the request (`engine.find_authority` with `engine.request_entities`; DG-KRN-APR-06), held by a principal whose own entity scope covers them all (`engine.own_scope_covers`: a delegation conveys the permission, not the view) — otherwise 403 `forbidden`, with `engine.EVERY_ENTITY_DETAIL` when the permission is held for some of the entities only — and, when the step names `required_role_id`, that role held for the same entities (`Principal.role_scopes`, from `effective_grants`); the any-role requirement of a step (`PERIOD_REOPEN`: a Controller, REQ-CLS-011) counts a role the same way (`decisions_of` → `notifications.role_codes_of` with the request's entities). After the separation checks it reads the subject under the tenant's SYSTEM scope (`db.session.system_entity_scope`; supervisor rulings R-64 (1) and R-70 (b): the content hash, the entities, the deciders a subject excludes and the hooks `on_approved`, `on_rejected` and `on_voided` — a recomputation of the combination group included — never depend on the decider's entity scope; the entity check above is what refuses a decider who does not cover the subject): `engine.current_entities` — the entities the subject states now, of its row or of the stored proposal (`SubjectSpec.proposal_entities`) — equal the set the request froze, unless that set is every entity; a difference voids the request like a changed content hash (`STALE_SUBJECT`; the void's audit event carries `after.entities`). Nothing is read for a decider whose own entity scope does not cover the request, so no request is voided because its decider could not see part of it. A content or entity function that finds no subject row the session may read raises `subjects.SubjectNotVisible` (a `LookupError`) or 404; in `decide` that is 404, never an escaped error and never a void — every other `LookupError` stays the defect it is. `SubjectSpec.excluded_deciders` is compared with the approver AND the delegator (`acting`), so a person the subject excludes — the owner of a waived item, the runner of a journal run (PRD BR-JE-01; `subjects.journal_run_runner`, with its own copy in `SubjectSpec.excluded_detail`), the author of a judgement record (04 T-CON-19 `reviewer_id`; `subjects.judgement_record_author` — DB-10 `tg_judgement_record__review` sees only the deciding person, and the author need not be the request's preparer), the author of a combination proposal (`subjects.combination_group_author`; ruling R-41 (3)) — is refused through a delegate as in person, at every step and in bulk approval; among several delegations `find_authority(avoid=…)` takes the first whose delegator is not barred (`engine._barred`: the preparer, the excluded deciders and everyone who decided the request), so a usable delegation is not shadowed by an older one of a barred person; an `on_approved` hook that excludes someone compares `engine.approvers_of` (approvers and delegators of every APPROVE decision), never the deciding principal alone (REQ-PLT-011). The author is read from `created_by`, so a `DRAFT` or `REJECTED` judgement record is changed only by its creator (`judgements._require_creator`, 403 `forbidden`; ruling R-64 (7) (a)) — the proposal of a combination group by nobody (`judgements.PROPOSAL_NOT_EDITED`, 409; rev 1.287, item COMBINATION-PROPOSAL-DISCARD-1). A person a later step of the request cannot do without is kept for it (`engine._reserved_for_later_step`; ruling R-66 (7)): when the people who could decide a later step (`engine._eligible_memberships`) would fall below its approver count once the approver and the delegator have decided, approve and reject answer 409 `invalid-transition` with `engine.SOLE_LATER_DECIDER_DETAIL`, `can_decide` is false, and `approval_queries.decidable` asks `can_decide` for every request with a later step. A subject may state its own check of the people who decide (`SubjectSpec.deciders(session, subject_id, entities, ordinal, user_ids, at)` → a `subjects.DeciderRefusal` per person refused; supervisor ruling R-92): `decide` asks it for the deciding person after the separation checks and before it writes — approve and reject alike — under the tenant's SYSTEM scope, with the ordinal of the approval the decision would be (`engine._next_ordinal`: one more than the approvals given, counted over the request); a refusal writes its `DENIED` audit event in a transaction of its own (`engine._record_refusal` → `audit.record_denied`; ruling R-98; DG-KRN-AUTH-05) and raises the subject's problem. Rev 1.251 (item APR-DENIED-AUDIT-1; 04 §16.10 rev 1.266): every other 403 of `decide` and of `withdraw` writes its `DENIED` event the same way before it raises, through `engine.record_denial`, the kernel's one writer of such an event (DG-KRN-APR-07) — for a request the caller reads, with the request and its subject (`detail.reason` is one of the `engine.DENIED_*` literals: the kernel's five checks, `mfa-required`, and `NOT_PREPARER` of a withdrawal); for a command refused before its request is read (`engine.require_person`; the step-up check of `POST /approvals/{id}/approve` and of `POST /approvals/bulk-approve`), with the id as sent and nothing of a request. A new 403 of the kernel takes a reason of its own and a line in the witnesses (`tests/domain/platform/test_approval_scope.py`); the detail of such an event never carries content of the request (DG-KRN-APR-10) — neither a summary nor what was sent with the refused decision; a 404, 409 or 422 records nothing. `can_decide` asks the same (`engine._refused_deciders`), `approval_queries.decidable` asks `can_decide` for every request of such a subject, and the NTF-01 recipients and the approvers counted for a later step leave out the people it refuses (`engine._admitted`, with the ordinal the step begins with). `IMPORT_COMMIT` is the one subject that states it (DG-KRN-APR-07). `FX_RATE_SET_VERSION` excludes the uploader of the import that created the version (`subjects.fx_rate_set_version_uploader`; ruling R-98). **Effective date of a superseding configuration version (rev 1.143; supervisor ruling R-113 (b); PRD ERR-75; 04 §16.5).** `lifecycle.ConfigVersionKind.chosen_by` names how the versions of a kind are chosen — `BY_DATE` (by a contract date), `BY_INSTANT` (at the instant of a computation or of an act), or none for a version that every reader names by id — and `lifecycle.effective_errors` refuses, for a version that supersedes a PUBLISHED one, an `effective_from` that reaches back; the message is the problem's `detail` too (`lifecycle.invalid`), because the version editors and the approval screen print a problem's detail. `lifecycle.submit` checks it before the request exists; `lifecycle.publish` checks it again inside `spec.on_approved`, at the instant of the decision: the 422 raised there leaves the deciding transaction, so no `approval_decision` row and no status change is kept and the request stays `PENDING` for a rejection or for the preparer's withdrawal. **Before the first legal entity (rev 1.214; item PINP-PERIOD-VALUE-1; PRD ERR-75 rev 1.178).** `ConfigVersionKind.entity_bound` says whether every reader that chooses a version acts on a legal entity's data — true for a registry version of `registry_versions.ENTITY_BOUND_CATEGORIES`, the accounting categories that hold no platform parameter, and false by default. While `lifecycle.has_legal_entity` answers false, `effective_errors` passes such a version whatever its date, `registry_versions.period_start_errors` does the same for the period-start rule, and `registry_versions.order_errors` lets it start before a PUBLISHED version that names no date — against a dated one the order stands (PRD ERR-80; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02); once a legal entity exists all three stand, the first at the decision as well (`backend/tests/domain/policies/test_before_first_entity.py`). A new IM-P kind states its `chosen_by`. |
| DG-KRN-APR-03 | `bulk_approve` decides each item in its own transaction and returns per-item status and problem (REQ-PLT-017). |
| DG-KRN-APR-04 | API clients, service accounts, SYSTEM principals (other than `AUTO_APPROVE`) and AI never decide (REQ-PLT-011). `decide` rejects them with 403 `forbidden` before any write. Rev 1.251 (item APR-DENIED-AUDIT-1): the attempt is recorded — `engine.require_person(uow, action=…, approval_request_id=…)` writes the `DENIED` event of DG-KRN-APR-02, reason `NOT_A_PERSON`, in a transaction of its own, with the id as sent and before the request is read; that event is the one write. |
| DG-KRN-APR-05 | Any command that changes a subject with a PENDING request calls `void_if_stale` in the same transaction. DG-ARC-08 fails when `SUBJECTS` lacks an E-08 value. **The approved basis (rev 1.40; D-98 candidate 101d).** `subject_content_sha256` is captured AFTER every system-side mutation of the subject in the same unit of work: `judgements.submit_judgement` applies the REQ-POL-010 hold (`HOLD_APPLIED` raises the contract's head) BEFORE `approvals.submit` hashes the content, deciding the hold from the same auto-approval evaluation `submit` makes (`engine.auto_approval_rule`) — an auto-approved record never holds, unless its topic is `NOT_A_CONTRACT` (rev 1.192; 04 T-CON-20 "Judgement holds"): that record's hold is released by the assessment that cites it, not by the review, so it is placed whatever the routing. **The hold follows the contract the record names (rev 1.192; ruling R-23, second order):** `contract_id`, whatever the subject; `judgements.UNHELD_SUBJECTS` names the two subjects that place none, a modification and an estimate version, whose own approval the record's review precedes. **The hold is found by its reason text (rev 1.192).** T-CON-20 has no column that names the record, so `holds.judgement_hold_reason` is the one writer and the one reader of the sentence: the submission that places the hold; the review, the supersession, the review of a later `COLLECTIBILITY` record and the Step 1 assessment that release it (`holds.release_system_holds` matches source `SYSTEM` and the reason); and `holds.release_hold`, which asks whether a `SYSTEM` hold is a record's before a person releases it. A reworded sentence finds nothing that was placed under the earlier one: the wording changes only with a revision that re-reads the stored holds (rev 1.192 changed it once, "awaits review" to "is not reviewed", when no seed and no fixture stored the earlier sentence). An approval hook re-validates the basis UNDER the locks that protect the subject (DG-KRN-DB-08 order), immediately before it applies the decision — `engine.assert_fresh_basis`, called by EVERY `on_approved` hook after its protecting locks and before its first write: `combination.apply_combination`, `judgements.review_judgement`, `activation.activate`, `estimates._approve_version`, `subjects._apply_event_submission`, `overrides._apply_ssp_override` (R3d-b), `close.commands._period_lock_approved` and `_period_reopen_approved` (rev 1.165; supervisor ruling R-116 (h): `assert_own_fresh_basis` directly after the period's state row is held `FOR UPDATE` — until then the two period hooks decided on a row that had changed while they waited for it), `modifications._approved` (rev 1.59; D-98 140 — the `MODIFICATION` request; for a regroup-after-posting pair the ONE spanning request applies both amendments under `lock_groups_then_contracts` in one unit of work or neither). Subject content describes the SUBJECT, never the approval's own state: decision-derived fields (status, decided_at, approver, request linkage) are excluded from every content function (D-98 101d note); a subject that cannot change between the pre-lock hash and the locks still calls the check — it is cheap and uniform. `decide` compared the basis before taking any lock (READ COMMITTED), so an append committed between that comparison and the hook's locks would otherwise be applied against. A difference raises `StaleBasis`; `decide` runs the decision's writes and the hook inside `uow.savepoint()` (DG-KRN-UOW-03), so the savepoint undoes them while the session keeps its tenant context and the request lock, then voids the request `STALE_SUBJECT`, commits the void and answers 409 `stale-approval` — the same refusal as the pre-lock check; no retry (Codex CONTEXT-R1: a transaction rollback here dropped `erev.context` and the void was never reached). **Own request only (rev 1.51; D-98 candidate 119; Codex 0216).** A hook re-validates the basis of ITS OWN request — the request whose subject it applies. A request id carried for provenance is not the hook's basis: BR-DAT-06 lets the import approval stand as the activation approval of the contracts the IMPORT_COMMIT job books, and the job's own authorised effects move exactly the heads `import_commit_content` pins, so re-hashing the IMPORT subject inside `activation.activate` refused every legacy import COMMIT (P5-RET-1). A subject whose approved application is a deferred job validates its basis EXACTLY ONCE, at the point the job consumes the approved request — under the authoritative locks (DG-KRN-DB-08 order: the named contracts' groups, then the contracts), before any booking or activation effect, refusing `StaleBasis` atomically (no partial events) — and that consumption yields an explicit composition relationship, `engine.ConsumedBasis` (`engine.consume_fresh_basis`: the request, its subject, the business keys it covers, the consuming transaction), which the job carries into the hooks it drives (`ApplyContext.consumed` → `contract_setup._activate`). `activation.activate` accepts EITHER its own CONTRACT_ACTIVATION request (the direct check under the group / contract locks, `engine.assert_own_fresh_basis`) OR that composition, verified — same transaction, the contract's external id among its keys, the same request — and NEVER a bare foreign request id (`LookupError`, not a skip). Freshness is never disabled globally, request ids are never erased from the lineage (`CONTRACT_ACTIVATED` still names the import approval), and an approved hash is never rewritten after effects. Codex 0226 credits the existing controls (the job's `_check_bases` against the diff-time heads, the upload lock, immutable inputs, the locked expected-head check of every append) and names the remaining interval — an external edit between the initial `_check_bases` (plain SELECTs) and a later plan's re-read of a draft head — which the consumption closes by a lock-bound design: the named contracts' groups and rows are locked at the consumption and HELD to the commit, so the initial check and every later plan's re-read run under the locks, an edit that landed before them is refused before any effect, and one that arrives after them waits for the commit; the approved bases (each key's approved head, None for an expected absence) travel in `ConsumedBasis.bases` and are ENFORCED at the booking (Codex 0342 R1): `contract_setup._book` admits a plan only against the approved basis of its key — an approved head must still be the head of the draft it replaces, an approved absence must still hold at the insert (a contract that appeared for that key in between is `StaleBasis`, the whole job rolls back), and a key without a basis entry is refused — never by adopting whatever draft is visible; the tenant-unique `contract.external_id` (`ux_contract__external_id`) is the exclusion for an approved absence between the check and the insert. |
| DG-KRN-APR-06 | Scope-set authority (rev 1.10; D-96). `find_authority` has a set form for subjects with `required_entity_ids`; `_covers(scope, None)` is not used for them (D-96): authority holds only when the own scope is `*` or a superset of the frozen set, or an in-force delegation whose delegator's `effective_grants` scope covers the set; applied at routing, inbox reads, `can_decide` (rechecked at decision time) and report `output` download. **Built for every subject (rev 1.87; supervisor ruling R-25).** `find_authority(session, principal, permission, entities, at=…, avoid=…)` takes `subjects.SubjectEntities` — the frozen set of the request (`engine.request_entities`: T-PLT-17 `entity_id`, `entity_ids`, `is_all_entities`) — and returns ONE authority that covers every entity, or None: the principal's own scope, or a delegation whose delegator's `effective_grants` scope covers them all; scopes of several authorities are never added up, and a delegation is taken only by a principal who reads the subject in full in its own right (`engine.own_scope_covers`; ruling R-41 (1); rev 1.295: ONE read permission of the subject for every entity, where under either authority the principal's entity scope covered them). `SubjectEntities.covered_by(scope)` is the decision rule (a tenant-level subject is covered by any holder; a subject that spans every entity only by scope `*`) and `touched_by(scope)` the listing rule (at least one entity). The inbox applies both in SQL on the stored columns (`approval_queries.visible`: the principal's own grants by `touched_by`, its delegated scopes only where it reads the request's subject in full; `assigned_clause` with `engine.decision_authorities`, one authority at a time, a delegated one under the same condition, and `_step_role_held`: the active step's role, when it names one, held by the principal for the request's entities; `approval_queries.decidable` completes the clause to `engine.can_decide` — the deciders a subject excludes, a barred delegator — for the inbox list, its total and the home count: ruling R-64 (4)), which is why the set is stored: the queue is paginated and counted in the database, and a live derivation would drift once the decision changes the subject. `engine.visible_to` is the same rule for one request, and `tests/domain/platform/test_approval_scope.py` pins the two against each other. NTF-01 and NTF-04 recipients are the holders who cover the whole set and those of their delegates who read the subject in full (`notifications.permission_holders_covering`, `entity_scope_covering` with `readers=`: every membership covers a tenant-level subject, one without an assignment too); NTF-01 keeps those of them who hold the step's role for the set (`engine._assigned_memberships`, `notifications.role_codes_of`). `submit` refuses, 403 `forbidden`, a preparer who does not read every entity of the subject (`engine.own_scope_covers`; ruling R-64 (6); rev 1.295: by ONE read permission, where it was her entity scope). The entities the preparer is held to are those of what the request would put in force: the entities of the request, unless the subject states fewer (`SubjectSpec.preparer_entities`; rev 1.87 part 9) — an import, whose uploader covers the rows that commit while the request names every entity any row names (DG-KRN-APR-07). The statement fails closed (`engine._preparer_entities`; ruling R-106 (b)): it narrows the check only when it names entities — at least one, all of them among the request's — and the request itself names entities; any other statement (an entity the request does not name, every entity, none) holds the preparer to the request's entities and the stated ones together. `tests/architecture/test_preparer_entities_seam.py` holds that no subject but `IMPORT_COMMIT` states it and no module but `domain/imports/commit.py` registers it. A principal that a job builds for a person carries her grants and is asked by permission (`sandboxes.sandbox_actor`: kind `USER`, `auth_method` `system`), and so is the operator signed in under a grant (`auth.operators`), whom a route admitted. `tests/unit/approvals/test_own_scope_principals.py` holds the predicate, the question and the twin; `engine.refuse_outside_scope`, `find_authority` and `visible_to` take the subject's type. `find_authority` answers the principal's own grants FIRST and asks the question only before it takes a delegation: an approver in her own right is asked nothing further (REQ-PLT-015 rests, for her, on the request's content, which `content_visible` answers by the step's permission). `approval_queries._own_scope_covers(principal)` is the question in SQL over the stored columns — per read permission she holds the subject types it reads (`readers.read_with`), and the any-permission types against the union of the scopes she holds (`readers.read_with_any`, `any_scope`) — and `content_visible` and `_assigned` put it behind the delegated branch alone. `notifications.entity_scope_covering(…, readers=)` asks it of every membership for NTF-01 and NTF-04 (`engine._eligible_memberships`); `permission_holders`, the notice of a failed close run, keeps the union. `engine._preparer_summary` is `content_visible` said for the preparer. `tests/unit/approvals/test_subject_readers.py` holds the table against `subjects.SUBJECTS` and against `file_access.STORED_PREVIEW_READERS`; `tests/domain/platform/test_read_in_full.py` the delegate whose roles name an entity she does not read, with the sentence of her refusal spelled once. |
| DG-KRN-APR-07 | A subject states its entities (rev 1.87; supervisor ruling R-25; 04 §16.10 rev 1.104 "Entity scope of a request"). `SubjectSpec.entity_id` returns the ONE legal entity of a bound subject, `SubjectSpec.entities` the `SubjectEntities` of a subject that can span several (`COMBINATION_GROUP`; `IMPORT_COMMIT`; `ACCOUNT_MAPPING_VERSION` — the entities of its own rules and of the version its approval ends, ruling R-64 (2); and every contract subject, through `subjects.contract_group_entities`: `CONTRACT_ACTIVATION`, `CONTRACT_VOID`, `MODIFICATION`, `MANUAL_EVENT`, `ATTRIBUTE_CHANGE`, `POLICY_OVERRIDE`, `SSP_OVERRIDE`, `ESTIMATE_VERSION`, a `JUDGEMENT_RECORD` that names a contract and, since rev 1.87 part 11, `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` — the contract of the adjustment; and, rev 1.289, `REGISTRY_VERSION` — `subjects.registry_version_entities`: the entity of an entity-scope version and EVERY entity for a tenant- or book-scope version, which until then was a tenant-level subject any holder decided, item POLICY-TENANT-SCOPE-ALL-ENTITIES-1) and `SubjectSpec.proposal_entities` the entities a subject without a row names in the proposal it hashes (`ROLE_ASSIGNMENT`: the entities of the proposed grant; ruling R-41 (4) — of a role assignment, or of an API client whose scopes the request grants, `subjects.api_client_grant_proposal`, rev 1.151); `engine.submit` freezes the answer on the request (`engine.entity_columns`) and `engine.decide` reads it again (`engine.current_entities`; DG-KRN-APR-02). An instance whose amount the dry run could not state is routed by `engine.possible_routed_steps` (`routing.possible_steps` over `routing.possible_winners`): every rule the other facts meet, best first, down to and including the first that states no condition on `amount.functional`, each a list of its own, and the subject's own steps where every such rule needs the amount). `imports.scope.answering_approvers` names, per approval subject the commit performs, the approver of the request's approval number k — k being the approvers that subject takes for the upload — and `ApplyContext.approver_of` hands that person to the act (`judgement_record.reviewer_id`, `ssp_book_version.published_by`; ruling R-98 (9) as refined). `subjects.import_commit_deciders` (`SubjectSpec.deciders`; DG-KRN-APR-02) asks the imports domain who may give the n-th approval (`SubjectLifecycle.deciders` = `imports.scope.decider_refusals`: the person holds, in their own right, the permission and the role of the n-th approver of every such approval, for every entity of the request; ruling R-92). `imports.scope.require_floor_met`, in the approval hook, stays the backstop of the approving decision. The record is one `DENIED` audit event written by `engine.record_denial(uow, *, action, reason, permission, approval_request_id, subject_type, subject_id, **facts)`, the kernel's ONE writer of such an event for the checks the kernel itself makes (DG-KRN-AUTH-05; `_record_refusal` stays beside it for the subject's own refusal of a decider, ruling R-98): the audit action of the refused command; a closed reason code, a module constant `DENIED_…` and never a sentence — `DENIED_PREPARER_SCOPE` here; the permission whose lack refused, empty where none is; the request where one exists; the subject where the caller holds it; and facts that are closed and content-free, never a comment or a summary — the audit log is read whatever a request withholds. After it has answered, `engine.submit` looks for a pending request again (`_refuse_pending`) and inserts, auto-approves and reads back inside `system_entity_scope`; `engine.withdraw` enters it only `through_subject` and calls the body `_withdraw`, which no other function names (`tests/architecture/test_withdraw_through_subject.py`); `void_if_stale` and `void_subject` run whole inside it (`_pending_of`). A subject command that re-derives its subject's content or basis behind the question reads it inside the block too: `modifications._stored_preview` (the basis), `modifications.submit` and `estimates.submit_version` (the digest their row keeps). `backend/tests/architecture/test_scope_questions.py` lists every call site of the kernel's question and of its kin — 84 functions, by the function each call resolves to — with what becomes of the statements that follow it: the request's row, under the tenant's scope already, put there by this revision, or not concerned, with the reason in its first word; a new call site fails until it is read and listed. The list holds the call sites, the tie of each entry to the door of DG-ARC-16 and a deferred job behind each preview's question; that a reason is true was read, function by function, and is run by `tests/api/test_read_scope_by_permission.py` and `tests/domain/platform/test_read_in_full.py`. |
| DG-KRN-APR-08 | Approval rules cannot lower a subject's own approval (rev 1.87; supervisor ruling R-26 on the security review's finding SN-9; 04 T-REF-26 and §16.10 rev 1.104 "Auto-approval and the routing floor"; REQ-PLT-016). Three limits, each held twice — refused by name at the rule upsert and at publication (`domain/policies/rule_sets.approval_rule_errors`, 422 `validation-failed`, rule `T-REF-26`) and enforced at submission in the kernel (`approvals/routing.py`), so a rule that reached the table another way changes nothing. (a) `routing.admissible`: an `APPROVAL_ROUTING` or `AUTO_APPROVAL` rule without a condition never matches, and an `AUTO_APPROVAL` rule matches only when a `subject.type` condition with `eq` or `in` names the subject types it covers (`routing.named_subject_types`); `_matched` and `rule_sets.evaluate` leave such rules out. The other discriminating condition of an `AUTO_APPROVAL` rule is `reconciliation.kind` (`routing.certifies`; supervisor ruling R-38 (v); BUILD_SPEC CLO-17): `approval_rule_errors` accepts a rule that carries it without a subject type — an auto-certification rule, which `domain/close/reconciliations.certifying_rule` alone reads — and refuses a rule with neither; the approvals engine never reads such a rule (`admissible` is unchanged), and `rule_sets.evaluate` answers a case that states `reconciliation.kind` from the rules that carry it, with no match for a case that states a variance. Other kinds keep their unconditional rules. (b) `routing.AUTO_APPROVABLE` maps each subject type a tenant's rule may approve to the principal kinds that originate it (`CONTRACT_ACTIVATION`: `API_CLIENT`, `SYSTEM`; `IMPORT_COMMIT`: `API_CLIENT`); `routing.auto_approval_admitted` is asked BEFORE any rule is read, and a SYSTEM principal that acts on behalf of a user is not admitted (ruling R-41 (7)).
