No command of a member writes such a pair: `_seeded_admitted` reads the rule set for a signed-in member only, so a request the rule approves at a submission carries its preparer, and `_auto_basis` states the rule's basis for no other principal (`tests/unit/approvals/test_seeded_admission.py`). `tests/architecture/test_bootstrap_grant_writers.py` lists the functions that refer to `engine.insert_request`, `engine.record_auto_approval`, `provisioning.grant_bootstrap_admin` and the two seeds, `provisioning.provision_tenant` and `sandbox_reset.create_empty_sandbox`, and the functions that insert into `approval_request`, `approval_decision` or `role_assignment` by name: another reference or another such insert fails there until 04 §14.3 item 2 says what it writes. The scan reads names — an insert whose table is held in a variable or built into a statement's text, as the snapshot load's is, is not seen), that setup is incomplete and that no other person has ever been active in the workspace while holding the step permission for every entity of the request (`routing.second_approver_has_existed`, read from `tenant_membership.activated_at` and the period and the entity scope of the assignments of a role that carries it; rulings R-38 (iv), R-66 (2) and R-73, and — rev 1.181, 04 §14.3 item 3 rev 1.197 — the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01: the exception ends one way and per request, once one other person's grants have covered the request's entities, and no command is refused in order to keep a second approver). Rev 1.210 (item APR-SETUP-RULE-2; 04 §14.3 item 3 and T-PLT-01 rev 1.224): the audit event of a grant the rule approves states, beside its basis, the entities of the request that another approver has covered (`engine._auto_basis`; `routing.entities_with_another_approver`, which reads the rows of `second_approver_has_existed` by its reading) — a second approver for some entities of a request does not constrain it, and the trail says so. And the rule ends when the conditions of PRD BR-PLT-02 hold: `setup.evaluate_setup_completion` runs in every command that can make one of them true, a membership becoming ACTIVE among them (`memberships.accept_invitation`, `users.reactivate_membership`), and `users.request_role_assignment` asks `setup.completion_due` BEFORE it submits — where the conditions hold and the stamp is not set it submits with `auto_approval=False`, so the request waits for a person, and the command's own evaluation sets the stamp. Rev 1.151 (the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01 on the report of item APR-SETUP-RULE-2): every submitter of the subject states the reading — `tests/architecture/test_setup_rule_submitters.py` finds the calls that submit `ROLE_ASSIGNMENT` and fails for one without `auto_approval`; a submitter takes the reading itself and evaluates last (`users.request_role_assignment`; the route of `POST /api-clients`, the layer that may read `domain.platform.setup`) or is handed it by a parameter without a default (`auth.api_clients.create_api_client`). A command that decides by the setup state and is no such request asks `setup.rule_ended` — the stamp, or the conditions where the stamp is due — and never the stamp alone: `reference.commands.open_period`, and the sandbox replay's `sandbox_periods._open`, which authorises as it does. Authoring refuses a rule that names a subject type outside `AUTO_APPROVABLE`, and `commands.create_rule_set_version` refuses a further version of a seeded approval rule set (`rule_sets.is_seeded_approval_set`; 409 `configuration-frozen`), which could only supersede the seeded rule. A new auto-approvable subject is a documented row of 04 §16.10 first, then an entry of this mapping. (c) `routing.apply_floor(steps, floor)` raises the routed steps to the floor — the subject's own steps (DG-KRN-APR-01) — counting approvers per permission and role (`routing._allocate`: every approver of a routed step counts towards at most one approver of one floor step, floor steps that name a role first), so a requirement a routed step already meets is never added again, whatever the order of the rule's steps; for what a floor step still lacks, a routed step with the permission, no role and no counted approver takes the floor's role in place when it asks for no more approvers than the floor step, else a routed step with the same permission and role gets the missing approvers (up to five), else the floor step is inserted behind the steps that serve the earlier floor steps. `routing.floor_gaps` is the strict form authoring uses (the indexes of the floor steps a rule's steps do not meet, counted the same way, over `routing.FloorItem` tuples of name, permission, approvers and role code); `rule_sets._static_floor` is the part of the floor a rule fixes by itself (`routing.floor_items`: the first step with the subject's step role; the second step when a `flags` condition guarantees a second-step flag). The any-role quorum of a subject (`quorum.floor_role_required`; `PERIOD_REOPEN`: a Controller) is applied by `engine._advance` to the first step that carries the subject's permission, so a rule that adds a step before it cannot shed it. The evaluation path applies the same limits (ruling R-41 (7)): `rule_sets.evaluate(…, rule_set_code=…)` — behind `POST /rule-sets/{id}/evaluate` and the example cases — reports no match where `routing.evaluation_admitted` refuses the case's subject type and source channel (it admits the `OPERATOR` channel for `AUTO-BOOTSTRAP`, on which provisioning records the bootstrap admin's own grant), and returns a matching routing rule's steps raised (`routing.evaluated_outputs`). Evaluation equals submission (ruling R-66 (8)): the engine applies `routing.evaluation_admitted` itself, a submission states `entity.code` as the codes of its entities and a case's one code is read as that set (`rule_sets.CODE_SET_FACTS`), and `tests/domain/policies/test_rule_paths.py` takes every seeded and demo rule through both paths. A condition the matcher cannot evaluate on its field's fact — an ordering or a prefix on a list or on true / false, a prefix on a number or a date, a value of another type — is refused at the rule upsert and at publication (`rule_sets.evaluable_error`; ruling R-66 (9)). Every limit coerces the rule set kind where it enters (`routing.rule_set_kind`), so a kind spelt as its value is never an unlimited kind. The fail-first witnesses are `tests/domain/policies/test_rule_floor.py`; `tests/unit/approvals/test_routing_floor.py` holds the pure functions. |
| DG-KRN-APR-09 | A delegation ends when its support is lost (rev 1.172; 04 T-PLT-21 "Limits and end"; PRD BR-PLT-07; supervisor ruling R-111 (4)). `approvals.delegations.end_unsupported(uow, cause=…)` ends — `transitions.apply` on the three revocation columns, one `approval_delegation.end` audit event each — every delegation that has not ended and whose delegator is not an `ACTIVE` member or does not hold every permission it names, or — rev 1.286; 04 T-PLT-21 rev 1.293 — whose delegate is a `REMOVED` member (the statement joins the delegate's row as it joins the delegator's; `Ended.delegate_status` is a member of the event's `detail` only for such an end; a suspended delegate keeps the delegation); `end_unsupported_rows(session, …)` is its core for a transaction without a unit of work (the erasure's other workspaces), whose caller appends the events. A function that writes `role_assignment`, `role_permission` or `tenant_membership` calls it AFTER a change that takes access away and BEFORE one that gives access (`users._set_status` does both), so that no delegation is unsupported across a command and none returns with a later grant; `backend/tests/architecture/test_delegation_end.py` finds such functions by what they write and fails for one that neither calls the sweep nor is listed there with its reason. `domain/platform/approval_delegations.py` holds the commands: `_administering` (the member's MFA-verified session and step-up, each refusal audited as the command's `DENIED` event), the delegate's confirmed factor, the end within 90 days of `uow.now`, `sod.assert_delegation_allowed`, and the administrator's end — `ADMINISTER` (`role.manage`) with `entity_scope.covers(entity_scope.held_scope(principal, ADMINISTER), entity_scope.assigned(session, delegator))`. |
| DG-KRN-APR-10 | The content of a request is read by who covers every entity (rev 1.191; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01 on finding 10 of the lane's report — a release blocker — and its rulings of the same day on the lane's pre-build line; item APR-CONTENT-SCOPE-1; 04 §16.10 rev 1.208 "Content of a request"; REQ-PLT-012). `approval_queries.content_visible(principal, authorities)` is `visible` with "every entity" for "at least one". Rev 1.295 (04 §16.10 rev 1.319): the principal's own grants hold the permission of a step for every entity — asked nothing further — or the principal reads the subject in full (`_own_scope_covers`) and prepared the request, decided it, or holds such a permission through ONE delegated authority; until that revision the own-scope condition stood before all three and read the principal's entity scope. It is the ONE predicate for what a request puts in force, and every read of that asks it: `approval_queries.approval_outs` — the single read, the list and the answers of approve, reject and withdraw — evaluates it for the page in one statement (`content_readable`) and answers the others the header with `content_withheld`: `subjects.withheld_summary` (the subject type's name in `subjects.SUBJECT_LABELS`, one per value of E-08 in the words of SCREENS §15.3, and the request's number) for `summary` and `subject.display`, null `amount` and `impact_preview`, empty `flags` and `attachments`, null decision comments — but the comment of a REJECTION for the preparer of the request (rev 1.231; 04 §16.10 rev 1.240; `approval_queries.rejection_reason_shown`: it is written to her, that decision's comment alone, and the answer stays a header), and null `reason_code` and `comment` of the request — but the two for its preparer, who wrote them (rev 1.241; 04 §16.10 rev 1.252; item APR-REQUEST-REASON-1; `approval_queries.submission_shown`, one predicate with the rejection's: she prepared the request); a decision's `reason_code` goes with its `comment` — `approval_queries._decision_out` answers the two together or neither, because the code is free text of the decider (rev 1.241; item APR-DECISION-CODE-CONTENT-1); it opens no preview file and reads no attachment for them. `file_access.request_content_visible` is the grant of the impact preview's owner `approval_request` and the `visible` rule of the attachment subject `approval_request`, for reading and for attaching; `attachments.preview_refusal` leaves a request whose content the caller does not read to the decision, which refuses it by name. The content rows of a subject (item APR-SUBJECT-CONTENT-1) and any later read of something a request puts in force ask the same predicate and add none. The list tells nothing a row withholds: a filter, a search column or a sort key that reads a content column of T-PLT-17 (`approval_queries.CONTENT_COLUMNS`) reads it through `approval_queries.shown`, NULL for a withheld row. The catalogue's sort key `amount` is replaced by the reader's own (`approval_queries.amount_key`, selected by `list_approvals` and put into the specification by the route's `approval_list`), and `tests/unit/approvals/test_content_scope.py` walks the catalogue, so a search or a range added on a content column fails there until it reads through `shown`. A notification is a read of the summary composed for its recipient: `engine._preparer_summary` gives the preparer the summary while she reads the request in full, or holds a step's permission for every entity of it, and the withheld form otherwise — in `ITEM_APPROVED`, `ITEM_REJECTED`, whose body carries the decider's comment for every preparer (rev 1.231: after the summary she is shown), and `APPROVAL_VOIDED`, where the people the request waited for are told the summary. Witnesses: `tests/domain/platform/test_approval_scope.py` (the predicate over a request of no entity, one, several and all; a delegate; a decider who lost an entity; the preparer and its notifications), `tests/api/test_approvals_api.py` (the answer, the files, the attachments, the list) and `tests/domain/imports/test_entity_scope.py` (the finding through the product). |

          query: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]], body: bytes, content_type: str) -> Started | Replay: ...

# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/api/deps.py

```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-IDEM-01 | Every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE route, except the API-C-01 unauthenticated routes, the mock routes (DG-API-09) and the operator route of DG-KRN-TEN-05, depends on `command(...)`. A missing or malformed `Idempotency-Key` (8 to 255 characters) → 422 `validation-failed` with `errors[0] = {field: "Idempotency-Key", rule_id: "API-C-04"}` (DG-OQ-06). Rev 1.108 (05 SBX-07 rev 1.64): after the permission guard and the operator refusal, and before the key is read, `command(...)` answers 409 `invalid-transition` when `RequestContext.tenant_status` is not `ACTIVE` — a sandbox archived by a reset or a failed load, or one whose load has not completed — so nothing is stored for the attempt; `tenant_status` is read with the session's or the API client's tenant (`sessions.ActiveTenant.status`, `api_clients.TokenPrincipal.tenant_status`), a worker's context keeps `ACTIVE`, and reads are not gated. |
| DG-KRN-IDEM-02 | `begin` runs in its own committed transaction and inserts `idempotency_record` (`state = 'IN_PROGRESS'`, `expires_at = now + 7 days`). `request_sha256 = sha256_hex({"method", "route", "path_params", "query" (sorted), "body"})`, where `body` is the parsed JSON for `application/json` and the SHA-256 of the raw bytes otherwise. On conflict: a COMPLETED record with the same hash returns `Replay`; a different hash raises 422 `idempotency-key-reused`; an IN_PROGRESS record raises 409 `idempotency-in-progress` (API-C-04, REQ-PLT-026). |
| DG-KRN-IDEM-03 | The route calls `complete` inside the business transaction, before commit, storing status, `Location`, `ETag` and body. Responses with status 401, 403, 409 `idempotency-in-progress`, 412, 428 or 429 are not stored, and any 5xx or unhandled exception triggers `abandon`, which deletes the IN_PROGRESS row in its own transaction. Rev 1.127 (item IDEM-LOCK-CONFLICT-1; supervisor rulings R-97 (6) and R-112 (d); 04 API-C-04 rev 1.144): two more problems are not stored, as a list by slug and not by status (`deps.UNSTORED_SLUGS`): `lock-conflict` and `period-closed`. The rule for each is to submit the request again — a `lock-conflict` met a busy row, and the resubmission of a posting the period guard refused is planned into the next open period (04 DB-07 (2), (3)) — and a stored 409 would be replayed to that resubmission for as long as the record lives, so the command would never run. For the deterministic uses of `period-closed` the second run is refused again and writes nothing. Every other 409 stays stored. |
| DG-KRN-IDEM-04 | A replay returns the stored status, headers and body plus `Idempotent-Replay: true`. Bodies above 1 MiB are stored as files (`response_file_id`, T-PLT-28). |
| DG-KRN-IDEM-05 | `precondition="contract"` parses `If-Match: "s<n>"` into `expected_version`; `"row"` parses `"r<n>"`. A missing header → 428 `precondition-required`; a mismatch detected by the handler → 412 `precondition-failed` (API-C-08). |
| DG-KRN-IDEM-06 | Adapter and import idempotency is separate: `contract_event.idempotency_key` and `subledger_posting.idempotency_key` are deterministic keys (T-CON-05, T-SL-01, research 06 P9). |

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-ERR-01 | Media type `application/problem+json`; body `{type, title, status, detail, instance, code, errors}` (API-S-Problem); `type = TYPE_BASE + slug`; `instance = "urn:erev:request:" + request_id`. `Problem("unknown-slug")` raises `KeyError` at construction. Rev 1.208 (item SSP-STUDY-SERIES-BASIS-1; supervisor ruling R-50 (c) and the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01): a refusal for something the command's body does not name is ONE problem without a `field`, and the sentence a person reads is its `detail`; `errors[]` holds that sentence, or its parts, without a `field`. A form maps `errors[].field` onto its own fields and shows its banner only for a problem none of whose errors names a field; the banner reads `detail`, else the title of the slug (DG-FE-05), so a sentence left in `errors[].message` alone is not shown, and an error that names a field the form does not hold is shown nowhere. A command that builds the body of another command judges what it can name of that body in its own terms before it calls: `ssp.calculator.create_draft_version` refuses a result its study proposes nothing for, and a run without results, with the sentence in `detail` (04 §16.14 rev 1.222) — before this revision the inner command answered `entries[0].value_basis`, and the dialog showed nothing. |
| DG-KRN-ERR-02 | Handlers: `Problem` → its JSON. `RequestValidationError` → 422 `validation-failed` with one `ProblemError` per Pydantic error (`field` is the dotted location without the leading `body`). `DBAPIError` with SQLSTATE `P0001` and a message starting `EREV-` → the slug whose `db_codes` contains the code, with `code` set. SQLSTATE `42501` (insufficient privilege, including RLS `WITH CHECK` violations) → 404 `not-found` for GET and 403 `forbidden` otherwise. SQLSTATE `40P01` (deadlock detected) → 409 `lock-conflict`: the transaction rolled back and nothing was saved; the client may resubmit, no automatic retry exists (DG-KRN-DB-08; D-98 candidate 101c; rev 1.36). SQLSTATE `55P03` (`lock_not_available`: a lock wait outlived the platform's `lock_timeout`, 10 s in `db/session.py`) → the same 409 `lock-conflict` with rule `LOCK_TIMEOUT` and its own detail — rolled back, nothing saved, resubmit; no automatic retry (D-98 candidate 141; rev 1.61). A `P0001` code with a registered rule (`EREV-REF-001` — raised by every DB-05 reference-data freeze trigger: legal entity, tenant identity, period, calendar, SSP book scope, product code (rev 1.143; `reference.commands.update_product` refuses that change first with 422 `validation-failed` on `code`, rule `DB-05`) → 409 `immutable-record`, rule `ENTITY_FROZEN` for all of them) carries the trigger's message as the problem `detail` — the frozen field and object — beside `code` (04 §15.2 rev 1.71; D-98 candidate 141 amendment 1). Like every other stored problem it is kept under the command's `Idempotency-Key` (DG-KRN-IDEM-03): a resubmission with the same key replays the 409, a new key runs the command again (rev 1.40). Rev 1.127 (04 §15.2 rev 1.144; supervisor rulings R-97 (5), (6)): SQLSTATE `40001` (a serialization failure) → the same 409 `lock-conflict`, with the deadlock's detail. SQLSTATE `57014` (a statement PostgreSQL cancelled, at the platform's `statement_timeout` or on request) → 503 `statement-timeout` with `Retry-After: 30` (`problems.STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS`; PRD ERR-66); the handler logs `http.statement_timeout` at WARNING with the SQLSTATE and the driver's error class, without a stack trace. `lock-conflict` and `period-closed` are not kept under the `Idempotency-Key` (DG-KRN-IDEM-03 rev 1.127); the `immutable-record` of the sentence before stays kept. |
| DG-KRN-ERR-03 | Any other exception → status 500 with `type = "about:blank"`, `title = "Internal Server Error"`, no `detail`, and the request id in `instance`. The stack trace goes only to the log. This adds no catalogue slug. Rev 1.97 (ruling R-53 (5); 04 API-C-05 rev 1.114): one class of database error is not a 500. `db/errors.py` `server_unavailable(exc)` is true for PostgreSQL class 53 (insufficient resources: `53000`, `53100`, `53200`, `53300`, `53400`), the connection exceptions `08000`, `08001`, `08003`, `08004` and `08006`, and the server states `57P01` (shutting down), `57P02` (crashed) and `57P03` (not accepting connections yet); and, when the driver reports no SQLSTATE at all, a connection it lost or could not open (`SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_CLASS`, `SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_STATES`; `server_unavailable_in(exc)` looks through an exception's cause and context chain). `unhandled_error_response` answers such an error with 503 `about:blank`, `title = "Service Unavailable"` and `Retry-After: 5` (`problems.SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS`) and logs `http.server_unavailable` at WARNING with the SQLSTATE and the driver's error class, without a stack trace. `from_db_error` returns None for these codes, so `run_command` abandons the idempotency attempt (DG-KRN-IDEM-03) and every `except DBAPIError` mapper re-raises them. A job attempt that meets one fails and is retried by its policy (DG-KRN-JOB-05). Rev 1.127 (04 API-C-05 rev 1.144; supervisor ruling R-103 (c)): the application's own connection pool that gives no connection within its wait is answered the same way. `db/errors.py` `pool_timeout_in(exc)` finds SQLAlchemy's `TimeoutError` in an exception's cause and context chain; the answer is 503 `about:blank` with `Retry-After: 5` and the same log line, with `driver_error_class` `sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError` and no SQLSTATE. It is the server's state, never a 409. The interface shows the PRD ERR-64 text for a slug-less 503. |
| DG-KRN-ERR-04 | Domain code raises `Problem`, and the engine raises `EngineError` (§7, mapped by the orchestrator). `fastapi.HTTPException` is forbidden (DG-ARC-05). |
| DG-KRN-ERR-05 | Import findings and row errors use `errors[]` with `sheet`, `row` and `rule_id` set to a finding code of the 04 §15.4 catalogue, which absorbs `docs/legacy/DEVIATIONS.md` §5 (for example `PROGRESS_OVER_DELIVERY`, `IMPORT_FILE_DUPLICATE`; D-73, B1-014). |
| DG-KRN-ERR-06 | What a database error answers (rev 1.127; supervisor rulings R-97 (5) and (6), R-103 (c), R-105). One predicate in `db/errors.py` splits a database error by SQLSTATE class (R-105 (2); lane QA-BE builds it on `server_unavailable` with item COMPUTE-TRANSIENT-NOT-FAILURE-1): **transient** — classes 08, 25, 40, 53, 55, 57, 58, 72 and XX, the period guard's `EREV-LED-003`, a class in neither list and a driver error without a SQLSTATE; **deterministic** — classes 0A, 21, 22, 23, 27, 2F, 42, 44, 54 and P0 other than the period guard. A computation (`compute_group`, DG-CMD-09) stores a deterministic error FAILED with its blocking item, as it stores a crash, and stores nothing for a transient one: the error leaves the computation (until that item is on main, `compute_group` lets the 503 set of DG-KRN-ERR-03 leave and stores the rest). What the error then answers: (1) `40P01`, `40001`, `55P03` → 409 `lock-conflict`; not kept for the `Idempotency-Key`. (2) `EREV-LED-003` → 409 `period-closed`; not kept. (3) Class 53, `08000`, `08001`, `08003`, `08004`, `08006`, `57P01`, `57P02`, `57P03`, a driver error without a SQLSTATE, and the pool timeout — which is no database error — → 503 `about:blank` with `Retry-After: 5`; no 5xx is kept. (4) `57014` → 503 `statement-timeout` with `Retry-After: 30`. (5) Every other transient state — `08007`, `08P01`, the other states of classes 40, 55 and 57, classes 25, 58, 72 and XX, an unknown class — → 500 `about:blank`, logged `http.unhandled_error`. (6) A deterministic error outside a computation → the slug of its §14.1 code or of SQLSTATE `42501` (DG-KRN-ERR-02), else 500. In no case is a refusal stored as the result of the work it interrupted. A job attempt that meets (1) to (5) fails and is settled by the kind's retry policy (DG-KRN-JOB-05; 05 §5.6): retried while attempts remain, FAILED after the last. The policy of `CONTRACT_COMPUTE` and what its last attempt stores are item JOB-COMPUTE-RETRY-1. |

DECIMAL_CONTEXT: Final[decimal.Context]
# prec=38, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP, traps=[FloatOperation, InvalidOperation, DivisionByZero, Overflow]
EXACT_PLACES: Final = 18                                    # TY-02 scale

def to_fraction(value: str | int | Decimal | Fraction) -> Fraction: ...
def round_half_up(x: Fraction | Decimal | int, minor_unit: int) -> int: ...      # returns minor units

def cumulative_posted(exact_allocation: Fraction, posted_allocation_minor: int, progress: Fraction,
                      minor_unit: int) -> int: ...
# D-11a: X = exact_allocation (currency units, unrounded); A = posted_allocation_minor (largest remainder, minor units);
# f_t = progress in [0, 1]. Returns C_t = min(max(round_half_up(X × f_t, minor_unit), 0), A) when A ≥ 0,
# max(min(round_half_up(X × f_t, minor_unit), 0), A) when A < 0, and A when f_t = 1.
def period_amounts(exact_allocation: Fraction, posted_allocation_minor: int,
                   cumulative_progress: Sequence[Fraction], minor_unit: int,
                   opening_posted_minor: int = 0) -> list[int]: ...
# Returns [C_1 − C_0, C_2 − C_1, …] with C_0 = opening_posted_minor.
def format_money(n_minor: int, minor_unit: int) -> str: ...

DecimalStr = Annotated[str, AfterValidator(validate_decimal_string)]   # ^-?\d{1,20}(\.\d{1,18})?$

```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-MONEY-01 | `round_half_up` implements ALG-01 §2.1.1 on integers (`sign(x) × floor(abs(x) × 10^e + 1/2)`, symmetric for negatives). `minor_to_decimal` and `format_money` never produce negative zero. |
| DG-KRN-MONEY-02 | `largest_remainder` implements ALG-01 §2.1.2 exactly: tie order larger fractional remainder, then larger weight, then ascending key by Unicode code point; `EngineError` codes `NEGATIVE_WEIGHT` and `TOTAL_WEIGHT_ZERO`; the result is independent of input order. Unit tests reproduce CHK-001, CHK-003a to CHK-003d. |
| DG-KRN-MONEY-03 | `cumulative_posted` and `period_amounts` implement ALG-01 §2.1.3 as confirmed by D-11a (rev 1.1). X is the exact (unrounded) allocation, f_t the exact cumulative progress, and A the posted allocation from `largest_remainder`. `C_t = round_half_up(X × f_t)`, bounded to [0, A] when A ≥ 0 and to [A, 0] when A < 0, and `C_t = A` when `f_t = 1`. The period amount is `C_t − C_{t−1}`; there is no plug to the last period (D-11). Rounding `A × f_t` instead of `X × f_t` is forbidden: CHK-007 requires `round(118.533201) = 118.53`, not `round(237.07 × 0.5) = 118.54`. A `progress` outside [0, 1] raises `ValueError`; stages validate progress first and raise their own catalogue codes. The parity suite runs the same helper (D-11a, DG-PAR-03). Unit tests reproduce CHK-004, CHK-005 and CHK-007. |
| DG-KRN-MONEY-04 | Minor units come from the currency table in the engine bundle, seeded from `ISO_4217`. No code assumes two decimals; DG-ARC-06 flags the literals `Decimal("0.01")`, `Decimal('0.01')` and `quantize(Decimal("0.01"))` outside `erev_engine/money.py`. |
| DG-KRN-MONEY-05 | `to_fraction` raises `TypeError` for `float` and `bool` and `ValueError` for strings with exponents. `db.types.MoneyType`, `ExactType` and `FxRateType` raise `TypeError` when bound to a `float`. A JSON number in a money or decimal field → 422 `validation-failed`, rule `API-C-06` (REQ-PLT-031). |
| DG-KRN-MONEY-06 | Stored scales: `erev.money` holds exactly the minor-unit places of its currency (DB-06); `erev.exact` stores `format_exact(x)`; `erev.fx_rate` NUMERIC(28,12). API money strings carry exactly the minor-unit decimals (`"1200"` JPY, `"12.30"` USD, `"1.250"` BHD); exact and rate strings have trailing zeros trimmed and no exponent (API-C-06). |
| DG-KRN-MONEY-07 | `decimal_from_cell` is the only place a float becomes a number (REQ-DAT-007): `Decimal(repr(value))` inside `decimal.localcontext()` with `FloatOperation` untrapped for that one statement. Only `erev_api.domain.imports` calls it, and the caller validates the allowed scale. |

| DG-KRN-TIME-02 | A command that supplies `effective_at` (a timestamp) is converted with `to_entity_date(effective_at, legal_entity.time_zone)` before period assignment (API-C-07, REQ-CLS-005, M-ARCH-05). |
| DG-KRN-TIME-03 | Default read parameters: `as_of = entity_today(clock, context entity time zone)`, `known_at = clock.now()` (API-C-10). The SPA passes `as_of` explicitly (BR-UX-02). |
| DG-KRN-TIME-04 | `posting_period` implements JET R2 and ALG-09 step 2-3. When the period containing `effective_date` has a state in `POSTABLE_STATES`, it is the posting period and the origin is `None`. Otherwise the posting period is the earliest later period whose state is in `POSTABLE_STATES` (`open`, `closing`, `reopened`; D-79, as ENGINE_SPEC S08-R-08 and 05 RCP-04), and the origin is the containing period. When no such period exists → 409 `period-closed`. Soft-close restrictions of REQ-CLS-003 are checked by `erev_api.domain.close` before posting. **The `LEGACY` book (rev 1.197; item PER-LEGACY-POSTING-PERIOD-1; supervisor ruling R-118 (h); 05 RCP-04 rev 1.153).** The LEGACY book has no close of its own and follows the primary book's: the DB-07 guard refuses a LEGACY line while the primary book's period is not postable (04 DB-07 rev 1.155) and the bundle hands the engine the primary's state (05 RCP-15 rev 1.94). `posting_period` answers by the same rule: for `LEGACY` a period is postable only when its own state row AND the row of the tenant's primary book for the same entity and period are postable — a missing primary row is not postable — and the later period is the earliest one postable in both. When no period is postable in both and the state that refuses is `closed` or `permanently_locked`, the 409 is PRD ERR-15's with `EREV-LED-003` and names the book whose period is closed: the primary's code where the LEGACY row itself is postable. `periods.followed_book(session, book_code)` names the book a book follows — the primary for `LEGACY`, none for any other book — and `periods._followed_rows` (rev 1.167) reads through it. Until rev 1.197 the helper read the LEGACY row alone and, for a date in a period the primary book had closed, answered that period, in which the guard refuses the line. The mirror of DB-07 on a command, `periods.refuse_closed_postings` (DG-CMD-03; PRD ERR-15), asks the books the entity keeps (`periods.kept_books`): every book it has period states for, less a book whose `entity_book` row is not enabled (04 T-REF-03) and a book the workspace has disabled — the books a computation posts in (05 RCP-15). A book the entity has stopped keeping takes no posting and its periods are no longer opened; asked, it would refuse every late event with no way out — the LEGACY book from the next lock of the primary book on. For a kept LEGACY book the mirror refuses an event dated in a period the primary book has closed while no later period is open in both books; until rev 1.197 that event was accepted and its LEGACY amount was posted in no period. The lock decision of the primary book opens the LEGACY book's next period with its own (DG-KRN-DB-08 (1a); 04 DB-07 rev 1.214; PRD BR-CLS-03 rev 1.143), so no lock leaves that state; it remains where the entity did not keep the LEGACY book when the period was locked and keeps it again, until the LEGACY book's next period is opened (`POST /periods/{id}/open`, or 05 SCH-05 on its start date). Rev 1.167 (supervisor ruling R-117 (c)): "the period was locked once and is not locked now" has one reading in Python, `periods.under_reopen(session, *, entity_id, book_code, period_id)` — the period state's `current_lock_id` names a `period_lock` of kind `REOPEN` (`periods.lock_kind`); for the `LEGACY` book, the row of the tenant's primary book counts as well, because the LEGACY book follows the primary's close — and one in SQL, the DB-07 guard that stores `is_post_reopen` and reads the same two rows for a LEGACY line (04 §14.1). `periods.auto_approval_barred` is the rule of PRD BR-CLS-04, BR-DAT-07 and BR-CLS-06 for one period: in soft close, or under reopen; `close/posting_guard.posts_into_restricted_period` and `imports/commands.posts_into_closing_period` call it, and `close/commands.soft_close_target` reads the record through `periods.lock_kind`. No module tests the state literal `reopened` for that fact. |
| DG-KRN-TIME-05 | `datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `date.today`, `time.time` and `time.monotonic` are forbidden outside `erev_api/clock.py` and `erev_api/logging.py` (DG-ARC-05). `erev_engine` reads no clock at all (§7). |
| DG-KRN-TIME-06 | `FrozenClock` is the only application clock in backend tests, the answer-key runner and the parity runner (DG-TST-14). Database-assigned timestamps (`now()` defaults and the DB-08 `recorded_at`) are real server times; tests assert their order and presence, never their values (docs/02-PRD.md E2E-07 applies the same rule to e2e). |
