| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-EVT-01 | `append_events` implements the T-CON-05 append protocol: `UPDATE contract SET head_stream_version = head_stream_version + :n WHERE tenant_id = :t AND id = :c AND head_stream_version = :expected`; zero rows → 412 `precondition-failed` with code `EREV-EVT-001`. It then inserts the `n` events with `stream_version = expected + 1 … expected + n`, `payload_sha256 = sha256_hex(payload)`, `request_id` from the context, marks `combination_group.dirty_since = uow.now`, and calls `audit.record_facts` (AUD-FACT). |
| DG-KRN-EVT-02 | Events whose E-03 "Approval" column is not "none", when routing requires approval, are not appended. The caller stores them in `event_submission` and calls `approvals.submit`. On approval `SubjectSpec.on_approved` appends them as the SYSTEM principal on behalf of the preparer (T-CON-24). `CONTRACT_ACTIVATED` and `CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` (E-03 approval `CONTRACT_ACTIVATION`) are never stored in an `event_submission`: the approved activation composes and appends them (DG-KRN-EVT-08; rev 1.88). Rev 1.109 (supervisor ruling R-77 (9)): nor is a `COLLECTIBILITY_ASSESSED` or a `SIGNIFICANT_CHANGE_FLAGGED`, nor the void of an assessment or of an activation event; `approvals.subjects._apply_event_submission` calls `step1.refuse_stored` under its locks before it appends, so what a submission may hold is decided where it is stored AND where it is appended. Rev 1.177 (BUILD_SPEC CTR-6; supervisor ruling R-120 (a); 04 §16.3 "Manual events" and T-CON-24, rev 1.194): `contracts.events.record_events` stores the request of a signed-in person — any principal that is not an API client — that holds a type of `events.MANUAL_TYPES` (E-03 approval `MANUAL_EVENT`) through `events._submit`, the one writer of `event_submission` for the route: subject `ATTRIBUTE_CHANGE` when the request names `LINE_ATTRIBUTES_CHANGED`, else `MANUAL_EVENT`. The evidence rule (`REQ-DAT-014`) is checked there, and the evidence files become attachments of the approval request (`attachments.attach`, subject `approval_request`). Both subjects register ONE lifecycle, in `contracts/events.py`: `on_approved` calls `approvals.subjects.apply_event_submission(…, check=events.check_stored)` and then `holds.compute`. The kernel function takes the submission, group and contract locks, asserts the fresh basis, refuses stored Step 1 events and, before it appends, calls `check` with the locked contract row and the events; `check_stored` runs the route's validation again on the stream as it stands and raises `approvals.engine.StaleBasis` on a finding, so `decide` voids the request as stale (DG-KRN-APR-05). A new writer of `event_submission` goes through `_submit`, and a new check of a stored batch goes into `events._check_batch`, which the storing and the appending side share. Rev 1.222 (items EVT-VOID-OWN-COMMANDS-1 and ATTR-SSP-PIN-1; the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-01; 04 §16.3 rev 1.231, "Voids on this route" and the `LINE_ATTRIBUTES_CHANGED` row): an approval is not reached by a lesser route. `events.request_void` stores a void only for a type of `events.VOIDABLE_TYPES` — `RECORDED_TYPES` less the Step 1 assessment, the twelve fact-capture types — and answers every other type with its sentence (`events.void_refusal`; 409 `invalid-transition`); an E-03 type that is on no list is refused. `locks.refuse_version_pin` refuses, on the events route and on its preview, a `LINE_ATTRIBUTES_CHANGED` whose `changes` name `ssp_book_version_id` or `ssp_version_label` (422, `REQ-SSP-006`): the approval of the SSP override command appends that event below the route (`policies.overrides`). `events.check_stored` applies both again to a stored batch, so a submission stored before either rule is voided as stale at its approval. A command that gains an approval of its own takes its event type off `VOIDABLE_TYPES`, and its payload member off the route, in the same change. Rev 1.223 (item EVT-BOUND-AFTER-MOD-1; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01; 04 §16.3 rev 1.232, "The quantity a delivery is checked against"): the delivery bound reads the quantity in force. `events.quantities_in_force` is the one fold — pure, over the contract's live events: the last booking's lines, every `REGROUPED`, and in stream order the `CONTRACT_AMENDED` lines after the booking — and `events._ledger` is its one caller, so `events.check_bounds` gives the route, its preview, `_check_batch` (a stored batch where it is stored and where it is appended), the CSV v2 event imports and the adapters' documents the same quantities. It reads the stream, not `obligation_version`: a group can be marked or its computation deferred when a request arrives. A command that changes an obligation's quantity by a new event type, or by a new member of an existing one, extends the fold in the same change; the legacy progress import keeps its own fold of the same rule (`imports.legacy_v1.progress._amended`). Rev 1.226 (item EVT-USAGE-MANUAL-1; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01; 04 §16.3 rev 1.238): `USAGE_REPORTED` is a member of `events.MANUAL_TYPES` — a usage report of a signed-in person waits as a `MANUAL_EVENT` request like the other five types, and an API client's or an import's is appended as before. Its word in the request summary is "usage" (`events.MANUAL_LABELS`, in E-03 order); it is no member of `events.EVIDENCE_TYPES`, so evidence is offered and not required. `MANUAL_TYPES` stays the one list that the seeds, the performance harness and the answer-key plan read. Rev 1.253 (item EVT-EVIDENCE-1; the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-02; 04 rev 1.268 T-CON-24 "The evidence of a submission"): until its approval the evidence of a submission is the request's attachment. `events._approve_submission` hands `subjects.apply_event_submission` three functions. `before_basis` runs under the submission, group and contract locks and before the basis is read again: `attachments.readable_evidence` locks and reads the files of the request's live attachments (DG-KRN-FILE-08), and a shredded one raises `StaleBasis`. `check` is `check_stored` and then REQ-DAT-014 for a person's event that needs evidence with no readable file left — a 422 that leaves the request pending, whose sentence is written for the approver who reads it (`EVIDENCE_GONE`). `applied` runs in the SYSTEM unit of work that appended: `events._attach_to_events` attaches every readable file to every appended event (`attachments.attach_evidence`, T-PLT-30 subject `contract_event`). `record_events` calls `_attach_to_events` for a direct append, in the caller's unit of work. `attach_evidence` is the one write of an attachment below `POST /attachments`: a command calls it only where it has authorised its caller for the subjects and the file, and it writes one AUD-FACT event per file. A channel that appends events for a caller who sent evidence calls `_attach_to_events` in the same unit of work. Rev 1.254 (item MANUAL-EVENT-PREPARER-SCOPE-1): the lifecycle this module registers for both subjects states `preparer_entities` (DG-KRN-APR-07) — the preparer of an event submission is held to the contracting entity of the contract she records the events on, read from the stored submission and never from the caller. Rev 1.296 (item USAGE-REPORT-PERIOD-ENDED-1; 04 §16.3 "The usage period of a report", rev 1.320; PRD IMP-148): `events.check_bounds` also holds the usage period of a report. `usage_period_refusal(start, end, effective)` is the pure rule — the sentence for a period that ends after the event's effective date, nothing for one that has ended by it, equal dates included — and `_period_finding` its finding under `USAGE_PERIOD_NOT_ENDED` at `events.<n>.payload.usage_period_end`. It stands in `check_bounds` and neither in `to_events` nor in the payload model: `check_bounds` is the one function every channel passes (the route, a person's submission, the previews, the CSV templates, the integration documents) and `check_stored` passes it again at the approval that appends a stored request, while `UsageReportedV1` cannot see its event's date and also parses stored payloads. `imports.csv_v2.usage.cross_findings` states the same finding per row at validation, from the row's own dates. A new caller of `append_events` that carries a usage report passes `check_bounds` first. |
| DG-KRN-EVT-03 | Payload models: `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)`; money fields `MoneyIn`; decimal fields `DecimalStr`; no personal data beyond ids (REQ-SEC-007). A payload change creates `<Name>V<n+1>` plus an `upcast` step; stored events are never rewritten. **Additive optional member (lane ENG-T1F, Codex T1F2-MEMO-R1, rev 1.27):** an added member with a null default is NOT a payload change under this rule when (i) its absence leaves every existing reading of the stored body unchanged, (ii) no existing member changes meaning, and (iii) no upcast could derive it from the stored body — an upcast would have to invent intent the body does not carry, which is exactly what "never rewritten" protects. Such a member is registered in 04 §16.3 with its absence semantics stated in the governing rule (the first: `MEMO_UPDATED.named`, ENGINE_SPEC CV-47 (a)); stored bytes and payload hashes are untouched; a member that fails any of (i)–(iii) still takes `<Name>V<n+1>` + `upcast`. **Exact opening amounts (lane ENG-C6, D-98 candidate 127 revision 1, rev 1.55):** exactly the eight money members of an `OPENING_BALANCE_ESTABLISHED` obligation (`OpeningObligationV2`: `revenue_cum`, `billed_cum`, `catch_up_cum`, `pre_standard_revenue_cum`, `remaining_allocation`, `remaining_billing`, `position_obligation`, `netting_reclass_amount`) are `ExactMoneyIn` — API-S-ExactMoney (04 rev 1.61 §16.0): the `{amount, currency}` shape with `amount` a `DecimalStr`, exact at input admission and transport (never quantized there; refused by name, API-C-06, outside the 20 / 18 digit bound). Every other payload money field stays `MoneyIn`; the fair-value and deposit members stay `MoneyIn` with their validators; ENGINE_SPEC S07-R-04's posted allocation / baseline rounding is unchanged; the version-2 registration took the `<Name>V<n+1>` + `upcast` path above (stored version-1 bodies and hashes untouched). |
| DG-KRN-EVT-04 | `enqueue` inserts `outbox_message` with `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, topic, dedupe_key) DO NOTHING` and registers an after-commit deferral of `OUTBOX_RELAY`. Messages are guaranteed to be sent only if the transaction commits (research 06 §14.5). |
| DG-KRN-EVT-05 | `relay` selects due messages (`status IN ('PENDING','FAILED') AND next_attempt_at <= now()`) `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, sets `DISPATCHING`, commits, dispatches outside the row transaction, then records `DISPATCHED`, or `FAILED` with backoff 30 s × 2^attempt capped at 1 hour. After 10 failed attempts the message becomes `DEAD`, and `JOURNAL_EXPORT` messages raise notification `EXPORT_FAILED` and an exception item. Handlers must be idempotent: journal exports use `journal_batch.external_id` (REQ-JE-012). Rev 1.110 (BUILD_SPEC CLO-14; security finding SC-N1; rulings R-32, R-71, R-75): a handler whose effect cannot be taken back decides on domain state it re-reads under the row locks of the commands that change that state — after the relay's committed claim and in a transaction of its own that ends before any network call — and the command that must not cross a dispatch reads the claim under the same locks. `JOURNAL_EXPORT` re-reads its batch under the run and batch locks (`export._locked_batch`); `commands.cancel_run` answers 409 while `export.dispatching` finds a message of the run `DISPATCHING`, whatever the age of its claim — the relay that takes a stranded message again completes the dispatch. The `JOURNAL_EXPORT` schedule is ADP-12 (8 attempts, `outbox.SCHEDULES`); its handler records the refused batch itself — `failed` through `exported` in one transaction, the `REJECTED` receipt, the exception item `JOURNAL_EXPORT_FAILED`, `EXPORT_FAILED` and the CTL-021 execution (`export._record_failure`) — for a `Permanent` error and for the last failed attempt, then re-raises so the relay settles the message `DEAD`. Rev 1.127 (supervisor ruling R-108 (b) (5); 04 T-INT-03 rev 1.144): recording `DISPATCHED` sets `last_error` to null; `attempt_count` keeps how often delivery failed before. Rev 1.128 (BUILD_SPEC CLO-15; 05 ADP-12): a handler error that carries `retry_after` seconds — the `Retry-After` an ERP stated with a 429 or 503 (`ports.Transient`) — moves the next attempt to the later of the schedule's wait and that wait (`outbox._dispatch`). The GL adapter of a batch is built per dispatch by `ports.gl_adapter_for` from the batch's adapter literal and a `GLContext` that carries the workspace code, the entity's chart and — for an ERP adapter — the `base_url` and non-secret `config` of the batch's `integration_connection`, read at the dispatch (`export._connection_of`); `worker.build_runtime` registers the NetSuite and QuickBooks Online factories over the SAR-15 client factory, tests register theirs over the in-process mocks. The journal export handler compares what it is about to send with what was approved (`export.recount`; item JRN-DISPATCH-RECOUNT-1, security finding N2 (a)): the chunk's line count and its four totals against the batch row read under the dispatch's locks, a difference raising `Permanent` before the adapter is built — a handler that sends stored rows re-derives the figures its approval covered rather than trusting the rows. Rev 1.136 (supervisor ruling R-110; item JE-CSV-FUNCTIONAL-1; 05 ADP-10 rev 1.92): what leaves the product states both amounts of a journal line. The payload builders of the two ERP adapters (`adapters/gl/netsuite.py`, `adapters/gl/quickbooks.py` `journal_body`) state a chunk in `JournalChunk.functional_currency` with `ChunkLine.debit_functional` / `credit_functional`, and the transaction currency and amounts as informational members when the two currencies differ; `export.render_csv` writes the transaction and the functional pair, `export.render_manifest` both totals. No builder converts an amount: a chunk line carries both. Rev 1.142 (item JRN-DISPATCH-DEAD-1; supervisor rulings R-118 (k) and R-119 (c); 05 ADP-31, ADP-32 rev 1.98): `last_error` and the relay's log line keep `outbox.error_name(error)` — the slug of a `Problem`, else the class; never the message. A topic may register `outbox.DEAD_HOOKS[topic]`: the relay calls it with the job context, the payload and the error when a message of the topic dies, before it records `DEAD`. A hook that raises leaves the message `DISPATCHING` with the attempt uncounted (log `outbox.dead_hook_failed`), and the relay that takes it again after 15 minutes dispatches it as the last attempt once more. `JOURNAL_EXPORT` registers `export.batch_died`, the one place a batch is recorded `failed`; the dispatch handler raises and records no failure itself. Rev 1.206 (item DEPLOY-ALERT-NAMES-1; 05 DPL-37 rev 1.162): the relay's line `outbox.dispatch_failed` (WARNING) is written once the outcome of the failed dispatch is known and carries `outcome`, what this relay recorded for the message: `FAILED` — a next attempt is scheduled; `DEAD` — the last attempt, recorded after the topic's dead hook returned; `UNSETTLED` (`outbox.UNSETTLED`) — nothing was recorded: the dead hook raised and the message stays `DISPATCHING` (the hook's own line `outbox.dead_hook_failed` precedes it), a later relay had taken the message, or the recording itself raised. A message is therefore called dead by exactly one line, and the hosted SLO-05 alert matches that line. |
| DG-KRN-EVT-06 | `notify` respects `notification_preference`. Email goes through topic `EMAIL` to the SMTP adapter, which is the fake adapter in dev, test and e2e (REQ-PLT-021, docs/02-PRD.md WLD-U-R4). An email whose link carries a secret names the token in `link_token` and keeps the place `{token}` in `link_path`; `outbox.email_link_path(payload, keyring)` completes it at dispatch with `KeyRing.link_token(purpose, reference, key_id=…)` — HMAC-SHA256 under the `security-hmac:<n>` key over `b"erev-link-token-v1"`, the purpose and the reference's 16 bytes, as 43 URL-safe characters. No payload holds a token (rev 1.134; 05 NTR-04, KEY-03). In a sandbox `notify` enqueues no `EMAIL`: a notification raised there is delivered in the app only, the mandatory kind included (05 SBX-08; rev 1.160). Rev 1.250 (items NOTIFY-ROLE-HOLDERS-SCOPE-1 and NOTIFY-DELEGATE-SCOPE-1; 05 NTR-02 rev 1.180): the two readers of recipients take the subject's scope. `role_holders(session, role_codes=, entity_id=, at=)` and `permission_holders(session, permission=, entity_id=, at=)` answer the memberships whose assignments cover the subject — an assignment for all entities or one that names `entity_id`; for a subject of the whole workspace, `entity_id` None, an assignment for all entities alone — and `entity_id` is a keyword no call can leave out. `permission_holders`, which `notify_permission_holders` reads, adds the delegates of those holders whose delegation names the permission and whose own entity scope covers the same subject (`entity_scope_covering`; supervisor ruling R-41 (1): a delegation conveys the permission, not the view), as `permission_holders_covering` does for an approval request. Until this revision every delegate of a holder was told — a delegate without the entity of a failed close run read "Job failed: Close run" (PRD NTF-05) — and a subject without an entity went to every holder of the permission, whatever entities the role named. |
| DG-KRN-EVT-07 | `emit_webhook` inserts one `webhook_delivery` per active subscribed endpoint and enqueues topic `WEBHOOK`. Deliveries are signed with HMAC-SHA256 in header `X-Erev-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` over `"<t>." + body`, with retries per T-PLT-36 (REQ-PLT-034). Rev 1.110 (ruling R-75 (c)): an emitter calls it in the unit of work that writes the state the event names, so the delivery exists exactly when the state does; the first emitters are `domain/journals/export.py` (`journal_batch.exported`, `journal_batch.acknowledged`). The other four kinds have no emitter yet (item WEBHOOK-EMIT-1). |
| DG-KRN-EVT-08 | **Step 1 status events (rev 1.88; supervisor ruling R-20 on security findings SN-13 / SN-12; 04 rev 1.105 §16.1, §16.3, §16.10; PRD SM-02 rev 1.34).** ENGINE_SPEC Table 2.2-A makes a book's status a function of the events, so the platform controls who appends the events that move it, and the engine is not changed. (1) `CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` and `CONTRACT_ACTIVATED` are appended by `activation.activate` alone — the approved `CONTRACT_ACTIVATION` request, the consumed import composition (BR-DAT-06) or the BS3-D-19 SYSTEM path; `events.refuse_activation_events` refuses them on `POST /contracts/{id}/events` and its preview (409), and the migration capture is the one other writer of `CONTRACT_ACTIVATED` (origin MIGRATION). This supersedes the direct append of `CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` of decision L4-1-Q-10. (2) The not-a-contract gate of L4-1-Q-10 — the `CONTRACT_ACTIVATED` the events route appends behind a not-probable assessment of a DRAFT contract — is narrowed: `events.step1_events` adds it only when `step1.every_book_not_probable` holds for the enabled books of the contracting entity with the request's events applied, and keeps it only when the dry run of the batch gives the contract NOT_A_CONTRACT in every book the group is computed in, each an enabled book of the contracting entity (`events._confirmed`; a group over the obligation budget or an `EngineError` confirms nothing). Every path that records events for a caller validates through `step1_events` (the events route, the CSV v2 recorded-events import); `header_projection` moves a DRAFT header to NOT_A_CONTRACT only for the assessment with the gate right behind it. (3) `events/step1.py` is the ONE reader of the Step 1 state of a stream: the events route, the activation checklist and command, and the `CONTRACT_ACTIVATION` subject content (`approvals.subjects.contract_activation_content`) call it, so the books an activation moves are the books its request hashed (REQ-PLT-014). (4) The criteria-met activation: `activation.activate` of a stored NOT_A_CONTRACT contract appends the `CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` events (stored NOT_A_CONTRACT → PENDING_REVIEW), then `CONTRACT_ACTIVATED` dated the latest criteria-met date (PENDING_REVIEW → ACTIVE) — two `append_events` calls, because DB-03 holds those two pairs and no pair NOT_A_CONTRACT → ACTIVE; each append audits its status change (DG-SM-03), so the trail shows `contract.pending_review` at the submission (the read-model move, L4-1-Q-18) and again, with `contract.active`, at the approval. A rejected or voided request audits `contract.not_a_contract`. (5) `events.request_void` refuses a `COLLECTIBILITY_ASSESSED`, a `CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` and a `CONTRACT_ACTIVATED`, and an assessment does not ride in an `ATTRIBUTE_CHANGE` submission: both paths would apply an event that Table 2.2-A reads under an approval that is not the activation's. **Rev 1.109 (supervisor rulings R-77 and R-80; independent review of the fix).** (6) Dates: Table 2.2-A reads the events in ENG-06 order, so `events.step1_outcome` refuses, once the stream holds a `CONTRACT_ACTIVATED`, an assessment dated before `step1.latest_date(dated, book)` and a `SIGNIFICANT_CHANGE_FLAGGED` dated before `step1.latest_date(dated, None)`, and in every status either of them dated after the later of the contracting entity's current date (05 TZ-03) and the contract's inception date (supervisor ruling R-84 (a)); for a DRAFT contract `activation.step1_record` requires `step1.current_at(stream, book, inception_date)` for every enabled book, because the activation event is dated the inception date. (7) Records are read with their facts by every reader — `step1.records` and `step1.serves` / `step1.reviewed` (contract, topic, book): the events route, the checklist and `step1.criteria_met`, which also requires topic COLLECTIBILITY and T-CON-19 `reviewed_at` later than the gate event's `created_at` (both are the unit of work's clock, so they compare; the event's `recorded_at` is the database's clock). (8) `step1_outcome` returns what became of the gate (`events.Step1Gate`: `appended` and the reason code `enums.Step1GateReason`, 04 E-132 — no message, the copy is the screen's; ruling R-84 (b)): the 201 body and the audit detail of `record_events` carry it, a deferred computation carries it in the job's result (`compute_job.defer_compute(result=…)`), and the preview job decides the gate as the append does (`lock = False`: it appends nothing). (9) An activation is not offered to the auto-approval rules when it carries criteria-met books or leaves a book NOT_A_CONTRACT (`activation.books_left_not_a_contract`); the condition sits at the `approvals.submit` call and `submit_activation` passes no routing decision of its own. (10) `combination._gated_member_errors` refuses a gated contract that would be computed in a book its entity does not keep — at create, at submit and in `apply_combination` under its locks; the books of the would-be group are those of each member's current bundle (`bundles.build`). **Rev 1.133 (supervisor ruling R-102).** (11) A Step 1 judgement is made on the booking it judges: `commands.replace_draft` voids, in the SYSTEM append that voids the earlier booking, every assessment `step1.read` finds standing (`Assessment.event_id`), and `events._step1_errors` refuses a record whose `reviewed_at` is earlier than `Step1Stream.booked_at` — the `created_at` of the latest standing `CONTRACT_BOOKED`. The comparison is not strict: the legacy composer reviews its record in the transaction that books. (12) An assessment cites a `REVIEWED` record on every channel (`_step1_errors`); the staleness basis of a `JUDGEMENT_RECORD` request (`approvals.subjects.judgement_record_subject_content`) stays whole. (13) The criteria-met path of a book under an ACTIVE header. `step1.read` replays the Step 1 part of Table 2.2-A per book over the stream in ENG-06 order and answers `Step1Stream.out`: per book, the event that put it out as not probable and still holds — the activation event that read a not-probable assessment of the book, or the not-probable re-assessment that followed a `SIGNIFICANT_CHANGE_FLAGGED` — until a `CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` of the book. `step1.criteria_met` answers, for a stored NOT_A_CONTRACT and a stored ACTIVE contract alike, the enabled books that are out and whose latest assessment is probable on a `COLLECTIBILITY` record reviewed after that event was recorded; `_step1_errors` refuses early, per book, what could never serve. The replay reads Step 1 events only and the engine decides: for an ACTIVE contract `activation.submit_activation` and `activation.activate` confirm each book from the dry run's status trace (formula `step1.status.v1`, measure `status@<event key>`): the node of the pending `CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` has reason `CRITERIA_MET`, and the segment before it is NOT_A_CONTRACT with reason `NOT_PROBABLE`, begun by the replay's event. Otherwise they refuse — by name when the segment has another reason (`STEP1_REENTRY_OTHER_REASON`, 04 table 15.4-I). `activate` then appends the `CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` events alone; `header_projection` moves nothing from ACTIVE, and `queries._read_status` leaves ACTIVE as it is while the request is pending. (14) The five criteria (supervisor rulings R-113 (f), R-115 (f); 04 T-CON-19): `schemas.db_json.Step1Criteria` is the shape of `questionnaire.criteria` for the topics COLLECTIBILITY and NOT_A_CONTRACT; `policies.judgements.step1_criteria_errors` holds (e) to the topic and (d) to the contract's `has_commercial_substance` at every write and requires all five at submission (422, rule T-CON-19). `step1.Record.criteria` carries the answers to every reader and `step1.unmet` names the criteria a record answers No to — (a), (b), (c), and (d) too for a criteria-met re-assessment, where the engine does not test commercial substance again, and (e) for a probable assessment (rev 1.192; 04 §16.3 (b) rev 1.209 — `step1.PROBABLE_TOPICS` is `COLLECTIBILITY` alone): `_step1_errors` refuses a probable assessment on such a record, `step1.criteria_met` moves no book on it, and `activation.step1_record` fails by name (`step1.CRITERION_NOT_MET`, PRD IMP-135) for any enabled book whose latest assessment rests on one. A record without `criteria` — the legacy composer's, written below the route — is not read for them. (15) The newest review (rev 1.271; item STEP1-CITE-LATEST-1; 04 §16.3 (b), T-CON-19 "Overtaken" rev 1.285): `step1.overtaken` answers, for REVIEWED records of the two Step 1 topics, the record of the OTHER topic — same subject, same book as SM-10 reads it — that was reviewed after each, by `step1.newer` (the later `reviewed_at`; on one instant the higher judgement number). It is the one reader for every place that asks: `_step1_errors` refuses an assessment on an overtaken record behind its three earlier findings and names the record that overtook it; `activation.step1_record` fails by name (`STEP1_RECORD_OVERTAKEN`, PRD IMP-143) for a book whose latest assessment rests on one, because a record can be overtaken after its assessment; `step1.criteria_met` moves no book on one, so the content of a criteria-met request that waits changes and its decision is stale (DG-KRN-APR-05); and `policies.judgements.judgement_outs` derives `overtaken_by` from it. `Standing.flagged_at` is the time the standing flag was recorded: a PROBABLE assessment that answers a flag is refused on a record reviewed before it (not strict), and on every record when the flag is of the same request (`flagged` without `flagged_at`); a not-probable assessment is bound by "newest" alone. (16) The reading at a record cutoff (rev 1.271; item RPT-BRIDGE-STEP1-CHAIN-1): `step1.read(..., recorded_by=...)` reads the events whose `created_at` is at or before the cutoff, and a void only when the `EVENT_VOIDED` itself was recorded by then — the contract's own Step 1 per book as it stood, whatever group computed it. A report run binds nothing more of the stream than its cutoff; one thing can change a reading afterwards: a row stamped at or before the cutoff by a unit of work that committed later. Witnesses: `tests/domain/contracts/test_step1.py`, `tests/domain/contracts/test_activation.py`, `tests/unit/events/test_step1_readers.py`. |

### 5.12 Jobs (KRN-JOB)

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/jobs/registry.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RetryPolicy:
    max_attempts: int = 1
    backoff_seconds: tuple[int, ...] = (30, 120, 600)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class JobOutcome:
    state: Literal["SUCCEEDED", "SUCCEEDED_WITH_EXCEPTIONS"]
    result: Mapping[str, Any]                               # {"href": "/api/v1/…", "counts": {…}}

Handler = Callable[["JobContext", Mapping[str, Any]], JobOutcome]

QueueName = Literal["compute", "imports", "close", "outbox", "reports", "maintenance", "integrations", "ai"]   # rev 1.1
QUEUES: Final[tuple[QueueName, ...]]                        # the eight names above, in this order (05 §5.6)
JOB_QUEUE: Final[Mapping[JobKind, QueueName]]               # one entry per E-14 value (DG-KRN-JOB-10)

def task(kind: JobKind, *, retry: RetryPolicy = RetryPolicy()) -> Callable[[Handler], Handler]: ...   # queue = JOB_QUEUE[kind]
def defer(uow: UnitOfWork, kind: JobKind, params: Mapping[str, Any], *, priority: int = 0,
          parent_job_id: UUID | None = None) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
def run_inline(kind: JobKind, params: Mapping[str, Any], *, tenant_id: UUID, principal: Principal,
               clock: Clock) -> JobOutcome: ...

# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/jobs/context.py
class JobContext:
    job_id: UUID
    tenant_id: UUID
    kind: JobKind
    principal: Principal
    clock: Clock
    def unit_of_work(self) -> AbstractContextManager[UnitOfWork]: ...
    def read_session(self) -> AbstractContextManager[Session]: ...
    def progress(self, done: int, total: int | None) -> None: ...
    def heartbeat(self) -> None: ...
    def cancel_requested(self) -> bool: ...

# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/worker.py
app: Final[procrastinate.App]
def main(*, queues: Sequence[QueueName] = QUEUES, heartbeat_file: Path) -> None: ...   # all queues by default (DG-KRN-JOB-11)
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-JOB-01 | There is exactly one registered handler per E-14 `job_kind`; DG-ARC-08 checks completeness. |
| DG-KRN-JOB-02 | `defer` inserts `job` (`state = 'QUEUED'`, `params`, `queue`, `priority`, `parent_job_id`) in the business transaction and registers an after-commit hook. The hook defers Procrastinate task `erev.run_job(job_id, tenant_id)` with `queueing_lock = str(job_id)` and records `procrastinate_job_id` in a short transaction. Rev 1.89 (04 T-PLT-27; supervisor ruling R-50 (a)): in the same business transaction `defer` buffers `job.start` through `uow.audit` — the unit of work's principal and request id, `after` without `params` — for every kind outside `TRANSPORT_KINDS` (`OUTBOX_RELAY`, `EMAIL_DELIVERY`, `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY`). The scheduler fan-out (`defer_for_active_tenants`, `defer_for_due_tenants`) holds no unit of work: it appends `job.start` as SYSTEM under the sweep's request id as the last statement of the tenant transaction that inserted and dispatched the job, so the audit chain head stays the last lock (DG-KRN-DB-08). A tenant whose transaction fails — its chain cannot take the event, for example — gets no job (the insert and the dispatch roll back with the event) and is logged `job.fan_out_failed` at error level; the fan-out continues with the next tenant, so one tenant never stops the others. Rev 1.183: the event carries the class of the exception and the place it was raised (`error_class`, `error_at`; DG-KRN-JOB-06), never its message. `domain.platform.jobs.cancel_job` writes `job.cancel` when it changes the job. No handler writes any of the three actions. |
| DG-KRN-JOB-03 | `erev.run_job` opens a tenant transaction and moves the job QUEUED → RUNNING by conditional update; zero rows (cancelled or already running) → return. It then acquires one of N per-tenant slots with `pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtextextended('erev-job:' \|\| tenant_id \|\| ':' \|\| k, 0))` for k = 0 … N − 1, where N = registry setting `platform.job_concurrency` (default 4). Rev 1.2 (05 JOB-03, OQ-ARC-14): a job whose `parent_job_id` names a `CLOSE_RUN` job in state `RUNNING` acquires and releases no slot, because the parent holds a slot while it polls its children (05 RCP-19) and `platform.job_concurrency = 1` would otherwise deadlock; a child whose parent is in any other state acquires a slot as usual. If no slot is free, it returns the job to QUEUED and re-defers with a 5-second delay. It runs the handler, writes the final state, `result` or `problem`, releases the slot and, on FAILED, notifies `JOB_FAILED` (REQ-PLT-029). Rev 1.117 (05 RCP-19 rev 1.73): the close-run job takes over a child that no worker has started by its second poll — it moves the child `QUEUED` → `CANCELLED` and computes the chunk in its own units of work — so a later delivery of the child's task returns at the state check. |
| DG-KRN-JOB-04 | Handlers are idempotent and chunked. Each chunk (one combination group, or at most 100 rows of set-based work) uses its own `jc.unit_of_work()`. Handlers report progress at most every 2 seconds and check `cancel_requested()` between chunks; when they owe a heartbeat is stated below (rev 1.266). A contract that fails is quarantined through an exception item while the job continues, ending `SUCCEEDED_WITH_EXCEPTIONS` (REQ-CLS-013). Rev 1.266 (item JOB-STALL-COMMIT-RACE-1; 05 JOB-04, JOB-06 rev 1.200). **The beat.** The sentence "heartbeat at least every 30 seconds" stood here and no handler was held to it: seven kinds are one unit of work and never beat, four are silent for one long stretch. What holds: a handler owes a beat for the time it spends OUTSIDE a transaction. Inside a unit of work it owes none — its job is not stopped while the transaction is open, and the commit writes the heartbeat. Outside one — an adapter's call, a fetch, a computation between two units of work — the sweeper stops the job after ten minutes without a beat, so a handler whose work outside a transaction can last that long calls `jc.heartbeat()` or `jc.progress()` there. A beat is the attempt's: `JobContext` writes it through `JobAttempt.beat`, which updates the job only while it is `RUNNING` under the attempt's task and raises `JobLost` otherwise. **The door.** A handler opens a transaction that writes in one of three ways. (a) `jc.unit_of_work()`. (b) `system_unit_of_work(jc.runtime, principal, …)` for another principal of the workspace (the migration import, the sync) or for another workspace (a sandbox load, a sandbox reset, the period replay). (c) Any other session — a platform-scope transaction, a copy step — whose first statement is `jc.enlist(session)`. (a) and (b) are units of work of the attempt (DG-KRN-UOW-04): in the job's own workspace `JobAttempt.enter` takes the job's lock, reads the job's row and registers the heartbeat as the unit's before-commit step (DG-KRN-UOW-02); in another workspace it does what (c) does — `JobAttempt.enlist`: the lock on the transaction's own connection, then the heartbeat in the job's workspace in a transaction of its own, lock first, so that a settlement under way is waited for before the beat reads the job. Each of them raises `JobLost` when the job is no longer the attempt's. The attempt (`JobAttempt`: the job, its workspace, the Procrastinate task) is made in one place, where the registry runs a handler, and travels in the runtime the handler is given (`JobRuntime.attempt`); the worker's own runtime carries none, and a `JobContext` with a job row cannot be built without one. A handler does not catch `JobLost` to go on — every later beat and door refuses again — and the registry ends such an attempt with the log line `job.attempt_lost` (warning: job, kind, attempt) and records nothing for it. **The list.** `backend/tests/unit/test_job_unit_doors.py` reads every function that is handed a job context or a job runtime, and the functions nested in them, outside the kernel: a transaction that can write and is opened without (a) or (b) passes (c) or stands in the test's closed list with what it rests on instead — the relay's and the deliveries' claims and records, which their record's own claim stamp fences (DG-KRN-EVT-05), the relay's read of a journal batch, and the directory reads of the worker's periodic tasks, which run under no job. A function that opens a transaction without being handed either is not seen by the scan. |
| DG-KRN-JOB-05 | Retries use Procrastinate retry with `RetryPolicy`. After the last attempt the job is FAILED with an RFC 9457 `problem`, notification `JOB_FAILED` and, for close runs, a close-cockpit blocker exception item (REQ-OPS-006, CTL-040). Rev 1.89 (04 T-PLT-27; supervisor ruling R-50 (a)): the transaction that records a terminal state also writes `job.finish` as SYSTEM under request id `job-<id>` with the state and the slug of the problem — the failing unit of work through `uow.audit`, the handler's final transition by an append that is the last statement of its transaction (DG-KRN-DB-08) — and only when the transition itself was applied, so a stale attempt (D-80) writes nothing. A retry (`RUNNING` → `QUEUED`) writes nothing. Rev 1.117 (05 JOB-07 rev 1.73): the close-run item is `CLOSE_RUN_FAILED` (04 §15.4); it is raised by the `on_failure` hook of the `CLOSE_RUN` handler (`domain/close/close_runs.close_failed`), which runs in the transaction that ends the job `FAILED`, records the run and its step `FAILED` and notifies the holders of `period.lock` for the entity; the kernel's own `JOB_FAILED` goes to the initiator. Rev 1.142 (item JRN-FAILED-CANCEL-1; 05 §5.6 rev 1.98): every error a handler raises is retried while attempts remain, whatever its class. A handler of a retried kind therefore raises only what another attempt can cure and RETURNS a decision that is final: the `JOURNAL_EXPORT` job in mode `CANCEL` or `HAND_OVER` ends `SUCCEEDED_WITH_EXCEPTIONS` with the refusal as a problem object in `result.refusal` (`export.Refused`), after it committed what the ledger said; an unreachable ledger is raised and retried. Rev 1.212 (item JOB-FAILED-ITEM-1; 05 JOB-07 rev 1.165): `_fail_job` is the one place a job ends `FAILED`. In its transaction, after the notification of a user initiator and the kind's `on_failure` hook, it raises the exception item `JOB_FAILED` when the kind's handler registered `task(…, failed_item=job_items.failed_item(source, reader))`: `reader(session, subject_type, subject_id, params)` reads the job's record and returns a `FailedSubject` — the legal entity, the period where the record has one, the record for the queue's links, and `key`, the record's business key where the job's subject id is not what a later job of the kind works on again (a journal run or a reconciliation that the job itself creates; a sync run of a connection) — or None when the record names no entity or several, and then nothing is raised. The registry cannot import the exception queue (DG-ARC-01): `domain.imports.job_items.failed_item` puts the queue's three functions — raise the item, say whether one is open, settle it — into the `FailedItem`, so a kind that has a reader has them and no registration order matters. The hook and the item each run in a savepoint of the unit of work (`uow.savepoint()`, DG-KRN-UOW-03): a failure is logged (`job.failure_hook_failed`; `job.failed_item_failed` with the exception's class and place), what it wrote and what it buffered in the unit of work — an audit event, an after-commit hook — is dropped, and the job still ends `FAILED`. Until this revision the hook's savepoint was the session's, so a hook that failed after `uow.audit` left its event to be written for rows that were rolled back. After the commit `_fail_job` raises the operator alert `JOB_FAILED` through `runtime.alerts` for a job whose initiator is not a user; a runtime without sinks (tests, `run_inline`) raises none, and a failure to raise is logged `job.failed_alert_failed`. A job that ends `SUCCEEDED` or `SUCCEEDED_WITH_EXCEPTIONS` settles the open item of its kind and record (`_settle_failed_item`): the reader and one probe of `ux_exception_item__open` first, a unit of work of its own only when an item is open; a failure is logged `job.failed_item_unsettled`. A new job kind whose record belongs to a legal entity registers its reader; a kind that raises an item of its own in its failure hook registers none (`tests/unit/test_job_failed_kinds.py` holds the list). Rev 1.233 (item JRN-EXIT-JOB-IDEMPOTENT-1; 05 §5.6 rev 1.174; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01 on review finding F10): a handler's return and the record of the job's end are two transactions (`registry._execute`), so a returned decision can be run again — the worker stops between them, the job stays `RUNNING`, and the sweeper queues the stalled job again while attempts remain. A handler that returns a decision it committed therefore leaves the decision where its job id finds it and looks there first: the two exit modes write `job_id` and the job's `counts` into the decision's audit event — `after` of a `SUCCESS`, `detail` of a `DENIED` — and an attempt that finds the event of its own job returns what it records (`failed_exits._decided`), asking nobody and writing nothing. A decision that left no event is decided again. |
| DG-KRN-JOB-06 | Sweeper (periodic, every 60 s, queue `maintenance`, per tenant through `platform_session("tenant_directory")`): requeues QUEUED jobs with a null `procrastinate_job_id` older than 60 s; fails RUNNING jobs whose `updated_at` is older than 10 minutes with problem detail "no heartbeat for 10 minutes", then retries them per policy. Rev 1.89 (04 T-PLT-27; supervisor ruling R-50 (a)): ending a job FAILED writes `job.finish` to its tenant's audit chain, so each job is settled in isolation — a job whose settlement fails (its tenant's chain cannot take the event, for example) is logged `job.sweep_failed` at error level and the sweep continues with the next job and the next tenant. Rev 1.183 (supervisor ruling of 2026-10-01 on R-118 (k)): `job.fan_out_failed` (DG-KRN-JOB-02) and `job.sweep_failed` carry `error_class` and `error_at` — the module and line of the last frame of `erev_api` or `erev_engine` in the exception's chain, read from its origin (`logging.raised_at`, DG-LOG-03) — and never the exception's message. The error events of the period tick (05 SCH-05 rev 1.139) carry the same two fields, so the three read alike. Rev 1.266 (item JOB-STALL-COMMIT-RACE-1; 05 JOB-06 rev 1.200): the ten-minute rule settles a `RUNNING` job only under the job's advisory lock (`registry.fail_attempt` with `stalled_before`). It asks for `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` on `erev-job-unit:<job id>` first — before the job's row, because a unit of work may hold the row as well: a row it inserted refers to the job — and when a transaction of the job holds the lock it reads the row without a lock, logs `job.sweep_passed_over` at info level with `job_id`, `job_kind`, `attempt` and `silent_seconds`, and leaves the job as it is; so at every pass. With the lock it takes the row `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` as before — a row another transaction holds is skipped without a line, as before — and holds both to its commit. The slug `job-stalled` and the detail "no heartbeat for 10 minutes" are the registry's (`STALL_SLUG`, `STALL_DETAIL`); `registry.job_failed_body` gives the notification's body for that problem (PRD NTF-05 rev 1.191), and the close run's own notice takes it from there. A job whose task never started it carries the same slug with another detail and keeps the general body: no handler ran. |
| DG-KRN-JOB-07 | Periodic schedule (UTC): `AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY` daily 02:00 per tenant; `RETENTION_SWEEP` daily 03:00; `OUTBOX_RELAY` and `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY` safety sweeps every minute. |
| DG-KRN-JOB-08 | The worker writes its heartbeat file every 15 seconds (DG-RUN-02; compose health check). |
| DG-KRN-JOB-09 | Long API operations return 202 with API-S-Job and `Location: /api/v1/jobs/{id}` (API-C-12). `run_inline` executes a handler synchronously with an equivalent `JobContext`; it is used only by the CLI (`erev job run`, `erev perf seed`), the seed, the unmeasured sandbox restore of the perf harness (DG-PERF-02; rev 1.2) and tests. The measured perf close runs through `perf-worker-<n>` processes (DG-PERF-08). |
| DG-KRN-JOB-10 | Queues (rev 1.1; D-75 Q5, B1-009). `JOB_QUEUE` equals the 05 §5.6 execution profile table: `CONTRACT_COMPUTE`, `REPLAY_VERIFY`, `POLICY_SIMULATION` → `compute`; `IMPORT_VALIDATE`, `IMPORT_DIFF`, `IMPORT_COMMIT`, `MIGRATION_IMPORT`, `MIGRATION_RECONCILE` → `imports`; `CLOSE_RUN`, `JOURNAL_RUN_CALCULATE`, `RECONCILIATION_GENERATE` (rev 1.104), `PERIOD_OPEN_REDIRTY` (rev 1.147) → `close`; `JOURNAL_EXPORT`, `OUTBOX_RELAY`, `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY`, `EMAIL_DELIVERY` → `outbox`; `REPORT_RUN`, `EVIDENCE_PACK`, `FORECAST_RUN`, `DEAL_PREVIEW`, `SSP_CALCULATOR` → `reports`; `AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY`, `TENANT_SNAPSHOT`, `SANDBOX_RESET`, `RETENTION_SWEEP` → `maintenance`; `SYNC_RUN` → `integrations`; `AI_TASK` → `ai`. The sweeper and the periodic fan-out tasks (DG-KRN-JOB-06, DG-KRN-JOB-07) use `maintenance`. `defer` writes `job.queue = JOB_QUEUE[kind]`. DG-ARC-08 fails when `JOB_QUEUE` misses an E-14 value or differs from the 05 table. |
| DG-KRN-JOB-11 | Workers consume all eight queues by default: `erev worker` without `--queues` and with `EREV_WORKER_QUEUES` empty calls `main(queues=QUEUES, …)`. `--queues` (a comma-separated list that overrides `EREV_WORKER_QUEUES`) restricts a worker for the hosted split of 05 DPL-31 (`compute,close` and the other six); an unknown name exits 2 with "unknown queue <name>". DG-RUN-02, DG-RUN-05, `make worker` and the perf harness never pass `--queues`. |
| DG-KRN-JOB-12 | Execution token and lock (rev 1.10, 1.11; D-96). `JobContext.task_id` and `JobContext.attempt` expose the execution token of the running Procrastinate task; `dispatch()` gains a `lock` parameter (Procrastinate `lock`: no two jobs with the same string run simultaneously — the operative serialisation control, together with the transactional advisory lock below; a `queueing_lock` only deduplicates WAITING jobs and is never the serialisation control), used as `verify:<group id>` for `REPLAY_VERIFY` children; handlers that write immutable per-attempt evidence take `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on the shared-state key in the writing transaction (TXN-05 pattern), bind the row to the token and fence the write on the job row still naming the task (D-80) (D-96). |
| DG-KRN-JOB-13 | Release identity (05 REL-05; D-80; rev 1.8). `insert_job` records the process's stamped release (`erev_api.controls.release.current_release()`, set by `stamp_release` at api and worker startup) as `params.engine_release_id` on every enqueue path, children included; the key is reserved and a caller that supplies it is refused (`ValueError`), so tests stamp through `remember_release`. Handlers and failure hooks receive the caller's params only (`handler_params`). `run_job` classifies the pin against `JobRuntime.engine_release` (the worker keeps the release it stamped): `match` runs; `mismatch` and `unpinned` (a job with no key, queued before REL-05 or by an unstamped process, is never assumed compatible) re-defer for 30 seconds with `release_mismatch_deferrals + 1` in the Procrastinate task arguments (`job.params` never changes after insert) and the eleventh delivery moves the job QUEUED → RUNNING → FAILED in one transaction with problem `release-mismatch` (503, detail naming the enqueuing release or the missing pin) and the `JOB_FAILED` notification; `malformed` (a key that is not a release id) fails at once with `validation-failed` (422, `errors[0].field` `params.engine_release_id`, `rule_id` REL-05); `unverified` (a runtime without a stamped release: tests, `run_inline`) runs and logs `job.release_unverified`. Nothing runs under the wrong release. The worker task `erev.run_job` runs with `pass_context=True` and hands the delivered Procrastinate task (`context.job.id`) to `registry.run_job(delivered_task_id=…)`, which compares it with the locked row's pointer at entry: a delivery whose task a successor already replaced is stale and returns before any slot, transition, dispatch or handler (log `job.stale_delivery`), whatever the worker's release; delivery ownership is never derived from the current pointer (only tests and inline callers omit the id and stand for the current task). Every later re-dispatch (release mismatch, SPEC-Q-162 slot contention, the sweeper's replacement of a stranded task) is fenced on that delivered task: it happens only while the row is still QUEUED under it (`_redispatch_if_owner`), so a pointer change after the first read creates no task and replaces no pointer; and it carries the deferral count, so capacity or recovery never resets the ten-deferral budget (a handler that ran and failed restarts it through the retry policy). Log events `job.release_mismatch_deferred`, `job.release_mismatch`, `job.release_pin_malformed` carry `enqueuer_release_id`, `worker_release_id` and `release_mismatch_deferrals`. Consumer stamping (rev 1.25; D-96; lane P5): `computation.persist()`, `compute_job`, `journals.summarise` and `reports.framework` obtain the `engine_release_id` they write from `erev_api.controls.stamping.process_release_id(current_release(), env=current_environment(), engine_version=…, latest_for_version=…)` — the process's own row, with the environment `stamp_release` recorded; a stamped row whose `engine_version` differs from the output's is refused (`release-mismatch`); a process without a stamped release fails closed unless the remembered environment is explicitly `dev` or `test`, where it falls back to the latest row of the running engine version and logs `release.stamp_fallback` (WARN); an unknown, unremembered or `e2e` environment fails closed like `production` — no e2e fallback, by design (D-98 60). The environment is recorded at the entrypoint boundary — `stamp_release` (api lifespan, worker start, `erev seed`) and `cli_services()` for every CLI command — so domain code never reads `get_settings()` for this (DG-KRN-CFG-01). |

class LocalFileStore:                                        # root = settings.file_root

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-FILE-01 | `store_file` validates size and media type per purpose (T-PLT-29 limits; REQ-SEC-012: `.xlsm`, `.xlsb` and archives rejected; an `.xlsx` must be a ZIP containing `[Content_Types].xml` and no `vbaProject.bin`). It computes SHA-256 while streaming, writes to `<root>/.incoming/<uuid>` and renames atomically to `<root>/<tenant_id>/<purpose>/<sha256>`. It returns the existing row when `(tenant_id, sha256, purpose)` already exists and is not shredded; a shredded row is refused by name, 409 `invalid-transition` / `FILE_SHREDDED` — 04 T-PLT-29 rev 1.73 (rev 1.63; D-98 145 Amendment 2). |
| DG-KRN-FILE-02 | Files are immutable. There is no delete path; retention flags change only through retention commands (T-PLT-29). |
| DG-KRN-FILE-03 | Downloads stream with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and the stored media type. `attachments.file_content` (`GET /files/{id}/content`) writes the `file.download` audit event through `audit.record_now` before it returns the bytes, and through `audit.record_denied` (`detail.reason = "not-readable"`) before the 404 of a file the caller may not read; an unknown id writes nothing (rev 1.172; 04 T-PLT-29 "Content reads are audited"; ruling R-111 (6)). |
| DG-KRN-FILE-04 | Spreadsheet exports pass every text cell through `erev_api.domain.reports.export_safety.sanitize_cell` (REQ-SEC-011). |
| DG-KRN-FILE-05 | `GcsFileStore` exists as an adapter for production and is never instantiated in tests. |
| DG-KRN-FILE-06 | A command that takes a file id from its caller binds it through `erev_api.domain.platform.file_access.bound(session, ctx, file_id)`: the `file_object` row when the id names a file the caller may read, `None` otherwise. The command answers `None` as it answers a missing file and selects nothing of `file_object` itself, so it looks at no property of a file before the read question is answered; the job that later works on the file reads it as SYSTEM. `FILE_BINDINGS` names every request member that names a file with the function that binds it (rev 1.172; 04 T-PLT-29 Binding; ruling R-111 (1)). |
| DG-KRN-FILE-07 | A command that destroys a stored file is bound to the legal entities of the records that reference it. `file_access.referencing_scopes(tenant_id, file_id)` reads them in a read-only session over every entity: every owner of the read registry, whatever the file's purpose, and every attachment through its subject, voided or not; a record that names no entity, and a file no record references, bind to every entity. An owner with a rule of its own (`grant`) states how its records are found (`referenced`), and the registry refuses an owner that has one without the other. `privacy.refuse_beyond_scope` compares the scopes with the caller's for the command's permission (`entity_scope.covers`), writes the `DENIED` event — the rule, the file's SHA-256 and purpose, the reason; never a record or an entity — and raises; `file.shred` and `file.request_shred` call it after the 404 of an unknown id and before any refusal that names a record, so that a refusal by reference names its record only inside the caller's scope. `tests/architecture/test_file_access.py` holds every evidence reference to be an owner of the read registry, so that no record a refusal names is outside the question (rev 1.211; 04 T-PLT-29 Shred scope; item FILE-SHRED-SCOPE-1, findings B3 and B5). |
| DG-KRN-FILE-08 | A command that counts a stored file as the document a rule asks for, or that can make a record hold it, reads the file through `erev_api.files.store.lock_readable(session, file_ids)`: the `file_object` rows locked `FOR SHARE` in id order to the end of the transaction, and the ids whose `shredded_at` is NULL. It never reads `shredded_at` beside the lock. `file.shred` and the approved shred take the row `FOR UPDATE` before they read the records that hold the file, so the later of the two sees what the earlier committed. The callers: the submission, the deferral request and the approval of a manual adjustment, the submission and the approval of an SSP version, the preparer's sign-off of a reconciliation, `POST /attachments`, and the migration import job before it reads its legacy database — the transaction that reads it moves the batch to `IMPORTING`, from where the batch holds the file (rev 1.248); the import commit locks its source `FOR UPDATE` itself. A share lock is a leaf: a caller takes it after its own record's locks (DG-KRN-DB-08) and takes no other lock after it (rev 1.211; 04 rev 1.216 T-PLT-29 "A document a rule asks for"; finding B2 of the review of the `EVIDENCE_SHRED` merge). Rev 1.253 (item EVT-EVIDENCE-1; 04 rev 1.268): two more callers — the approval of an event submission, for the files of its request's evidence (`attachments.readable_evidence`: after the submission, group and contract locks, before the basis is read again), and `attachments.attach_evidence`, for the file it attaches to events. |
| DG-KRN-FILE-09 | A destruction in the file store follows its durable decision, never the other way round. The transaction that decides a shred (`privacy._decide`, called by `shred_file` and `shred_approved`) marks the row and writes `file_object.shred` and calls nothing of the store; `privacy._complete` destroys the key — `lifecycle.shred_sidecar`, its only caller in the application — sets `shred_completed_at` and writes `file_object.shred_complete`, in a transaction of its own. Three roads reach it and no other: `privacy.continuation`, registered with `UnitOfWork.after_commit` on the unit of work that commits the decision (the hook of an approved request registers it on the kernel's unit of work, with the context of the principal that decided); `shred_file` for a row decided and not completed; and `domain.platform.shred_completion.run` (SCH-16), one SYSTEM unit of work per file. `_complete` is idempotent on a key already destroyed and destroys only a key the workspace owns (`files.store.owns_key`). A reader never asks the store whether a file is shredded: the row's `shredded_at` answers, from the decision on. `backend/tests/architecture/test_shred_order.py` holds the callers in both directions, so a new road is added there with its code (rev 1.225; 05 rev 1.171 PRV-07 b; 04 rev 1.237 T-PLT-29 "Decide, then destroy"; finding B4 of the review of the `EVIDENCE_SHRED` merge). | A key destroyed inside the deciding transaction is gone when that transaction fails, and nothing says who destroyed it or when |
| DG-KRN-FILE-10 | The associated data of a stored file names the workspace of its storage key, never the workspace of the row that names it. One function decides whose object a row may open — `files.store.content_tenant`: the row's own workspace, or the source of its sandbox, and no other — and three readers build their context from it: `open_file` (through `_content_workspace`, which reads the row's `tenant.source_tenant_id` only for a key of another workspace and raises `ForeignStorageKey` with the log line `files.foreign_storage_key` otherwise), the verifier's `check_file` (the source handed in from the tenant directory; `foreign_storage_key`) and `lifecycle.rewrap_sidecar`, which takes the workspace from the key (`key_tenant`) and has no parameter for it. `put_file` writes under the caller's own key. No other function calls `encryption_context`: `backend/tests/architecture/test_file_context.py` holds its callers, and a new reader of a stored file's content is added there with its rule (rev 1.257; 05 rev 1.196 SBX-03; 04 rev 1.274 T-PLT-29). | A reader that names the row's workspace cannot open one copied file in a sandbox; one that names the key's workspace without the source rule opens another workspace's object |

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-REG-01 | `resolve` implements the T-PLT-32 resolution: APPROVED obligation override, APPROVED contract override, `pob_template_version.policy_values`, `product.policy_values`, PUBLISHED BOOK version, PUBLISHED ENTITY version, PUBLISHED TENANT version, framework default (`default_asc606` or `default_ifrs15` by book). Levels not in `allowed_levels` are skipped. Forced defaults are never overridden. Only rows effective or approved at or before `known_at` count. In release 1.0 the two override levels meet no row (rev 1.298; 04 T-CON-23 "Not offered in release 1.0"): `resolve` reads `policy_override` only where a contract is named, which `GET /policies/resolve` alone does — bundle assembly names none (05 RCP-15) — and the creation of an override is refused (DG-KRN-REG-06). |
| DG-KRN-REG-02 | For `pin = 'K'` the value resolved at inception is recorded in `contract_version.pinned_policies` and reused until an approved re-run re-pins (REQ-POL-007). **A group's first version (rev 1.143; item PIN-K-COMBINATION-1, supervisor ruling R-112 (i)).** A group has no `pinned_policies` before its first version in a book; when its members were computed before — the first computation after an approved combination — `bundles.build` takes the recorded values of the latest version, in the book, of a member's former group (`bundles.former_pinned_policies`): the member with the earliest inception date, then external id, first, and its most recent former group first, the order of the product pins (`bundles.former_groups`). A parameter those values do not hold resolves at this computation, as every parameter does when no member was computed in the book before. A contract taken out of a group again returns to its own group and to the values recorded there. `pin = 'P'` values resolve per posting period. **Level P and the product (rev 1.93; security ruling R-21, finding SN-7).** The level-P values of a line's product and template, and the members of the product the engine reads (`ProductInput`), are contract-pinned in the same sense, but a product has no versions, so the value itself is recorded: `computation.persist` writes `contract_computation.pinned_refs.products` (04 T-CON-07 rev 1.110) from the bundle it computed — never from a second read of the product — for every product carried by a member contract past `DRAFT` in a book, and `bundles.build` takes a recorded product, its components and the level-P values of its obligations from the group's latest SUCCEEDED computation. T-REF-20 is read only for a product not recorded yet: a contract still `DRAFT` in every book (nothing of it posts, and a repaired product must reach it — REQ-REF-014), or a line added later for another product, which is recorded by that computation. A product that computation does not list is looked up, before T-REF-20 is read, in the latest SUCCEEDED computation of each member's former groups (T-CON-04 history) — as in the first computation after an approved combination — the member with the earliest inception date, then external id, first, and its most recent former group first; a contract taken out of a group again computes in its own group on the pin recorded there. A change of the product — approved, 04 API-R-23 — therefore reaches only contracts that first leave `DRAFT` after it; `apply_to_existing` for product changes is not offered in 1.0. **The SSP versions a contract was priced from (rev 1.163; item PIN-READBACK-1; supervisor ruling R-116 (d)).** POL-070 is pinned per pricing, not per group, and by read-back, not through `pinned_policies`: `bundles.recorded_ssp_versions` reads, per book, the version of each obligation's own pricing from T-CON-11 `ssp_book_version_id` at the group's latest version and the versions of its modification weights from `pinned_refs.ssp_weights` of that version's computation, and `_policies` hands them as one `OBLIGATION` row of level `O`, source `RECORDED`, value `{recorded, recorded@<event key>}` (05 RCP-15 rev 1.119). A member the group has not computed is read at its most recent former group; a computation that did not include the contract's `CONTRACT_ACTIVATED` is not read (`bundles._behind_the_gate`: a draft's computation is provisional); an obligation with a version-naming `LINE_ATTRIBUTES_CHANGED` is read before the first such event. `computation.persist` writes `pinned_refs.ssp_weights` through `bundles.ssp_weight_members` from the trace it computed — the `ssp_entry` sources of the `mod_weight@<event key>` nodes — never from a second selection. The row is no level-P value: `product_pin_members` records level-P rows only. In the engine a reader of SSP names the pricing it makes (`s05_allocation.Record`) or prices by date; it never interprets the row itself (ENGINE_SPEC S05-R-03). **A level P value that no computation reads (rev 1.300; item PRODUCT-POLICY-VALUE-NOT-READ-1, register index 309; 04 T-REF-20 and T-REF-23 rev 1.323; POLICIES §0.5 rule 1 rev 1.125; PRD ERR-103).** `bundles._policies` hands a product's and a template's value to the engine at `OBLIGATION` scope, level `P`, and `PolicyResolver.resolved` takes an `OBLIGATION` row only for a read that passes `obligation=`. The engine reads three parameters that list level P with `contract=` alone — `usage.tier_minimum_method` (stage 04 `vc.elements` and `buildup.realised`, stage 05 `original._realised_component`), `upfront_fee.recognition_period` (stage 03 `options._benefit_period`) and `pob.shipping_as_fulfilment` (stage 03 `elections.shipping`) — so `reference.products.policy_values_errors`, the one check of the four doors that store level P values (`POST /products`, `PATCH /products/{id}`, the proposal of a product's policy values, the outputs of an obligation template version), refuses them by `LEVEL_P_NOT_READ` under rule id `POLICY_PRODUCT_LEVEL_NOT_READ`: the framework's default of the first two is admitted, no value of the third. The sentence of a refusal names its parameter by the code (the template field `{key}`): the obligation template editor shows it in its banner, without the field (SCREENS §11.2 rev 1.81). The engine is not changed. The set has its witnesses: `backend/tests/architecture/test_level_p_readers.py` holds the five reads and every other naming of the three in the engine against the source, `backend/tests/unit/policies/test_level_p_not_read.py` the product's assembly and the door, and `backend/tests/unit/answer_keys/test_level_p_row_not_read.py` two runs of the whole engine. A template version's example cases (`templates.run_test_cases`) give the engine the version's level P values at `CONTRACT` scope as well; no reader of the three is reached there (stages 01 and 02 and `build_lines` of stage 03), and with the door no version holds such a value. |

A kind whose create takes an advisory lock and reads the versions without locking them supplies that lock: registry versions per scope key (`presets.serialise_key`), account mapping versions per tenant (`mapping.serialise_versions`), import mapping profile versions per code (`mapping_profiles.serialise_code`). A test that needs a second publication in a key while a version is open makes it by rows (`support.rows.publish_registry_version`): no command can (PRD SM-04). |

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-EXP-01 | Every number the engine stores or the UI displays has a trace node produced by the code that computed it, never reconstructed afterwards (research 06 §19.1, REQ-RPT-018). `obligation_version.trace_nodes`, the native `ContractVersionOut.trace_nodes` and `BalanceOut.trace_nodes`, and `schedule_line.trace_node_id` point to node ids. Scope (D-97 (8)): every `erev.money` and `erev.exact` column of T-CON-08, T-CON-09 and T-CON-11 the engine publishes, zeros included. A computed column links the node that produced the stored value: after a reallocating boundary the boundary node `<column>@<event key>:<subject>:-`, never the inception node when the two differ (T1-F-2); a column summed over several nodes links a sum node emitted by the producing stage. An echoed input links an `input.echo.v1` node whose input is the canonical input field as a `SourceRef` (`detail.member`, `detail.value`) or the node it copies. Only explicitly documented exceptions stay unlinked; the engine test `test_trace_linkage.py` enumerates the expected columns per family and fails when one is detached. |
| DG-KRN-EXP-02 | Node ids are deterministic: `<measure>:<subject key>:<period key or '-'>` (T-ENG-03), for example `revenue:POB #2:FY2026-P03`. The period slot may carry the qualifier `returns` for a version-date re-measurement beside a boundary node of the same event and measure (ENGINE_SPEC CV-50: `allocation_adjustment@<event key>:<ob>:returns`; `expected_returns_amount@<event key>:<group>:returns`, `transaction_price@<event key>:<group>:returns`). A duplicate id raises `EngineError("TRACE_DUPLICATE_NODE")`. |
| DG-KRN-EXP-03 | Value encoding: a posted amount node holds `format_money` with the currency minor unit and `rounding_residue = format_exact(exact − posted)`; an exact node holds `format_exact(x)` and `rounding_residue = None`. The exact value of any posted measure is therefore `value + rounding_residue` (used by the parity runner, DG-PAR-05). |
| DG-KRN-EXP-04 | `formula_id` names a pure function in `FORMULAS`. `reevaluate` recomputes every node with a formula from its inputs and params in topological order; P14 requires the recomputed values to equal the stored values exactly (research 06 §18.3). Source-reference inputs carry their value in `params["value"]`. **Exact inputs (rev 1.52; D-98 candidate 117 F1, Codex 0235):** for a formula registered in `formulas.EXACT_INPUT_FORMULAS` (`books.unit_revenue_rate.v1`, `alloc.original_total.v1`) a node-id input contributes its DG-KRN-EXP-03 exact value — the recomputed value plus the input node's STORED `rounding_residue` (trace data, not recomputed; the value itself for an exact node) — so the formula binds raw operands against the same reconstruction the emitting step read through `TraceBuilder.exact`; every other formula keeps receiving the recomputed value. |
| DG-KRN-EXP-05 | Storage: one `calc_trace` row per `contract_version` with `trace` = canonical JSON of the `Trace`, `trace_sha256` and `node_count`. A trace above 64 MiB fails the computation with problem `eng-trace-too-large` (T-ENG-03). |
| DG-KRN-EXP-06 | `explain_measure` returns API-S-Explain. `value` equals the stored number exactly; `nodes` is limited by `depth` (default 6, maximum 20); `narrative` is rendered only from `NARRATIVES` templates and never by AI (REQ-AI-006 is a separate endpoint); `drill` links contract, obligation, schedule lines, subledger lines and source rows (REQ-RPT-017). |
| DG-KRN-EXP-07 | Narrative templates format money as `<ISO code> <amount>` with en-US grouping and minor-unit places (DS-FMT-05) and dates as `DD MMM YYYY` (DS-FMT-16). |
| DG-KRN-EXP-08 | Exact of a posted measure that names a companion (rev 1.66; ENGINE_SPEC CV-64 rev 1.30 as amended; D-98 134 AMENDMENT 1; D-98 candidate 149): when a posted node's `params.exact_node` names its exact companion (`<measure>_exact:<subject>`), a consumer's `exact(m)` for that measure is the COMPANION's own serialized `value` (an exact node: `format_exact`, no residue), read only after the own-version trace identity and hash, the actual `trace_nodes` linkage, the availability check (`params.exact_basis` = unavailable; neither param = legacy) and `erev_engine.trace.exact_companion_failures(trace, reevaluate(trace))` have passed for that node; DG-KRN-EXP-03's `value + rounding_residue` is NOT the companion's value (signed half-up at 18 places does not commute with translation by P on opposite-signed ties), so a consumer never forms it in place of the companion, never assumes Q18(A) = P + Q18(A − P), and never treats an unavailable or legacy activity as posted-as-exact. The checker skips nodes without `exact_node`, so zero failures alone never prove availability. First consumer: RPT-10 / RPT-12 LM-CL-55 (04 §17.1 rule 4a). |

### 5.17 Canonical serialisation and hashing (KRN-CAN)

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_engine/canonical.py (standard library only)
def canonical_bytes(obj: Any) -> bytes: ...
def sha256_hex(obj: Any) -> str: ...
```

| Id | Value type | Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| DG-KRN-CAN-01 | Mapping | JSON object; keys must be `str` (else `TypeError`); sorted by Unicode code point; separators `,` and `:`; no whitespace; UTF-8 without escaping non-ASCII |
| DG-KRN-CAN-02 | `str` | JSON string as is (no normalisation) |
| DG-KRN-CAN-03 | `int` | JSON integer; `bool` is encoded as `true` or `false` and never as an integer |
| DG-KRN-CAN-04 | `Decimal` | JSON string `format(d, "f")` (preserves the stored scale; no exponent); NaN and infinity raise `ValueError` |
| DG-KRN-CAN-05 | `Fraction` | JSON string `format_exact(x)` |
| DG-KRN-CAN-06 | `float` | `TypeError` |
| DG-KRN-CAN-07 | `date` | `"YYYY-MM-DD"` |
| DG-KRN-CAN-08 | `datetime` | must be timezone-aware (else `ValueError`); converted to UTC; `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ"` |
| DG-KRN-CAN-09 | `UUID` | lowercase hyphenated string |
| DG-KRN-CAN-10 | `Enum` | its `.value` |
| DG-KRN-CAN-11 | `list`, `tuple` | JSON array in order |
| DG-KRN-CAN-12 | `set`, `frozenset` | JSON array sorted by the canonical bytes of the elements |
| DG-KRN-CAN-13 | dataclass instance | mapping of its fields |
| DG-KRN-CAN-14 | `None` | `null` |
| DG-KRN-CAN-15 | anything else (including Pydantic models, which callers dump with `model_dump(mode="python")` first) | `TypeError` |

`sha256_hex(obj) = hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(obj)).hexdigest()`. Content hashes (approval subjects, idempotency requests, engine input and output bundles, calc traces, report outputs, ledger seals, audit HMAC input) all use this module. [J] One encoder means a hash computed by the API, the engine or a verification job always agrees.

### 5.18 Unit of work (KRN-UOW)

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/uow.py
class UnitOfWork:
    ctx: RequestContext
    session: Session
    clock: Clock
    now: datetime
    keyring: KeyRing
    files: FileStore

    @property
    def principal(self) -> Principal: ...
    def audit(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None: ...                     # audit.record(self, **kwargs)
    def defer(self, kind: JobKind, params: Mapping[str, Any], **kwargs: Any) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
    def enqueue_outbox(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
    def notify(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None: ...
    def after_commit(self, fn: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...
    def commit(self) -> None: ...

@contextmanager
def unit_of_work(ctx: RequestContext, *, clock: Clock, keyring: KeyRing, files: FileStore,
                 statement_timeout_ms: int = 60_000) -> Iterator[UnitOfWork]: ...
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-UOW-01 | `unit_of_work` opens `tenant_session(ctx.principal.db_context, …)` and sets `now = clock.now()` once. |
| DG-KRN-UOW-02 | `commit()` runs, in order: (1) `session.flush()`; (1a) the before-commit steps in registration order (rev 1.266; item JOB-STALL-COMMIT-RACE-1): `before_commit(fn)` is taken until `commit()` is called, and its one caller is a job's unit of work, whose step writes the attempt's heartbeat on the job's row (DG-KRN-JOB-04), the unit's last statement before the chain head; (2) `audit.chain.flush(self)`; (3) `session.commit()`, where deferred constraint triggers (DB-06, DB-16, DB-17) fire and failures map to problems through `from_db_error`; (4) after-commit hooks in registration order. A hook exception is logged and does not change the response (the job sweeper recovers deferrals, DG-KRN-JOB-06). Rev 1.266: a commit that fails at (1a), (2) or (3) rolls the transaction back before the error leaves `commit()` (`discard()`), whatever the error is. A session commits the transaction it finds open when its block is left without an error (`db.session`), so until this revision a caller that took an error which is no database error — a step that refuses, a chain without its head — and left its block normally would have committed its writes without their audit events. No caller did; a handler that takes `JobLost` at its commit now could. A database error maps to its problem as before. |
| DG-KRN-UOW-03 | Calling `commit()` twice raises `RuntimeError`. Leaving the context without committing rolls back and discards buffered audit events and hooks. `savepoint()` (rev 1.40; D-98 candidate 101d, Codex CONTEXT-R1) is a nested transaction for writes the unit of work may have to undo WITHOUT ending it: on an exception the savepoint is rolled back and the audit events and hooks buffered inside it are dropped, while the session keeps its tenant context (the app engine clears `erev.context` only on a transaction rollback, DG-KRN-DB-04) and every lock taken before it; `discard()` (a transaction rollback) is never followed by another statement on the same session. |
| DG-KRN-UOW-04 | Background jobs obtain units of work from `JobContext.unit_of_work()`, with the SYSTEM principal or the on-behalf-of principal recorded on the job. Rev 1.266 (item JOB-STALL-COMMIT-RACE-1; 05 JOB-06 rev 1.200): a job's unit of work is a unit of work of the job's ATTEMPT. `jobs.context.system_unit_of_work(runtime, principal, …)` is the one function that opens it — `JobContext.unit_of_work()` calls it with the job's principal, a handler calls it with `jc.runtime` and another principal — and with a runtime that carries an attempt it passes the attempt's door before it yields (DG-KRN-JOB-04). The worker's own runtime carries none: the units of work of the sweeper, of a settlement and its failure hook, and of the periodic tasks are no attempt's. |
| DG-KRN-UOW-05 | `as_system()` (rev 1.126; supervisor ruling R-95; 05 TXN-10) is a context manager for the computation of a combination group. Inside its block the unit of work's principal is `system_principal(tenant_id, on_behalf_of_id=…)` — on behalf of the caller, or of the caller's own on-behalf-of when the caller is already SYSTEM — and the transaction runs under the tenant's scope and as SYSTEM (`system_entity_scope` with `system_user`, DG-KRN-DB-05); leaving the block restores the principal and both settings, also when the block raises. It is re-entrant: inside itself it does nothing. Rows stamped inside carry `created_by` NULL and `created_by_kind` SYSTEM, and audit events buffered inside carry the actor SYSTEM with `on_behalf_of_id`. It is entered before the computation's savepoint. `compute_job.compute_group`, `computation.persist` and `computation.recompute` run their bodies inside it and `bundles.build` runs its reads inside `system_entity_scope`, so no caller chooses the scope of a computation (DG-ARC-16). No other code uses it. |

class EnvSecretStore:                                         # local provider: values from Settings (.env)
