```python
class GcpSecretManagerStore: ...                              # hosted artifact; never instantiated in tests

# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/adapters/keys/provider.py (05 SAR-21)
class KeyProvider(Protocol):
    def hmac_key(self, key_id: str) -> bytes: ...
    def current_hmac_key_id(self, purpose: Literal["audit-hmac", "security-hmac"], tenant_id: UUID | None) -> str: ...
    def wrap(self, dek: bytes, context: Mapping[str, str]) -> bytes: ...
    def unwrap(self, blob: bytes, context: Mapping[str, str]) -> bytes: ...
    def secret(self, ref: str) -> SecretStr: ...

class LocalKeyProvider:                                       # adapter over SecretStore; no keyring file
    def __init__(self, store: SecretStore) -> None: ...

class GcpKeyProvider: ...                                     # hosted artifact (Cloud KMS, Secret Manager)

# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/auth/keyring.py
class KeyRing:
    def __init__(self, provider: KeyProvider) -> None: ...
    def tenant_audit_key(self, audit_hmac_key_id: str) -> bytes: ...
    def security_event_key(self, hmac_key_id: str) -> bytes: ...
    def new_tenant_audit_key_id(self, tenant_id: UUID) -> str: ...        # "audit-hmac:<tenant id>:1"
    def encrypt(self, plaintext: bytes, *, context: Mapping[str, str]) -> bytes: ...
    def decrypt(self, blob: bytes, *, context: Mapping[str, str]) -> bytes: ...

def build_keyring(settings: Settings) -> KeyRing: ...         # composition roots only (DG-KRN-CFG-01)
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-KRN-KEY-01 | Master keys (D-75 Q8). `EnvSecretStore.get` serves exactly three names, `EREV_AUDIT_HMAC_MASTER_KEY`, `EREV_SECURITY_EVENT_HMAC_KEY` and `EREV_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, each 32 bytes written as 64 lowercase hex characters (DG-KRN-CFG-02). Any other name raises `KeyError`. |
| DG-KRN-KEY-02 | Derivation. `LocalKeyProvider.hmac_key(key_id)` returns HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869; `cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf.hkdf.HKDF` with `length = 32` and `salt = None`) over a master key, with `info = "erev:" + key_id` encoded as ASCII. Key ids `audit-hmac:<tenant id>:<n>` use `EREV_AUDIT_HMAC_MASTER_KEY`; `security-hmac:<n>` uses `EREV_SECURITY_EVENT_HMAC_KEY`; `kek:<n>` uses `EREV_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. `<tenant id>` is the lowercase hyphenated UUID and `<n>` a positive integer without leading zeros; any other form raises `ValueError`. Two tenants therefore never share an audit key, and rotation increments `<n>` without a new master key. |
| DG-KRN-KEY-03 | Provider selection by `EREV_KEY_PROVIDER`: `local` → `LocalKeyProvider(EnvSecretStore(settings))`; `gcp` → `GcpKeyProvider` over `GcpSecretManagerStore`. `EREV_ENV` in {`dev`, `test`, `e2e`} requires `local` (DG-KRN-CFG-02). |
| DG-KRN-KEY-04 | Encryption. `KeyRing.encrypt` generates a random 32-byte DEK, encrypts with AES-256-GCM (96-bit random nonce; the canonical bytes of `context` as associated data, §5.17) and stores the DEK wrapped by `wrap`. `LocalKeyProvider.wrap` uses AES-256-GCM under `hmac_key("kek:1")`. The blob is `b"erev1"` ‖ KEK id length (1 byte) ‖ KEK id ‖ wrapped DEK ‖ nonce ‖ ciphertext with tag, so `decrypt` selects the KEK by id. |
| DG-KRN-KEY-05 | No keyring file exists locally: no `.data/keys/`, no `EREV_LOCAL_KEYRING_PATH`, no `erev keys init`. 05 CMP-07, CFG-11, CFG-12, SAR-23, DPL-13, OPR-15 and OPR-17 are read with `LocalKeyProvider` over `.env` master keys as the local provider (D-75 Q8). `make backup` copies `.env` instead (DG-MK-backup). |
| DG-KRN-KEY-06 | `tenant.provision` computes `KeyRing.new_tenant_audit_key_id(tenant_id)` before inserting the tenant row and stores only the id in `tenant.audit_hmac_key_id` (05 SAR-24). No key material is stored in the database or logged. Rev 1.108 (05 SBX-02, SBX-07; KEY-05): a JOB that creates a tenant — the sandbox load, the empty sandbox of a reset — does the same through `sandboxes.provision_audit_key`: the tenant row first under that id, then the key through `JobRuntime.key_provisioner` (built by `worker.build_runtime` with `build_tenant_key_provisioner`; hosted, the Secret Manager provisioner, which creates the tenant secret and reads it back; `None` derives locally), inside the transaction that inserts the row, so a sandbox commits only with a key that can be read. A provider that DENIES the authority (hosted: a process identity without the provisioning role — `auth.keyring.provisioning_denied` classifies it, so the domain does not import the adapter's error) is the named refusal of the job, 412 `precondition-failed` `SANDBOX_KEY_PROVISIONING_DENIED` (`sandboxes.key_provisioning_denied`; supervisor ruling R-60 (d)); every other failure of the authority propagates unchanged. |
| DG-KRN-KEY-07 | Tests in `backend/tests/unit/test_keys.py`: RFC 5869 test case 3 (SHA-256, zero-length salt and info) through the same HKDF construction; per-tenant keys differ for two tenant ids and are identical across processes; `encrypt` then `decrypt` round-trips, and decryption fails when the context changes; `repr(EnvSecretStore(...))` and captured logs contain no key value (DG-LOG-07). |

## 6. Backend conventions

### 6.1 The command pattern (CMD)

Every state-changing operation, whether it comes from HTTP, an import, an adapter, a job, the CLI or the seed, is a command handler that follows these steps in this order.

| Step | Id | Name | What the step does | What it must not do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | DG-CMD-01 | Authorize | The route dependency has checked the permission and MFA (DG-KRN-AUTH-03). After loading the object, the handler calls `require_for_entity` with the object's entity. It applies separation checks (`sod.assert_assignment_allowed`, approver ≠ preparer) and the sandbox guard `ensure_production(uow)` as the first statement of export, posting-to-GL and conversion commands (403 `sandbox-restricted`, REQ-PLT-022). The three that destroy a stored file — `file.shred`, `file.request_shred` and the effect of an `EVIDENCE_SHRED` decision — call it once the file's row is read, for a file whose storage key is not the workspace's own (`files.store.owns_key`: the key's first segment against the workspace's id, pinned by `tests/unit/test_sandbox_guard.py` against `files.store.storage_key`): a copy shares its stored files with its source, and what a sandbox stored itself is its own (rev 1.211; 05 SBX-08). | Trust the UI for hiding actions (BR-UX-05) |
| 2 | DG-CMD-02 | Load and lock | Reads the rows the command depends on with `FOR UPDATE`, in DG-KRN-DB-08 lock order. It checks preconditions: `expected_stream_version` for contracts (T-CON-05) and `row_version` for IM-M and IM-P rows (API-C-08). Missing or out-of-scope rows → 404 `not-found`. | Lock rows it does not change |
| 3 | DG-CMD-03 | Validate | Applies domain rules and collects all findings; raises one 422 `validation-failed` whose `errors[]` lists each finding with its `rule_id`. Checks period states (DB-07 mirror), policy levels (T-PLT-32) and transition pairs (DG-SM-02). | Stop at the first finding when several can be reported |
| 4 | DG-CMD-04 | Compute | Builds the engine input bundle through `erev_api.domain.contracts.bundles.build(session, group_id=…, known_at=uow.now, pending_events=[…], trigger=…)` and calls `erev_engine.compute(bundle)`. Pending events are events of this command not yet inserted. An `EngineError` in a decision command → 422 `validation-failed` with `rule_id` = the engine code. Rev 1.98 (BUILD_SPEC CLO-12; supervisor ruling R-51 (a)): the builder resolves every `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT_APPLIED` event, stored or pending, into the members of its T-SL-05 row in natural keys (`bundles.adjustment_payloads`, `adjustment_members`: `kind`, `book_code`, `entity_code`, `period_key`, `obligation_key`, and the kind's `amount` \| `ratio` \| `remaining`, `periods` or `lines`) and sets the event's `manual_adjustment_key` to the adjustment number, so the engine reads the adjustment without the database (04 §16.3; ENGINE_SPEC_B S09-R-38 to S09-R-41, S14-R-09a); an id without a visible row resolves to nothing and the engine refuses the event by name. Rev 1.217 (item MAP-RULE-FOREIGN-1; supervisor ruling of 2026-10-01; 05 RCP-15 rev 1.168): of the published account mapping version the builder hands over the rules that name no product and no entity or one the bundle holds (`bundles._account_mapping`, `_rule_in_bundle`). A rule written for another product or entity is left out: its code is a natural key the bundle does not hold (DG-ENG-02), and a rule handed over with its condition dropped is a rule for every product or entity at the specificity of the rule it was. The same holds for any condition of a configuration row the builder resolves to a natural key: a row whose key the bundle cannot state is left out or refused by name, never handed over without it. Witnesses `tests/domain/contracts/test_bundle_account_mapping.py` (a product's rule, an entity's rule, and a computation stored before) and `tests/unit/test_bundle_account_mapping_rules.py`. | Call the engine more than once per combination group per command; read the database from inside the engine |
| 5 | DG-CMD-05 | Persist append-only | Inserts facts (events, decisions, versions, schedules, traces, postings and seals) and applies status changes through `transitions.apply`. IM-M updates check `row_version`, and IM-X projections are updated in the same transaction. Engine output goes through `computation.persist(uow, bundle, output)` (DG-CMD-10). | UPDATE or DELETE IM-A rows; write any row outside this transaction |
| 6 | DG-CMD-06 | Audit | Writes exactly one audit event per affected object (AUD-CMD) or one summary (AUD-FACT) through `uow.audit` or `audit.record_facts`. | Log personal data (§6.6) |
| 7 | DG-CMD-07 | Emit | Registers notifications, outbox messages, webhooks and job deferrals as rows in this transaction. | Call external systems (HTTP adapters, SMTP, AI providers) inside the transaction |
| 8 | DG-CMD-08 | Commit | `run_command` calls `idempotency.complete` and then `uow.commit()` (DG-KRN-UOW-02); the response is built from committed state. | Commit from inside the handler |

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/api/deps.py (route helper)
def run_command(cmd: CommandContext, deps: KernelDeps, fn: Callable[[UnitOfWork], BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any]], *,
                status_code: int = 200, location: Callable[[Any], str] | None = None,
                etag: Callable[[Any], str] | None = None) -> Response: ...

# Canonical shape of a route and its handler
@router.post("/contracts/{contract_id}/submit-activation", operation_id="contracts_submit_activation",
             response_model=ContractOut, responses=problem_responses("forbidden", "not-found",
             "precondition-failed", "precondition-required", "validation-failed"))
def submit_activation(contract_id: UUID, body: SubmitActivationIn,
                      cmd: CommandContext = Depends(command("contract.create", precondition="contract")),
                      deps: KernelDeps = Depends(kernel_deps)) -> Response:
    return run_command(cmd, deps, lambda uow: contract_commands.submit_activation(
        uow, contract_id=contract_id, expected_stream_version=cmd.expected_version, body=body))

# backend/erev_api/domain/contracts/commands.py
def submit_activation(uow: UnitOfWork, *, contract_id: UUID, expected_stream_version: int,
                      body: SubmitActivationIn) -> ContractOut:
    group_id = repo.get_contract(uow.session, contract_id)["combination_group_id"]       # 2 (unlocked read: which group to lock)
    group = repo.lock_group(uow.session, group_id)                                     # 2 DG-KRN-DB-08: group row first …
    contract = repo.get_contract(uow.session, contract_id, for_update=True)          # 2 … then the contract row
    if contract["combination_group_id"] != group_id:                                  # 2 membership re-verified under the locks
        raise problem("precondition-failed")
    require_for_entity(uow.ctx, "contract.create", contract["contracting_entity_id"]) # 1
    checklist = activation.evaluate(uow.session, contract)                             # 3
    if checklist.errors:
        raise problem("validation-failed", errors=checklist.errors)
    pending = [EventIn(event_type=ContractEventType.CONTRACT_ACTIVATED, effective_date=contract["inception_date"],
                       payload=ContractActivatedV1(checklist=checklist.items))]
    bundle = bundles.build(uow.session, group_id=group["id"], known_at=uow.now, pending_events=pending,
                           trigger=ComputationTrigger.COMMAND)                          # 4
    output = erev_engine.compute(bundle)                                               # 4
    append_events(uow, contract_id=contract_id, expected_stream_version=expected_stream_version,
                  events=pending, origin="API")                                        # 5
    computation.persist(uow, bundle, output)                                           # 5
    uow.audit(action="contract.submit_activation", object_type="contract", object_id=contract_id,
              object_version=str(expected_stream_version + 1), comment=body.comment)   # 6
    uow.notify(...)                                                                     # 7
    return queries.contract_out(uow.session, contract_id, known_at=uow.now)            # 8 in run_command
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-CMD-09 | Two command families. **Decision commands** (activation, modification approval, estimate approval, manual adjustment approval, void, policy override approval — which meets no override in release 1.0, 04 T-CON-23 rev 1.322) compute before persisting and fail closed: an engine error rolls everything back. **Fact-capture commands** (`POST /contracts/{id}/events`, import commit, adapter sync, migration import) persist the facts and mark the group dirty in unit of work A. They then compute in unit of work B. When B fails, the computation row is FAILED or QUARANTINED, an exception item is raised (REQ-CLS-013), and the response still returns 201 with `computation.status`. When B would exceed its budget (more than 200 obligations in the group, or 30 seconds of engine time measured before persisting), the route defers `CONTRACT_COMPUTE` and returns 202 (API-R-30). Rev 1.97 (item RES-53-COMPUTE-1; ruling R-53 (5)): a database error of the DG-KRN-ERR-03 "server could not do it now" class inside unit of work B is not a result of the computation. `compute_group` re-raises it before its catch-all stores anything: no FAILED computation, no exception item; the caller's transaction rolls back (a fact-capture command answers 503 and saves nothing, its events included), and a `CONTRACT_COMPUTE` job's attempt fails and is retried by its policy. Every other exception is recorded as before. Rev 1.98 (BUILD_SPEC CLO-12; supervisor ruling R-51): the manual adjustment approval is the `on_approved` hook of subject `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` (`journals/adjustments.py`) and runs in this order inside the decision's transaction: the DG-KRN-DB-08 locks; `assert_fresh_basis`; for a request flagged `DEFER_PAST_LOCK` only `is_deferred_past_lock = true`; otherwise `SUBMITTED` → `APPROVED`, `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT_APPLIED` appended as SYSTEM with the request id, for a journal kind `subledger.post` of the approved lines (posting kind `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT`, key `adjustment:<id>`, `manual_adjustment_id`; the adjustment period, or the first open period with it as origin), `APPROVED` → `POSTED` with `applied_event_id` and `subledger_posting_id`, then `computation.recompute` of the group — an `EngineError` rolls the whole decision back and the request stays `PENDING`. Rev 1.126 (supervisor rulings R-95 and R-97 (5); 05 RCP-18, RCP-20, TXN-10): both families compute as SYSTEM on behalf of the caller under the tenant's scope (DG-KRN-UOW-05), so the outcome of a computation does not depend on the entities its caller may see. In unit of work B `compute_group` decides by the class of what was raised (R-105); this replaces rev 1.97's "every other exception is recorded as before", and the class of rev 1.97 is part of the transient table and keeps its 503. An `EngineError` is stored QUARANTINED. A `Problem` is rolled back and re-raised: it is the command's answer and is never stored. A database error for which `db.errors.is_transient` answers true — the SQLSTATE classes `08`, `25`, `40`, `53`, `55`, `57`, `58`, `72` and `XX` (a lock timeout `55P03`, a deadlock `40P01`, a serialization failure `40001`, a cancelled statement `57014`, resources, the connection), a class in neither table, an error without a SQLSTATE, and the period guard's `EREV-LED-003`, recognised by its §14.1 code in the message of a `P0001` — is not a failure of the computation: the savepoint is rolled back and the error propagates; the command answers 409, or the kernel's answer for that SQLSTATE, and saves nothing, the job fails its attempt, and no computation row, exception item or control execution is stored. A deterministic database error — the classes `0A`, `21`, `22`, `23`, `27`, `2F`, `42`, `44`, `54` and `P0` other than the period guard — and any other exception are a crash on this group that a retry would meet again: stored FAILED with the exception item, and a fact-capture command still returns 201. `db/errors.py` holds the two tables and the predicate, which the mapping of database errors to problems and the retry predicate of jobs share. Rev 1.234 (item JRN-COMPLETENESS-TRANSIENT-1; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01): the completeness assertion's read of a run's held detail file (`journals.completeness._held_ids_from_file`) decides by the same table — a transient database error, an unavailable server or a pool timeout is re-raised, and only a failure that says something about the file (missing, shredded, unreadable, mis-hashed, malformed) answers "unverifiable", inside a savepoint, so that a database error which is not re-raised leaves the transaction usable for the statements that follow. Rev 1.157 (item CTR-BALANCE-ROWS-1; supervisor ruling R-114 (g)): `computation.persist` stores the rows of a version through `computation._insert_rows` — each run of rows that name one column set is one INSERT. A statement of several rows takes its columns from the first: a later row that names fewer is refused, and one that names more loses them without an error. The rows `_row` builds name the columns the engine output carries, so they may differ (the T-CON-09 rows of two contracting entities with different functional currencies); no other statement of `computation.py` carries a list of rows (`tests/unit/test_computation_rows.py`). Rev 1.224 (items REGROUP-BEFORE-POSTING-1 and REGROUP-AFTER-POSTING-AMOUNT-1; 04 §16.1 rev 1.234; ENGINE_SPEC S06-R-27 rev 1.148): a command that is applied without an approval request because nothing has posted tests that nothing CAN post, not only that nothing has. In release 1.0 `contracts.regroup.regroup` is taken between two `DRAFT` contracts and for nothing else: there it applies its pair at once; it refuses — 409 `invalid-transition`, before its first write, so that a new target is not booked either — a contract that is not a draft while neither has a posted line, and every regroup after a posted line. The after-posting pair is withdrawn until it is rebuilt: its code stays behind the refusal and is reached by no route. The pair's rows are dated `holds.entity_date` — the contracting entity's current date (05 TZ-03) — and never the UTC date of `uow.now`. Rev 1.282 (item COMPUTE-BEHIND-GROUP-1; 05 RCP-20 rev 1.207): in `compute_group` an `EngineError`, and any other exception that is not transient, of a bundle that is behind its group is not stored (`_no_finding_of_a_bundle_behind`): it is no finding about the group as it stands and ends 409 `lock-conflict`, as `persist` would have ended the computation (DG-CMD-10). |
| DG-CMD-10 | `computation.persist(uow, bundle, output) -> Mapping[str, Any]` writes `contract_computation` (`input_sha256 = bundle.sha256()`, engine release), then per book `contract_version`, `obligation_version`, `contract_version_balance`, `schedule`, `schedule_line`, `calc_trace`, and `subledger_posting` with its lines and seal (idempotency key `compute:<contract_computation_id>`, DB-06). It clears `combination_group.dirty_since` and audits AUD-FACT. When a SUCCEEDED computation with the same `input_sha256` and `engine_version` exists, it returns that computation and writes nothing (`ux_contract_computation__idempotent`, research 06 P9). Rev 1.10 (D-96): …and writes `computation_evidence` (T-CON-25) with the raw-file digests computed over the bytes written; it refuses with `release-validation-pending` unless the process release is enabled for the tenant (T-PLT-43); while any entity/book portion of a group's `release_group_processing` state (T-PLT-46) is `PENDING` or `DEFERRED_NO_OPEN_PERIOD` it appends each portion's next state (re-applying S08-R-08 to the portion's origin periods for deferral, whether or not postings were produced; a deferral retains `unresolved_origin_period_keys` and the produced posting ids; only an empty unresolved set is terminal — rev 1.12, v5) and records `posting_attribution` (T-SL-11) for every posting it produces, with the attribution input view compared to the previous head's evidence (D-96; rev 1.11 per portion). Rev 1.123, second row (supervisor ruling R-97 (1); item LED-SEAL-REOPEN-RACE-1): `journals/subledger.py::post` seals the lines as they are stored — it sends `is_post_reopen = false`, takes back the value the DB-07 guard stored (`INSERT … RETURNING`) and hashes that; it reads no period state, so a change of the state in flight at the insert cannot part the seal from the stored posting (04 §14.1, the DB-06 note). Before its first insert `persist` calls `period_ends.window_held`: the group row `FOR UPDATE`, then — under the scope of the computation that asks, the tenant's every entity (DG-KRN-UOW-05; until rev 1.245 through a block of DG-KRN-DB-05 that issued no statement inside a computation; DG-ARC-16 (3) holds the read to that one caller) — the read that finds whether a close run of one of the group's entities has a `SUCCEEDED` first period-end step for a period that is still postable, which holds the state rows of those periods `FOR SHARE` (DG-KRN-DB-08 (1c)). `after_computation(bundle, held)` then decides the mark from what was held and reads nothing: only inside a window it runs the three period-end passes dry over the bundle of the computation — three engine runs more inside a window, none outside (05 PERF-03). The module also holds the engine entry of a pass (`engine_pass`) and the rule of an unposted period end (`unposted`), which `domain/close/period_end.py` imports; the shared compute path changes in two calls of that module — one before the first insert, one in the statement that writes the head. Rev 1.140 (PRD ERR-72; supervisor rulings R-105 (3) and of 2026-10-01 on the lane's measurement; 04 §14.1 "A command recorded before a lock" rev 1.157; 05 RCP-18 rev 1.96): directly after `window_held`, `persist` calls `_refuse_a_lock_met(uow, bundle, found)`. When the bundle holds an event whose `recorded_at` is the transaction timestamp — an event recorded in this transaction — it reads `period_lock` for the bundle's entities and books and raises `problems.period_state_moved()` — 409 `lock-conflict` under `problems.RULE_PERIOD_STATE_MOVED` — when a record's `cutoff_known_at` is later than `bundle.known_at`, the bundle's record-time cutoff (`bundles.record_cutoff`); the comparison is strict. The rule's name and its two sentences are the kernel's (`erev_api/problems.py`): `approvals.engine.decide` catches the problem of a hook (`is_period_state_moved`) and answers with the decision's form, `PERIOD_STATE_MOVED_DECISION_DETAIL` — "Decide again" — after the decision's savepoint is rolled back; the request stays pending. The problem leaves `compute_group` by its `Problem` branch (DG-CMD-09): the savepoint is rolled back, nothing is stored, and the command's transaction ends with it. The read takes no lock, so the order of DG-KRN-DB-08 is unchanged; it stays AFTER `window_held` — before the window's rows are shared a lock decision in flight is neither committed nor waiting, and the read would prove nothing. A product line without a key would be read back in the spelling of decision L3-1-Q-32 and, where that is not its subject, reversed and posted again at every later computation — the defect of the item — which is why the door refuses it: `tests/architecture/test_subledger_door.py` pins the three callers and their argument, and that nothing else inserts into the table. A test builder that posts through the door without the argument, or inserts a row, writes a line without a key; the table admits it (the column is nullable until the builders supply it), and `tests/support/ledger_door.py` makes a product command post that way for a witness of such a line. It reads under the tenant's scope, which it opens itself as `period_ends.hold_windows` does (`system_entity_scope`; both call sites stand in the list of DG-ARC-16 (2)), and through the module's private read: it does not name `period_ends.window_held`, which stays the computation's alone (DG-ARC-16 (3), rev 1.245). Its callers: `compute_job.defer_compute`; `compute_job._refused`, before a `QUARANTINED` or `FAILED` computation is stored; `imports.commit._apply_plans`, after the plans; `integrations.sync.ingest_document`, inside the document's savepoint; `policies.overrides._apply_ssp_override`. The job of an import runs a commit refused under this rule once more (`imports.commit._commit_after_a_lock`), and the job of a sync run its apply transaction — `ingest_document` passes this refusal on instead of recording a failure (`integrations.sync.run_sync`; 05 §5.6 rev 1.195). Every function that appends to a stream is named with its ending by DG-ARC-19. | DG-CMD-11 | Handler location and naming: `erev_api/domain/<area>/commands.py`, function `<verb>_<object>` with signature `(uow, *, <ids>, expected_version?, body) -> <Name>Out`. Routes contain no domain logic. |
| DG-CMD-12 | Status codes: 200 for a command on an existing resource, 201 for creation (with `Location`), 202 for a job (API-C-12). Single-resource responses carry `ETag` (API-C-08). |
| DG-CMD-13 | Queries (`queries.py`) use `tenant_session(read_only=True)`, apply API-C-10 time-travel semantics and never write. A GET route writes nothing either, with one bounded exception (rev 1.89; security finding SC-8, supervisor ruling R-32; 04 T-CLS-03 rev 1.106): before the close cockpit and checklist reads, the route brings the stored checklist up to date through `close.commands.materialise_checklist` in a SYSTEM unit of work — it commits only when an item was missing or an automatic gate's stored result differed, writes no audit event, and does nothing else (no monitor run, no exception item, no notification). One audit event is the exception (rev 1.291; item CLO-WAIVER-COVERS-LATER-1; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02 20:22; 04 T-CLS-03 rev 1.305): when that materialisation is the first evaluation to count more than a waiver covered, the item's move `WAIVED` → `FAILED` is stored with its `close_checklist_item.evaluate` event, as SYSTEM — a waiver's lapse is a change of a control's state and is audited whoever stores it. Every other store of a read stays silent: one move, once per approved waiver (the item then names no request, and a second lapse needs a second approval). `close.gates._store` is its one place: the flag that keeps a reader's store silent yields to that move alone. (rev 1.115; supervisor rulings R-76 and R-85) **To-date measures.** The contract, obligation and balance reads serve the to-date measures of 04 API-C-10 through `domain/contracts/to_date.py`: `load_nodes` reads the period nodes of the versions of one read in one statement over `calc_trace` and one over `period`; `version_at`, `balance_at` and `measured_at` are pure. The period that contains a date is found among the nodes, each of which carries its period's end (`params.as_of`), so the module reads no entity's calendar: `legal_entity` is RLS-TE and a reader's entities need not cover the performing entity of an obligation or another member of the group. A measure the trace cannot answer raises `to_date.Unreadable` (rule id `API-C-10`); no caller replaces it with the version's stored column. `GET /contracts/{id}`, the obligation reads and the balance read refuse by name; a list row and the API-S-Contract a command answers with carry `kpis: null` instead (`contract_out(..., refuse=False)`, the default a command takes), because a command is not undone by the read of its result. The version reads pass no overlay and answer the version as stored. (rev 1.157; supervisor ruling R-114 (f)) **The remainder at the cut.** `to_date.remainder_at` gives the scheduled and the awaiting-trigger amount of an obligation at the cut (04 API-C-10 rev 1.174 and 1.179; rev 1.162, supervisor ruling R-118 (a)): revenue recognised since the version date leaves the scheduled amount first and the awaiting-trigger amount for what the scheduled amount cannot cover, with no predicate — the reader follows the split the engine stored; revenue that a cut before the version date gives back returns to the part the version's own trace names (rev 1.292; 04 API-C-10 rev 1.178; item ENG-USAGE-FIXED-SCHEDULE-1; supervisor rulings R-116 (a) and R-118 (a)): `nodes_of` keeps, per obligation, the `pattern` and `held` parameters of the version-state node `scheduled_amount:<obligation>:-` (`Nodes.patterns`; the measure stands in `MEASURES` and in `WITHOUT_BALANCES`, and `nodes_at` keeps every version state, so a list read and a report have it), `version_at` hands them to `remainder_at`, and the revenue returns to the scheduled amount when the node says `DETERMINISTIC` and not held (ENGINE_SPEC_B S09-R-45, S09-R-44), to the awaiting-trigger amount otherwise; a look-back whose trace holds no such node of the obligation raises `Unreadable`, and so does a remainder below zero. The module names no recognition method and no hold type: the predicate is the engine's (`erev_engine.stages.s09_recognition.is_deterministic`, read by the engine at three places), and the reader takes the engine's word for it from the trace. `ObligationAt` carries both amounts and `VersionAt` what left each (`scheduled_moved`, `awaiting_moved`); `queries.py` serves those and counts `pending_trigger_count` at the cut, and reads neither amount from the stored column once a cut was read. `tests/answer_keys/test_answer_key_reads.py` holds the rule against the corpus: for every obligation at every checkpoint the reported allocation is the revenue, the scheduled and the awaiting-trigger amount, neither part is below zero, and each part equals the leaf a key states for it. **The explanation of a balance (rev 1.157; item EXPLAIN-BALANCE-LINKS-1).** A read that serves a figure names its Explain address in `links`; a screen builds none from ids. `queries._balance_links` gives the three addresses of a T-CON-09 row — the row's id and the period the balance was read at — to the header's balance entries and to the balances read, null where no node holds the figure. `tests/domain/contracts/test_to_date_reads.py` follows every `links.explain…` address the contract reads send, as sent, to a 200: a link that names a subject the Explain route does not find fails there. **Reports at a date (rev 1.162; item RPT-ASOF-FIGURES-1; supervisor ruling R-116 (c)).** A report that states an obligation at a date reads it through `domain/reports/cuts.py`, this rule's reader for the versions of a run: `load(session, version_ids, days)` reads the versions, their obligation versions, the member contracts' external ids and the period nodes once, for the dates the run states; `Versions.at` and `Versions.balance` state an obligation and a member's balances at the cut of one of those dates — another date is the caller's mistake and raises `ValueError`; `obligations_at` is the read for the versions and dates of a run. A report holds every version of its entities and a trace holds a node per measure, subject and period, so `to_date.load_nodes(..., days=)` reads `PORTION` versions per statement and keeps of each trace only what a read at those dates reaches (`to_date.nodes_at`, pure): of every period series the first and the last node and, around each date and around the horizon that caps it, the last node before and the first on or after; of a member's undated balances the latest node at or before each kept period; every version state; no release of a consideration payable, whose movement is measured from the version's own date — so a report takes the obligations and the balance rows of a read and never `VersionAt.release_moved`. A contract read still takes the nodes of its page of versions whole. `scheduled_after` is the one rule the reports add (ENGINE_SPEC_B S15-R-01 rev 1.127): the schedule lines of the periods after the cut state the scheduled part of an obligation's remainder when it has one, and a version whose later lines do not add up to that part is refused by name (`ScheduleUnreadable`, rule `S15-R-01`). `revenue_waterfall.population` — and through it the dashboard's revenue panel and the frozen WATERFALL dataset —, `rpo.measure` with `rpo_of` — and through them the RPO report, its rollforward, the dashboard's RPO figure and the frozen RPO dataset — and `latest_contract_status.build` state their figures so. **The waterfall's entity (rev 1.195; supervisor rulings R-78 (d) and R-121 (g), and the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-01 on the lane's finding on the Home; SCREENS_B RPT-01 rev 1.69, SCREENS §2.5 rev 1.41).** `revenue_waterfall._obligations` selects an obligation by its PERFORMING entity (`obligation_version.performing_entity_id`), which is the row's entity for its label, its periods, its as-of period and the functional-currency test; `_recognized` reads the `REVENUE` subledger lines of that entity's books (`subledger_line.entity_id`), so no line is stated under an entity whose journal does not hold it, and `TO_WATERFALL_EQ_JE_REVENUE` compares one entity's revenue with the same entity's journal. The frozen WATERFALL dataset reads the same population, and so does the Home's revenue panel. `dashboard.home` reads its three figure panels — revenue, contract liability, RPO — inside `every_entity_scope`, as the reports' jobs read their datasets: an obligation of the context's entities can be performed by, or belong to a contract of, another entity, whose `contract` or `schedule_line` rows a reader of one entity does not see — under the caller's scope the Home left such revenue out for a reader of the performing entity and was refused whole by rule S15-R-01 for a reader of the contracting entity, where a reader of every entity got the figures. The panels return sums and no row; the context's entities are the caller's own; pending approvals, open exceptions and the close panel stay under the caller's scope. Until rev 1.195 the population was read by the contracting entity. **Entry at activation, late events and the look-back (rev 1.196; item RPT-RPO-ROLLFWD-1; supervisor ruling R-121 (g); ENGINE_SPEC_B S15-R-24a, S15-R-12, S15-R-08 rev 1.161).** `tie_outs.ENTRY_EVENTS` names the events at whose effective date a contract enters the disclosures (`CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` for the book its payload names). `rpo.load` keeps, per version, the entry date of each contract among the version's causes (`_Version.entries`), and `rpo.chains_of` dates the first included version of a contract's chain by it — never before the version it follows — so `Store.version_at`, `rows_at`, `rollforward_lines` and the dashboard's RPO figure read the contract from that day; `contract_history.latest_where(entered=True)` applies the same rule in SQL for RPT-11 (`_entries`: the first included version by record time and number, its entry events found by id through `unnest` of the version's causes), and RPT-12 and RPT-30 call it without. `rpo.ROLLFORWARD_LINES` holds `LATE_EVENTS` where the engine's own rollforward has it: the closing version's revenue to the day before the range less the opening version's, both read through `Store.at`; the report's columns and the frozen `RPO_ROLLFORWARD` dataset take the line from that tuple, and the re-lock difference, which keeps a list of its own, declares `late_events` a measure (`relock_diff.KEY_COLUMNS`; a unit pin ties that list to the report's money columns). `to_date.version_at` brings an obligation that stage 15 left out at d_v because it was satisfied by then — its state node carries no `excluded` parameter and the stored status is `SATISFIED` — back into the RPO of a cut at which it is not yet satisfied (`rpo_moved` falls by its remainder at the cut). No module of `domain/reports` names `scheduled_amount` or `awaiting_trigger_amount` of a version table in a statement (`tests/architecture/test_report_cut_figures.py`): a builder that prints a version's own row at its effective date selects the row whole and says which date it prints (`contract_history`). `tests/answer_keys/test_answer_key_reads.py` holds for every obligation at every checkpoint of the corpus that what the reports state as scheduled is the scheduled part, so that the waterfall's total is the allocation and the RPO the remainder, and that the kept nodes answer as the whole trace does — at every checkpoint's date and, at a key's last checkpoint, at every period end of the group's entities and a week before each. **An entity reference beyond the caller's scope.** Who may read a contract reads its obligations whole (04 API-S-Obligation). `queries._entity_refs` first reads the references under the caller's scope; for an entity that scope excludes it reads again under the tenant's scope — `system_entity_scope(session)`, DG-KRN-DB-05 (rev 1.126: the block replaces the second read-only session this row described at rev 1.115) — and selects `id`, `code` and `name` of `legal_entity` for those ids. No other statement runs inside the block and no other column of the entity is read there. |
| DG-CMD-14 | Handlers never call route functions or other handlers' transactions. Shared logic lives in domain modules that take a `UnitOfWork` or a `Session`. |
| DG-CMD-15 | Previews are one helper (rev 1.59; D-98 140 Q-1). A command that previews a change calls `events.dry_run_summary(session, current, known_at, pending_events, *, pending_contract_id)` — `bundles.build(…, DRY_RUN, …)`, the engine once, `impact_summary` — and writes nothing: `events.run_preview`, `estimates._dry_run`, `adjustments.run_preview` and the measure of `adjustments.create` / `update` / `submit` (rev 1.98: the adjustment's `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT_APPLIED` pending beside its T-SL-05 row; `dry_run_summary(…, book_code=…)` summarises the book the adjustment names, default the primary book), `modifications.run_preview` (exactly ONE candidate applying boundary pending — the row's `CONTRACT_AMENDED` — beside the row as a pending native T-CON-06 input), `modifications.classify` (NO applying event: `pending_events = ()` and `pending_modifications = (row,)`; the engine's stage 13 `_pending_proposals` proposes for the bundle modification no event applies, so classification applies nothing; rev 1.69 — D-98 140 AMENDMENT 15: `classify` writes `proposed_treatments`, `chosen_treatments` where unset, `treatment_summary`, resets the preview members, and writes the `ssp_basis` CLASSIFICATION DEFAULTS — the version the dry run actually selected per line of the row (`selected_ssp_versions` over the output's `ssp_book_version_key` for existing obligations; the proposal detail `ssp_version[<key>]` for added lines, mapped to the APPROVED version id), `is_override` false, no justification; an authored `is_override = true` entry is kept; the S06-R-03 override checks (`separate_errors`' label rule, `ssp_basis_mismatches`, `ssp_selection_mismatches`, `ssp_applied_mismatches`) and `booking_body`'s `custom_attributes` pin read override entries only) and CTR-16's contract provider, which iterates the helper per affected group. A preview's provenance is the bundle's `input_sha256` and `engine_version` carried inside the stored `IMPACT_PREVIEW` file (REQ-PLT-015), together with the candidate's retained basis — the target contract id and head, the content hash of the row the candidate was built from and every consumed group member's id and stream head; a command that consumes a stored preview (`modifications.submit`) re-derives that basis under the protecting locks and refuses a stale preview (422 REQ-PLT-015 `PREVIEW_STALE`) instead of relabelling its result with the current heads, and approval re-verifies the content hash (`assert_fresh_basis`, DG-KRN-APR-05). A regroup-after-posting pair applies ONE applying boundary per side — the `REGROUPED` event over the referenced native rows, both sides in one unit of work or neither — never a `CONTRACT_AMENDED` beside it. A dry run never writes a `contract_computation` row, a version or a line. (Amended in place 2026-09-21 under rev 1.59 per D-98 140-A2 — Codex production-20260921-1608 §1 / 1614 §2.) (Amended in place 2026-09-21 under rev 1.59 per D-98 140-A14 — Codex production-20260921-2029: for a `SEPARATE_CONTRACT` choice `modifications.run_preview` verifies the `ssp_basis` override — an APPROVED id, the line's label, POL-070 `NAMED_VERSION` — BEFORE the dry-run booking and the version the booking actually selected AFTER it, both before the `IMPACT_PREVIEW` is stored; a failure fails the job by name (`S06-R-03`) and retains no pointer / hash — the same checks `/submit` re-runs over the retained selection.) (Rev 1.75, lane FIX-A: `impact_summary` takes each obligation's catch-up from the dry-run version's `catch_up_amount` — the catch-ups of the events first included in it, ENGINE_SPEC_B S09-R-36 — never from a difference of `revenue_cum` between the stored and the dry-run version; `modifications.run_preview` passes the helper's summary through `boundary_summary`, which measures the ONE candidate boundary's remaining allocation and RPO at the boundary from its `catch_up@<event key>` nodes (`boundary_measure`: A − C per side with C by CV-63 `cumulative_posted`) and names the chosen treatments; `modifications.classify` also returns the BR-MOD-01 prefill — `questionnaire_prefill` over the row's `mod_class@` / `mod_price_test@` nodes — in `prefill_reasons` and the response's `questionnaire`, and writes none of it; the stored `IMPACT_PREVIEW` document carries the request's `before` / `after` members (`request_sides`) and `modifications.submit` hands the row's retained file and hash to `approvals.submit`, DG-KRN-APR-01.) |

### 6.2 State machines (SM)

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/db/transitions.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TableTransitions:
    table: str
    status_column: str | None                               # None when only a column allow-list applies
    updatable_columns: frozenset[str]                        # the IM-S column list of the 04 table header
    pairs: frozenset[tuple[str, str]]                        # allowed (from, to) status pairs
    editable_while: frozenset[str] = frozenset()             # statuses in which every column may change

TRANSITIONS: Final[Mapping[str, TableTransitions]]           # every IM-S table of docs/04-DATA_MODEL.md

def apply(session: Session, table: str, row_id: UUID, *, to_status: str | None,
          set_values: Mapping[str, Any], expected_status: str | None = None,
          expected_row_version: int | None = None) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
def transition_trigger_sql(table: str) -> str: ...
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-SM-01 | `TRANSITIONS` is the single source for DB-03 (04 §14.1). Pairs come from the 04 enumerations and table notes (E-12, E-13, E-26, E-34, E-40, T-REF-07, T-CON-24 and the others) and must equal the PRD state machines (docs/02-PRD.md SM-nn), which use the same E literals (B1-006). Where a literal differs, 04 governs (D-73); a differing pair is a spec question for the supervisor, recorded as SPEC-Q (DG-DONE-12), not a local choice. |
| DG-SM-02 | `apply` validates the pair and the column allow-list in Python first → 409 `invalid-transition` with `errors[0].rule_id = "DB-03"`; then it issues the conditional UPDATE (`WHERE id = :id AND status = :expected_status [AND row_version = :v]`). The database trigger enforces the same rule (`EREV-TRN-001`). |
| DG-SM-03 | Every status change writes an audit event `<table>.<to_status lowercase>` with `before.status` and `after.status`. |
| DG-SM-04 | DG-ARC-07 regenerates `transition_trigger_sql` for each table and compares it with the function source installed after `upgrade head`. |

### 6.3 Lists: pagination, filtering and sorting (LST)

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/api/lists.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class FilterSpec:
    name: str
    column: sa.ColumnElement[Any]
    kind: Literal["exact", "in", "min", "max", "from", "to", "bool"]

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ListSpec:
    resource: str
    sort_keys: Mapping[str, sa.ColumnElement[Any]]          # API-R catalogue sort keys
    default_sort: str                                        # "-id"
    filters: Mapping[str, FilterSpec]
    search_columns: tuple[sa.ColumnElement[Any], ...] = ()

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ListParams:
    limit: int; cursor: str | None; sort: str | None; q: str | None; count: bool
    filters: Mapping[str, tuple[str, ...]]

def list_params(request: Request, limit: int = Query(50, ge=1, le=500), cursor: str | None = None,
                sort: str | None = None, q: str | None = None, count: bool = False) -> ListParams: ...
def paginate(session: Session, stmt: sa.Select[Any], spec: ListSpec, params: ListParams) -> ListResult: ...
def encode_cursor(sort: str, filters_sha256: str, last_values: Sequence[Any]) -> str: ...
def decode_cursor(cursor: str, *, sort: str, filters_sha256: str) -> list[Any]: ...
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-LST-01 | Keyset pagination over the sort columns plus `id` (UUIDv7) as the final tie-breaker. Response body `{"items": […], "next_cursor": string or null}` (API-C-09, API-S-List). There are no offset parameters. |
| DG-LST-02 | `limit` defaults to 50 with a maximum of 500. `sort` accepts `key` or `-key` from the resource's catalogue keys; an unknown key → 422 `validation-failed`, rule `API-C-09`. The default order is `-id`. |
| DG-LST-03 | Cursor = base64url (no padding) of canonical JSON `{"v": 1, "s": sort, "f": filters_sha256, "k": last_values}`. A cursor whose `s` or `f` differs from the current request → 422 `validation-failed`, rule `API-C-09`. RLS scopes every page, so a tampered cursor exposes nothing. |
| DG-LST-04 | Filters are exact-match query parameters named after fields. A repeated parameter means IN. Range filters exist only where the catalogue lists them (`value_min`, `value_max`, `from`, `to`, `created_from`). Unknown parameters → 422. |
| DG-LST-05 | `q` performs a case-insensitive substring match with `ILIKE` over the listed search columns. `%`, `_` and `\` in the input are escaped. No extensions (NC-18). |
| DG-LST-06 | `count=true` adds response header `X-Erev-Total-Count`, computed as `SELECT count(*) FROM (<stmt> LIMIT 100001)`; the value is `100000+` when capped. The DataGrid uses it for `aria-rowcount` (DS-CMP-10; DG-OQ-07). |
| DG-LST-07 | List queries are read-only and use indexes that lead with `tenant_id` (NC-03). |
| DG-LST-08 | Order (rev 1.164; supervisor ruling R-116 (b)). `ORDER BY <key> [DESC], id DESC`; a row without a value for the key comes last in either direction. For a key that is never NULL in a row of the list — a NOT NULL column of the table (or table alias) the list's `id` belongs to — `paginate` leaves `NULLS LAST` out of the statement: the order is the same, and a b-tree read backwards supplies it, whereas `DESC NULLS LAST` is no order an index yields and sorts the whole filtered set before the limit. A column of a joined table, an expression and a column of a subquery keep the clause. The cursor comparison is the same for every key. |
| DG-LST-09 | Enumeration filters (rev 1.164; supervisor ruling R-116). A filter value that is one of its `FilterSpec.choices` — checked before the statement is built — is bound as a value of the column's type; any other filter value is text cast to the column's type (DG-LST-04). The difference is what PostgreSQL knows when it plans: the first is a constant, the second is converted only when the statement runs. A partial index on a status or a kind is proved from a constant alone (DG-KRN-DB-10 (2)): with `status = CAST(:text AS <enumeration>)` a list by status entered no partial index and read every row of the tenant. |
| DG-LST-10 | No member that costs a statement per row (rev 1.182; supervisor ruling of 2026-10-01 on the lane's pre-build line, item PERF-PERIODS-LIST-1; 04 §16.8 rev 1.199). A list answers a page in a number of statements that does not depend on the number of its rows: the page itself, and ONE statement for each member that is read from other tables, for all rows of the page at once, keyed by the rows' ids. A member that needs a statement of its own for each row — a count over other tables, the evaluation of a gate, a derived figure — does not belong to the list: the single read of the resource carries it, and 04 says that the member is null in a row of the list, and why. `GET /periods` is the precedent: `blockers` cost a statement over 23 tables for every row and no reader took them from the list; `close_run` and `current_lock` are read for the page in two statements (`close.queries.list_period_views`). Before a per-row statement is rewritten as one statement over the page it is MEASURED: built over the rows it is planned without the constants of the single read and, where it names a partition by a value, without pruning (04 rev 1.199, log row). Enforcer: a test on the route that counts the statements of two page sizes with `tests/support/plans.py` `sent` and holds them equal (`backend/tests/api/test_periods_list_page.py`). |
| DG-LST-11 | Search is not a list's `q` (rev 1.178; supervisor ruling R-116 (f), item G-5; 04 §16.13 rev 1.195). `GET /search` finds a record by the BEGINNING OF A WORD of its `primary` or `secondary`, and the rule has one implementation, the database's: 04 §16.13 "Matching and order" states the two expressions — how `q` is split into terms and when a text matches a term — and `domain/contracts/search.py` asks the database for the terms and binds each as the tail of the pattern; no second definition of a word exists in Python. A scope is ONE statement over the scope's rows under the caller's row policy: it selects `id`, `primary`, `secondary`, the instant the row was last written and what `href` and `status` need, keeps the rows every term matches, orders by (exact `primary`, `primary` alone matches, the rest), then newest, then `id`, and takes `limit + 1`. A member that is not in the scope's own rows is read for the page at once (DG-LST-10: the status of the obligations). The cursor is the list kernel's (`encode_cursor`), bound to `q` and the scope. A scope never matches with `ILIKE '%…%'` — a substring cannot be answered by an index, and the sentence of 04 must not change when the key table of item SEARCH-KEYS-1 replaces the scan; the `q` of a list stays DG-LST-05. Enforcer: `backend/tests/api/test_search_api.py`. |

### 6.4 API routes and schemas (API)

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-API-01 | One router module per API-R row under `erev_api/api/v1/`, named after the resource (`contracts.py`, `ssp_books.py`, `journal_runs.py`). The router tag is the API-R id and name, for example `API-R-28 Contracts`. |
| DG-API-02 | Paths, fields and enum values follow API-C-14 and NC-19 exactly. |
| DG-API-03 | Schemas live in `erev_api/schemas/<resource>.py`. Class names drop the `API-S-` prefix and append `In` for requests and `Out` for responses (`API-S-ContractCreate` → `ContractCreateIn`, `API-S-Contract` → `ContractOut`). Request models use `ConfigDict(extra="forbid")`. Response models are built explicitly from row mappings. |
| DG-API-04 | `operation_id = "<resource>_<verb>"` and stays stable; the generated TypeScript client depends on it. |
| DG-API-05 | Every route declares `responses` for each problem slug it can return, through `problem_responses(*slugs)`. |
| DG-API-06 | Middleware echoes or generates `X-Request-Id` (API-C-15) and sets `X-Erev-Tenant-Kind` on authenticated responses (API-C-02). |
| DG-API-07 | Rate limiting per API client (API-C-16) uses an in-process token bucket keyed by `api_client.id`. Login and MFA endpoints are limited per normalised email and source address (REQ-SEC-004); the other unauthenticated routes of the sign-in surface share the per-address bucket through one dependency, `admit_address` (rev 1.134; 05 SAR-13). A multi-instance deployment approximates the limit per instance; the runbook states this. |
| DG-API-08 | `/api/v1/healthz` returns 200 when the process runs. `/api/v1/readyz` returns 200 when a connection as `erev_app` passes the role guard and the Alembic head in the database equals the code head. |
| DG-API-09 | Mock adapters (D-72; rev 1.1). Mock servers for NetSuite, QuickBooks Online, Salesforce, Stripe and the OIDC IdP are routers mounted in-process under `/api/v1/__mocks__/<adapter>/…`, with `<adapter>` ∈ {`netsuite`, `qbo`, `salesforce`, `stripe`, `oidc`}, plus `/api/v1/__mocks__/__admin/reset`, `/api/v1/__mocks__/__admin/faults` and `/api/v1/__mocks__/__admin/state` with the behaviour of 05 ADP-21 to ADP-24. `create_app()` mounts them only when `EREV_ENV` is `dev`, `test` or `e2e`, and never under `production`. They are registered with `include_in_schema=False`, so `docs/api/openapi.json` never contains them, and they are unauthenticated in those environments (DG-KRN-AUTH-03). Adapters reach them at `http://127.0.0.1:<EREV_API_PORT, or EREV_E2E_API_PORT under e2e>/api/v1/__mocks__/<adapter>`; 05 CFG-19 `EREV_MOCKS_BASE_URL` is not used. Unit tests use `httpx.MockTransport` or `httpx.ASGITransport` over the same handlers. No process binds a port outside `docs/00-GOAL.md` §5. Rev 1.128 (BUILD_SPEC CLO-15; 05 ADP-22, ADP-23): the NetSuite and QuickBooks Online mocks keep a ledger of the journals they receive and answer a computed trial balance; `POST /api/v1/__mocks__/<adapter>/__erp/documents` and `POST /api/v1/__mocks__/netsuite/__erp/accounts` state what the ERP itself holds. They are mock administration like `__admin/*`: mounted with the mocks, absent under `production` (DG-ARC-04, `test_mock_routes_absent_in_production`). [J] No extra ports on a shared machine. |
| DG-API-10 | The OpenAPI document is OpenAPI 3.1 with `info.version = "1.0.0"`, committed as `docs/api/openapi.json` (DG-LAY-07, REQ-PLT-032). |
| DG-API-11 | A response member that names a person is API-S-Actor, read with its row (rev 1.122; 04 §16.0). A member whose value is a principal — `created_by`, `published_by`, `resolved_by`, `approver`, `on_behalf_of` — is `ActorOut`, or `ActorOut` or null where it may name nobody, and never a bare id that a client resolves through `GET /users` (`user.manage`). The name is read where the row is read: `erev_api.domain.platform.actors.named(<id column>, tenant_id=<tenant column>)` is a labelled column of the row's own SELECT — one scalar lookup on the primary key of `app_user` and one on the primary key of `api_client` — and `actors.actor(id, kind, named)` builds the member from the row (`actors.member` and `actors.member_actor` for a row that names a person by membership); the builders written before this rule read the names of a page in one statement (`approval_queries.display_names`). Either way a page costs the same number of statements for one row and for fifty: a read per row is a defect, and a test of a list that shows a person pins the count. `display_name` comes from the identity tables as they stand at the read and never from an event or audit payload (05 PRV-07), and nothing in the lookup depends on the reader's entity scope (`app_user` RLS-NONE-U, `api_client` RLS-T). The Actor replaces the id. It sits beside an id only where that id is a key a command takes — `ExceptionItemOut.owner` beside `owner_membership_id`, the key of `assign` (04 §16.14) — and is then read-only. Enforcer: `backend/tests/architecture/test_person_members.py` reads the OpenAPI document and fails on a response member named `*_by`, `*_by_id`, `on_behalf_of_id`, `actor_id`, `approver_id`, `preparer_id`, `reviewer_id` or `signer_id` that is a bare uuid and is not in its list. The list is closed — it holds the members that reach no screen as a person today and is only ever shortened, each member converted with the screen that first shows it: `AttachmentOut.created_by` and `.voided_by`, `FileOut.created_by`, `FxRateSetVersionOut` and `FxRateSetVersionDetailOut` `.created_by` and `.published_by`, `MappingProfileOut.published_by`, `PobTemplateVersionOut.created_by` and `.published_by`, `RuleSetVersionOut.published_by`, `SodRuleOut.published_by`, `TenantOut.created_by`, `.updated_by` and `.ai_disabled_by`. `TenantSnapshotOut.created_by` left the list with SF-15:sandbox, the screen that shows it (rev 1.160; 04 rev 1.177). |
| DG-API-12 | A route whose request body is a multipart form is an `UploadRoute` (`erev_api/api/uploads.py`; rev 1.172; 04 API-C-17; ruling R-111 (8)). FastAPI parses a form before it solves a route's dependencies, so a plain route receives and spools the body before its guard runs. `UploadRoute` runs `admit_upload` first: the route's session guard (`get_request_context`: session or token, CSRF, rate, second factor), `refuse_operator_command`, `refuse_inactive_tenant` and `validate_idempotency_key`, then `attachments.upload_ceiling(ctx)` — the largest T-PLT-29 limit among the purposes the caller may upload, 0 for none. A declared length above the ceiling plus `MULTIPART_OVERHEAD_BYTES` is refused before the body is read (403 through `attachments.authorize` for a ceiling of 0, else 422 `upload-type-not-allowed`), and the handler reads the body through a `receive` that counts to the same bound. The command dependency then runs as on every command, guard included. `backend/tests/architecture/test_routes.py` holds every multipart route to `UploadRoute` and to `middleware.UPLOAD_PATHS`. Rev 1.270 (item AUTH-BEFORE-BODY-1): the session question in front of the body is no longer the upload route's alone — `GuardedRoute.get_route_handler` asks it for every route with a guard (DG-KRN-AUTH-09), and the command's guard is answered from what the identity store answered to `admit_upload` unless the form took longer than `KEPT_FOR`. `UploadRoute` keeps what only an upload needs before its form is parsed: the operator's and the tenant-status refusals, the key, the ceiling and the bounded `receive`. |


| Id | Rule | Rationale [J] |
|---|---|---|
| DG-MIG-01 | `backend/alembic.ini` and `env.py`: owner URL from `Settings.owner_database_url()`; `version_table_schema = "erev"`; `transaction_per_migration = True`; role guard DG-ENV-12 before running. Rev 1.264 (item MIGRATION-STATEMENT-TIMEOUT-1; 05 TXN-03 rev 1.199): `env.py` takes its engine from `erev_api.db.session.migration_engine()`, the one engine whose connections carry `statement_timeout` from `Settings.migration_statement_timeout_seconds` (`EREV_MIGRATION_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 30 to 86400, default 1800) in place of the request's 30 s; `lock_timeout` stays 10 s, as on every connection. A revision's statement may run long; its wait for a lock may not. A revision and `migration_ops` therefore set neither timeout — no `SET`, no `set_config` of `statement_timeout` or `lock_timeout` — which `tests/unit/test_migration_timeouts.py` holds: a statement that needs more time is given it by the setting, for that run (runbook, "Migrations"). | Migrations run as `erev_owner` only (D-42); a schema change is not a request, and a schema change that waits for a lock holds the requests behind it (rev 1.264) |
| DG-MIG-02 | Revisions are handwritten; autogenerate is never used. File name `NNNN_<slug>.py`, `revision = "NNNN"`. The docstring names the BUILD_SPEC item and the 04 ids created (T-…, E-…, DB-…). | RLS, triggers, grants and partitions are invisible to autogenerate |
| DG-MIG-03 | One revision per BUILD_SPEC item that changes the schema. A revision is self-contained for the objects it creates: tables with keys and indexes, composite foreign keys to existing tables (NC-06), RLS templates, IM-class triggers and grants (`apply_class`), transition triggers, partitions. A foreign key to a table created later is added by the revision that creates that later table. The 04 §18 table fixes dependency order, not revision boundaries (DG-OQ-02). | The DB-14 lint stays green after every item |
| DG-MIG-04 | Every revision implements `downgrade()`, which removes exactly what `upgrade()` created, in reverse order (DG-OQ-01). Exception (rev 1.48, lane F-SNP; D-98 candidate 118): a row a later revision seeds into an append-only table (DB-01 refuses DELETE with EREV-IMM-001 — `registry_parameter`, `permission`, …) is not deleted by its `downgrade()`, which is then a documented no-op whose docstring names the row and the table-creating revision whose downgrade drops the table with the row; DG-MIG-08's rationale governs (append-only data is never dropped by a rollback) and the round trip stays complete because the creating revision removes the table. First instance: 0063 `platform.snapshot_retention_families` (0003 creates `registry_parameter`). | Supports the round-trip test; DB-01 |
| DG-MIG-05 | `backend/tests/pg/test_migrations.py`: `test_single_head`; `test_upgrade_downgrade_upgrade` (reset schema, `upgrade head`, snapshot the catalogue of schema `erev` and the Procrastinate objects, covering tables, columns, types, constraints, indexes, policies, triggers, function sources and grants; `downgrade base`; assert that no application objects remain; `upgrade head`; assert the snapshot equals the first); `test_lint_after_upgrade` (DB-14). | Catches broken downgrades and non-deterministic DDL |
| DG-MIG-06 | Enum values are added with `add_enum_value` in a revision before any code uses them. Downgrade uses `remove_enum_value`: rename the type, create the type without the value, alter columns with `USING col::text::<type>`, drop the old type. It fails when a row uses the value. Rev 1.171: a check constraint or an index whose stored expression holds a constant of the type — a status check over enum literals, the predicate of a partial index — is dropped before the rename and re-created after the old type is gone, from the definition the catalogue printed before the rename (`EnumDependent`; found through `pg_depend`). A check created in the revision that adds a label compares the column as text (the 0060 precedent): a new label is no enum literal before the transaction commits. | PostgreSQL cannot drop enum values directly; a stored expression keeps constants of the renamed type, and the column's conversion then finds no operator between the two types (first met by revision 0114 on E-12) |
| DG-MIG-07 | Migrations seed only global catalogues: `currency` from `ISO_4217`, `permission` from `CATALOGUE`, `registry_parameter` from `POLICY_PARAMETERS` and `PLATFORM_PARAMETERS`, `report_definition`, `import_template`. Tenant data is never seeded by migrations. Report-definition texts (rev 1.34; D-98 candidate 98): the catalogue (`erev_api.domain.reports.catalogue`) is the source of truth; until the first production database exists, a definition-text change regenerates the 0048 `REPORT_DEFINITION_SEED` literal from `catalogue.seed_statement()` so `test_revision_seed_equals_fresh_rendering` stays the drift oracle and every lane / test database rebuilds; from 1.0 a definition-text change never edits 0048 — it adds a versioned `report_definition` row (version n+1; IM-A, no UPDATE) through a new Alembic revision and the seed test compares the latest version. Metadata corrections of seeded `registry_parameter` rows (rev 1.53; D-98 candidate 125): a seeded row is never updated; a correction of its `value_schema` / `description` / `source_ref` / `section` is appended as a complete T-PLT-47 `registry_parameter_correction` row by a new Alembic revision (first: 0066), every catalogue reader uses the effective relation (latest correction COALESCEd over the seed) for rows, filters, search and pagination, and the seed drift oracle compares the revision's literal with the Python catalogue. | 04 §18 revision 0002 content; T-RPT-01 versioning |
| DG-MIG-08 | Downgrades run only in the round-trip test on `erev_test` or `erev_rv_*`. Production and the dev database are forward-fix only; `make migrate` never downgrades. | Append-only data must never be dropped by a rollback |
| DG-MIG-09 | The revision introducing jobs installs the Procrastinate schema SQL shipped with the pinned library version into schema `public`, as `erev_owner`, with the §14.2 grants to `erev_app`. Its downgrade drops those objects. A Procrastinate version change needs a revision applying the library's migration scripts. | NC-01 |
| DG-MIG-10 | Each partitioned parent (`audit_event`, `schedule_line`, `subledger_line`) is created with `create_monthly_partitions` from 2018-01 through 2032-12 plus a default partition, in the same revision (04 §1.6). | PT-MPE, PT-MOC |
| DG-MIG-11 | Every table starts from `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC`; privileges come only from `apply_class` and the explicit §14.2 rows. | DB-13 least privilege |
| DG-MIG-12 | A migration never reads a live Python enum: nothing under `db/migrations/versions` imports `erev_api.enums`, and every revision that creates an enum type passes `create_enum` a literal tuple of labels equal to the labels at that revision's authoring state (inline, a module constant, or a `for name, labels in ENUMS` loop over a module-level literal of pairs). A later label enters the history only through an `add_enum_value` revision (DG-MIG-06). `tests/architecture/test_migration_enum_literals.py` enforces both without a database: the source rule, and the DG-ARC-09 replay of every `upgrade()` under `migration_ops.recording()` — no `ADD VALUE` repeats a label the type already holds, and literal-at-creation ∪ added labels equals the Python mirror's members with the created labels in the mirror's order. | A type created from the live enum already holds every later label, so the later `add_enum_value` revision fails on a fresh database (`DuplicateObject`) while it passes on an upgraded one — the history stops being reproducible (F-ADM landing d350a37a post-check; D-98 candidate 108) |
| DG-MIG-13 | **RLS-independent migration guards (rev 1.60; D-98 128 AMENDMENT 1; integrated batch #6 ci return on 0067).** A migration guard that must observe tenant-table rows as `erev_owner` may not rely on an `EXISTS` (or any query) that `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` can hide: revisions run on the owner connection WITHOUT a tenant context, the tenant policies target `erev_app` (`migration_ops.enable_rls` forces RLS for the owner too), so such a query silently sees no rows while `ADD CONSTRAINT` validation scans every physical row. The guard validates through the constraint itself or another RLS-independent construct — e.g. `ADD CONSTRAINT … CHECK (…)` inside a `DO` block whose `EXCEPTION WHEN check_violation` re-raises the revision's named refusal (`EREV-MIG-<rev>`) — and never weakens RLS, alters roles, synthesizes data or deletes rows; the refusal PROPAGATES so the whole revision transaction rolls back (`transaction_per_migration`), and compatible data must still produce the original effect. A trigger body is not in scope: it runs in the invoking tenant session. Witness both branches in `tests/pg` over a POPULATED database (the round trip of DG-MIG-05 passes only on an empty one). Precedent: 0067's downgrade guard corrected in place (the dev-guide 1.48 pattern for procedural downgrade text). **A new check over earlier pre-release rows (rev 1.96, second row; 01 D-99 (3)).** When a revision adds a check that rows of an earlier pre-release schema do not satisfy, and the revision must still apply to such a database — it carries a change every database has to receive — the check is added `NOT VALID`, which enforces it for every row written from then on, and is validated in the same transaction inside a `DO` block: on a database without such rows (every database created at head) it ends validated; otherwise the validation's `check_violation` is caught inside the block, the constraint stays `NOT VALID`, a NOTICE names the revision (`EREV-MIG-<rev>`) and the revision continues. No row is rewritten and no value synthesized; the validation itself is the RLS-independent probe. Both branches are witnessed in `tests/pg`. First instance: 0084 `ck_period_lock__cutoff_known_at` (`tests/pg/test_migration_0084_lock_cutoff.py`). **A check a downgrade restores over later rows (rev 1.216; the supervisor's message of 2026-10-01 13:32; PRODUCT DEFECT of revision 0111).** The same form serves a downgrade that puts back a narrower check than the rows its revision admitted satisfy: the check is restored `NOT VALID` and validated in a `DO` block; over such rows it stays `NOT VALID`, a NOTICE names the revision and the walk continues, and on a database without them it ends validated, so the DG-MIG-05 round trip is unchanged. The downgrade deletes no such row — the owner connection does not see tenant rows, and a guard deletes nothing — and does not refuse over them: provisioning seeds them for every tenant, so a refusal would stop every walk down through the revision over a populated database. First instance: 0111 restores the gate list of 0047 over a tenant's `CLOSE_RUN_COMPLETED` template row (`tests/pg/test_migration_0111_gate_check.py`); until then it re-added the list validated and failed with a bare `check_violation`, which stopped the walks of `test_migration_0067_downgrade_guard.py` and `test_migration_0084_lock_cutoff.py`. The NOTICE names what the rows that stay mean to the application of the earlier revision, as measured for 0111 on main 15ccedb6 (Alembic head 0108): it evaluates thirteen gates, so the kept gate's checklist item keeps the status it holds — the cockpit lists the line, blocking and `FAILED`, before and after the lock — and its lock request and decision read their own thirteen results: the period was locked on a certification of thirteen codes. The rows stop no lock there; only the upgrade restores the gate. **A revision an earlier pre-release ledger cannot cross (rev 1.268; revision 0124; 04 §18 rule 17).** Revision 0124 adds `subledger_line.subject_key`, which is inside the sealed line document, and refuses a table that already holds a line — the one case so far in which a populated pre-release database is REFUSED and not kept with a NOTICE: no key can be derived for a posted line, a sealed line is never rewritten, and the seals of the earlier postings would no longer verify either way. The emptiness of a tenant table is asked through the validation scan of a check that every existing row fails (`CHECK (subject_key IS NOT NULL)`, added and dropped in the same block), never through a query; the `check_violation` is re-raised as `EREV-MIG-0124` with a sentence that says what the person does next — reset the database and seed it anew (01-DECISIONS D-99 (3)). Both branches are witnessed in `tests/pg` on an empty and on a populated database. |

### 6.6 Logging and personal data (LOG)

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-LOG-01 | structlog emits JSON lines to stdout, redirected to `.run/<process>.log` (DG-RUN-31). Standard fields: `ts` (UTC ISO 8601), `level`, `event`, `logger`, `request_id`, `tenant_id`, `principal_kind`, `job_id`, `duration_ms`, plus event-specific ids and counts. `EREV_LOG_FORMAT=console` is for foreground developer runs only. Rev 1.97 (ruling R-37 (c); 05 OPR-20 rev 1.53): an `erev` command that is not the api or the worker logs to **stderr** through the same pipeline. `cli._cli_settings()` reads the settings and installs it (`configure_logging(level, fmt, stream=sys.stderr)`); `migrate`, `db lint`, `db reset` and `db revision` call it first, and `cli_services()` calls it for every command that builds the operator services. A command that does neither must open no database and emit no log line; `backend/tests/unit/test_cli_logging.py` holds that list (`version`, `healthcheck`, `registry-seed`, `openapi`, `controls-report`, and `api` and `worker`, whose composition roots install the pipeline on stdout) and fails on a command outside it. |
| DG-LOG-02 | `event` names are `<area>.<event>` in lowercase snake case, for example `contract.computed`, `journal_run.exported`, `http.request`. |
| DG-LOG-03 | Forbidden in logs: personal data (emails, names, phone numbers, IP addresses, user agents), credentials, tokens and keys, amounts and prices, contract text, AI prompts and responses, and raw query strings. Allowed: ids, codes, counts, durations and statuses (REQ-OPS-005, REQ-SEC-007). Rev 1.183: an event that reports an exception without its stack trace may carry the exception's class (`error_class`) and the place it was raised (`error_at`, from `logging.raised_at`): the module and line of the last frame of `erev_api` or `erev_engine`, read from the origin of the chain, so that a problem raised from a database error names the place of the statement and not of the mapper; null when no frame of the chain is this code base's. Such an event carries no message: a message can quote values. |
| DG-LOG-04 | Each request logs one `http.request` line: method, route template, status, `duration_ms`, `request_id`, `tenant_id`, `principal_kind`. |
| DG-LOG-05 | Unhandled exceptions log `event = "http.unhandled_error"` with the stack trace and `request_id`. Problem details are not logged. |
| DG-LOG-06 | `print()` is forbidden (ruff T20). The standard `logging` module is used only through the structlog bridge. |
| DG-LOG-07 | The autouse fixture `no_personal_data_in_logs` (`backend/tests/support/log_guard.py`) applies to `api/`, `domain/` and `unit/` tests. It fails a test when a captured log event has a forbidden key (`email`, `display_name`, `name`, `phone`, `ip`, `source_ip`, `user_agent`, `amount`, `price`, `password`, `token`, `secret`, `prompt`, `response_text`) or any value matching an email pattern. |
| DG-LOG-08 | Security and audit evidence goes to `security_event` and `audit_event`, never only to logs. |

### 6.7 AI conventions (AI; D-46)

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_api/adapters/ai/provider.py
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AIRequest:
    template_id: str
    template_version: int
    model: str
    parameters: Mapping[str, Any]
    system: str
    messages: tuple[Mapping[str, str], ...]
    input_sha256: str
    max_tokens: int

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AIResponse:
    text: str
    response_sha256: str
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    latency_ms: int
    model: str
    stop_reason: str

class AIProvider(Protocol):
    def complete(self, request: AIRequest) -> AIResponse: ...

class FakeProvider: ...                                       # deterministic fixture lookup; never touches the network
class AnthropicProvider: ...                                  # anthropic SDK adapter; 60-second timeout
def get_provider(settings: Settings, *, tenant_ai_enabled: bool) -> AIProvider | None: ...
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-AI-01 | `get_provider` returns `None` when `settings.ai_kill_switch` is true or the tenant registry value `ai.enabled` is false (REQ-AI-002, REQ-AI-010). It returns `FakeProvider` when `EREV_AI_PROVIDER=fake`, which is the default and the only value allowed under `EREV_ENV=test`, under `EREV_ENV=e2e` and when `EREV_PERF_RUN=1` (rev 1.2; 05 AIA-02; DG-KRN-CFG-02). `scripts/e2e.sh` and `backend/tests/perf/conftest.py` fail before starting any process when `Settings.ai_provider` is not `fake`. |
| DG-AI-02 | `FakeProvider` answers from `backend/tests/fixtures/ai/<template_id>/v<version>/<input_sha256>.json`, falling back to `default.json` in the same directory; a missing fixture raises `FileNotFoundError`. PRD fixtures such as `fake/contract-review/kinsley-marrow.json` (WLD-F-29) live under this tree. |
| DG-AI-03 | AI calls run only inside `AI_TASK` jobs, never inside a request transaction and never on the money path. Each output becomes an `ai_proposal` row (status `proposed`) with citations (record ids, report run ids, document page and character spans). Accepting a proposal is the normal command run as the accepting user, with its approvals and SoD (REQ-AI-003, CTL-045). |
| DG-AI-04 | `erev_api/domain/ai` may write only `ai_proposal`, `ai_model_log`, files of purpose `AI_PROMPT_LOG` and `exception_item` rows of source `ANOMALY`; DG-ARC-11 enforces this. |
| DG-AI-05 | Prompt templates live at `backend/erev_api/domain/ai/prompts/<template_id>/v<n>.md` and are immutable once used; a change creates `v<n+1>`. |
| DG-AI-06 | Every call inserts `ai_model_log` with template id and version, model id, parameters, input SHA-256, response SHA-256, token counts, latency and user (REQ-AI-004). Contract text is sent only when `ai.send_contract_text` is true. Emails and phone numbers are redacted when `ai.redact_contact_details` is true. `ai.monthly_token_budget` is a hard stop that marks the proposal `failed` with detail `budget_exhausted` (REQ-AI-009). |
| DG-AI-07 | Numbers: `erev_api.domain.ai.numbers.validate_numbers(text, allowed)` extracts every numeric token and requires each to equal a trace value or a cited record value. Otherwise the narrative is discarded and the deterministic narrative is shown (REQ-AI-006, REQ-AI-008). |
| DG-AI-08 | Provider errors and timeouts mark the proposal `failed` and write nothing else (REQ-AI-010). |
| DG-AI-09 | `import anthropic` appears only in `backend/erev_api/adapters/ai/anthropic.py`. The default model id comes from registry parameter `ai.model` (T-PLT-31, D-46); no model id literal appears elsewhere. |
