To add a caller: the entry with its reason, and TXN-07 |
| DG-ARC-19 | `test_stream_appenders.py` (rev 1.218; supervisor rulings R-122 (j) and of 2026-10-02; item PIN-WINDOW-APPENDER-1) | A function of `backend/erev_api` calls the stream's `append_events` and the test's list does not name it with how its transaction ends; a named function appends no more; a function named `COMPUTES` calls no computing function in its body; a function named for a `CALLER` whose named caller computes nothing; a function named `TAIL` whose named function — itself, or the one that ends its transaction or savepoint — does not call `period_ends.refuse_appends_a_lock_met`; or `compute_job.defer_compute` or `compute_job._refused` does not call it. `DRAFT` names an appender that acts on a draft and ends without the check. To add an appender: decide which of the four it is, and name it |
| DG-ARC-20 | `test_membership_reads_name_the_tenant.py` (rev 1.256; USERS-MEMBER-TENANT-1) | A statement of `backend/erev_api` (migrations apart) reads `tenant_membership` — the table under its name, a name it is imported or assigned under, as an attribute of its module, an alias of it, a local name assigned from an expression that holds it, or `member_select()` continued — and leaves the tenant of a row source open (DG-KRN-DB-12), in a function that is not on the closed list `CROSSES_TENANTS` (function, one reason each), or a listed function holds another such read than its one, or none. Each SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE of a Python statement is read by itself; a write or a lock exempts its own row and no source beside it; a tenant condition counts only where every row must meet it, and not against a column of a table without the tenant policy. It also fails when: an expression that holds the table leaves its function with the tenant open (a `return`, an argument, a default value); a row source of the table is made outside a function, or a module names the table's columns there without an entry in `EXPRESSIONS`; SQL text names the table; `member_select` is not one SELECT with the tenant named; a module takes a table from the model by name without an entry in `BY_NAME`, or selects such a table without its tenant outside `BY_NAME_OPEN`; a module that opens an identity session calls `of_session_tenant` outside `IDENTITY_AND_BINDER`. Not seen: a condition that a helper builds, and a statement completed in a later Python statement — it is read where it is made |
| DG-ARC-21 | `test_shown_identity.py` (rev 1.293; IDENTITY-BEFORE-ACCEPTANCE-READERS-1; rev 1.294: the lists follow the rule by status) | A function of `backend/erev_api` outside `domain/platform/users.py` (migrations apart) reads `app_user.display_name` or `app_user.last_login_at` itself — a column of the table or of an alias of it, by attribute or by subscript, or a SELECT of the whole row — and is in neither closed list of the test with its reason: `OF_A_MEMBERSHIP` for a function that names `tenant_membership` too, `BY_USER_ID` for one that does not; a listed function reads them no more; a named reader of a membership's person no longer takes the rule (`SHOWN_NAME`, `SHOWN_DISPLAY_NAME`, `SHOWN_LAST_LOGIN`, `shown_name`, `member_select`); or `users.request_role_assignment` takes the member's name from its caller (DG-KRN-DB-13). Not seen: SQL text, a table handed in as an argument, and a user id a caller took from a membership before it calls a `BY_USER_ID` reader |

## 7. Engine package conventions (ENG)

`docs/accounting/ENGINE_SPEC.md` and `docs/accounting/ENGINE_SPEC_B.md` (one precedence rank, DG-READ-01) own the calculation pipeline (stages, data flow, trace content), and `docs/accounting/POLICIES.md` owns the algorithms. This section fixes the packaging, purity and determinism contract that every stage must satisfy.

```python
# Binding signature: backend/erev_engine/__init__.py
ENGINE_VERSION: Final[str]                                  # semantic version, "1.0.0" at release
def compute(bundle: InputBundle) -> OutputBundle: ...

# Binding signature: backend/erev_engine/bundle.py (field detail per ENGINE_SPEC)
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class InputBundle:
    format_version: int                                     # 1
    engine_version: str                                     # must equal ENGINE_VERSION
    trigger: ComputationTrigger                             # E-87
    known_at: datetime                                      # record-time cutoff; data only, never compared with a clock
    tenant_preset: str                                      # "DEFAULT" or "LEGACY_PARITY"
    currencies: CurrencyTable
    books: tuple[BookInput, ...]                            # book code, resolved policies (DG-KRN-REG-03), account mapping
    entities: tuple[EntityInput, ...]                       # code, functional currency, periods with states
    group: GroupInput                                       # combination group key, member contract keys, inception date
    contracts: tuple[ContractInput, ...]                    # header and booking lines, keyed by external_id
    events: tuple[EventInput, ...]                          # sorted (effective_date, record_seq, event_key)
    ssp_versions: tuple[SspVersionInput, ...]
    pob_template_versions: tuple[TemplateInput, ...]
    rule_set_versions: tuple[RuleSetInput, ...]
    estimate_versions: tuple[EstimateVersionInput, ...]
    fx_rates: tuple[FxRateInput, ...]
    posted: tuple[PostedAmountInput, ...]                   # posted cumulative amounts per book, entity, obligation, role, period
    def sha256(self) -> str: ...

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OutputBundle:
    engine_version: str
    input_sha256: str
    books: tuple[BookOutput, ...]                           # contract version, obligation versions, balances, schedules,
                                                            # journal entries (balanced), trace, proposed treatments
    diagnostics: tuple[Diagnostic, ...]                     # non-blocking findings such as LATE_EVENT
    def sha256(self) -> str: ...

# Binding signature: backend/erev_engine/errors.py
class EngineError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str, *, subject_key: str | None = None,
                 formula_id: str | None = None, detail: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> None: ...
```

| Id | Rule | Rationale [J] |
|---|---|---|
| DG-ENG-01 | Purity: `compute` is a pure function of the bundle. The engine performs no database, filesystem, network, environment, clock, randomness, locale, threading or logging access; DG-ARC-02 enforces the import allow-list. | D-10; research 06 §5.1 rules 1-2 |
| DG-ENG-02 | Determinism: every iteration over a mapping or set is sorted; events are ordered `(effective_date, record_seq, event_key)` (research 06 §5.1 rule 4). Objects are identified by natural keys (`external_id`, `obligation_key`, `period_key`, entity code, estimate `element_code`), never by generated UUIDs; the orchestrator maps keys to ids when persisting. `OutputBundle.sha256()` is identical across runs, processes and machines for identical canonical input, and a permutation of commuting arrivals (stable identities and payloads, dependency- and order-sensitive relationships kept, only the arrival metadata permuted) gives figure-identical books and total-identical stage 12 layers while `input_sha256` and same-date layer keys may differ (CV-26 (a) and (b), D-97 (6) v3.2; PROP:P8). | Replay determinism (G5) |
| DG-ENG-03 | Numbers: ratios and exact values are `Fraction`; posted amounts are `int` minor units; `Decimal` appears only in bundle fields and is converted with `to_fraction`. `compute` runs its body inside `decimal.localcontext(DECIMAL_CONTEXT)`, and calls `guards.no_floats(bundle)` on entry and `guards.no_floats(output)` on exit; a float anywhere raises `EngineError("FLOAT_DETECTED")`. Rounding happens only through `erev_engine.money` (ALG-01). | D-11; research 06 §5.1 rule 3 |
| DG-ENG-04 | Trace: every value in the output has a trace node (DG-KRN-EXP-01 to 04), and `reevaluate(trace)` reproduces every node (PROP:P14). | D-10, D-45 |
| DG-ENG-05 | Fail closed: `compute` asserts, before returning, that the posted allocations sum to the allocation basis per combination group and book (Σ `a_posted` = `allocation_basis` = `total` − `expected_returns` − `consideration_payable`, ENGINE_SPEC S04-R-02; P1; rev 1.2, ENGINE_SPEC:OQ-A-04), that Σ `allocated_amount` = `transaction_price − consideration_payable_amount` per contract version (04 DB-17 V1 as amended under ENGINE_SPEC_B:OQ-B-02), that `allocated_amount = revenue_cum + scheduled_amount + awaiting_trigger_amount` per obligation (DB-17), and that journal entries balance per (entity, book, currency, period, entry) (D-16). A violation raises `EngineError("ENGINE_INVARIANT_VIOLATED")` with the failing identity in `detail` (CTL-012). | Nothing unbalanced reaches persistence |
| DG-ENG-06 | Error codes are codes of the 04 §15.4 finding and exception code catalogue (D-73), which absorbs the POLICIES.md codes and the DEVIATIONS.md §5 engine-stage codes (for example `NEGATIVE_WEIGHT`, `TOTAL_WEIGHT_ZERO`, `TERM_NOT_WHOLE_MONTHS`, `MOD_REMAINING_NEGATIVE`, `MOD_PROGRESS_UNDEFINED`, `VC_ALLOCATION_NEGATIVE`, `NON_FINITE_AMOUNT`), plus `ENGINE_VERSION_MISMATCH`, `FLOAT_DETECTED`, `TRACE_DUPLICATE_NODE` and `ENGINE_INVARIANT_VIOLATED`. The engine never returns partial output. Messages contain no personal data. | One vocabulary with imports and the parity suite |
| DG-ENG-07 | Stage modules under `erev_engine/stages/` take the names and order that ENGINE_SPEC (both files, DG-READ-01) fixes. Each stage is a pure function over frozen dataclasses and imports only `erev_engine` public modules, never another stage's private helpers. Public modules (rev 1.2; ENGINE_SPEC:OQ-A-01): `__init__`, `bundle`, `money`, `canonical`, `currencies`, `dates`, `progress`, `trace`, `formulas`, `enums`, `rules`, `errors`, `guards`, `stages/__init__` (constants `STAGES` and `BOUNDARY_HANDLERS`) and `stages/state`; rev 1.22 (D-96; lane P5) adds `upgrade` — the evidence codec, `INPUT_TRANSFORMS`, the CV-25 / L1 / attribution views and the L2 diff of 05 RCP-28a — as an **orchestration-only** public module: no stage imports it and it runs no stage; it imports only `bundle` and `canonical`. | Reviewable, replaceable stages |
| DG-ENG-08 | Books are computed per book inside one call. Shared stages may be memoised only within that call (research 06 D11). Module-level mutable state and cross-call caches (`functools.cache` over bundle data) are forbidden. | No leakage across tenants or calls |
| DG-ENG-09 | Behaviour switches are policy values in the bundle (POL keys and `tenant_preset`), never tenant ids, environment variables or `if legacy:` flags. | D-32: the preset is a policy set |
| DG-ENG-10 | Versioning: `ENGINE_VERSION` follows semantic versioning. A change that alters any output for an existing input bumps minor (new capability) or major (changed result); a refactor with byte-identical outputs bumps patch. On first start of a new version the API inserts `engine_release` (T-PLT-38). Upgrade replay verification follows REQ-OPS-011. Example (D-93 (5), 2026-09-19): adding `direction` to the canonical estimate input turned VC-FS-02 from an error into an output and changed every input hash (canonical form and version stamp), so the 0.x-line bump is one minor step, 0.2.0 → 0.3.0 (the D-91 A4 reading); compatibility is stated as two separate facts — normalised value equality and actual hash inequality — never conflated; stored computations replay version-pinned to their `engine_release` (RCP-28..30) with no silent rewriting or reposting of history; historical-integrity replay (RCP-28/29) and candidate-upgrade validation (REL-06 `UPGRADE_VALIDATE` / `REPLAY_VERIFY`, mandatory SOP-3 work) remain separate requirements that the lane's bounded hash sweep does not execute. Rev 1.10 (D-96): candidate validation constructs a separate candidate input through `erev_engine.upgrade.INPUT_TRANSFORMS`; source bytes and hashes are never replaced; an unavailable runtime or transform is recorded without an engine execution (D-96). Rev 1.25 (D-96 (3); lane P5): `stamp_release` reads the manifest's `validation_level` (absent → `PATCH`, undeclared; a value outside PATCH / MINOR / MAJOR is a manifest error, REL-03 stop) and persists it on T-PLT-38; `controls.validation_level.stamping_decision` names the path — `FIRST_RELEASE`, `RESTART` (row present, nothing checked), `VERSION_CHANGE` (the declaration must reach `semver_level(previous global release → candidate)`, else the process stops before the insert), `SAME_VERSION_REBUILD` (recorded; its T-PLT-43 row is created `PENDING` by `initial_validation`, reason `SAME_VERSION_REBUILD`, so the `release-validation-pending` gate holds until the REL-06 preparation path or a validation enables it, and the declaration is evaluated there, because the artifact's own row must exist before a `PreparationRow` can name it; D-98 59). | Every computation is traceable to a release (CTL-032) |
| DG-ENG-11 | Engine tests live in `backend/tests/engine/`, build bundles through `backend/tests/support/bundles.py` and may not request database fixtures (DG-TST-05). Each CHK row of POLICIES.md that exercises a helper or stage in isolation has a unit test named `test_chk_<nnn>_<slug>`. | Answer keys first (D-71) |
| DG-ENG-12 | Performance budget: median `compute` time ≤ 10 ms for a combination group of ≤ 10 obligations over 24 periods on the build machine, reported by `make perf`. The budget is not a gate by itself; G9 is. | Research 06 §12.5 inference (U-05) |

## 8. Frontend conventions (FE)

### 8.1 Source layout

```text
frontend/src/
├── main.tsx
├── app/
│   ├── router.tsx               route table (DG-FE-02)
│   ├── providers.tsx            QueryClientProvider, I18nProvider, ThemeProvider, AnnouncerProvider
│   ├── shell/                   TopBar, IconRail, ContextPill, CommandPalette, SandboxBanner, NotificationsPanel, UserMenu
│   ├── auth/                    RequireSession, MfaGate
│   └── errors/                  RouteError, NotFound
├── routes/<area>/<screen>.tsx   one module per screen of SCREENS.md or SCREENS_B.md (DG-READ-02)
├── components/
│   ├── ui/                      base controls
│   ├── data-grid/               DS-CMP-10
│   ├── line-editor/             draft lines a form holds and saves in one body (DS-CMP-10 form-held variant; rev 1.119)
│   ├── filter-bar/              DS-CMP-13
│   ├── money/                   <Money>, <Num> (DS-CMP-26)
│   ├── explain/                 Explain panel and ExplainTrigger (DS-CMP-15)
│   ├── charts/                  the only importer of recharts (DS-LINT-08)
│   ├── ai/                      proposal components; the only importer of Sparkle (DS-LINT-07)
│   ├── icons/registry.ts        the only importer of @phosphor-icons/react (DS-ICO-02)
│   ├── record/                  RecordHeader, KpiStrip, Tabs, FiveStepTracker, DiffView
│   ├── feedback/                Banner, Toast, Skeleton, EmptyState, JobProgress
│   └── form/                    field wrappers and error summary (DS-CMP-21)
├── lib/
│   ├── api/                     client.ts, schema.d.ts (generated), problems.ts, commands.ts, jobs.ts, query-keys.ts, queries/<resource>.ts
│   ├── format/                  formatMoney, formatNumber, formatPercent, formatRate, formatDate, formatTimestamp, formatPeriod, formatCompact, parseMoneyInput
│   ├── i18n/                    t.ts, plural.ts, pseudo.ts
│   ├── a11y/announce.ts
│   ├── theme/

├── messages/en.json

└── design-gallery/              DS-VER-06, compiled only with VITE_EREV_DESIGN_GALLERY=1
```

### 8.2 Rules

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-FE-01 | Stack majors: React 19, TypeScript 5, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS 4, React Router 7, TanStack Query 5, TanStack Table and Virtual, Recharts, Phosphor icons (D-41; DS-ICO). No other state library, component kit or icon set. |
| DG-FE-02 | Routing: `createBrowserRouter` in `src/app/router.tsx`. Route paths follow `docs/design/SCREENS.md` and `docs/design/SCREENS_B.md`, which own the path of each SF id (D-73, D-74). There is no fallback route (rev 1.2; PRD:Q13): a screen item whose SF id neither file lists is `BLOCKED:` under DG-READ-04. The route object of a primary screen has `id = "SF-nn"` (for example `"SF-03"`); a secondary screen has `id = "SF-nn:<slug>"` with the slug SCREENS names; every route object carries `handle = {sf: "SF-nn", screen: "<screen id>", titleKey}` (SCREENS SCR-IA-06; SCREENS:OQ-S-09). Screen modules load through `lazy`. A session loader redirects to `/sign-in`, and `MfaGate` forces `/mfa/enrol` for users who must enrol (REQ-PLT-005). Rev 1.91: both second-factor steps are read from API-S-Session (`mfa_enrolment_required`, `mfa_required`; `GET /session` carries them, so a reload reads the same step) — a session that owes the challenge is sent to `/sign-in/mfa?next=<path>`; the API enforces the step (DG-KRN-AUTH-03), and a call it refuses with `mfa-required` makes `RequireSession` read the session again. Unknown paths render `NotFound`. The `/design` route exists only when `import.meta.env.VITE_EREV_DESIGN_GALLERY === "1"`. |
| DG-FE-03 | The URL carries view state: filters, sort, saved view id, tab and the context pill (entity, period, book), as search parameters (DS-CMP-13, BR-UX-01). **Writes of view state (rev 1.215; item KIT-FILTER-LEAVING-1).** A control writes view state as a navigation that names no path — `navigate({ search })`, `navigate("?…")`, `setSearchParams`, a `<Link to="?…">`, a fragment — and the router resolves such a navigation against the address it holds at that moment, not against the address the control was rendered for. (1) *A control of a page that is leaving writes nothing* (SCREENS §0.5 SCR-URL-33). `guardLeavingPages` of `src/app/router.tsx` wraps the router that `createAppRouter` builds and the memory router of the test harness (`renderApp` of `src/test/app.tsx`); it drops a navigation that names no path when the route it comes from is no longer among the matched routes. A navigation that names its path, and one from a route that is still matched (the shell; a layout whose inner page changed), pass unchanged, and no call site changes. The guard reads the route in `fromRouteId`, which React Router's `useNavigate` passes to `router.navigate`: an upgrade of React Router that renames it or stops passing it turns the cases "a control of a page that is leaving writes nothing" of `src/app/router.test.tsx` and the chip case of `src/routes/approvals/toolbar.test.tsx` red. *The limit:* the guard knows routes, not records. A page that stays on one route while its record changes (contract A to contract B under `/contracts/:contractId`) is not caught, and a control rendered for the earlier record writes onto the later record's address; a case of `src/app/router.test.tsx` states it. *A page is leaving from the moment a navigation to another pathname is on its way* (rev 1.230; item KIT-FILTER-LEAVING-2). Until the next page's module and loaders have arrived the router still holds the old address and the old routes are still matched, so a write without a path passed the guard, was resolved on the page being left and cancelled the member's navigation — a press (a chip of the contracts list while the reports page was on its way: the member stayed on `/contracts?f.status=is:DRAFT`) and the answer of an awaited command (the report view's 202). The guard therefore also drops a navigation that names no path while `router.state.navigation.location` names another pathname than `router.state.location`. Pathnames are compared: a navigation on its way to the same pathname — a filter being applied while a loader runs — drops nothing, so that two writes in quick succession both arrive. Once the router has moved, the limit above stands as it is. (2) *The FilterBar (DS-CMP-13) starts a write from the search the router holds*, not from the search it last rendered: `useLiveSearch` of `src/lib/url/live-search.ts` answers the search of a navigation on its way to the path on screen, else the search of the router's address, and under a router that keeps no such state (a component test's `MemoryRouter`) the search last rendered. A second chip removed before the first removal is rendered therefore does not put the first chip back. The hook reads `UNSAFE_DataRouterContext`; the cases of `src/components/filter-bar/FilterBar.test.tsx` turn red when an upgrade takes it away. (3) *A write after an awaited command is made for the page that sent it, while that page is on screen* (rev 1.229; item RPT-VIEWER-LATE-RUN-1). The continuation of an awaited command outlives its component: it still navigates after the component is gone, and under one route the guard of (1) lets it through, so the answer of one record's page would be written onto the next record's address. A component that writes after an `await` therefore keeps whether it is still mounted and, where its page can change under it, the path it sent the command from (`useLivePath` of `src/lib/url/live-search.ts`), writes only while both hold, and starts the write from the router's search. Two sites follow it: `useReportRun` of `src/routes/reports/viewer/useReportRun.ts` discards the answer of a creation whose view is gone — a view is keyed by its report, and the next report under `/reports/:reportCode` took the first report's `run` and parameters — and `SavedViewSelector` chooses a saved view, or leaves a deleted one, only on the page that sent the command. *A write that names its own path* (rev 1.230; item KIT-FILTER-LEAVING-2). The guard of (1) sees only a navigation that names no path. A component that writes `{ pathname: location.pathname, search }` in an effect or after an `await` names the page it was rendered for, and a late one takes the member back to the page they left, or keeps them on it. Such a write asks `usePageStays` of `src/lib/url/live-search.ts` first: the component is mounted, the router is at the path it rendered for, and no navigation to another pathname is on its way. Three sites follow it: `ExplainPanel` of `src/components/explain/` does not write `explain` for a page that is leaving, and a figure opened there is not carried to the next page; `src/routes/home/home.tsx` writes its context once Home is the page that stays, also after a navigation that did not arrive; `src/routes/contracts/modification-detail.tsx` opens nothing with the answer of an edit the member has walked away from. The like effect of `src/routes/data/exceptions.tsx` is the first effect of its page and was not made late in any case built; it stays as it is. |
| DG-FE-04 | Server state uses TanStack Query only. `src/lib/api/client.ts` exports `api = createClient<paths>({ baseUrl: "/api/v1" })` (openapi-fetch) with middleware that adds `X-CSRF-Token` and `X-Request-Id`, redirects on 401, and parses `application/problem+json` into `ApiProblem`. Query hooks live in `src/lib/api/queries/<resource>.ts` and use keys from `query-keys.ts` (`[resource, scope, params]`). Defaults: `staleTime: 30_000`, `retry: 1` for queries, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. Every read passes `as_of` = end date of the context period (BR-UX-02). |
| DG-FE-05 | Commands use `useCommand({method, path, ifMatch, invalidates})` from `src/lib/api/commands.ts`. It creates `Idempotency-Key = crypto.randomUUID()` once per user intent and reuses it when that intent is retried; sends `If-Match` when given; never retries automatically; never applies optimistic updates to accounting data; invalidates the listed keys on success. An intent is one body: the key is reused while the same body is resubmitted, and the intent ends — the next `submit` creates a new key — on a 2xx, on a different body, on `reset()` and on an answered problem the API keeps: the API stores every problem below 500 except 401, 403, 412, 428, 429 and 409 `idempotency-in-progress` as the first response of its key and replays it (DG-KRN-IDEM-03), so the resubmission that its detail asks for must carry a new key to be decided at all, and a kept problem means the command's transaction rolled back, so a new key cannot run anything twice. A lost response, a 5xx and an answer the API does not keep leave the key in force, so that a retry cannot run the command twice (rev 1.132; supervisor rulings R-97 (6) and R-102 (e), item W-21; the premise of SPEC-Q-197 that only successes are stored no longer holds). **Commands outside the hook (rev 1.156; item W-23).** A command that a component sends without `useCommand` — a step of a press that sends several commands, a command per record of a bulk action, a grid cell save, a file upload, a command of a module function — takes its key from `useCommandKeys()` of the same file, the keys of that component instance, and never makes one where it is sent: a key made per call is a new key on every press, so a lost response followed by a second press ran the command twice, and a create left a second record. A step is the method, the path and the body (an upload names its file); its key follows the rule above — kept through a lost response, a 5xx and an answer the API does not keep; ended by a success and by a problem the API keeps. Inside a sequence a step that succeeded keeps its key (`keep`; `sendStep` for the contract commands) until the sequence completes and calls `clear()`: when a later step fails or gets no answer, the second press sends the earlier steps again under their keys, the API replays the answers it stored — the same record, whatever `If-Match` says by then, because the hash of a request holds its method, route, parameters and body and not that header (DG-KRN-IDEM-02, DG-KRN-IDEM-04) — and the sequence continues at the step that failed. A form edited between the two presses is another body, hence a new step and a new record. The keys go with the component: a drawer that closes starts anew. A press that got no answer leaves the screen as it is and says so; it is not an unhandled rejection. `frontend/eslint.config.js` (`no-restricted-syntax`, tested by `frontend/config/eslint-idempotency.test.ts`) reports the header `Idempotency-Key` as an object key, as the name given to `Headers.set` or `append`, assigned to a member and as the name of a `[name, value]` pair in every file of `frontend/src` but `src/lib/api/commands.ts`; the e2e suite, an API client of its own, may write it. On 412 it refetches and shows the banner "This record changed. Reload to see the latest version."; problem `errors[]` map to form fields; a 202 response starts `useJob(jobId)`, which polls `GET /jobs/{id}` every 2 seconds (DS-CMP-24). Every `submit` carries an attempt identity: a later `submit`, a change of the command's `path` or `reset()` supersede the attempts before them, whose answers no longer reach the hook's own `pending`, `problem`, `banner` (412) or `jobId` state — the caller awaiting a superseded `submit` still receives that attempt's outcome. The cache refresh of an answer is bound to the keys listed when that command was submitted, never to the keys of a later `path`: a 200 or a 412 refreshes them on arrival, a superseded 202 refreshes them at once because its job is neither adopted nor polled (so that is its only refresh from this hook), and the job a current 202 adopts refreshes them when it reaches a terminal state (rev 1.16 attempt identity, D-97 (38); rev 1.18 refresh binding, Codex FWR-CMD-R1/R2 cases C09/C10; the `useReportRun` attempt rule generalised to every command). The CSRF token from `GET /session` is held in module memory, never in `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`. **A command's answer is received whole (rev 1.209; item KIT-202-BODY-1).** `send` of `src/lib/api/client.ts` reads a copy of the body of every answer to a command (any method but GET) to its end before it hands the answer on, so that an answer whose caller needs only the status or a header — a 202 adopted by its `Location` — does not stay open in the browser: measured in Chromium, 0 of 32 such answers ever finished, for the developer tools and for a tool that waits for a response to finish, while later requests were not delayed. The answer handed on is untouched and its body is the caller's to read; an answer to a read is left to its reader. |

## 9. Testing

### 9.1 Layers and directories

| Id | Directory | Scope | Database | Run by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DG-TST-01 | `backend/tests/engine/` | Pure engine: helpers, stages, CHK unit tests | none (fixtures forbidden, DG-TST-18) | `make test`, `make ci` |
| DG-TST-02 | `backend/tests/architecture/` | DG-ARC tests | none, except DG-ARC-07 and DG-ARC-09 parts marked `pg` | `make test`, `make ci` |
| DG-TST-03 | `backend/tests/unit/`, `domain/`, `api/` | Kernel, commands, queries, HTTP contract | `erev_test` as `erev_app` | `make test`, `make ci` |
| DG-TST-04 | `backend/tests/pg/` | G6 suite (§9.4) | `erev_test` as `erev_app` (owner only to simulate tampering with a data-fix ticket) | `make test-pg` (also collected by `make test`) |
| DG-TST-05 | `backend/tests/answer_keys/`, `parity/`, `properties/`, `perf/` | G4, G3, G5, G9 | engine runner none; platform runners `erev_test` | the specialist gate targets |

A collection hook in `backend/tests/conftest.py` orders `engine/` and `architecture/` tests first, so a pure regression fails before any database work.

### 9.2 Markers

```toml
# backend/pyproject.toml
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config -ra --durations=25"
testpaths = ["tests"]
markers = [
  "control(control_id): designated system control CTL-NNN proven by this test (G7)",
  "parity: legacy golden parity case (G3)",
  "answer_key: accounting answer key (G4)",
  "property: Hypothesis invariant (G5)",
  "pg: isolation, immutability, chain, invariant, lint and migration suite (G6)",
  "perf: performance benchmark (G9)",
  "slow: a single test that takes more than 10 seconds",
]
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-TST-06 | `@pytest.mark.control("CTL-NNN")` takes exactly one id matching `^CTL-\d{3}$` that exists in `controls.yaml`; `pytest_collection_modifyitems` raises a collection error otherwise. A test may carry several control markers. The tests tagged for a control exercise the control's failure path — at least one of them (for example CTL-014: a preparer's approval attempt returns 403 `self-approval` and writes no decision). The rule is read of a control, not of each test: a tagged test may assert a clause of the control's row operating (rev 1.252; supervisor ruling of 2026-10-02). |
| DG-TST-07 | `parity`, `answer_key`, `property`, `pg` and `perf` are applied through module-level `pytestmark` in their directories. A test with any of these markers may not live elsewhere. |
| DG-TST-08 | `slow` is required on any test that exceeds 10 seconds in `make ci` durations output. `make test` excludes `slow` unless `SLOW=1`; `make ci` includes it. |
| DG-TST-09 | `pytest.skip`, `xfail` and `skipif` are forbidden in `parity`, `answer_key`, `property`, `pg` and `control` tests. Elsewhere a skip needs a reason naming a BUILD_SPEC item. |

### 9.3 Database fixture strategy

| Id | Fixture or rule | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| DG-TST-10 | `test_database` (session scope) | Forces `EREV_ENV=test`; asserts the database is `erev_test` or `erev_rv_*`; takes the advisory lock (DG-TST-11); drops schema `erev` with CASCADE and the Procrastinate objects in `public` as `erev_owner`; runs `alembic upgrade head` as `erev_owner`; runs the DB-14 lint as `erev_app`; yields `TestDatabase(clock)`, whose `app_engine` and `owner_engine` answer the engines of the process's factories at each use (rev 1.269; item TEST-ORDER-DEPENDENCIES-1): the fixture keeps no engine, because a test that reaches `dispose_engines()` — the CLI's switch of environment, the end of `worker.main` — makes the factories build new engines, and a value that kept the first ones left every module after it disposing a pool the product no longer used, so that a connection opened before a schema rebuild answered `cache lookup failed for type <oid>` in whatever ran next. Applied migrations as owner and exercised RLS as `erev_app` (D-40, D-42). |
| DG-TST-11 | Serialisation | `SELECT pg_advisory_lock(0x6572657654455354)` on a dedicated owner connection held for the whole session. A second test process waits instead of dropping the schema under the first. |
| DG-TST-12 | `db` (function scope) | Opens an `erev_app` connection, begins a transaction and yields a session factory whose sessions use `join_transaction_mode="create_savepoint"` and set `connection.info["erev.context"]` (DG-KRN-DB-04). Code under test that commits releases savepoints only. The outer transaction rolls back at teardown. Deferred constraint triggers (DB-06, DB-16, DB-17) never fire under this fixture, so tests of those use `committed_db`. |
| DG-TST-13 | `committed_db` (function scope) | Real transactions and commits through the production session factories. Isolation comes from a fresh tenant per test (`tenant_factory`, provisioning command with a random tenant code). Rows are never cleaned up; the next session resets the schema. API tests (`tests/api/`) always use `committed_db`, because FastAPI runs synchronous endpoints in a worker thread with its own connection. |
| DG-TST-14 | `clock` | A `FrozenClock` at `2026-09-12T12:00:00Z` installed on `app.state.clock` and on units of work; tests advance it explicitly. Rev 1.276 (the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02 08:53 on the lane's list of test clocks): a witness whose point is the ORDER of a record time and an application instant stands on the record clock — the frozen clock moved onto the server's present (`support.worlds.on_record_clock`, `support.record_clock`) — and never on a clock held ahead of the server's. A record time is the server's (DG-KRN-TIME-06) and an instant such as a reconciliation's `as_of_known_at` or a lock's cutoff is the later of the application instant and the transaction timestamp: under a clock held ahead, every row recorded within the lead lies before every such instant, and a case of the kind "recorded after the instant was fixed" cannot occur (a fixture an hour ahead hid such a case of item REC-GEN-LOCK-1 for a day). A test sets no ABSOLUTE instant that the server's clock has still to pass: on that day the two clocks change sides and the test's answer may change with them. Instants are computed from the world's own dates and lie at or behind the fixture's frozen instant, or follow the record clock. Where a rule can only be put into force by an application date that the server has passed — a version effective on the first day of a period that has not started (04 §16.5) — the witness stands on the frozen clock and its docstring says which clock decides what. |
| DG-TST-15 | No network (autouse) | Monkeypatches `socket.socket.connect` and `socket.create_connection` to allow only `AF_UNIX` sockets and loopback addresses (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`); any other destination raises `NetworkBlocked` (`docs/00-GOAL.md` §5; REQ-SEC-008). |
| DG-TST-16 | Principals and factories | `tests/support/principals.py` builds the signed-in members, colleagues and enrolled actors that tests dress with the ten default roles (`tests/support/reference.py` assigns them). The answer-key personas `ak-preparer`, `ak-approver`, `ak-ssp-analyst` and `ak-ssp-approver` do not live there: the platform plan's PERSONAS steps create them (`tests/support/answer_keys/platform_plan.py`, DG-AK-41) and `tests/support/answer_keys/db_personas.py` stands them in for the DB-bound adapter tests (rev 1.42, D-98 candidate 107a; corrected in place — the earlier sentence named `principals.py` as their source). `tests/support/factories.py` creates data through domain commands (provision tenant, entity and calendar, products, published SSP book version, booked and activated contract). Raw inserts are allowed only in `tests/support/rows.py` (`ROW_BUILDERS`) for the pg suite. |
| DG-TST-17 | API client | `fastapi.testclient.TestClient(create_app(...))` with the clock override; requests send `Idempotency-Key` and, for cookie sessions, `X-CSRF-Token` through helpers in `tests/support/api.py`. |
| DG-TST-18 | Engine isolation | `backend/tests/engine/conftest.py` fails any test that requests `test_database`, `db` or `committed_db`. |

### 9.5 Answer-key YAML schema (G4)

This section is the binding contract for the answer-key corpus in `docs/accounting/answer-keys/`. Answer-key engineers author files to it. The build loop implements the loader and the runners that consume them.

#### 9.5.1 Directory layout and file rules

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-AK-01 | Path: `docs/accounting/answer-keys/<family>/<id>.yaml`, where `<family>` is the lowercase form of `families[0]` (a POLICIES.md §0.7 code: `rnd`, `ssp`, `alc`, `stp1`, `pob`, `vc`, `ret`, `mr`, `brk`, `sfc`, `ncc`, `cpc`, `tax`, `ifrs`, `rec`, `roy`, `mod`, `pos`, `je`, `dlt`, `fx`, `ent`, `cost`, `loss`, `late`, `disc`, `onb`, `par`). The only other allowed entries are `docs/accounting/answer-keys/README.md` and the directory `docs/accounting/answer-keys/_coverage/`, which holds the answer-key authors' coverage notes and is never read by the loader (rev 1.2; D-76; OQ-AK-15, OQ-AKT-15, OQ-AKI-21). |
| DG-AK-02 | One file holds exactly one scenario. Variants of one research example (Case A, Case B) are separate files that share `derived_from`. |
| DG-AK-03 | Encoding UTF-8, LF line endings, 2-space indentation. Every decimal, date and timestamp is written as a quoted string. |
| DG-AK-04 | `id` matches `^(RND\|SSP\|ALC\|STP1\|POB\|VC\|RET\|MR\|BRK\|SFC\|NCC\|CPC\|TAX\|IFRS\|REC\|ROY\|MOD\|POS\|JE\|DLT\|FX\|ENT\|COST\|LOSS\|LATE\|DISC\|ONB\|PAR)-[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]{0,78}[A-Z0-9]$`. Its prefix equals `families[0]` and the file name. A key derived from a research 04 key uses that key id as the suffix (`REC-S2-EX11-CASEA-OWNPRICES`). A key that carries a POLICIES.md CHK contains the CHK id in its id (`RND-CHK-004`) (POLICIES.md §0.3). The containment check is case-insensitive, and key ids carry the upper-case form: CHK-003a is contained in `RND-CHK-003A` (rev 1.2; D-76; OQ-AK-01). |

#### 9.5.2 Top-level fields

| Id | Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DG-AK-10 | `schema` | const `"erev-answer-key/1"` | R | Any other value fails loading |
| DG-AK-11 | `id` | string | R | DG-AK-04; unique across the corpus |
| DG-AK-12 | `title` | string ≤ 200 | R | |
| DG-AK-13 | `status` | `active` \| `withdrawn` | R | Withdrawn keys are validated and reported, never run |
| DG-AK-14 | `families` | array of family codes, ≥ 1, unique | R | First element fixes the directory |
| DG-AK-15 | `tags` | array of `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` | O | Resolves `AK-FAM:<slug>` hints of `docs/03-REQUIREMENTS.md` (DG-AK-33). Other tags, for example `r04-s<n>`, are allowed and carry no coverage meaning (rev 1.2) |
| DG-AK-16 | `summary` | string | R | Plain-language scenario and why the figures are right |
| DG-AK-17 | `authority` | `{codification: [..], ifrs: [..], practice: [..], urls: [..]}` | R | Codification paragraphs in FASB format (`606-10-32-28`, `340-40-25-1`); IFRS as `IFRS 15.74`; practice guidance labelled. `codification` may be empty only when `families[0]` is `RND` or `PAR` |
| DG-AK-18 | `derived_from` | `{research04: [..], research05: [..], chk: [..], golden: [..], dev: [..]}` | O | Ids verbatim (`S2-EX11-CASEA-OWNPRICES`, `FS-02`, `CHK-004`, `GT-12`, `DEV-071`) |
| DG-AK-19 | `requirements` | array of `REQ-<AREA>-NNN`, ≥ 1 | R | Each exists in `docs/03-REQUIREMENTS.md` |
| DG-AK-20 | `policy_refs` | array of `POL-NNN` | O | Each exists in POLICIES.md §1 |
| DG-AK-21 | `review` | `{author, authored_on, reviewer, reviewed_on, status}`; status `pending` \| `approved` \| `changes_requested` | R | G12 evidence; `make answer-keys` reports the count not approved |
| DG-AK-22 | `runner` | `engine` \| `platform` | R | `engine`: `erev_engine.compute` over bundles built in memory; `platform`: commands on `erev_test` (DG-AK-41) |
| DG-AK-23 | `books` | array of E-02 codes, ≥ 1 | R | Books computed; checkpoints reference only these |
| DG-AK-24 | `world` | object (§9.5.3) | R | |
| DG-AK-25 | `contracts` | array (§9.5.4), ≥ 1 | R | |
| DG-AK-26 | `timeline` | array (§9.5.5), ≥ 1 | R | |
| DG-AK-27 | `checkpoints` | array (§9.5.6), ≥ 1 | R | |
| DG-AK-59 | `notes` | array of strings | O | Documentary clarifications of the key's inputs, each citing the D-number that ruled it (D-97 (2)); the loader and the runner read nothing from it |
| DG-AK-60 | The lock-snapshot dataset registry `erev_api/domain/reports/snapshots.py` (RPS-SNAP; rev 1.58; D-98 139; design note PRODUCTION-F-RPS-RPS-SNAP-DESIGN.md) exposes `SnapshotScope(entity_id, book_code, period_id, known_at)`, `DatasetBuilder = Callable[[UnitOfWork, SnapshotScope], Encoded]`, `SNAPSHOT_DATASETS` (twelve adapters keyed by the E-64 literal; SNAP-2 (design §14; CTR-17 slice 1 landed): F-CTR's `modification_register` is DATE-selected — `_period_bounds` supplies the lock period's first / last day as `from_date` / `to_date`, `PERIOD_BOUNDS_MISSING` refuses by name without them; rev 1.73: F-CLO's `manual_adjustment_register` is PERIOD-selected — the lock's period as `from_period_key` = `to_period_key`, functional currency view) and `SNAPSHOT_DEPENDENCIES` (empty since twelve of twelve; the shape kept for a future kind — a kind absent from the registry is refused by name); F-CLO's `close/snapshots.py::freeze_datasets` resolves it by name (`close/dependencies.py::snapshot_registry`). `freeze_waterfall` and `freeze_rpo` produce their kinds LONG-FORM from the builders' real consumed populations (`revenue_waterfall.population`; `rpo._run`) at the re-lock key contract's grain (`KEY_COLUMNS` = `close/relock_diff.KEY_COLUMNS`, pinned by a test); the ten `_wrapped(kind, report_code)` adapters run the real `build()` and drop the presentation `TOTAL:<ISO>` rows (A2). Every adapter derives the report request of the lock's scope with `scope_parameters(definition, scope, entity_code, period_key, known_at=cutoff_of(kind, scope))` — the request a user would make (entity code, book, the report's own period selector: `period_key` for `contract_balances` / `rpo`, `from_period_key` = `to_period_key` otherwise; `known_at` = the cutoff as UTC text ⇒ `historical` basis) normalised like `framework._resolve` (schema defaults, `PARAMETER_DEFAULTS`, booleans false, `parameter_errors` on the closed schema) but WITHOUT the caller's `report.run` scope filter (the freeze's authorisation is the lock decision's; `entity_ids` = the lock's entity by construction) — runs the builder with `period_lock_id` / `binding` / `sources` None and encodes with `encode_report(kind, data, drop_presentation_totals=...)`: the engine's `encode` over `row_key` + every report column in report order as text-kind cells of the CSV renderer's CANONICAL DS-FMT-25 text — `outputs/csv.py::canonical`, the text WITHOUT the spreadsheet formula guard (A4, D-98 139 amendment 4 (Codex production-20260921-1653); the live exports' `cell` is `guard(canonical)` for the text kinds and unchanged): identity and text cells carry the admitted value itself, the guard is applied at the export boundary (`locked.export_csv(dataset, kinds)` → `csv_output.export_cell`: the guard by each column's DECLARED kind from `snapshots.declared_kinds` — text kinds guarded, machine kinds never, an undeclared header text (Codex 1739 §3 (c)); `framework._render_locked` serves it for the as-locked CSV — byte-identical to the frozen file and `output_sha256` = `file_sha256` whenever no cell needs the guard); the long-form `row_key` is `row_key_of(kind, row)` = `obligation:` + the kind's `KEY_COLUMNS` each CV-21 percent-encoded (`out_of_period_register.encode_component`) and joined with `:` — `decode_row_key` inverts it, so the key is a pure, injective function of the identity columns; `REQUIRED[kind]` (the key columns + `CURRENCY_COLUMNS[kind]`) read by name — a missing header / row column or an empty required cell outside `EMPTY_KEY_ADMITTED[kind]` refuses by name; `EMPTY_KEY_ADMITTED` names `line_code` and `contract_external_id` for the two rollforwards — a builder states a row's inapplicable key component as `None` and never leaves the field out of the row — and `ROW_IDENTITY[kind]` names the components of which every row carries at least one (a rollforward row is a line row or a by-contract row; one with neither refuses by name; rev 1.79); optional cells None = ""; `CURRENCY_OF[kind]` binds each money column to the row's currency column and a differing money currency refuses by name; the builder's `control_totals` verbatim. `cutoff_of(kind, scope)` is `scope.frozen_at or scope.known_at` for `JE_POPULATION` (S15-R-18b Q5) and `scope.known_at` otherwise. Refusals are by name and save nothing: `SnapshotRefusal(kind, reason)` (a `RuntimeError` like F-CLO's `ProducerMissing`) for an absent entity / period / definition, a closed-schema finding, a repeated row key or a missing column; `SnapshotDependencyMissing` from `dataset_for(kind)` for the remaining register kind. At the lock decision (rev 1.96; ENGINE_SPEC_B S15-R-18c; supervisor ruling R-19) the consumer passes ONE freeze cutoff — `close/freeze.py::freeze_cutoff`, the later of the decision's application instant and its transaction timestamp — as `known_at` and as `frozen_at`; answers a `SnapshotRefusal` by name: 409 `invalid-transition`, rule `S15-R-18`, naming the kind and the reason (`freeze.dataset_refused`; `close/dependencies.py::snapshot_registry` resolves the refusal type with the datasets and the scope), never an unhandled error; and refuses, after the freeze and again after its last lock write, a period whose retained rows lie beyond the cutoff or moved while the lock was being decided (`freeze.assert_covered`, rule `S15-R-18c`; the guard reads in a read-only transaction under the tenant's SYSTEM scope — `freeze.system_reads`, supervisor ruling R-42 (d) — so that its result does not depend on the decider's row-level scope; the cutoff is stored on the lock, `period_lock.cutoff_known_at`, R-40 (c); witnesses `tests/unit/close/test_freeze.py`, `tests/domain/close/test_lock_freeze_db.py`). Never an empty dataset as a substitute; the registry is CPU-testable (`tests/unit/reports/test_snapshot_registry.py`), its DB witnesses are `tests/domain/reports/test_snapshot_registry_db.py`. **Reader-independence (rev 1.123; supervisor ruling R-94 (a); ENGINE_SPEC_B S15-R-18c rev 1.88).** `close/snapshots.py::freeze_datasets` hands every producer a READER, not the caller's unit of work: `close/freeze.py::system_unit(uow)` — a unit of work of the tenant's SYSTEM principal over a read-only transaction of its own, with the caller's instant (`now`), key ring and file store — so a producer sees every entity's rows whoever decides the lock, and the caller's unit of work is used for the writes alone (`store_file`, the `lock_snapshot` rows). Consequences a producer relies on and must keep: it reads COMMITTED rows only (nothing the caller wrote and has not committed), it cannot write or take a row lock (the transaction is read-only: a statement that tries is refused by the database), and it takes its cutoffs from the `SnapshotScope`, never from the reader's clock. Witness per kind: `tests/domain/close/test_freeze_scope_db.py` (WLD-K-04, a decider scoped to AVM-US against a decider of every entity). **One reader per lock decision (rev 1.165; 05 TXN-03 rev 1.121; supervisor ruling R-116 (h)).** `close.commands._period_lock_approved` opens `freeze.system_unit` once — before the activity read — and closes it after the last coverage read: `freeze.activity_before_freeze(…, reader=…)`, the producers (`freeze_datasets(…, reader=freeze.held(reader))`) and both `freeze.assert_covered(…, reader=…)` reads use that one session, so a decision holds two pooled connections at its peak and checks the second one out once (four times before). The reader keeps `tenant_session`'s default isolation level, READ COMMITTED: the coverage reads must see what is committed when they run, so this reader is never raised to REPEATABLE READ (witness `test_f7_c_the_one_reader_sees_a_run_committed_while_the_datasets_are_produced`). A caller that names no reader — the close run's DATASET_FREEZE step, the sandbox period replay — opens its own as before. **The idle bound of a freeze (rev 1.165; 05 TXN-03 rev 1.121; supervisor ruling R-119 (d)).** EVERY caller of `snapshots.freeze_datasets` calls `freeze.allow_idle(session)` for its own transaction before the freeze, and for a reader it holds; `freeze_datasets` calls it for the reader it opens itself: the caller idles while the reader produces a dataset and the reader while its caller stores a file or writes, and the 60 s of a connection ended either one. A new caller adds its call; `tests/unit/test_idle_in_transaction.py` reads the package's source and names a caller that does not. |

Field names equal the 04 column names of the table cited. References use business codes, never uuids.

Rev 1.2 (D-76): `assurance_cost_per_unit` is an exact string (POL-022 `ENGINE`, JET-16; 04 B3-D02); `is_franchisor_preopening_service` is a boolean, default false (POL-202; 04 B3-D21); `split_basis` ∈ {`relative_ssp`, `fixed_percentage`} |

Rev 1.2: `method` literals are E-47 (`observable`, `adjusted_market`, `cost_plus_margin`, `residual`, `legacy_range`) and `distinctness` literals E-105; `point_value`, `low_value`, `mid_value`, `high_value` and `observable_point` are unit SSPs, and the allocation weight is the SSP times the line quantity (OQ-AKI-07); residual entries carry `low_value` and `high_value` (OQ-AKT-12). `observable_point` → T-REF-30 `observable_point` (POL-072 `OBSERVABLE_POINT`; 04 B3-D06; D-76). `population` (`runner: engine` only; B3-DG-12): digit strings with 1 ≤ `observation_count` and 0 ≤ `inside_count` ≤ `observation_count`, the T-REF-33 statistics of the transaction population attached to a range entry, evaluated by DG-AK-45 Rev 1.8 (D-93 (4)): `value_basis` is E-49 (`AMOUNT` when absent, `PERCENT_OF_LIST`; `PER_INCREMENT` and `PER_BOOKED_TERM` pending lane ENG-C1b): for a `series` product it declares whether the entry prices one increment, the booked term or the remaining increments at d (ENGINE_SPEC S06-R-11; 04 T-REF-30); a series entry without a basis is refused by the loader (fail closed; every corpus series entry is annotated, lane ENG-C1b — an omitted basis is not an `AMOUNT` declaration).
