Obligation targets of a portfolio estimate resolve in each member contract. A portfolio estimate reaches the engine through one `ESTIMATE_CHANGED` item per member contract (04 T-CON-13 `applied_event_ids`). An `estimate: <element_code>` handle resolves first in the item's contract, then in the portfolios that list the contract; a handle that resolves in two places fails loading |
| `policies` | `{tenant: {<POL key>: value}, entities: {<entity code>: {…}}, books: {<book>: {…}}}` | T-PLT-32 PUBLISHED versions; keys and literals per POLICIES.md §1. Value shapes (rev 1.2; D-76; OQ-AK-16): an option literal is a string; a list-valued option is a list of strings (`rpo.time_bands: ["12", "24"]`); a parameterised option is an object `{option: <literal>, <parameter>: <string>}` (`pob.immaterial_promise_relief: {option: APPLY_RELIEF, immaterial_threshold_pct: "0.01"}`); a structured value is an object with the members POLICIES §1 names (`sfc.discount_rate_basis: {basis, annual_rate, compounding?}`, `compounding` ∈ {`MONTHLY` (default), `ANNUAL`}, D-76). The same shapes apply to `policy_values` and `policy_overrides[].value` |

Enumeration literals most often written in keys, verbatim from 04 §3 and POLICIES §1 (D-73; rev 1.1):

| Enumeration | Literals | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| E-01 `account_role` (33 values, D-14a) | `REVENUE`; `CONTRACT_LIABILITY`, `CONTRACT_ASSET`, `UNBILLED_RECEIVABLE`, `ACCOUNTS_RECEIVABLE`, `BILLING_CLEARING`; `REFUND_LIABILITY`, `RETURN_ASSET`, `DEPOSIT_LIABILITY`, `CONSIDERATION_PAYABLE`, `CUSTOMER_INCENTIVE_ASSET`; `COST_TO_OBTAIN_ASSET`, `COST_TO_FULFILL_ASSET`, `CONTRACT_COST_AMORTIZATION`, `CONTRACT_COST_IMPAIRMENT`; `LOSS_PROVISION`, `LOSS_EXPENSE`, `WARRANTY_PROVISION`, `WARRANTY_EXPENSE`; `INTEREST_INCOME`, `INTEREST_EXPENSE`, `FX_GAIN_LOSS`, `INTERCOMPANY_DUE_TO`, `INTERCOMPANY_DUE_FROM`; `NONCASH_CONSIDERATION_ASSET`, `SALES_TAX_PAYABLE`, `PRE_STANDARD_REVENUE`, `ROUNDING`; `COST_OF_REVENUE`, `CONTRACT_COST_CLEARING`, `RECEIVABLE_CONTRA`; reserved: `RETAINED_EARNINGS`, `FINANCING_OBLIGATION` | Reserved roles may appear in `account_mapping` but never in checkpoint `subledger` or `journals` lines, because no 1.0 posting uses them (DG-AK-32) |
| `clearing_purpose` (D-14a) | `BILLING`, `UNAPPLIED_CASH`, `AP_SUPPLIER`, `INVENTORY`, `EQUITY`, `INVESTMENTS` | Only on `BILLING_CLEARING` mapping rows and subledger lines |
| E-21 `ratable_convention` (POL-090, D-75) | `DAILY`, `MONTHLY_EVEN`, `MID_MONTH` | `MONTHLY_EVEN` replaces `MONTHLY_WHOLE_MONTHS` and equals it on whole-month terms |
| Registry option literals | POLICIES §1, for example `billing.posting` `ERP` \| `ENGINE`; `material_right.exercise` `CONTINUATION` \| `MODIFICATION`; `je.posting_mode` `GROSS` \| `DELTA` | Keys and literals exactly as in POLICIES §1 (D-13a, D-21a) |

#### 9.5.4 `contracts[]`

| Field | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `external_id` | R | Contract handle and `contract.external_id` |
| `customer`, `contracting_entity`, `transaction_currency`, `inception_date` | R | API-S-ContractCreate |
| `signature_date`, `payment_terms`, `termination` (`{party, has_penalty, notice_days}`), `has_commercial_substance`, `region`, `channel`, `contract_type` | O | API-S-ContractCreate; `contract_type` is free text (OQ-AKI-17) |
| `renewal_of` (rev 1.2) | O | Handle of the contract this contract renews, booked at a lower `seq`; maps to `contract.renewal_of_contract_id`, accepted on `POST /contracts` (04 B3-D18; D-76 renewal handle; OQ-AK-14; POL-025, REQ-MOD-017) |
| `scope_605_35` (rev 1.2) | O | Boolean, default false; T-CON-01 column `scope_605_35` (ENGINE_SPEC_B:OQ-B-12, interim `custom_attributes.scope_605_35`; D-76; OQ-AK-10, OQ-AKI-03); read under POL-151 |
| `payment_schedule` (rev 1.2) | O | `[{date, amount}]`, dates ascending, amounts money: the D-76 billing plan, as the booking payload member `payment_schedule[]` of ENGINE_SPEC:OQ-A-09 adopted by 04 B3-D05 (OQ-AK-09; no class member, B3-DG-01). It feeds the POL-046 financing test (S04-R-10) |
| `noncash_consideration` (rev 1.2) | O | `[{units, fair_value_per_unit, measurement_date, variability, asset_type}]`, `variability` ∈ {`FORM`, `PERFORMANCE`}: the booking payload member of ENGINE_SPEC:OQ-A-07 adopted by 04 B3-D03 (D-76; OQ-AK-07 through `units`, without an estimate kind; S04-R-18) |
| `consideration_payable` (rev 1.2) | O | `[{amount, promise_date, related_obligation_keys, distinct_good_fair_value?, committed_purchases?, share_based}]`: the payload member of ENGINE_SPEC:OQ-A-08 adopted by 04 B3-D04 (D-76; OQ-AK-08; S04-R-14, S04-R-16). An absent `distinct_good_fair_value` means that the whole amount reduces the transaction price (no distinct good, or a fair value that is not reasonably estimable); `committed_purchases` is the release base under POL-049 `COMMITTED_PURCHASES`. A contract may instead use the `EXPECTED_PURCHASES` encoding that DG-AK-34 maps to these members (OQ-AKI-04), never both |
| `combination_group` | O | Handle; contracts sharing a handle are combined, with `combination_criterion` (`25_9_A`, `25_9_B`, `25_9_C`) on the first member |
| `lines` | R | API-S-ContractLine fields: `obligation_key`, `product_code`, `stratification`, `quantity`, `total_price`, `unit_price`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `performing_entity_code`, `ssp_version_label`, `ssp_override_justification`, `account_overrides` (role → account code), `scope_flag`, `out_of_scope_amount`, `bundle_parent_obligation_key`, `memo_1` to `memo_3` |
| `policy_overrides` | O | `[{policy_key, value, obligation_key?, rationale}]`, APPROVED at booking (T-CON-23). Rev 1.299 (register index 308; release 1.0): the engine runner stores them so; the platform runner creates none — the product offers no policy override — and a platform key that declares one is not passed: one finding beside its figures (`platform_runner.key_verdict`) |
| `judgements` | O | `[{handle, topic, subject_obligation_key?, book_code?, conclusion, rationale?, questionnaire?}]`, REVIEWED records (T-CON-19) referenced from payloads by `judgement: <handle>`. `rationale` (rev 1.26; D-98 54) is the T-CON-19 column `rationale` (`JudgementCreateIn.rationale`); the engine runner ignores it; the platform runner refuses the judgement by name when it is absent (never derived from `conclusion`). `book_code` (rev 1.2; D-76 per-book judgements; OQ-AK-13; B3-DG-07) is an E-02 code of `books`, T-CON-19 column `book_code`; absent means the judgement applies to every book. `questionnaire` (rev 1.3; ADJUDICATION.md R-SCH-17) is the T-CON-19 column `questionnaire`. It holds exactly the members that 04 T-CON-19 lists for the topic: booleans as YAML `true` or `false`; dates and decimals as quoted strings; `obligation_key` and `integrates_into_obligation_key` as obligation handles of the contract (`""` means the contract, for `SFC_ASSESSMENT`); `estimate_key` as an `element_code` of the contract (D-93 (3), rev 1.8: the engine's S04-R-04 `claim_enforceable` and `CONSTRAINT` readers accept that element code and the ENGINE_SPEC §0.4 qualified key `<contract external_id>/<element_code>`; the record may sit on the contract or on the element's obligation through `subject_obligation_key`); `product_code` and `discount_exception_bundle` as product codes. It is required when the topic's schema has required members, because a record without them cannot be submitted. A topic without required members may omit it; the record is then evidence only, and the engine reads no outcome from it. Keys supply the outcomes the engine reads, for example: `SFC_ASSESSMENT {obligation_key: "", significant: true, exception_32_17: NONE}`, so that a significant gap or a template with `sfc_assessment_required` raises no `SFC_REVIEW_REQUIRED` (ENGINE_SPEC S04-R-10); `BILL_AND_HOLD` with the four 606-10-55-83 members for a `BILL_AND_HOLD` trigger (ENGINE_SPEC_B S09-R-12); `OTHER {claim_enforceable: true, estimate_key}` for a claim (S04-R-04); `OTHER {discount_exception_bundle}` for an approved discount exception (S05-R-11) |
| `estimates` | O | `[{element_code, estimate_kind, method, obligation_key?, vc_element_type?, allocation_target?, target_obligation_keys?, allocation_criteria_evidence?, direction?, versions: [{version_no, effective_date, scenarios?, parameters?, unconstrained_amount?, most_conservative_amount?, constrained_amount?, rate?, expected_total_amount?, expected_quantity?, amortization_months?, currency?, rationale}]}]` (T-CON-12, T-CON-13); versions are APPROVED when the timeline applies them. Rev 1.2 (D-76): `parameters` is the T-CON-13 parameter object of the estimate kind, validated against its JSON schema (for example `RETURN_RATE` `{carrying_cost_per_unit, recovery_cost_per_unit, window_end_date}`, `ROYALTY_ACCRUAL` `{usage_period_start_date, usage_period_end_date}`; OQ-AKI-01, OQ-AKT-16); `scenarios` is `[{outcome, probability, amount}]` with probabilities summing to 1; `direction` ∈ {`INCREASE`, `DECREASE`} (T-CON-12; 04 B3-D16). Amount columns hold magnitudes (OQ-AKT-10). When `direction` is absent, the loader derives `DECREASE` for estimate kind `IMPLICIT_PRICE_CONCESSION` and for `vc_element_type` ∈ {`IMPLICIT_PRICE_CONCESSION`, `REBATE`, `VOLUME_TIER`, `PRICE_PROTECTION`, `SLA_CREDIT`, `DISCOUNT`, `RETURN`, `REFUND`, `PENALTY`} (topics convention T-03), else `INCREASE` (B3-DG-17). `allocation_criteria_evidence` (D-91; lane commit db5d965) is the element-level T-CON-12 `erev.memo` member, the 606-10-32-40(a) and (b) attestation of a targeted element; the engine runner carries it into every version's `parameters` beside the T-CON-13 parameters, where the shared S05-R-14 / S08-R-04 evidence predicate reads it (present and non-empty is evidenced); `VC-D91-01-TARGETED-THEN-UNTARGETED-CHANGE` is the first key that carries it |
| `material_rights` | O | `[{obligation_key, option_type, incremental_discount_ratio?, is_discount_available_without_contract?, expected_purchase_amount?, ssp_method, expiry_date?, likelihood_estimate?, is_legacy_quantity_ssp_dollars?}]` (T-CON-14) |
| `modifications` | O | `[{reference, effective_date, kind, template_mode?, questionnaire?, lines, price_change_amount?, chosen_treatments?, ssp_basis?}]` (T-CON-06); `chosen_treatments` omitted means the engine-proposed treatments are chosen. Rev 1.2 (OQ-AKI-06; B3-DG-15): all lines of one modification use one of two forms. Delta form, marked by `action` ∈ {`ADD`, `REMOVE`, `CHANGE`}: the T-CON-06 `lines` members `obligation_key`, `action`, `product_code`, `quantity_delta`, `consideration_delta`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `stratification`, `selling_entity_code`, `account_codes` (role → account code), `ssp_version_label`, `memo_1` to `memo_3`; `consideration_delta` is ΔC of the line and `price_change_amount` is the SATISFIED_PERFORMANCE part (ALG-04 §2.5.5; topics convention T-09). Terms form, without `action`: the API-S-ContractLine fields of `lines` above, carrying the post-modification terms of each affected line; `price_change_amount` is the signed ΔC of the contract. A terms-form line that the conversion reads as CHANGE (its obligation key in force at the modification date — a booked line or a line of an earlier modification — under a kind other than `REMOVE_OBLIGATION` or `TERMINATION`, with no `end_date` before that date) carrying `quantity` 0 and a non-zero finite `total_price` is refused at load with the line's `quantity` pointer: a removal of every unit prices 0 (D-97 (1c) v3; `support.answer_keys.terms.terms_line_action` is the conversion's own classification). ADD, REMOVE and TERMINATION lines, zero-price lines and malformed numbers are unaffected, each with a control. A key-format rule of the test loader, not API or import enforcement. A modification with `lines: []` changes the price only, with the signed ΔC in `price_change_amount`. `questionnaire` maps obligation keys to answer objects whose members are T-CON-06 questionnaire members, for example `added_goods_distinct`, `priced_at_ssp`, `remaining_goods_distinct_from_transferred` (booleans) and `price_change_settlement` ∈ {`FUTURE_PRICING`, `CREDIT_OR_REFUND`} (04 B3-D07; B3-DG-16) |

A money field (`total_price`, `amount` and the others typed Money in 04 §16) is written either as `{amount, currency}` or as a string; a string means the contract's `transaction_currency`.

#### 9.5.5 `timeline[]`

| Field | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `seq` | R | Integers 1, 2, 3, … without gaps |
| `kind` | R | `event` \| `period_state` \| `command` (`command` only for `runner: platform`) |
| `contract` | R for `event` | Contract handle |
| `event_type` | R for `event` | E-03 literal. `CONTRACT_BOOKED` with `payload: {}` books `contracts[]` as defined; `CONTRACT_ACTIVATED` with `payload: {}` supplies a passing checklist |
| `effective_date` | R for `event` | Date in the contracting entity's time zone. Effective dates may decrease with `seq` (late and backdated events); events apply in (effective_date, seq) order (DG-AK-44; rev 1.2) |
| `recorded_at` | O | `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ"`; strictly increasing with `seq`. The engine runner uses the value as the event's record time. The platform runner cannot backdate record time (DB-08), so it preserves the order and captures real server times (DG-AK-41). Default: `max(local noon of effective_date in the entity time zone converted to UTC, previous recorded_at + 1 second)`; items without an effective date use previous + 1 second; `seq` 1 defaults from its effective date |
| `payload` | R for `event` | 04 §16.3 payload fields; handles instead of ids: `modification: <reference>`, `estimate: <element_code>` with `version_no`, `judgement: <handle>`, `obligation_key`. Rev 1.2: `modification` supplies `modification_id` and, for `CONTRACT_AMENDED`, `treatments` (chosen, else proposed), `lines` and `ssp_basis` from `contracts[].modifications[]`; `estimate` with `version_no` supplies `estimate_version_id` and `previous_estimate_version_id`; `judgement` supplies `judgement_record_id`; `new_lines` of `MATERIAL_RIGHT_EXERCISED` use the §9.5.4 line fields. `BILLING_RECORDED` may carry `tax_lines: [{tax_type, amount, principal_or_agent}]`, the 04 §16.3 payload members, with `principal_or_agent` ∈ {`PRINCIPAL`, `AGENT`} (D-76 tax lines; rev 1.3, ADJUDICATION.md R-SCH-16, replacing the T-SRC-05 members of B3-DG-08), instead of `tax_amount`; the runner then sets `tax_amount` = Σ `amount`. Members that 04 §16.3 does not list and that are not named here fail loading |
| `is_manual` | O | Default false; `runner: platform` routes manual events through approval with the approver persona |
| `entity`, `book`, `period_key`, `state` | R for `period_state` | Target E-04 state. The engine runner updates bundle period states; the platform runner executes the close commands that reach the state |
| `command` | R for `command` | `{name, params}` with `name` in `close_run`, `journal_run`, `lock_period`, `reopen_period`, `publish_fx_rate_set`, `import_upload` (`params.template_code`, `params.fixture` relative to `backend/tests/fixtures/`) |
| `expect_problem` | O | `{code, rule_id?, status?}`: the step must fail with this problem code or engine code and leave state unchanged; the timeline continues. For engine keys (D-79): the item enters only the bundle of its own step, whose `compute` must raise `EngineError` with that code; it never enters a checkpoint bundle or a later step bundle, and the step's CV-15 findings are that checkpoint's `ERROR` exception rows |

#### 9.5.6 `checkpoints[]`

| Field | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | R | Slug, unique in the key |
| `after_seq` | R | `known_at` = `recorded_at` of that timeline item |
| `as_of` | R | Date. [J] (rev 1.162; supervisor ruling R-118 (a)) When `as_of` is a period end after the version's date, the engine runner compares the version and obligation members through its own to-date overlay on the period nodes of the trace (`support.answer_keys.runners`, `to_date`), which takes the revenue since the version date from `scheduled_amount` whatever the obligation's pattern; the product's reader takes it from the scheduled amount first and then from the awaiting-trigger amount (04 API-C-10 rev 1.179). The overlay is the oracle's side and keeps its rule: no leaf of the corpus tells the two apart (`tests/answer_keys/test_answer_key_reads.py` sets the reader beside every leaf a key states), and an oracle's comparison rule moves only with a case that needs it |
| `book` | R | One of `books` |
| `contracts` | O | Contract blocks (below) |
| `subledger` | O | Subledger blocks (below) |
| `journals` | O | `runner: platform` only: `[{run: {entity, period_key, mode, grain}, match, lines: [{account, dr?, cr?, contract?, legacy_key?}]}]` over `journal_line` |
| `reports` | O | `runner: platform` only: `[{report_code, parameters, cells: [{row_key, column_key, value}]}]` over report runs (API-R-49 cell keys). Rev 1.2 (D-76): `parameters` are the parameter keys of the report definition (SCREENS_B RPT-nn; for example `entity_codes`, `book`, `period_key`, `from_period_key`, `to_period_key`, `time_bands`); cell keys follow the OQ-AK-11 convention of the table "Report cell keys" below, normalised by DG-AK-35 |
| `period_states` | O | `runner: platform` only: `[{entity, book, period_key, state}]` |
| `groups` (rev 1.2; OQ-AKT-06; B3-DG-13) | O | `[{group, balances: [{entity, <API-S-ContractBalance field>: money, functional: {…}}]}]`: labelled balances of a combination group per legal entity (DG-AK-57); `group` is a `combination_group` handle of `contracts[]` |
| `exceptions` | O | `[{code, severity, contract?, obligation_key?, subject?}]`; exact set for listed codes. `code` is a 04 §15.4 catalogue code; `severity` is the finding severity `ERROR` or `WARNING`, compared with `exception_item.severity` through the 04 §15.4 mapping (`ERROR` ↔ `BLOCKING`, `WARNING` ↔ `WARNING`) (D-73, B1-014). Rev 1.2 (B3-DG-12): a row with `subject` compares a DG-AK-45 range-validation finding instead of an exception item; `subject` = `ssp:<ssp book code>:<version label>:<product>`, where the version label is `legacy_version_label`, else `effective_from_date`. Rev 1.6 (D-90d; L9-RUN-Q-1): a row's `contract` and `obligation_key` match the decoded leading CV-21 component of the finding's `subject_key` (`_subject_parts`); findings carry no line dimensions, so the D-90 `contract_key` attribution of the subledger block does not apply to them. A finding whose subject is a group-level key (`<group>@<entity>`: stage 12 FX_RATE_MISSING and S12-INV-03; a stage 10 refund component key) is listed by a row without `contract` |

Contract block:

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `contract` | Handle (R) |
| `status_in_book` | E-17 literal |
| `version` | Subset of `contract_version` columns: `transaction_price`, `fixed_consideration`, `vc_constrained_amount`, `vc_excluded_amount`, `expected_returns_amount`, `consideration_payable_amount`, `financing_adjustment_amount`, `noncash_consideration_amount`, `sales_tax_excluded_amount`, `out_of_scope_amount`, `total_ssp`, `revenue_cum`, `billed_cum`, `rpo_amount`, `scheduled_amount`, `awaiting_trigger_amount`, `modification_boundary_no`. Signed members are asserted with their sign (rev 1.3; ENGINE_SPEC S04-R-02; ADJUDICATION.md R-SGN-01): `expected_returns_amount` and `consideration_payable_amount` are ≤ 0 (for example `"-300.00"`), and `financing_adjustment_amount` is negative for a deferred payment and positive for an advance payment |
| `obligations` | `[{obligation_key, <any T-CON-11 value column>: value}]`; unknown column names fail loading |
| `balances` | `[{entity, <API-S-ContractBalance field>: money, functional: {…}}]` |
| `schedule` | `[{obligation_key \| cost_asset, schedule_kind, line_type (default NORMAL), amounts: {<period_key>: money}}]` or `[{…, period_key, amount, cumulative_amount?, quantity?}]` |
| `modifications` | `[{reference, proposed_treatments: {<obligation_key>: E-23 literal}, treatment_summary?}]` |
| `trace` | `[{measure, subject_key, period_key?, value, formula_id?}]`; asserts the node exists with that value |

Subledger block (`runner: engine` compares the journal entries in `OutputBundle` for periods ending on or before `as_of`; `runner: platform` compares `subledger_line` rows with `recorded_at ≤ known_at`):

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `period_key`, `entity` | R |
| `match` | `exact`: the non-zero aggregated keys for the period, entity, book (and `contract`, when given) equal the listed lines, so `lines: []` asserts that nothing posted; `subset`: the listed lines exist with these amounts. Lines are net per grain key (DG-AK-56; rev 1.2) |
| `contract` | O filter. Under `runner: engine` (rev 1.5; D-90) an entry belongs to the contract named by the `contract_key` its lines carry; `contract_key` is the member-contract line dimension that `backend/erev_engine/stages/s14_posting/intents.py` `_dimensions` sets beside the S14-R-13 dimensions. Attribution fails closed: every line of the entry carries the same `contract_key`, the value is a member of the checkpoint's combination group, and it does not contradict a contract embedded in the subject or in a component source (`<group>@<entity>/<KIND>/<source>`). An entry that cannot be attributed is reported as a mismatch through `subledger()`, never dropped silently and never reported twice. "Never reported twice" is per contract-filtered block key (period_key, entity, contract, entry key) (rev 1.6; D-90d; L9-RUN-Q-5): each block is one assertion, so an entry no member can claim appears once in each member's block of the same period and entity; unfiltered blocks never report it. Blocks without `contract` aggregate as before; `runner: platform` blocks are unchanged |
| `grain` | `role` \| `role_account` (default) \| `role_account_obligation` |
| `lines` | `[{account_role, clearing_purpose?, account?, obligation_key?, entry_kind?, origin_period_key?, counterparty_entity?, dr?, cr?, functional_dr?, functional_cr?}]`; exactly one of `dr` and `cr` per line (POLICIES.md §0.9); `clearing_purpose` as in `account_mapping` (D-14a) |

Report cell keys (rev 1.2; D-76; OQ-AK-11; 04 B3-D19; SCREENS_B RPT-03, RPT-04, RPT-06, RPT-08). Keys write the OQ-AK-11 vocabulary; DG-AK-35 normalises the row keys, and the platform runner compares the report run value named here.

| Report code | Row keys in keys | Column keys in keys | Value compared in the report run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rpo` | contract handle; `TOTAL` | For the resolved POL-201 bands [b1, …, bn]: `within_<b1>_months`, then `months_<b(i)+1>_to_<b(i+1)>` for i = 1 to n − 1, then `after_<bn>_months`, and `total`. Default bands [12, 24]: `within_12_months`, `months_13_to_24`, `after_24_months`, `total` | Section 1 row `contract:<external id>` or the totals row `TOTAL:<currency>`; the run row's flat band field named by the band key (`within_<b1>_months`, `months_<b(i)+1>_to_<b(i+1)>`, `after_<bn>_months`; default `within_12_months`, `months_13_to_24`, `after_24_months`) beside `total`, `current` and `noncurrent`, or `total` (rev 1.18; the API `bands` list is column metadata, not the row shape) |
| `contract_balance_rollforward` | entity code | `opening_contract_liability`, `billings`, `revenue_from_opening_liability`, `revenue_from_period_billings`, `fx`, `closing_contract_liability` | Section 1 rows `OPENING`, `BILLINGS`, `REVENUE_FROM_OPENING`, `REVENUE_FROM_PERIOD_BILLINGS`, `FX_REMEASUREMENT` and `CLOSING` respectively, field `contract_liability`; activity is signed, so revenue lines are negative |
| `revenue_from_opening_liability` | entity code; contract handle | `opening_contract_liability`, `revenue_recognized`, `revenue_from_opening_liability` | Section 2 fields `opening_contract_liability`, `revenue_recognized` and `revenue_from_opening` respectively, from the row of the contract, or summed over the rows of the entity |
| `disaggregation` | `timing:POINT_IN_TIME`; `timing:OVER_TIME`; `<dimension>:<value>` | `revenue` | Field `total`, summed over the matching rows: `timing:<pattern>` matches every row whose `row_key` ends with `:<pattern>`; `<dimension>:<value>` matches the rows whose dimension value is `<value>` when the run's `dimension_code` is `<dimension>` |
| any other code | the `row_key` values of the report definition | the field names of the report definition | The cell with that row key and field |

A row of zeros the report does not state (rev 1.219). In a `reports` block, a row whose every expected measure is exactly zero compares clean when the report run states no row that matches it: a report states the rows it has figures for, not a grid of zeros (`disaggregation` states a timing row only where a revenue line exists in the range; 606-10-50-5 asks for the categories revenue falls into). The rule is narrow. A row the run does state is compared as stated; a row with any non-zero expected measure that the run lacks is a mismatch in every cell, its zero cells included; and the rule does not apply to subledger lines, balances or contract figures.

#### 9.5.7 Comparison rules

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-AK-50 | Types come from the 04 column domain of the field (`erev.money`, `erev.exact`, `erev.fx_rate`, enum, date, integer, boolean, text), resolved through `erev_api.db.tables`. |
| DG-AK-51 | Money: the expected string has exactly the minor-unit places of the currency in context (transaction currency, or the entity functional currency inside `functional`). The engine value must be equal (D-17: exact to the minor unit). |
| DG-AK-52 | Exact values and rates: the expected string has d decimals, 0 ≤ d ≤ 18 (≤ 12 for rates). The key passes when the engine's full-precision value rounded ROUND_HALF_UP to d places equals the expected value. |
| DG-AK-53 | Enums, text, dates, integers and booleans: equality. Absent fields are not asserted. |
| DG-AK-54 | Implicit assertions for every checkpoint: posted allocations sum to the allocation basis per combination group and book, and Σ `allocated_amount` = `transaction_price − consideration_payable_amount` per contract version (P1; DB-17 V1; rev 1.2, ENGINE_SPEC:OQ-A-04, ENGINE_SPEC_B:OQ-B-02); `allocated_amount = revenue_cum + scheduled_amount + awaiting_trigger_amount` per obligation (DB-17); journal entries balance per (entity, book, currency, period) (D-16); `reevaluate(trace)` reproduces every node (P14). |
| DG-AK-55 | All mismatches of all checkpoints are collected before the test fails; the failure message lists key id, checkpoint, object, field, expected and actual. |
| DG-AK-56 | Subledger aggregation (rev 1.2; D-76; OQ-AKI-02; fx-entity-books convention C-05). Actual lines are summed per grain key: `account_role`; `clearing_purpose`; `account` for `role_account` and `role_account_obligation`; `obligation_key` for `role_account_obligation`; `origin_period_key`; `counterparty_entity`; and `entry_kind` when every listed line of the block names it. A key whose net transaction amount and net functional amount are both zero is omitted. The expected side is `dr` or `cr` by the sign of the net transaction amount or, when that amount is zero, by the sign of the net functional amount; such functional-only lines (FX remeasurement) carry `dr: "0.00"` or `cr: "0.00"` with `functional_dr` or `functional_cr`. |
| DG-AK-57 | Group balances (rev 1.2; OQ-AKT-06). A `groups[].balances` value equals, per entity and field, the sum over the member contracts of the T-CON-09 labelled balances of each member's latest version known at `known_at`; the engine runner sums the member balances of `OutputBundle`. Member contract blocks keep their own `balances` (T-CON-09 member rows). |
| DG-AK-58 | Period-close passes (rev 1.13; D-94 (3)). Before a checkpoint dated at a period end is compared, the runner runs the period-close passes of that period in the order `FX_REMEASUREMENT`, `CLOSE_RELEASE`, `NETTING_RECLASS` (`support.answer_keys.runners.CLOSE_PASSES`), each reading the earlier passes as posted (05 RCP-08(b)): the FX pass measures the period-end position (JET-10d) first, the release pass then posts the `TIME` amounts of the period (the dated 606-10-25-7 releases, JET-01b) at the remeasured carrying, and the netting reclass runs last. RCP-08 does not order the first two; FX first keeps the L6-5 checkpoint oracle (`test_l6_5_checkpoint_runs_the_fx_remeasurement_pass_first`). Totals are identical under the other order; only the pass carrying the period-end amounts differs. |

#### 9.5.8 Loader contract

```python
# Binding signature: backend/tests/support/answer_keys/loader.py
ANSWER_KEY_ROOT: Final[Path]          # REPO_ROOT / "docs/accounting/answer-keys"
SCHEMA_ID: Final = "erev-answer-key/1"

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class LoadedKey:
    key: AnswerKey                    # Pydantic model of §9.5.2 to §9.5.6, extra="forbid"
    path: Path
    sha256: str

class AnswerKeyError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, path: Path, pointer: str, message: str) -> None: ...   # pointer = JSON Pointer

def discover(root: Path = ANSWER_KEY_ROOT) -> list[Path]: ...
def load(path: Path) -> LoadedKey: ...
def load_all(*, families: Iterable[str] = (), ids: Iterable[str] = (), requirements: Iterable[str] = (),
             include_withdrawn: bool = False, root: Path = ANSWER_KEY_ROOT) -> list[LoadedKey]: ...
def coverage(keys: Sequence[LoadedKey]) -> CoverageReport: ...

# Binding signature: backend/tests/support/answer_keys/runners.py
def run_engine(key: LoadedKey) -> RunResult: ...
def run_platform(key: LoadedKey, db: TestDatabase) -> RunResult: ...
def assert_checkpoints(key: LoadedKey, result: RunResult) -> None: ...

# backend/tests/answer_keys/test_answer_keys.py
pytestmark = pytest.mark.answer_key
@pytest.mark.parametrize("loaded", load_all(**selection_from_env()), ids=lambda k: k.key.id)
def test_answer_key(loaded: LoadedKey, request: pytest.FixtureRequest) -> None: ...
```

The runner's checkpoint report run opens its unit of work, and runs its job, on the record-time clock — one `SELECT clock_timestamp()` read, the clock that stamps the checkpoint — so its record-time `known_at` validates against record time (the framework refuses a `known_at` later than `uow.now`): the business clock is never substituted for the cutoff, the cutoff never advanced, the check never bypassed; journal runs keep the application clock. ACT-1 refuses a principal mapped for the client that is not an API client; the database platform reads the client from its committed creating step with the grants of a token of its scopes (`api_client_grants`); the lane's stand-in is an `api_client` row (`db_personas.integration_principal`). A manual progress, milestone, cost or acceptance item is refused by name for want of the evidence document the key schema does not state (`request_models.EVIDENCE_GAP`); no key of the corpus marks an item manual. Rev 1.213 (item AK-PLATFORM-RUNNER-1; the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-01): what the runner supplies beyond the key. A key states a world, contracts and events, not the workflow the product asks of the people who enter them; where the product asks for more, the runner supplies it through the product's commands as a person would, test-side — never an input or an expected value of a key. Most of it is conversion and states nothing: everyone accepts the invitation they were sent before they act; an SSP version is submitted with a study page of the runner's own and approved by a decision of `ak-ssp-approver`; a policy value and a report parameter go in the JSON type their own schema declares; a decision states the subject digest of its request — for a judgement record the request's own, never the record's `content_sha256` (04 §16.10) — and the digest of the impact preview the request shows (REQ-PLT-015); the approval of an activation is the activation, and the plan calls no hook after it; a key product that omits `principal_agent` is created as `PRINCIPAL` (D-83 ruling 1); a `legacy_range` SSP entry sends no band (04 T-REF-31); each entity's calendar holds the fiscal years the key's dates reach, and only the periods of `world.periods` are opened; under a preset other than `DEFAULT` the key's tenant values of the preset's category go into the preset's own version, in the edit that dates it; and the runner's process stamps its release before the first computation (05 REL-03). Three things are statements, made before each activation where the key is silent (04 table 15.4-I; `platform_plan._activation_prerequisites`): (1) the contract's order reference is its own `external_id`; (2) one reviewed `COLLECTIBILITY` record of the contract, of no book, whose five criteria of 606-10-25-1 are answered Yes, and per enabled book of the contracting entity a probable `COLLECTIBILITY_ASSESSED` event that cites it, dated at the contract's inception — the date of the activation, which reads the assessment in force there — recorded by `ak-preparer` (a person's assessment is none of the event types that wait for a second person); (3) per obligation of a contract of two or more obligations a reviewed distinct review that confirms the conclusion of the obligation's template. A contract for which the key itself states Step 1 — a judgement of topic `COLLECTIBILITY` or `NOT_A_CONTRACT`, or a `COLLECTIBILITY_ASSESSED` item — gets no record of the runner's. The bound: the runner states only what the key's expected values already imply — a key whose expected outcome is a contract that is not one, or an obligation that is not distinct, is refused by the runner by name (`platform_plan.STEP1_BOUND`, `DISTINCT_BOUND`), not given the default statement. The database platform stops at the first step it refuses by name: no later step is run and each names that step, no block is compared, and the key ends not run with that reason — never on a refusal of the product's own. Rev 1.219 (the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-01 on the runner's reads and its world): (a) a checkpoint's subledger is the group's sealed postings through the checkpoint's cutoff — the posting of every computation of the group known at or before `known_at[after_seq]`, not the as-of computation's alone (READ-2 as amended): the product posts each computation's increments, so the as-of computation's posting alone is one increment of a key's cumulative block. A posting is placed by its computation's `known_at`, the record time a contract version is placed by — its own stamps are the application clock's — and a posting no event's computation wrote (a close run's pass, a manual adjustment) is refused by name until the plan's close-run step places it. Comparison rules and tolerances do not move. (b) Until the plan runs the product's close run (item AK-CLOSE-RUN-STEP-1), a block whose expected figures hold a period-end pass (DG-AK-58) is not run on the database platform, with that item by name, and never compared as mismatches: the oracle computes the passes with every checkpoint, the product posts them in a close run. Such a block is a subledger block — one period, entity and, where it names one, contract — or a journal run that the oracle's own books answer differently with the passes than without (`platform_runner.close_pass_blocks`); every block the passes leave as it is is compared. (c) A `LEGACY_PARITY` key's plan creates the parity templates `LEGACY-DISTINCT`, `LEGACY-NONDISTINCT`, `LEGACY-MATERIAL-RIGHT` and `LEGACY-VC` through the template lifecycle, as it creates the key's own, unless the key defines the code itself. In the product the migration import's confirmed prerequisites (`domain/migration/prerequisites.py`) name these templates, bind the products they create to them and refuse a SKU whose parity template the workspace lacks; nothing but the template lifecycle writes a template, so the plan's lifecycle steps stand in for that authoring and are no product path of their own — the plan runs no import. (d) The reader hands the comparison the group under the key's group name: the product numbers its groups (`CG-<contract number>`), and the contract version's subject and the group nodes of the hash-verified trace — their ids, the inputs that cite them and the root measures — are handed over under the name the key gives the group, as an obligation is handed its entity codes back; no value moves, and the comparison side stays free of the product's numbering on every platform. Rev 1.246 (item AK-CLOSE-RUN-STEP-1; the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-01 on the lane's measurement of a whole close run in the worlds of POS-CHK-012 and POS-CHK-117): the plan runs the product's close run. (a) Where a checkpoint's blocks expect a period-end pass — the blocks rev 1.219 (b) left not run, found as there (`platform_runner.pass_blocks`, until this revision `close_pass_blocks`) — the plan has a step of phase `CLOSE` right after the last step of the checkpoint's last item and before the next item: `close_runs.start` (`POST /close-runs`) as the preparer, who holds `period.close`, for the entity and period of those blocks and the checkpoint's book, each once; two checkpoints after one item share a run. The runner is the worker: it runs the `CLOSE_RUN` job the command deferred to its end — steps 1 to 13, no lock, no approval, no export. A run that does not end `SUCCEEDED` fails the key by name — the run, its status, the step it stopped at and that step's problem — and is never a step not run: the product was asked for its close run and did not give it. A run needs nothing a key's world lacks (it calculates its own draft journal run; its export, acknowledgement and tie-out steps record what they find) and leaves the period `open`. (b) The step's application instant is local noon of the checkpoint's as-of date in the entity's time zone, at least one second after the item it follows; the next item keeps its own record time, which may be the same instant. (c) The step stamps `known_at[after_seq]` again: a checkpoint reads at the stamp taken after its close run. (d) One rule for what the product stamps with the application clock — a posting no event's computation wrote (a close run's pass, a manual adjustment) and a period state's transition. The plan sets that clock to an item's business time, so such a stamp says nothing at a server-time cutoff. The row is placed by the transaction that wrote it (`subledger_posting.created_txid`, `period_state_transition.created_txid`: the server's `txid_current()`, 04 DB-06 and DB-07): it is at or before a checkpoint when that transaction began before the transaction horizon — the first transaction id not yet assigned — which the runner reads with the checkpoint's stamp and keeps beside it in its ledger. The placement rests on the steps running one after another, each committed before the next begins: the order of their transactions is then the order of the steps, also where two steps carry one application instant, and a runner that ran steps side by side would have to place these rows by another rule (rev 1.252). The subledger read of rev 1.219 (a) therefore refuses no posting for want of a place: a close run's release posting is its group's; its FX and reclass postings are the entity's and name no group (05 RCP-08 (b)), and of those a group's entries are the ones whose lines name one of its contracts. READ-5 answers a period's state from the transitions whose transaction began before the horizon; until this revision it compared their application-clock stamps with the server cutoff and answered every checkpoint with the period's latest state (no platform key has a period-state item or block). A platform that kept no horizon refuses both reads by name. A posting of an event's computation stays placed by its computation's `known_at`. (e) One run journalises a seal (04 DB-16 — the runs of every mode count), so after the close run of (a), whose own draft run holds the period's seals, and after an earlier block's run, a further run of a journals block would cover nothing (measured in the world of POS-CHK-012: no line, both times). Until rev 1.263 such a block was not run on the database platform, by name — of GT07's four journal runs the second of ME1 and both of ME2; rev 1.263 gives every journals block its run. A key's own `close_run` command stays unbuilt: §9.5.3 names no parameters for it. Rev 1.263 (item AK-JOURNAL-RUN-PLAN-1; the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-02 on the lane's measurement and on its build): the plan makes the journal run of a journals block. (a) A step of phase `JOURNAL` per block, the checkpoints in the key's order and each checkpoint's blocks in theirs, right after the checkpoint's last step — after the close run of rev 1.246 (a) where the plan has one — and before the next item: `journals.commands.create_run` (`POST /journal-runs`) as the preparer, who holds `journal.run`, for the block's entity, period, mode and grain in the key's primary book. The step stamps nothing. The checkpoint's journals read creates nothing: it answers the lines the step read and kept in the runner's ledger, and a block whose step did not run is not run, by name. (b) The step reads the run that stands for the block's entity, book and period when that run is the period's whole journal in the block's form — the only run that is not cancelled, of the block's mode and grain, from the first seal to the last one sealed (for a `DELTA` run its LEGACY range likewise): the close run's own draft run right after the close run, for a block of the mode and grain the policies resolved (POL-005, POL-006). Otherwise it cancels the standing runs, latest first — the product refuses any other order (ruling R-52 (b)) — through `journals.commands.cancel_run`, and creates the block's own, whose `JOURNAL_RUN_CALCULATE` job the runner works. The lines are read at once, so the cancel a later block needs does not take them. What the product refuses — a cancel, the create, a calculation that leaves no run — fails the key by name, as a close run that does not succeed does. (c) The step gives no cutoff: the command takes the application clock, and the step's application instant is the latest of any step before it. `summarise.covered_to` compares a run's cutoff with `sealed_at`, which the product stamps with that clock, so the run covers exactly the seals that exist at the step; a seal a later item writes does not exist yet. Until this revision the runner made the run when the checkpoint was read — after the whole plan — with the checkpoint's server stamp as the cutoff, which the business instant of every seal precedes (measured in the world of POS-CHK-012: a run made at the end of the plan with the stamp taken before the close run held the reclass that run posted after the stamp, and its range ran over a seal of a later item). (d) After a checkpoint's last block the run of that block stands, `draft`; the close run's own run stands cancelled where a block needed another form. No platform key reaches a journals block yet — GT07 stops at its contract's nondistinct obligation — so the witness of this revision is POS-CHK-012 with a GROSS and a DELTA block given to the key in memory, their expected lines the oracle's own (`tests/domain/answer_keys/test_platform_journal_plan_db.py`); a `DELTA` run beside a LEGACY book is not witnessed. The reasons of a period that locks or reopens say what is true (the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02): the product has the commands, and the plan builds no sequence for a period state and finds no parameters named for a key's own `lock_period` or `reopen_period` command (§9.5.3). Rev 1.278 (lane QA-BE, EX42's conversion; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02): what the runner supplies before an estimate version is submitted (04 T-CON-13 and §16.14 rev 1.241, table 15.4-D; PRD ERR-93, ERR-94, IMP-138, IMP-140; `platform_plan._estimate_prerequisites`). Two things are conversion and state nothing: an estimate version is created at its own `ESTIMATE_CHANGED` item — after its predecessor was approved, since one version of an element is open at a time — and no longer drafted at the booking; and a variable-consideration, EAC or return-rate version is submitted with an evidence page of the runner's own, uploaded as an `ATTACHMENT` and attached to the version by `ak-preparer`, as an SSP version is with its study page. `POST /files` and `POST /attachments` thus serve two subjects of the plan: a step that is an estimate's prerequisite carries the plan's marker, which decides its conversion, the permission it answers to under ACT-2 and the id the ledger gives back. A fourth thing is a statement, made before the submission of a variable-consideration version whose key states no `CONSTRAINT` judgement of the element: (4) one reviewed `CONSTRAINT` record whose subject is the version — the subject SCREENS §8.4 sends, and one that places no hold on the contract (04 T-CON-20 "Judgement holds" rev 1.209) — of no book, naming the element by its code, concluding that a significant reversal of the constrained amount is not probable, with `remote` No. `ak-preparer` creates the version, prepares the record on it and sends it, `ak-approver` reviews it, and `ak-preparer` names it on the version. The key's expected values imply the statement: the key takes the version's constrained amount into the transaction price. A key that states a `CONSTRAINT` judgement of the element — naming it by its code, by the engine's estimate key or by that key and the version — gets no record of the runner's, and its version is created with the key's own. The bound: a key that expects the submission refused gets the conversions and no record. Measured on the database platform with EX42: a record whose subject was the contract held and released the active contract — `HOLD_APPLIED` and `HOLD_RELEASED` on its stream, one computation more — and the key compared clean all the same; with the version as the subject the stream holds the key's own events. |
| DG-AK-42 | Selection variables: `FAMILY` → `families`, `ID` → `ids`, `REQ` → `requirements`. A filtered run skips the coverage check and writes its report as the named diagnostic `answer-keys-filtered` (rev 1.43), never the canonical `answer-keys` report. |
| DG-AK-43 | The report `.run/reports/answer-keys/report.json` lists per key: id, path, `sha256`, runner, result, mismatches and review status; rev 1.43 adds `scope` (kind and the explicit selection) and `corpus` (every corpus key id, the SHA-256 over the sorted `id:sha256` lines, active and withdrawn counts) so a consumer can bind the report's membership to the actual corpus. |
| DG-AK-44 | Event order (rev 1.2; D-76; OQ-AKT-20; topics convention T-16). Events apply in (effective_date, seq) order. The engine runner sets `record_seq = seq`, so the DG-ENG-02 order equals it; events with one effective date apply in `seq` order, including status changes such as `CONTRACT_CRITERIA_MET` and receipts. The platform runner executes items in `seq` order, so record sequencing (DB-08) yields the same order. `period_state` items take effect at their `seq` position. |
| DG-AK-45 | SSP range validation (rev 1.2; OQ-AKT-08; B3-DG-12). For each `world.ssp_books` entry that carries `population`, `run_engine` evaluates POLICIES §3.3 for each range row with the pure helper `erev_api.domain.ssp.range_validation.validate_ranges`: h = max(`high_value` − `mid_value`, `mid_value` − `low_value`) ÷ `mid_value`, c = `inside_count` ÷ `observation_count`, and the tenant value of POL-073 `ssp.range_validation`. It records `RANGE_TOO_WIDE` and `COVERAGE_TOO_LOW` findings with the severity that POL-073 `mode` gives (04 §15.4) and compares them with the checkpoint `exceptions` rows that carry `subject`. The helper imports no database module, and the SSP publication command calls the same function. |

#### 9.5.9 Complete example

The figures below were recomputed with exact rationals under POLICIES.md ALG-01 on 2026-09-12 (`.scratch/design-arch-guide/example_key2.py`). They follow ALG-01 §2.1.3 as confirmed by D-11a. Rev 1.1 writes the ratable convention as `MONTHLY_EVEN`, which equals the former `MONTHLY_WHOLE_MONTHS` on this whole-month term (D-75), so no figure changes. The file illustrates the schema. Answer-key engineers may adopt it into the corpus after revenue-accountant review; the build loop does not write into `docs/accounting/`.

### 9.6 Golden parity runner (G3)

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-PAR-01 | Scope: all 122 tests of `docs/legacy/golden/golden-tests.json`. Test ids, kinds, `steps_through`, `window`, `contract`, `pob` and legacy values come from `golden-tests.json`; expected values, `tolerance`, `classification`, `dev_id` and `related_dev_ids` come from `docs/legacy/golden/deviations.json` `tests[<id>]` (D-17; `docs/legacy/DEVIATIONS.md` §2). One parametrised pytest case per id, marker `parity`, module `backend/tests/parity/test_golden_parity.py`. Case ids are `<kind>::<test id>` (for example `contract_position::rollforward-02-Contract1`), so `make parity K=contract_position` selects a kind. |
| DG-PAR-02 | Fixtures (`scripts/build_fixtures.py`, `make fixtures`): (1) UAT workbooks: for each golden step 01 to 14, read `docs/legacy/golden/NN-<slug>/step.json` (`file`, `file_sha256`). The source is `legacy-harness/erev_copy/<file>`, else `~/dev/erev-legacy/<file>` opened read-only. Verify SHA-256 and copy to `backend/tests/fixtures/legacy_uat/NN-<slug>/<basename>`. (2) Probe inputs: `legacy-harness/out/probes/inputs/*.xlsx` → `backend/tests/fixtures/legacy_probes/`. (3) Shipped database (SQLite as a file format only; D-40a, DG-LAY-11): `legacy-harness/fixtures/ASC606.shipped.db`, verified against `docs/legacy/golden/manifest.json` `shipped_db_sha256`, → `backend/tests/fixtures/legacy_db/ASC606-shipped-step04.db` (docs/02-PRD.md WLD-F-15). (4) Write `backend/tests/fixtures/manifest.json` (`{path, sha256, bytes, source}`). The builder runs with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, never imports `eRev.py`, never writes outside `backend/tests/fixtures/`, and refuses to overwrite a committed fixture with different bytes. When a source is missing and the fixture is absent, it exits 1 with `BLOCKED: legacy fixture <path> unavailable`. Fixtures are committed. |
| DG-PAR-03 | Integrity preconditions, checked once per session: `sha256(golden-tests.json)` equals `deviations.json` `inputs.golden_tests_sha256`; both files hold the same 122 ids; `self_check_failures` is empty; and (rev 1.2, D-11a, B1-001) `deviations.json` `posting_rule_id` equals `EXACT-CUM`, the composition implemented by `erev_engine.money.cumulative_posted` (DG-KRN-MONEY-03), and the keys of `probe_status_mapping` are exactly `authority`, `COMMITTED`, `COMMITTED_WITH_FINDINGS`, `REJECTED` and `error_code` (DG-PAR-10). [F] On 2026-09-12 the regenerated file carries `posting_rule_id: "EXACT-CUM"` and these five keys. Otherwise every case fails with "deviations.json is stale; the supervisor must rerun research-harness/deviations/build_deviations.py". |
| DG-PAR-04 | Scenario: tenant code `legacy-parity-test`, provisioned in `erev_test` (`committed_db`), personas `ak-preparer` and `ak-approver`. Periods 2023-01 to 2023-12 stay `open`. Books `ASC606` (primary) and `LEGACY`. Before step 01, the `LEGACY_PARITY` preset version is created, tested, submitted, approved by `ak-approver` and published (DG-KRN-REG-05). Rev 1.214 (item PINP-PERIOD-VALUE-1): it is dated at the first day of the legacy calendar, 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z — the scenario has no legal entity yet (PRD ERR-75 rev 1.178) — so that every legacy period takes it (05 RCP-15 "The value of a period"). Steps 01 to 14 replay in order through the legacy v1 import pipeline (upload → validate → dry-run diff → submit → approve as `ak-approver` → commit; D-30, REQ-MIG-002). The template comes from the step handler (`browse_file_SSPs` → SKU SSP template, `browse_file_Contracts` → contract setup, `browse_file_Deliveries` → progress tracking, `browse_file_RetroMod` / `browse_file_ProsMod` / `browse_file_POB_specific_VC` → contract modification with E-24 `template_mode` `retrospective`, `prospective` or `pob_price_change`). The upload date parameter is `step.json` `date_input`. The application `FrozenClock` starts at `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` and advances one hour per step. After step NN commits, the runner records `known_at[NN] = SELECT clock_timestamp()` (DB-08 assigns `recorded_at` from the server clock). Step 00 (reset) is a no-op because the tenant is new. Entities `Mock Entity 1` and `Mock Entity 2` are created by the import (LM-CL-09). Rev 1.4 (D-88 L7-1-Q-6; rc stand-in): after each golden step or probe upload commits, the runner stands in for the close run's `NETTING_RECLASS` step through `backend/tests/support/parity/netting.py`. It builds a `CLOSE_RELEASE` bundle per group with a head computation, runs the engine pass over the framework books, and seals the TIME intents of FY2023 periods through `computation._post_book` under a `SUCCEEDED` `close_run` per entity, book and period. It writes no computation or version rows. The posting key `release:<close_run_id>:<group_id>`, where 05 RCP-08(b) names `reclass:<close_run_id>:<entity_id>`, is accepted for the rc because the legacy views ignore posting keys. Post-rc, CLO-20 replaces the stand-in call in `scenario.through` with the close-run step and must keep 121 of 122. |
| DG-PAR-05 | Value sources (full precision). `exact(m)` for an obligation version: the column value when the column is `erev.exact`; for an `erev.money` column, `Fraction(Decimal(node.value)) + Fraction(node.rounding_residue)` of trace node `obligation_version.trace_nodes[m]` (DG-KRN-EXP-03). ENGINE_SPEC must emit trace nodes whose measure names equal these column names (DG-OQ-05). |
| DG-PAR-06 | Probes (`legacy_probe`): each probe runs in its own fresh tenant under the preset and replays `docs/legacy/golden/probes/<id>/probe.json` `sequence` (reset items skipped; button labels mapped as in DG-PAR-04; files from `legacy_probes/` or `legacy_uat/` by basename; `date_input` as the upload date). It asserts, when the expected object contains them: `import_status`, `error_code` and `detail` (DG-PAR-10); `findings[]` (DG-PAR-11); `versions_before` and `versions_after` (count of `obligation_version` rows in book ASC606 before and after the last sequence item, which equals the row count of `legacy_contract_history_export` over all dates); `watched_latest` (rev 1.2: each item names `contract` and `pob`; its other keys are legacy column names of `legacy_contract_history_export`, read from the latest obligation version in book ASC606 through the 04 §17 LM-CL rows, for example `Current Rev Rec - Cumulative` → `revenue_cum` (LM-CL-61) and `Current Period` → `effective_date` (LM-CL-13), at DG-PAR-05 full precision for `erev.money` columns); and journal expectations (rev 1.2): an expected key `je_gross_<label>` or `je_delta_<label>` is compared with report `legacy_je_summary` in the gross or adjustment view over the window `probe.json` `reports[<same key>].window`, field by field as in the `journal_entry_totals` row of the kind table below. Rev 1.4 (D-88 L7-1-Q-7): when `reports` has no entry named for an expected key `je_<gross\|delta>_<YYYY>_<MM>`, the window is `reports['je_<gross\|delta>'].window`, but only if it equals [`YYYY-MM-01`, the last day of that month]; in any other case there is no window and the key fails with `JOURNAL_NO_WINDOW`. Expected values and probe fixtures are never edited. Rev 1.1 (B1-002): an expected object named for one upload (for example P4 `first_2_28_upload` and `second_2_28_upload`) describes, in order, the sequence items that upload the same file, and carries `import_status`, `findings`, `sha256` and, for a refusal, `error_code`. `versions_before_<suffix>` and `versions_after_<suffix>` count around the upload the suffix names (`second` → the second upload). `sha256` is `import_upload.file_sha256`, or for a refused upload the SHA-256 the runner computed over the uploaded bytes. Provenance keys are not asserted: the `condition` and `mapping` members of `import_status_basis` (its `e40_import_status` and `problem` members are asserted, DG-PAR-10), `error_code_source`, `legacy_oracle`, and keys starting with `legacy_replica_` (rev 1.2: names verified against the regenerated `deviations.json`). |
| DG-PAR-07 | Tolerances (D-17; DEVIATIONS.md §2.2): unit-level amounts and quantities pass when `abs(exact − Fraction(expected)) ≤ Fraction(1, 10000)`; journal amounts must equal expected exactly to the cent; codes, counts and texts must be equal. Negative zero equals zero. An expected `null` requires a null actual. |
| DG-PAR-08 | Report `.run/reports/parity/report.json`: per id `{kind, classification, dev_id, passed, mismatches: [{field, expected, actual, legacy}]}`; counts by kind and class; the B ids of `deviations.json` `signoff_required`, each with its DEVIATIONS.md sign-off status; cent-difference cases of class DEV-002 carry the single class sign-off (D-17a). |
| DG-PAR-09 | No case may be skipped or marked xfail (DG-TST-09). Expected values are never edited, because the documents are read-only; a disagreement is fixed in code or recorded as a spec question (DG-DONE-12). |
| DG-PAR-10 | Probe import status (normative; rev 1.1, B1-002). The expected `import_status` values `COMMITTED`, `COMMITTED_WITH_FINDINGS` and `REJECTED` are runner classifications, not stored statuses; E-40 gains no value. The runner classifies each probe upload with the table "Probe import-status mapping" at the end of this section. `deviations.json` `probe_status_mapping` restates that table in prose under its `authority`; the runner never parses it, and DG-PAR-03 checks only its key set (rev 1.2). When the expected object carries `import_status_basis`, its `e40_import_status` must equal the observed E-40 status (null when no `import_upload` row exists), and its `problem` members `slug`, `status` and `errors[].rule_id` must equal the problem response. A terminal state that no row matches (an approver's E-40 `REJECTED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`) is a mismatch. Probes never reject an approval: an upload that validates is submitted and approved by `ak-approver` until `COMMITTED` (DG-PAR-04). Finding severities are `ERROR` and `WARNING` (D-30a; 04 §15.4). |
| DG-PAR-11 | Probe findings (rev 1.1). An upload's findings are its 04 §15.4 catalogue findings: file-stage findings first, then row findings ordered by sheet, Excel row number and code. `findings[]` is compared as an ordered list over `code`, `severity`, `worksheet_row` (the Excel row number; header row = 1), `worksheet_rows` when present (rev 1.2; DEVIATIONS:OQ-D11, D-76: every contributing Excel row, ascending, compared as a list of integers; `worksheet_row` is the lowest of them, and the finding message names every row) and `pob` (the finding's `business_key` with each `" / "` separator replaced by one space, for example `Contract 1 / POB #2 / Software 1` → `Contract 1 POB #2 Software 1`). For any other key of an expected finding whose value is a string or a list of strings (for example `blank_memos`), each string must appear verbatim in the finding's message. An empty expected `findings` list requires zero findings. |

|---|---|---|
