### 9.7 Hypothesis profiles and invariants (G5)

```python
# backend/tests/conftest.py
from hypothesis import HealthCheck, settings
from hypothesis.database import DirectoryBasedExampleDatabase

_DB = DirectoryBasedExampleDatabase(str(REPO_ROOT / "backend/.hypothesis"))
settings.register_profile("dev", max_examples=20, deadline=2000, database=_DB, print_blob=True)
settings.register_profile("ci", max_examples=100, deadline=None, derandomize=True, database=None,
                          print_blob=True, suppress_health_check=[HealthCheck.too_slow])
settings.register_profile("thorough", max_examples=1000, deadline=None, derandomize=False, database=_DB,
                          print_blob=True, suppress_health_check=[HealthCheck.too_slow])
settings.load_profile(os.environ.get("HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE", "dev"))
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-PROP-01 | Profiles: `dev` for local runs (default when `HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE` is unset); `ci` for `make test` and `make ci` (derandomised, reproducible); `thorough` for `make properties` (G5). Platform-layer properties (database-backed) cap examples through `platform_settings()` at 25 under `ci` and 100 under `thorough`. |
| DG-PROP-02 | A failing example found by any profile is pinned with `@example(...)` in the same test before the fix is committed. |
| DG-PROP-03 | Strategies live in `backend/tests/support/strategies.py`: currencies with minor units 0, 2, 3 and 4 (JPY, USD, BHD, CLF); SSP weights including zeros and ratios up to 1:10^12; positive and negative transaction prices; 1 to 200 obligations; monotone progress paths and paths with returns; billing paths; FX rate paths; permutations of the arrival order of commuting events (research 06 §18.3). No strategy produces floats (`floats()` is forbidden). |

| Invariant | Statement (research 06 §18.3; D-12 sign) | Layer | Module |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Posted allocations sum exactly to the allocation basis per combination group × book × currency: Σ `a_posted` = `allocation_basis` = `total` − `expected_returns` − `consideration_payable` (ENGINE_SPEC S04-R-02); the reported `transaction_price` is the build-up total, and Σ `allocated_amount` = `transaction_price − consideration_payable_amount` per contract version (04 DB-17 V1; ENGINE_SPEC_B S09-R-23, OQ-B-02). Rev 1.2 (ENGINE_SPEC:OQ-A-04) | engine | `tests/properties/test_prop_p01_allocation_sum.py` |
| P2 | Each allocation lies within one minor unit of its exact relative-SSP quota | engine | `test_prop_p02_allocation_quota.py` |
| P3 | Zero SSP gives zero allocation; allocation is permutation-invariant; `allocate(−T) = −allocate(T)` | engine | `test_prop_p03_allocation_symmetry.py` |
| P4 | Schedules sum to the allocation at completion; for non-negative allocation and progress in [0, 1], 0 ≤ cumulative ≤ allocation; cumulative lies within half a minor unit of exact | engine | `test_prop_p04_schedule_bounds.py` |
| P5 | Journal debits equal credits per batch × entity × book × currency, in transaction and functional currency | engine and platform | `test_prop_p05_journal_balance.py` |
| P6 | Rollforward ties: opening + billings − revenue ± reclass ± FX remeasurement = closing, for contract liability and contract asset; `net_position = cumulative billed − cumulative revenue` (D-12 overrides the inverted sign printed in research 06, DG-OQ-08) | platform | `test_prop_p06_rollforward.py` |
| P7 | RPO = allocated transaction price − cumulative revenue for unsatisfied or partially satisfied obligations; waterfall totals equal schedule totals | engine and platform | `test_prop_p07_rpo.py` |
| P8 | Replay determinism. (a) Recomputation of one bundle yields byte-identical canonical output (trace and postings) and an identical `OutputBundle.sha256()`, in-process and across processes (CV-26). (b) A shuffled arrival of commuting events — an interleaving of a group's contract streams that keeps each stream's own order, so record sequence and tuple position change and event keys, payloads and every dependency- or order-sensitive relationship do not (the CV-26 (b) domain, D-97 (6) v3.2; research 06 §18.3) — yields identical obligation versions, balances, schedules, posting intents, diagnostics and trace values outside the stage 12 layer lineage, whose per-measure, per-period totals agree. The output hash is not compared in (b): it covers `input_sha256`, which encodes the arrival order, and the keys of same-date layers carry the arriving event (rev 1.29; ruled by D-97 (6) as CV-26 (a) and (b); rev 1.30) | engine | `test_prop_p08_determinism.py` |
| P9 | Idempotency: resubmitting an event or import with the same key creates no new lines | platform | `test_prop_p09_idempotency.py` |
| P10 | Split invariance: one delivery of q on a date equals deliveries q1 + q2 on that date | engine | `test_prop_p10_split_invariance.py` |
| P11 | Closed-period immutability: after lock, no command sequence changes lines of the locked period; late events create origin-tagged lines in the open period | platform | `test_prop_p11_closed_period.py` |
| P12 | FX: contract-liability layer functional amounts never change after creation; consumed layers end at zero; remeasurement never posts to revenue; at every period end and at settlement, contract assets, receivables, refund liabilities, deposit liabilities and consideration payable denominated in a currency other than the functional currency carry functional amount = transaction amount × closing rate, the difference posted to `FX_GAIN_LOSS` in every book (D-25, D-25b; rev 1.2); a contract-liability layer created by a refund-liability or deposit release takes the release carrying less the contract-asset settlements the release makes, within one minor unit per layer involved of round(amount × spot), and each release ties consumed = settled + created per source (D-87 L6-5-Q-26; D-88 L7-6-Q-2; D-89b; rev 1.5) | engine | `test_prop_p12_fx_layers.py` |
| P13 | Books with identical policy hashes produce identical allocation outputs | engine | `test_prop_p13_book_equivalence.py` |
| P14 | Re-evaluating every calc trace reproduces the stored numbers exactly, and every node names a registered formula | engine | `test_prop_p14_trace_reevaluation.py` (rev 1.29: generated groups in the ASC606 and IFRS15 books and the golden Contract 2 step 09 bundle in the ASC606 and LEGACY books; P14 is also enforced by DG-AK-54 in the answer-key runner and by inline `reevaluate(trace)` assertions in the stage tests) |
| Stateful | `RuleBasedStateMachine` with rules `create_contract`, `record_progress`, `record_billing`, `modify`, `change_vc`, `publish_fx_rates`, `start_close`, `lock`, `reopen`, `submit_late_event`, `void_event`; P1, P4, P5, P6 and P11 checked after every step; oracle = a simple reference implementation (research 06 §18.4) | platform | `test_prop_state_machine.py` |
| Metamorphic | Scaling every exact money input by 10^k within currency limits scales every homogeneous exact money figure by 10^k exactly (trace node exact values, schedule `cumulative_exact`, exact amount columns), except that a stored exact amount column that carries the CV-51 / DG-KRN-EXP-03 18-place encoding of its producing node — `allocated_exact` when the version links an `allocated_amount` node, `original_ssp_selected` when it links the `residual_ssp` node, the contract `total_ssp` when its node is linked — scales within the single-encoding tolerance (1 + 10^k) / (2·10^18) (D-98 candidate 116, addenda 1 and 2; raw columns stay exact); the unit revenue rates (CV-47 (b)) are not members of that exception: `original_unit_revenue_rate` keeps the strict exact scaling law (its engine conformance is D-98 candidate 117, an ENG-T1F item), and `remaining_unit_revenue_rate` alone is judged by the narrowed remaining-only law of D-98 candidate 116 ADDENDUM 3 REVISION 4 — a stated change from exact equality of at most (1 + 10^k)·h / (2·q̂) with h = 10^-18, i.e. 5.5·10^-18 at k = 1 and q̂ = 1, with no currency term — which applies only when (1) both worlds lie inside the positively whitelisted CONSTRUCTED input family, inspected on the bundle and its defaults: ordinary distinct STANDARD PRINCIPAL obligations recognised TIME_ELAPSED DAILY / MONTHLY_EVEN or POINT_IN_TIME with LINE_START / LINE_END dates, warranty NONE, no policy values, not excluded from netting attribution; ordinary distinct principal products without bundle components or policy values; contracts without judgements, material rights, modifications, non-cash consideration, consideration payable, payment schedules or termination / renewal terms and with commercial substance; SSP entries as positive observable AMOUNT points; booking lines with only the six API-S-ContractLine members, positive prices and quantities of at least one; only CONTRACT_BOOKED, CONTRACT_ACTIVATED, DELIVERY_RECORDED and BILLING_RECORDED events, none manual; the DEFAULT preset without rule sets, estimates, FX rates or posted input; and the two worlds differ only in money amounts (same contracts, dates, calendars, quantities, keys and event order); (2) the row's raw premises hold — raw `original_allocated_exact` scales exactly, raw `progress_ratio` is invariant within [0, 1], raw and decoded `remaining_quantity` are invariant, the rate links `remaining_unit_revenue_rate:<subject>:-` — the `books.unit_revenue_rate.v1` node whose inputs are exactly `remaining_allocation:<subject>:-` and `remaining_quantity:<subject>:-`, whose `allocation` parameter equals the numerator node's exact value and whose separately encoded value lies within h/2 of the stored raw quotient; the numerator is the posted `rec.remaining.v1` allocation node with a residue, citing only the same subject's `revenue_cum:<subject>:-` (an unadjusted `rec.revenue_cum.v1` node the row's `revenue_cum` column links, whose posted value is that column and whose decoded exact value lies within h/2 of X·f) and posting exactly the row's `allocated_amount` less that posted revenue (the row's `remaining_allocation`); the quantity is the input-free exact `rec.remaining.v1` quantity node the row's `remaining_quantity` column links, equal to the raw column and to its `quantity` parameter (the `original_quantity:<subject>:-` node's value) less `consumed`; every column, link and node is resolved by name and an absent source fails with that name (Codex production-20260921-0214 C2); no modification boundary, obligation kind STANDARD; and (3) the per-world anchor abs(N̂ − X·(1 − f)) ≤ h/2 holds with X the raw `original_allocated_exact` and f the raw `progress_ratio` (the pre-recognition guard is f = 0, N = X; an inactive segment never substitutes the original X); then abs(N̂′ − 10^k·N̂) ≤ (1 + 10^k)·h/2, for a nonzero q the stored rate equals N̂ ÷ q exactly on each world and abs(rate′ − 10^k·rate) ≤ (1 + 10^k)·h / (2·abs(q)), and a zero q stores 0 exactly; (4) any row or world outside the theorem fails a named prerequisite or keeps the strict exact law, nothing inherits the tolerance, NULL rates stay exact, and the trace-node scaling law and every other oracle are unchanged (supersedes the provisional 1.47 wording of the wave-3 merge prep — tolerance divided by quantity for both linked rates — which was not approved; Codex production-20260921-0041 / 0053 / 0135 / 0139); dimensionless and non-money quantities (ratios, counts, day fractions, progress) are excluded from the scaling assertion and compared for identity; every posted figure scales within an operation-appropriate derived bound along its derivation (a single rounding: half a minor unit; a largest-remainder share: up to two-thirds of a minor unit, as 100.00 over three equal weights shows; the bound composes the operations on the derivation path, with absolute coefficients, and the residues are validated against the same composition); a figure computed from rounded or intermediate discontinuous inputs is compared through those inputs, not assumed homogeneous; attributions that turn on a posted zero / non-zero or a posted tie — ALG-02 step 5 (POL-121) over unconditional and conditional POBs and the S10-R-21 classification — are compared as the pool per entity and period at group, member and obligation level (nodes of `contract_asset`, `unbilled_receivable`, their current parts and `netting_reclass_amount`; `NETTING_RECLASS` posting targets, deltas and intents; debit-role layers; the balance debit pair over member rows); every other assertion is per subject; the pool is confined to the named ALG-02 / S10-R-21 attribution family and preserves the accounting unit (group, entity, book, currency, period) plus the applicable event and intent dimensions; every subject still needs a valid own output-to-node lineage — pooled scaling is never a link exception; the generator has one group and one entity, so the measured examples do not establish a multi-group or multi-entity law. The two pinned counter-examples (BHD 0.227 UR → 0.005 / 2.265, total 2.270; K-1@US01 15.649 → 158.183, K-2@US01 0 + 0.865 UR → 6.957 CA, totals 16.514 → 165.140) are the normative examples (rev 1.30, D-97 (7) v3.2). One batch equals several arrivals: an effective-date slice or a record prefix computed and sealed as `posted`, then the full stream, gives the cumulative intents of the full stream computed at once, and the same versions, balances and schedules (RCP-05, S14-R-04). A calendar shift by whole months with equal day counts per period leaves every figure unchanged once period keys, dates and date ordinals are read relative to the inception (`DAILY` and point-in-time lines). An IFRS15 book whose resolved policies equal the ASC606 book's gives identical obligation versions, balances, schedules, intents (by shape and amount) and trace values (research 06 §18.5) | engine | `test_prop_metamorphic.py` |

The G5 statement of `docs/00-GOAL.md` §3 maps to P1 (allocations sum), P4 (recognition never exceeds allocation at completion), P5 (debits equal credits), P6 (rollforward) and P8 (replay determinism). `make properties` runs all rows.

### 9.8 Playwright harness (G8)

```ts
// Binding shape: frontend/e2e/playwright.config.ts
// The closed world's run (DG-MK-e2e `CLOSE=1`, rev 1.277) is named by scripts/e2e.sh.
const CLOSED_WORLD = process.env.EREV_E2E_CLOSE === "1";

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "./projects",
  outputDir: "./.results",
  forbidOnly: true,
  retries: 0,
  timeout: 120_000,
  expect: { timeout: 10_000 },
  reporter: [["list"], ["json", { outputFile: "../../.run/reports/e2e/report.json" }]],
  use: {
    baseURL: `http://127.0.0.1:${process.env.EREV_E2E_WEB_PORT ?? "5279"}`,
    trace: "retain-on-failure",
    screenshot: "off",
    video: "off",
    locale: "en-US",
    timezoneId: "UTC",
    viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 },
  },
  projects: CLOSED_WORLD
    ? [
        { name: "closed", testMatch: /closed\.spec\.ts$/, fullyParallel: true },
        {
          name: "qa-rc",
          testMatch: /qa-rc\.spec\.ts$/,
          fullyParallel: false,
          use: { trace: "off" },
        },
      ]
    : [
        { name: "avenmoor-serial", testMatch: /avenmoor-serial\.spec\.ts$/, fullyParallel: false },
        { name: "fresh-tenant", testMatch: /fresh-tenant\.spec\.ts$/, fullyParallel: true },
        { name: "industry", testMatch: /industry\.spec\.ts$/, fullyParallel: true },
        { name: "screens", testMatch: /screens\.spec\.ts$/, fullyParallel: true },
        { name: "design", testMatch: /design\.spec\.ts$/, fullyParallel: false },
        { name: "crawl", testMatch: /crawl\.spec\.ts$/, fullyParallel: true },
      ],
});
```

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-E2E-01 | Isolation: e2e always uses ports 8199 and 5279, database `erev_e2e`, `EREV_ENV=e2e`, and a production build served by `vite preview` (DG-RUN-04 to DG-RUN-06). The dev stack is never used. |
| DG-E2E-02 | `scripts/e2e.sh` runs the projects as separate invocations in this order: `avenmoor-serial --workers=1`, `fresh-tenant --workers=4`, `industry --workers=2`, `screens --workers=2`, `design --workers=1`, `crawl --workers=2` (docs/02-PRD.md E2E-04 to E2E-06; the route crawl of DG-E2E-13 last, rev 1.116). `PROJECT` restricts the list. Rev 1.277 (item RV-AS-LOCKED-DEFAULT-1): these six are the projects of the open world, where every period of 2026 is open as the seed leaves it. `make e2e CLOSE=1` (DG-MK-e2e) is the run of the closed world and has a list of its own: `closed --workers=2` (`frontend/e2e/projects/closed.spec.ts`: the screens of a locked period — the reports as locked and on current figures, the locked cockpit, the permanent-lock request). `frontend/e2e/playwright.config.ts` lists the closed world's projects where `EREV_E2E_CLOSE=1` and the six otherwise, so neither run lists or runs a row of the other world: `frontend/config/e2e-projects.test.ts` asks `playwright test --list` both ways, and `backend/tests/unit/test_e2e_script.py` holds the script's side — the list, the seed, the variable and the two refusals. A row that writes leaves the closed world as it was seeded for the project that runs after its own. Rev 1.280 (DG-E2E-14): the closed world has a second list, of projects run by name only — `qa-rc --workers=1`. A `CLOSE=1` run without `PROJECT` is the first list alone; `PROJECT` may name `qa-rc`, alone or with `closed`, and it then runs after the first list as its own invocation on the same seeded stack. The configuration lists both projects where `EREV_E2E_CLOSE=1`, and the two tests hold `qa-rc` as they hold `closed`: the listing both ways, and in the script's test that it runs only when named, after `closed`, with one worker, and is refused by name without `CLOSE=1`. Rev 1.285 (register index 280): one row is the exception. The row that takes a period to its permanent lock — `closed.spec.ts` "SF-08:report rpo of a permanently locked period marcus and elena" — leaves the world changed for good: January 2026 of AVM-US permanently locked and an approved PERIOD_LOCK request. Nothing takes that back, so the row runs last in its serial group, and every project that runs on that world after it reads that state. |
| DG-E2E-03 | Journeys: one module per PRD journey, `frontend/e2e/journeys/j-nn-<slug>.journey.ts`, exporting `export function jnn(): void` that declares `test.describe("J-nn <PRD journey title>", …)`. Each acceptance item is a `test.step` whose title starts with its id (`J-05-AC-2 …`, E2E-01). An alternate path is a separate `test("J-nn-ALT-n <title>")` in the same describe. `projects/avenmoor-serial.spec.ts` sets `test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" })` and calls the journeys in E2E-04 order. `fresh-tenant.spec.ts` calls J-01, J-20, J-21 and J-23. `industry.spec.ts` calls J-24. |
| DG-E2E-04 | `SPEC` semantics: a journey id in the serial project runs the E2E-04 prefix up to and including that journey (`EREV_E2E_UNTIL=J-nn`), because later journeys depend on earlier outcomes. Any other journey id runs alone (`--grep "^J-nn "`). A comma-separated list runs each. A path is passed to Playwright as a file filter. |
| DG-E2E-05 | Fixtures (`frontend/e2e/support/fixtures.ts`): `personas` signs in each WLD-U persona through the UI with `EREV_DEMO_PASSWORD` and a TOTP code computed by `otpauth` from `EREV_DEMO_TOTP_SECRET` (WLD-U-R2, E2E-08), caching storage state under `e2e/.results/auth/<persona>.json`; `api` is a request context for exact-decimal assertions; `screens` and `a11y` are described below; `network` is described in DG-E2E-08. |
| DG-E2E-06 | Screenshots: `screens.capture(page, name)` waits for `document.fonts.ready`, asserts the Inter font is loaded, masks `[data-volatile]` elements, disables animations, and writes `frontend/e2e/.screens/<spec slug>/<nn>-<name>.light.png` and `…dark.png` by setting `data-theme` on `<html>` and waiting two animation frames. It appends an entry to `frontend/e2e/.screens/index.json` (journey, step id, surface id, both files) for designer review (G8, G12). Screenshots are gitignored and never asserted pixel by pixel. |
| DG-E2E-07 | Accessibility: `a11y.check(page, surfaceId)` runs `@axe-core/playwright` with tags `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`. It fails on any violation of impact `serious` or `critical` and writes the full result to `e2e/.results/axe/<spec slug>/<surface>.json`. Every journey checks each surface it visited (E2E-09). `screens.spec.ts` covers every screen of SCREENS.md and SCREENS_B.md in both themes (DS-VER-05; DG-READ-02). `design.spec.ts` covers DS-VER-06 to DS-VER-09. |
| DG-E2E-08 | Network guard: `context.route("**/*")` allows only `127.0.0.1` hosts and `data:` and `blob:` URLs; any other request is aborted and recorded, and the test fails when the record is non-empty (REQ-SEC-008). |
| DG-E2E-09 | Determinism: journeys pass explicit effective dates and periods (E2E-07); `page.waitForTimeout` is forbidden; locators prefer `getByRole` and `getByLabel`, with `data-testid="<sf id>-<element>"` only where no accessible name exists; records are found by external id or name, never by generated numbers (WLD-R-07). |
| DG-E2E-10 | Money assertions happen twice: the API value as an exact string and the rendered text per DS-FMT-04 to DS-FMT-06 (E2E-02). |
| DG-E2E-11 | Artifacts: traces retained on failure under `e2e/.results/`; JSON report `.run/reports/e2e/report.json`; no automatic retries. |
| DG-E2E-12 | Fresh tenants (rev 1.1; REQ-PLT-038, PRD E2E-05, BR-PLT-01). `frontend/e2e/support/tenants.ts` exports `createTenant({code, name, reportingCurrency, demo, admin})`, which runs `backend/.venv/bin/erev tenant create …` through `child_process.execFile` (no shell) with `EREV_ENV=e2e`, parses the JSON line of DG-KRN-TEN-04 and fails the `beforeAll` on a non-zero exit. Codes and admins are those the PRD names for each journey (for example `--code harbourline --admin tomas@demo.erev` for J-01). `make e2e` resets `erev_e2e` on every invocation, so these codes are free; a duplicate code fails with `TENANT_CODE_EXISTS` (DG-KRN-TEN-02) and fails the spec. The harness never calls `POST /api/v1/operator/tenants`. |
| DG-E2E-13 | Route crawl (rev 1.116; supervisor ruling R-67 (b); browser-QA findings Q-9 and Q-30: two defects reached browser QA because no e2e step opened their routes). `projects/crawl.spec.ts` is the last project. It reads `frontend/src/app/router.tsx` as source (`support/routes.ts`: every route object with an `id` and a `path`, a child under its parent's path), so a new route is crawled without an edit to the spec, and the route table of SCREENS §0.4 for the permission of each screen; it declares one test per route. **Opening.** The test opens the route as the first persona of `maya`, `tomas`, `nikhil` and then the other WLD-U personas that holds the permissions of the route's row (one persona per permission when none holds them all; a `public` route signed out; RT-02 after the password step). A path parameter comes from the table `SEEDS` of the spec: a record found through the API by its business key (DG-E2E-09), or found-or-created as the screens rows create it when only an earlier project would have left it (`support/world.ts`: the journal run, the SSP calculator run). A route the project does not open is named in `NOT_OPENED` with its reason, or in `NOT_SEEDED` when the demo world holds no record, and its test asserts that the world still holds none; a route whose record only a row of project `screens` leaves behind (a chain verification, an integration connection and its run) is named in `LEFT_BY_SCREENS`: in `make e2e`, where this project runs after `screens`, a missing record fails, and a run of this project alone on a fresh world lists the route with that reason; no route is skipped silently, and a parameter without a `SEEDS` entry or a redirect without its target in `LANDS_ON` stops the project before any page opens. **Checks**, after the page has settled and after every action below: the route error boundary (`X-banner-route-error`), "Page not found" on a route other than `*`, the no-access state, the SCR-URL-21 banner, an API request of the page that answers 400 or above and that no entry of `ALLOWED` names (method, path, status, an optional query pattern, and the rule that makes the answer correct or the item that owns the defect), an API request that failed on the network, an uncaught script error, and a landing route other than the route itself or its `LANDS_ON` target. **Actions**, on the shared components only: one click on every sortable column header (`aria-sort`) of every DS-CMP-10 grid; one term typed into every DS-CMP-13 quick search; every field of every filter bar applied once with the first value its editor offers and removed again; every DS-CMP-07 panel tab of the first level opened, with the grid and filter actions repeated there. A field whose editor offers nothing to choose is recorded as not driven with the reason. A page has settled when no request is in flight, none has finished within 300 ms and no region is busy (`aria-busy`, `role="progressbar"`); the wait is `expect.poll`, never `page.waitForTimeout` (DG-E2E-09). **Record.** Each test attaches its record (persona, URL, landing route, headers clicked, filters applied, panes opened, what was not driven, findings) and writes it to `frontend/e2e/.results/crawl/<route>.json`. The crawl checks that a screen opens and that what its controls send is admitted; it does not replace the SCREENS_B §15 audit rows of `screens`, which assert what a screen shows. |
| DG-E2E-14 | The release candidate's multi-role browser QA (rev 1.280; PROGRESS.md D-99 (7); the supervisor's acceptance of 2026-10-02). `frontend/e2e/projects/qa-rc.spec.ts` with `frontend/e2e/support/qa/` is a pass, not a gate: its product is a record, and it leaves the world changed. **Who.** The eleven personas of PRD §2.3 and a twelfth member the pass makes through the product — invited by a Tenant Admin with one role for one legal entity, decided by the second administrator, accepted from the invitation's link — because the seed gives every role for all entities. **What.** Nine sections, one test each, one worker, in this order: sign-in, landing, rail and sign-out of every seeded member; the member for one entity; the entity bound as that member (03 REQ-PLT-012; PRD BR-UX-06: a record of another entity is answered exactly as an id that names nothing, by the API, by a typed address and to a command; every route she can open; what "All entities" offers her and totals); the workspace bound (03 REQ-PLT-001: a record of another workspace by id, by address and to a command, as a member of two workspaces and as a member of one; and what a workspace is shown of a person another workspace made, before she accepts — D-80 rule 5); one contract from draft to revenue; the open month's close to its lock as PRD J-13 walks it; where a lock request is decided — the request's own screen, read and not pressed; denial per member, read against the API document — every operation whose `x-erev-permission` a member lacks answers 403; the figures of the months the seed closed, each fact read from every place that states it, and the contract balance roll-forward as each lock froze it. A test before them writes the head and the world the pass found, and one after them writes the record. **Rules of the pass.** A check writes one row — check, persona, address, expected with its reference, observed, result — to `${EREV_RUN_DIR}/qa-rc/rows.jsonl` when it is made, and never asserts the product: a test of the project fails only on what the committed fixtures assert (DG-E2E-08) and on a section that cannot run, which is written as a row first. A finding is of three classes and no other — a wrong figure, a bound that does not hold, a core flow that stops — and is read a second time before its row says `FINDING`; seen once it is written as seen once. A step of a flow is taken on the screen, twice, before the same command goes through the API, and the row says which it was. An item the register already holds is marked `KNOWN` with its index. Everything else the pass sees is one parked line. No wait of the pass is without an end: a check that throws, or that has not ended in twenty minutes — a flow step in fifty — is written as not run with what stopped it, and the pass goes on. The pass repairs nothing, and `page.waitForTimeout` stays forbidden (DG-E2E-09). **Running it.** `make e2e CLOSE=1 PROJECT=qa-rc`, or `PROJECT=closed,qa-rc` for both (DG-MK-e2e, DG-E2E-02): the closed world, by name only, on a stack seeded for it. After `closed` the pass meets January 2026 of AVM-US permanently locked (rev 1.285) and reads it as a closed month. The pass itself invites a member and locks September, so no other project runs after it on that world. The project records no trace: a section is one test of many minutes and hundreds of pages, and a trace is written while a test runs whether or not it is kept; the record has a capture a row. **The record.** A record is of one world: the run directory outlives a stack, so the project's first test reads the world — the id of the Avenmoor workspace, which every seed makes anew — and sets the rows, the state and the captures of an earlier world aside as `qa-rc-<world>` before it writes its own; nothing is removed. The lane reads the rows, confirms each finding by hand and writes `docs/qa/RC-multi-role-qa-<date>.md` in the form of `docs/qa/G12-multi-role-qa-2026-09-17.md`; the captures stay under the run directory until the record has been read. |

### 9.9 Performance harness (G9)

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-PERF-01 | Volume tenant (rev 1.1; D-75 Q7; 05 PERF-10 to PERF-15). Tenant `perf-volume` (`kind = production`, `is_demo = true`) lives in database `erev` and is built only by `make perf-seed`, through `erev_api.domain.demo.volume.seed(contracts=10_000, obligations=50_000, months=24, seed=20260912)` using commands in chunks (REQ-OPS-009). The generator manifest covers all 24 months. The seed appends months 1 to 23, closes and locks them with the PERF-15 personas — rev 1.243: `perf-accountant@demo.erev` prepares a month's close and requests its lock, `perf-reviewer@demo.erev` approves its journal run and `perf-controller@demo.erev` decides the lock (DG-MK-perf-seed) —, holds back the month-24 events, and stores a snapshot as of the month-23 lock (T-PLT-34; rev 1.243: purpose `STORED_BACKUP`, DG-MK-perf-seed (5)). Generation time is not measured (PERF-04 warns above 60 minutes). Perf tests never generate or modify `perf-volume`. Rev 1.177 (BUILD_SPEC CTR-6; 05 PERF-15 rev 1.133): `volume._record_batch` sends each contract-month as `perf-accountant`; a request the product stores as an event submission — it holds a delivery, a return, a milestone or a cost event — is approved by the cast's event reviewer (`VolumeCast.event_reviewer`: `perf-reviewer`, whose `revenue_reviewer` role carries `event.approve`; `priya` in the demo cast), with one evidence document per entity and month (`volume.evidence_document`) named where `volume.needs_evidence` says the product asks for it. `perf_seed.read_ledger` counts a contract-month as appended from its APPLIED submission as from a direct append's audit event, and a submission an interrupted run left SUBMITTED is approved on resume, never sent a second time. `GENERATOR_VERSION` is 10; it was 5 from rev 1.177. Rev 1.226 (item EVT-USAGE-MANUAL-1; 05 PERF-15 rev 1.187): a usage report is a manual event too, so `_record_batch` stores the contract-months that hold one as event submissions and the event reviewer approves them; evidence is not asked for a usage report, and the version went from 5 to 6 with the seeded state. Rev 1.247 (BUILD_SPEC CTR-12; 04 §16.14 rev 1.241; 05 PERF-15 rev 1.191): `volume._apply_estimate` gives each estimate version it submits what the product asks of it — one generated evidence document of its own (`volume.estimate_evidence_document`), stored and attached by `perf-accountant`, and, for a variable-consideration version, a `CONSTRAINT` judgement record of that version, which the cast's reviewer reviews before the version is submitted (`volume._ready_estimate_version`). A version an interrupted run left a draft is made ready from its persisted state — its attachment, its record and the record's status — and nothing is sent a second time; the version went from 6 to 7 with the seeded state. Rev 1.253 (item EVT-EVIDENCE-1; 05 PERF-15 rev 1.192): the approval of a contract-month attaches the entity's evidence document of the month to every event it appends (T-PLT-30 subject `contract_event`), and the generator version was raised with the seeded state. Rev 1.273 (item ACT-FLAGS-1; 05 PERF-15 rev 1.204; the supervisor's order of 2026-10-02 at the merge of the item, MANIFEST-BINDING-1): every generated contract states `acceptance_clause` and `side_letter` false and the request of an activation states the flags of its record and its amount in US dollars, so the seeded state changes — the requests' flags, amounts and steps — and the generator version was raised with it, to 9; the manifest and the event set are unchanged. Rev 1.243 (05 PERF-15 rev 1.182; item PERF-SEED-LOCK-1): `volume._append_month` sends a contract-month in the steps of `volume.month_steps` — the events a contract records in a month are sent by effective date, an `ESTIMATE_CHANGED` and a `CONTRACT_AMENDED` through their own commands at their place among the dates and the events between two such commands as one append. The comment of an append is its mark in the resume ledger (`volume.append_comment`): the last append of a contract-month carries "Volume month <n> (perf:<16 hex>)" and an earlier append of a month that a command divides "Volume month <n> part <k> of <parts> (perf:<16 hex>)". `perf_seed.read_ledger` reads both (`months_from_audit`, `parts_from_audit`): a contract-month of one append that the ledger holds is skipped whole, and a divided one is walked again step by step — an append the ledger holds is counted as reused and not sent, and a command finds its own version or modification. `volume.late_arrivals` counts on the manifest the events that arrive after a later-dated event of their contract, which are the `LATE_EVENT` items a seed raises and waives. An activation of USD 1,000,000.00 and more routes a second step held by a Controller (PRD §2.5): `perf-reviewer` decides the first and `perf-controller` the second, as for an estimate version — until this revision the seed named one approver and stopped at the first such contract, which the 24 months' manifest does not hold at 1/1000 and the test story's seven months' manifest does. `perf_seed.run` takes the manifest's months — 24; only a test seeds fewer — and appends and locks all but the last. `volume.seed` makes the bulk recompute of 05 PERF-15 only while every period of the manifest's months is `open` (`volume.recompute_due`): a run that finds one in soft close or locked — a resumed seed, or one that extends an earlier `--through-month` — has had it and does not recompute a group without a new event. `GENERATOR_VERSION` is 10 from the supervisor's join of rev 1.243 with the revisions above, on 2026-10-02 (the lane's branch numbered it 6): the seeded state changed with the order of a contract-month. With that order an estimate change is applied after the events dated before it, where it was applied ahead of its contract-month's other events, so its impact and the steps of its approval change too: measured at 1/1000, the first EAC change of VOL-C-000005 carries GBP 46,378.46 and takes the Controller's second step, where it carried GBP 30,918.98 and took one, and VOL-C-000004's first likewise. A cast's reviewer and controller are therefore two people, since no approver decides two steps of one request: `perf-reviewer` and `perf-controller`, and marcus and elena in the cast of the interim database test (`volume.DEMO_CAST`). Rev 1.268 (item ENG-COST-READBACK-1; 04 T-SL-04 `subject_key`): the seeded ledger stores the subject of every line, and it no longer holds the pairs a later computation posted again for a cost asset, a refund-liability component and a contract-level loss unit. `GENERATOR_VERSION` is 11. Rev 1.296 (item USAGE-REPORT-PERIOD-ENDED-1; 04 §16.3 rev 1.320; 05 PERF-15 rev 1.214): a usage report of the dataset ends its usage period at its own date — the month's first day to the report's date — where it named the whole month, which the door refuses. `GENERATOR_VERSION` is 13; version 12 was withdrawn with register index 87 and never seeded. Rev 1.292 (item ENG-USAGE-FIXED-SCHEDULE-1, returned behind register index 306; ENGINE_SPEC_B S09-R-45 rev 1.126; 05 PERF-15 rev 1.212): the engine calls the fixed fee of a usage obligation deterministic, so a seed stores the dataset's usage obligations with their remainder scheduled, where it was awaiting trigger, and with schedule lines to their term end; no posting moves. `GENERATOR_VERSION` is 14. |
| DG-PERF-02 | Close in a sandbox copy (rev 1.1; D-75 Q7). (1) Not measured: restore the stored snapshot of `perf-volume` — rev 1.243: the `STORED_BACKUP` the seed's step (5) asks (DG-MK-perf-seed), restored as the product's `POST /tenant/sandboxes` restores a stored snapshot, by a `TENANT_SNAPSHOT` job in load-only mode over the row's own id, `known_at` and purpose — into a new sandbox tenant whose code starts with `perf-run-` (REQ-PLT-024; 05 SBX-02 to SBX-05). When an ACTIVE `perf-run-*` sandbox exists, use `run_inline(JobKind.SANDBOX_RESET, …)`, which ARCHIVES it (05 SBX-07) — rev 1.243, as that branch stands and is not built here: the harness refuses such a run by name (`prior_active_refusal`), and a reset goes back to the sandbox's seed snapshot (`SANDBOX_SEED_REQUIRED`), which nothing rules yet for a sandbox restored from a stored backup; otherwise use `run_inline(JobKind.TENANT_SNAPSHOT, …)` with the stored snapshot as source. Rev 1.243, as the product stands (supervisor ruling R-10: the sandbox-side close replay, SNP-2b, is not built): the load replays no lock of the source. It opens the periods, recomputes every group and replays each soft close; each lock the seed made is then refused by the close gates, which the replay evaluates in the sandbox — it holds no journal run of its own (journals are never copied, 05 SBX-03), so `JE_BALANCED`, `JE_COMPLETE` and `BATCHES_ACKNOWLEDGED` fail for every period, and the load's recompute answers each late event of the generator with an open `LATE_EVENT` item again, the waivers being the source's, so `EXCEPTIONS_CLEARED` fails for the periods of an entity that holds one. Every period state the seed locked — months 1 to 23 for every entity and book — is therefore named in the load's `blocked_periods` and stands at `closing` in the restored sandbox, with one `SANDBOX_REPLAY_BLOCKED` warning and no lock; the load succeeds and `derived_mismatches` does not count it (05 SBX-05 compares the monetary state). In that state a close of a later month does not run — measured on 2026-10-02 in the story of the seed, six months locked, by a close of July 2025 for VOL-US: start-close is accepted; the close run passes its first six steps — the release of schedules and the remeasurement find nothing to post — and ends FAILED at the contract balance reclassification (`NETTING_RECLASS`), 409 `invalid-transition`: "Feb 2025 has period-end amounts no close run has posted; run its close first." (the period-end order, supervisor ruling R-112). The month it names is the first whose period end holds amounts no close run of the sandbox has posted — February there, not January, the first at `closing`. A lock request is refused besides while an earlier period is not closed (BR-CLS-08; measured where the close run had nothing to post: "Lock Jan 2025 first."). How (2) is measured until SNP-2b is built is not decided by this revision. The load's `derived_mismatches` (05 SBX-05) — the count of the job's result, which is the load report's; rev 1.108: never a member of the export manifest, 04 T-PLT-34 — must be 0; otherwise the test fails with "perf sandbox copy not deterministic". Rev 1.243: a load that compared nothing proves nothing, so the run also ends by name, with the counts, when the load left a contract group without a recompute (`groups_not_recomputed` above 0: "perf sandbox copy proves nothing: …") and when the sandbox does not hold the contract events `perf-volume` recorded at or before the snapshot's `known_at`, or holds none ("perf sandbox copy is not perf-volume as of the snapshot: …"); a copy that passes states that count in the report. Then append the month-24 events of the manifest to the sandbox through the batch append path (05 TXN-09) — rev 1.177 (BUILD_SPEC CTR-6): a request that the product answers with an event submission is approved by `perf-reviewer@demo.erev` before its events are counted (`prepare.append_month_24`), with the entity's evidence document of month 24 where it is asked —, and publish a platform registry version with `platform.job_concurrency = 8` for the sandbox, approved by `perf-reviewer@demo.erev` (05 PERF-20; rev 1.2). (2) Measured (rev 1.2; 05:OQ-ARC-10, D-76): with `api-perf` and the four `perf-worker-<n>` processes running (DG-PERF-08), the harness signs in as in DG-PERF-03 and, for each entity in entity-code order (`VOL-DE`, `VOL-UK`, `VOL-US`), sends `POST /api/v1/close-runs` for period `FY2026-P12` and book `ASC606` (API-R-39). The workers execute each close run's steps in 04 order from `CUTOFF` to `DATASET_FREEZE`, which include the 05 PERF-01 steps: `RECOMPUTE_DIRTY` (child `CONTRACT_COMPUTE` jobs, 05 RCP-19), `RELEASE_SCHEDULES`, `FX_REMEASUREMENT`, `NETTING_RECLASS`, `INVARIANTS`, `JOURNAL_SUMMARIZATION`, `EXPORT` (CSV adapter; journal batches stay CSV-only in the sandbox, 05 SBX-08), `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_WAIT`, `GL_TIE_OUT` and `DATASET_FREEZE` with its twelve E-64 datasets. Rev 1.3 (BUILD_SPEC BS4-D-03, BS4-D-04, BS4-D-16): `EXPORT`, `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_WAIT` and `GL_TIE_OUT` are observation steps (04 T-CLS-01), so the measured window has two passes. First, one close run per entity. Then the harness approves every journal run, exports its batches through the CSV adapter, acknowledges every exported batch with `POST /api/v1/journal-batches/{id}/acknowledge` (API-R-38), builds the trial balance CSV from the exported batches and attaches it with `POST /api/v1/reconciliations/{id}/attach-trial-balance` (API-R-40). Rev 1.243: a journal run that states no line (API-S-JournalRun `totals.line_count` 0) is left as the close run calculated it — not submitted, which item JRN-EMPTY-RUN-1 refuses, and so neither approved nor exported; on the dataset's manifest every entity has events in month 24. Then a second close run per entity, whose observation steps record the full export, acknowledgement and tie-out. The Controller certification and the `LOCK` approval wait are not measured. The harness polls `GET /api/v1/close-runs/{id}` every 2 seconds. Wall time from the first 202 response to the completion of the last second-pass close run's `DATASET_FREEZE` step ≤ 600 seconds (G9; rev 1.3); a step that ends with a problem, or a blocking exception item of the close run, fails the test. |
| DG-PERF-03 | API latency (rev 1.1; the pass criterion, confirmed by D-76): after DG-PERF-02, use `api-perf` (DG-RUN-09: uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8199 with `EREV_ENV=dev`, database `erev`, PID file `.run/api-perf.pid`; started by DG-PERF-08), sign in as `perf-controller@demo.erev` with `EREV_DEMO_PASSWORD` and a TOTP code from `EREV_DEMO_TOTP_SECRET`, and select the perf sandbox with `POST /api/v1/session/tenant`. After the unmeasured restore of DG-PERF-02 (1), the harness starts `api-perf` (DG-RUN-09) and `perf-worker-1` to `perf-worker-4` (DG-RUN-09a) through `scripts/proc.sh start` and waits for their readiness checks. | Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-GATE-01 | An item is never ticked while a gate its acceptance hints name is red (D-71: engine items are not ticked until their keys pass). |
| DG-GATE-02 | A regression found in an area outside the current item is fixed before the next item starts. When the fix is not possible within the loop's authority (for example it needs a document change), the loop writes `BLOCKED:` at the top of PROGRESS.md with the failing test ids and the document references. |
| DG-GATE-03 | A flaky test is a defect: it is made deterministic, never retried or skipped. |
| DG-GATE-04 | PROGRESS.md cites exact counts from the report files, never "tests pass". |

### 10.2 Git hygiene

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| DG-GIT-01 | Commit after the item's gates pass. Message: first line `<BUILD_SPEC item id>: <imperative summary>` (≤ 72 characters); body with the evidence counts; then the attribution trailer required by the harness. |
| DG-GIT-02 | Stage and commit in one shell command with explicit pathspecs: `git add -- <new or changed paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <the same paths>`. The index is never left populated between commands (several agents may share one checkout). |
| DG-GIT-03 | After committing, run `git show --stat HEAD` and confirm that only intended paths are included. A mistake is corrected with a new commit, never by rewriting history. |
| DG-GIT-04 | Never commit `.env`, `.run/`, `.data/`, `.scratch/`, `.ralph/`, `frontend/e2e/.screens/`, `frontend/e2e/.results/`, reports, build outputs, `node_modules/`, virtual environments, or binaries other than committed fixtures under `backend/tests/fixtures/` (each at most 5 MiB). |
| DG-GIT-05 | Never modify the supervisor documents of D-§0 (`docs/00-GOAL.md`, `docs/01-DECISIONS.md`, `docs/02-PRD.md`, `docs/03-REQUIREMENTS.md`, `docs/04-DATA_MODEL.md`, `docs/05-ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/dev-guide.md`, `docs/BUILD_SPEC.md`, everything under `docs/accounting/`, `docs/design/`, `docs/research/`, `docs/legacy/`, and `PROMPT.md`). |
| DG-GIT-06 | `PROGRESS.md` is committed with each item through the same pathspec command. |

### 10.3 Forbidden commands

| Id | Forbidden | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| DG-FORBID-01 | Reading or printing secrets: `cat .env`, `grep … .env`, `echo $EREV_*`, `env`, `printenv`, or logging settings values | `scripts/check_env.py --names` (names only) |
| DG-FORBID-02 | Stopping processes by pattern or port: `pkill`, `killall`, `kill $(lsof …)`, `lsof -t … \| xargs kill`, `kill %n` | `scripts/proc.sh stop <name>` (DG-RUN-11) |
| DG-FORBID-03 | Server, database and role administration: `brew services`, `pg_ctl`, `createdb`, `dropdb`, `createuser`, `dropuser`, `psql` as a superuser or the OS default role, `ALTER SYSTEM`, `CREATE DATABASE`, `DROP DATABASE`, `CREATE ROLE`, `ALTER ROLE`, `DROP ROLE`, `CREATE EXTENSION`, `DROP SCHEMA` outside DG-ENV-13 | Migrations as `erev_owner`; test fixtures |
| DG-FORBID-04 | Writing to `/tmp`: `mktemp` without `-p "$TMPDIR"`, `/tmp` paths in code, scripts or configuration | `.run/tmp` (DG-RUN-30) |
| DG-FORBID-05 | History-changing or index-sweeping git: `git push`, `git pull`, `git fetch`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, `git checkout -- .`, `git restore .`, `git stash`, `git rebase`, `git commit --amend`, `git add -A`, `git add .`, `git add -u`, `git commit -a`, `--no-verify`, `git config`, `git worktree` | DG-GIT-02 |
| DG-FORBID-06 | Loop control: invoking `ralph.sh` or any loop script, creating or deleting files under `.ralph/`, editing `PROMPT.md` | Stop condition of PROMPT.md |
| DG-FORBID-07 | Deploy and publish: `terraform plan`, `apply`, `import`, `destroy`; `gcloud`; `docker push`, `docker login`; `docker compose` with a project other than `erev-verify` and, for `make restore-drill` alone, `erev-verify-drill` (rev 1.97); `npm publish`; `uv publish` | none for the loop; the supervisor runs the §4.5 targets |
| DG-FORBID-08 | Network access in tests or ad hoc commands: `curl` or `wget` to a non-127.0.0.1 host; package installs and lock-file updates outside `make setup`, including `uv add`, `uv lock`, `uv pip`, `npm install` and `npm update` (rev 1.2; D-76, DG-OQ-13) | Mock adapters (DG-API-09); fake AI provider (DG-AI-02); `make setup LOCK=1` for a new dependency (DG-ENV-08) |
| DG-FORBID-09 | Touching legacy and research artefacts: writing under `~/dev/erev-legacy`, `legacy-harness/` or `research-harness/`; importing `eRev.py`; running `legacy-harness/run.sh` or `research-harness/deviations/build_deviations.py` | `make fixtures` (DG-PAR-02); the supervisor reruns harnesses |
| DG-FORBID-10 | `sudo`; `rm -rf` outside the repository; editing `~/.claude`, shell profiles or global git configuration | none |
| DG-FORBID-11 | Background servers with `--reload`; Vite or uvicorn on ports other than §3.1; Playwright `webServer` blocks | `make dev-up`, `make e2e` |
| DG-FORBID-12 | Running a supervisor target or its script: `make audit-deps`, `make zap-baseline`, `make docker-build`, `make compose-verify`, `make tf-validate`, `make backup`, `make restore-verify`, `make restore-drill` (D-48a; rev 1.1; rev 1.3 lane P6; rev 1.97 lane OPS) | Record `SUPERVISOR VERIFICATION NEEDED: make <target>` in PROGRESS.md (DG-MK-00h) |

### October 7 continuation: close-gate waiver identities

`close.gates._blocker_populations` owns the predicates for both cockpit counts and waiver
members. Gate evaluation aggregates their IDs from one statement; reconciliations read kind,
current row ID, status and overtaken state together. Do not reintroduce separate count and
membership filters. A waived gate retains its approved member set, while each evaluation
compares the current set. Additions or replacements lapse the waiver; a subset remains covered.
Legacy count-only waivers fail closed when blockers remain. This is membership coverage,
not a seal of every mutable field of each source record.

The checklist waiver approval hook holds the period before checklist rows, refreshes the
automatic gates under tenant scope and checks its own request's content hash before applying.
A stale basis rolls the decision and refresh back through the kernel savepoint and voids the
request. This also protects decisions made without an intervening cockpit refresh. Submitted
identities are retained in the request audit; lapse events retain the before/after identities.
The existing bounded lapse audit applies to identity changes as well as growth, and historical lock certifications are not rewritten.

For the approvals gate (B1-11), submission also stores the original result as `waiver_basis`
inside the same JSONB result. Evaluation preserves it while the request is pending, and the
content hash uses that basis. Final approval refreshes the current pending population and
requires it to be a subset of the submitted identities. Completed requests may drop out;
new pending requests cannot inherit review. A fully cleared gate voids its unneeded waiver.
Approval retains the original covered scope and removes the temporary basis; rejection or
voiding removes the temporary basis with the request pointer. Other gates keep strict pending
basis checks. No migration or historical lock rewrite is needed.

### October 7 continuation: Step 1 scope and import computation

Step 1's subject-content callback is registered by the contracts domain through
SubjectLifecycle.content; the approvals kernel does not import the domain to hash it.
After the caller's contract authorization, record_events previews the group's full
entity scope. step1_approval.lock_basis holds every member's book, judgement and
posting windows; requires_review examines all affected entities/books;
same_effective_day checks their time zones; content seals the complete group basis.
These tenant-bound system-scope calls return no cross-entity rows to the caller.

IPL-11 import children are stored computations, not previews. The commit queues one
CONTRACT_COMPUTE job per affected group after validating the uploader's scope and
source rows. Dispatch follows transaction commit; report readers retain their own
entity permissions. These sites are explicitly enumerated by DG-ARC-16 and
DG-KRN-APR-07 architecture checks.


### Import monetary read-back — October 7, 2026

An import template may register `reconcile_amounts(session, plan, applied, context=...)`.
The commit calls it after applying the plan, inside the same narrowed transaction.
It must independently reconstruct expected monetary facts from the validated source
rows and read the actual persisted targets. Returning unequal source/stored maps
raises CONTROL_TOTALS_MISMATCH and rolls back the whole batch, including source
records and deferred calculations. Evidence is retained under loaded.monetary_checks.
A callback must cover every amount column before it enables the loaded.amount_sums
comparison. Those sums follow IPL-06 file-column semantics, including repeated cells;
they are calculated only after the independent read-back proves the written facts.

The CSV `invoices` template implements this callback for document totals,
signed source lines, positive invoice/credit events, tax components and currencies.
Repeated tax rows contribute each tax once and one logical invoice line; their
repeated amount cells still count in the file-column total.

Costs, pre-standard revenue and usage also register the callback. Their shared
reader binds each stored event to the expected contract, event type, effective
date and source record before comparing amount and currency. Signed amounts stay
signed; an absent rated usage amount stays null, distinct from explicit zero.
The callbacks cover all monetary columns of these three one-event-per-row templates.
The CSV SSP values reader independently reconstructs entry prices, ratios and bands
from validated rows, including value basis, quantity unit, currency and entry keys.
It reads the actual entries and complete band sets for the emitted book version.
Legacy-range bands are independently derived and compared at TY-02 NUMERIC(38,18)
precision with half-away-from-zero rounding. SSP numeric inputs are flattened as
text columns; their explicit monetary_checks evidence is required even when the
file's amount_sums map is empty. Bands are grouped by entry in linear time before
comparison.

Contract imports compare each stored booking line's total price, out-of-scope amount,
unit price, quantity and currency against its validated source row, keyed by obligation
and product. Contract and payload transaction currencies must agree with the file.
Both new bookings and draft replacements carry the import upload/source-record IDs;
replacement imports now pass those through the existing replace_draft command. A
monetary mismatch rolls back the replacement and preserves the previous draft.
Estimate imports reconcile scalar amounts, rates, quantities, amortization months,
kind-specific parameters and complete scenario evidence from the stored version.
Contract/element identity, method, currency, direction, allocation target and obligation
are also checked. New elements use the command's declared defaults; omitted settings
of existing elements retain their existing meaning, while explicit file values must
agree. Source figures are reconstructed from validated rows, not the emitter's plan
body. Money/exact columns compare at their declared database scale; JSON scenarios
retain their decimal precision.

Legacy SKU SSP imports independently translate validated legacy cells into canonical
SSP inputs and use the same persisted entry/range reader. Currency comes from the
upload tenant's reporting currency. The emitter's request builder is not reused.
For legacy templates without flattened columns, verified file-column totals use
the upload's pinned template header definitions. Whole-version quarantine remains
atomic.

Legacy contract setup checks source-order line prices/quantities separately from
booking-event prices/quantities, currencies and source-record identity. Split uploads
reconstruct retained draft lines from immutable earlier bookings. VC rows must produce
linked approved estimate versions with matching magnitude, currency, effective date
and import approval. Newly created elements also match the source sign and defaults;
existing elements retain their established settings. A missing VC writer cannot pass
commit. Tests that observe that port now call its real writer. Legacy progress and
modification monetary readers remain incomplete and are not claimed as covered.
